`CHANGELOG.md`:

```md
# Changelog

All notable changes to SlopStation are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the project uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). The release job publishes the
section matching the pushed tag as the GitHub release notes.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.3.1] - 2026-11-14

### Fixed

- The desktop app hung on the boot splash ("waiting for the engine to accept connections"):
  the window CSP allowed only `http:` to the engine, so the 0.3.0 websocket event stream threw
  and the client retried it forever instead of falling back to SSE. The CSP now allows
  `ws://127.0.0.1:*`, and a websocket that cannot be created falls back to SSE on the same ticket.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- **PS5 backend** over ps5debug-NG v1.3.2: `target.ps5_connect/ps5_disconnect/ps5_reconnect/ps5_auto/ps5_notify`
  and `debugger.ps5_*` (attach, 30 breakpoint slots, 4 DR watchpoints, continue/step/suspend/resume,
  registers, threads, port-755 stop events, console info/notify/print/foreground app). The memory,
  scanner and disassembly tools work on a PS5 through the same backend abstraction; `docs/ps5.md`
  documents the protocol source, ports and limits.
- **Multi-console manager**: `target.consoles_list/consoles_save/consoles_remove/consoles_switch` keep
  saved endpoints (host, port, notes, default pid, title filter, auto-connect) with a per-console
  profile (named watchlist set + scan width/kind). Switching detaches cleanly (session, breakpoint and
  watchpoint slots, scan state), restores the target console's profile and falls back to the previous
  console when the new one does not answer. Targets panel gained the saved-consoles card, the status
  bar an active-console quick switch.
- **Tern onboarding**: `slopstation` is registered in `%APPDATA%\tern\settings.json` (`agents.mcp`,
  http, `${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN}` bearer) and is the only client written when Tern is installed. New
  `mcp_onboard_clients` (empty = auto) and `mcp_token_in_configs` (default off) settings, plus a
  Settings banner listing client configs that still hold a plaintext token.
- **MCP**: `resources` (`slop://state/target`, `slop://state/image`, `slop://guide/<topic>`) and
  `prompts` (the guide playbooks); `notifications/progress` for a `tools/call` carrying
  `_meta.progressToken`; per-tool rate limits (`mcp_rate_limits`); `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`.
- **Scanner**: host-side unknown-initial-value scans for the usermode backend, relative-change kinds
  (`changed_by_more_than`, `changed_by_less_than`, `increased_by`, `decreased_by`), multi-level pointer
  scans with per-level offset ranges/wildcards/alignment and module-relative roots, `memory.scan_export`
  (CSV), `memory.diff export:{csv|json}`, IDA/x64dbg/CE/C signature renderings, Cheat Engine `.CT`
  watchlist import/export, and per-entry freeze rates (`interval_ms`).
- **Debugger**: hit-count breakpoints (`hits`, `hit_mode`), logging breakpoints (`log`, `continue`),
  `ps4_trace_start/stop/status` continuous JSONL traces with a ring buffer, breakpoint slot ownership
  (`owner`, `force`), `debugger.stop/state/log` SSE events, PE `.pdata` callstacks on the local backend
  and thread-aware stepping.
- **Static analysis**: Hyperion function starts merge into the shared function index (`source` marked,
  `disasm.index_updated` event); the decompile cache is keyed by type/name generation so edits re-render;
  inter-procedural call-argument types and RTTI `this` promotion; `disasm.load_self` with a decrypted-dump
  path (`docs/encrypted-self.md`); `disasm.strings {decode:true}` XOR/ROT/base64/UTF-16 previews;
  `re.libsig {sig_path}` IDA FLIRT import; CFG `graph` (nodes/edges) on `disasm.blocks` and `xray.cfg`.
- **Emulation**: persistent sessions (`emulate.session_create/session_step/session_run/session_destroy`)
  with bounded snapshot/restore, dynamic backward slicing (`emulate.slice`), Orbis syscall emulation
  (`orbis_syscalls`), and ARM64 emulation for Mach-O/iOS images (`arch:"arm64"`).
- **Lua**: `slop.log(level, msg)` with levels, `slop.api()` plus `script.api`, named snippets
  (`script.save/list/load/delete` + a Snippets sidebar with examples), and `slop.*` completion in the
  Scripts editor.
- **Network**: `network.import_pcap` (classic pcap and pcapng, Ethernet/SLL/raw-IP), pcapng export with
  per-packet comments (`network.annotate`), QUIC long-header awareness in `deep_inspect`/`stats`, and
  `proxy.status` MITM state.
- **Persistence**: `sessions.db` schema migrations (`PRAGMA user_version`), `fs_root` jail for every `fs`
  action, `notes.export`/`notes.import` for Git-shareable `symbols/<hash>.json`, and a patch journal that
  survives a restart.
- **UI**: a Pseudocode tab (highlighted, clickable tokens, `types.changed` re-render) with a
  dependency-free CFG graph; Structs (ReClass-style catalog editor with live `read_field` values) and
  Unpacker (packer verdict, patch passes, journal, revert) tabs; X-ray, Patches, Network and Emulator
  panels; a PS5 card in Targets; a disassembly minimap; snapshot-diff highlighting and a caret
  inspector in the hex editor; help search over the generated docs index; layout export/import; a
  typed i18n catalog (English/German) with a language selector; and a theme editor with named custom
  themes and JSON round-trip.
- **Notes**: `notes.push` / `notes.pull` share `symbols/<hash>.json` through any HTTP symbol store.
- **Tooling**: `app.diag_bundle` (support zip) with Settings "Copy diagnostics" and a crash-banner "Open
  log folder"; libFuzzer targets for the ELF/PE/Mach-O/.ipa/ZIP/ps4debug-NG/.NET parsers; coverage and
  `/analyze` ratchets; gitleaks; release-artifact mitigation checks; winget/Scoop/Chocolatey manifests;
  an mdBook site over `docs/` with tutorials; `tools/gen_help_index.mjs`.

### Changed

- The frontend, the e2e driver and the supervisor use `/api/v1` and `/api/v1/events`; `/api` and
  `/events` remain as deprecated aliases with a `Deprecation` header.
- `--port <n>` is honoured (it beats `SLOP_MCP_PORT` and the settings port), and the engine probes the
  endpoint before announcing `SLOP_ENGINE_READY` or reusing `engine.json`.
- Client configs reference `${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN}` instead of the literal token; token rotation follows the
  same policy.
- `script.run {unsafe:true}` needs per-run `confirm:true` unless `script_unsafe` is on;
  `script.api/list/load` are read-only actions.
- Proxy captures are redacted at storage time (`proxy_redact_secrets`, default on), and `proxy.replay`
  strips credentials unless `with_secrets:true`.
- Unicorn is built with the aarch64 backend alongside x86.
- The ps4 test suite uses a per-test ephemeral debug-event port instead of the machine-global 755.
- The event stream is also served over WebSocket (`/api/v1/events/ws`, RFC 6455); the UI prefers it
  and falls back to SSE. The weekly bench lane gained a 1,000,000-row virtualized-list case with a
  scroll-frame budget.

### Fixed

- Loopback no longer implies trust: the bearer token is required unless the engine runs with
  `--insecure-dev`.
- `pe_parse` read out of bounds on a crafted `e_lfanew` that wrapped in 32-bit arithmetic (found by
  fuzzing).
- `libsig` pattern masks compared only the low bit of each byte, so signature hits were false positives.
- A Lua script stuck in native code (a tight `slop.mem.read_bytes` loop, one huge `string.rep`) now ends
  at `timeout_ms`.
- An emulated run that stops on an invalid instruction or an unhandled guest exception reports its
  registers and memory instead of failing the tool call.
- `ps4_composites_on_local_debugger` and `ps4_chaos_peer_close_drops_socket_and_reconnect_restores` no
  longer flake on a busy machine, and the suite runs against a per-run scratch profile instead of the
  developer's `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.

### Security

- Breakpoint slots record their owning client; foreign slots require `force:true`.
- Captured HTTP credentials no longer persist anywhere the engine exposes.
- `/guard:cf` and `/CETCOMPAT` are deliberately not used: the Unicorn JIT executes generated code that
  neither mitigation can validate, so either one faults the first emulation run (`SECURITY.md`).
- Token generation is confirmed CSPRNG (`BCryptGenRandom`, 32 bytes), including the `--stdio` bridge.

## [0.2.3] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- `target.ps4_send_payload {host, port=9090, path?}`: stream the bundled (or a
  given) `.bin`/`.elf` payload to the console's BinLoader over one fresh TCP
  connection. The Targets payload card has **Send to console** with a loader
  port, and the connect form has **Discover** (UDP broadcast, PS4 consoles).
- The payload card can send the latest downloaded payload, not just the
  bundled one.

### Changed

- CI is lighter: the tests job builds and uploads the engine, so the separate
  engine job is gone; packaging runs only in the tag release workflow, which
  reuses the successful main build's artifacts instead of rebuilding.

## [0.2.2] - 2026-11-14

### Fixed

- The workspace now fills the window when neither the engine nor the update
  banner is visible; the main grid row was landing in the banner's auto row,
  leaving the lower half black.

## [0.2.1] - 2026-11-14

### Fixed

- The portable zip now unpacks into `SlopStation/` (the dist folder was still
  named `reverse-slop`).

## [0.2.0] - 2026-11-13

### Added

- Auto-update: release builds check GitHub on launch, download the signed
  installer with progress, and offer **Install & restart**; Settings → Updates
  shows the running version and a manual check.
- Single-file portable: the packaging job appends the engine to the app exe
  (`SLOPENG1` overlay) and extracts it on first run, so the portable download
  is one exe. The installer still ships the engine resource.
- `memory.scan_save` / `memory.scan_load`: persist an address-list scan to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\scans\<name>.json` and resume it after an engine
  restart (rows are capped at 500k; a pid mismatch needs `force:true`).
- `memory.watch_freeze_once` and `memory.watch_undo`: a hold that releases after
  the first write-back, and a restore of the value captured when the freeze was
  armed.
- `ps4_status` now reports a `capabilities` object (native scan, turbo scan,
  write_multi, proc_modules, proc_snapshot, assemble, elf_rpc, gdb bridge) and a
  `payload_note`, so an upstream ps4debug-NG payload is visible before a command
  fails.
- Automatic console reconnect with exponential backoff after a dropped
  connection (`ps4_auto_reconnect` setting, default on). An intentional
  `ps4_disconnect` is never undone.

### Fixed

- .NET metadata: attacker-controlled table row counts are clamped to the
  stream before any vector is sized (the owner-table fill was a heap OOB write
  on a crafted assembly); signature/TypeRef recursion is depth- and cycle-capped;
  the EH-section walk can no longer spin on a zero-size section.
- MCP: the hidden `app` tool (settings, token rotation, shutdown) is rejected on
  `/mcp` and remains reachable only through the UI `/api` channel; `proxy replay`
  and `fs` writes are classified as mutating for the confirm gate.
- Audit log and `proxy.entry` redact bearer tokens, `Authorization`, `Cookie`
  and token-ish query values by default (`reveal:true` opts out per call).
- `fs` refuses paths inside the engine data dir (settings, token, audit log,
  session store), including hits from search/grep walks.
- GDB Remote: `P`/`G` reads and writes map r8-r15 to their real registers
  (the old code added the register index to the value).
- Debug-event listener on TCP 755 accepts only the attached console, and each
  connection is drained on its own thread so a silent peer cannot block the
  payload's connect-back.
- `watch_add {freeze:true}` latches the live value instead of writing zero.
- Unknown-initial rescans compare values that straddle a stash chunk boundary.
- Lua sandbox: `slop.image.load` requires `script_unsafe` (host file access).
- Empty bearer token fails closed: a token is generated and persisted, or the
  MCP server refuses to start.
- `types.add_member` no longer self-deadlocks on the catalog mutex.
- ZIP: valid zero-length deflated entries extract (zlib needs a non-zero output
  window).
- PE parser: `e_lfanew + 24` no longer truncates to 16 bits, section offset
  arithmetic widens before adding, a zero-raw-size section no longer hides
  later sections, and an unmapped import-name RVA no longer reads offset 0.
- Loaders: SELF rebuilds and ELF files are capped at 2 GiB; Mach-O `LC_MAIN`
  entry underflow is guarded.
- Decompiler expression emission is depth-capped; `parallel_for` swallows a
  throwing body and cannot hang on a concurrent pool stop.
- ASan lane runs the `mcp` area (minus the Unicorn-backed emulate cases) so the
  HTTP/JSON/SSE/fs surface is sanitized.
- Tauri CSP adds `script-src`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'` and
  `frame-ancestors 'none'`; the proxy token field is masked.

### Changed

- The NSIS installer installs per-user (`currentUser`), so installs and
  updates need no UAC prompt.
- CI: PRs run only the lanes their paths touch; ASan, `/analyze`, clang-tidy
  and packaging run on main/tags (a PR can opt into packaging with the
  `ci:package` label). The test lane retries only failed CTest entries.
- Release builds sign the installer for the Tauri updater and publish
  `latest.json` next to the setup exe.

- `app/e2e`: end-to-end driver that spawns the real engine and the
  `SlopTarget` fixture — `npm run smoke` (API battery, also runs in the new
  nightly CI lane `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`) and `npm run screenshots`,
  which regenerates the README screenshots from the live UI; wrapped by
  `tools/screenshots.ps1`.
- `ROADMAP.md`: prioritized plan distilled from the full audit (`docs/AUDIT.md`).
- `CODEOWNERS`; full project audit with 115 findings (`docs/AUDIT.md`);
  README screenshots regenerated from the real app against the fixture.
- MIT `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` (generated by
  `tools/gen_third_party_notices.py`), shipped in the installer and the
  portable build.
- Single product version in `VERSION` (CMake, VERSIONINFO, manifests) synced
  into the frontend/Tauri manifests by `tools/sync_version.ps1`; CI checks it
  and the release tag.
- VERSIONINFO resources in `reverse-slop-engine.exe` and `reverse-slop.exe`.
- CMake presets for Debug, AddressSanitizer and `/analyze`, plus `testPresets`;
  `SLOP_BUILD_UI`, `SLOP_SANITIZE`, `SLOP_ANALYZE` options; `.clang-tidy` and
  `tools/clang_tidy.ps1`.
- CI lanes for ASan tests, `/analyze`, clang-tidy, the legacy ImGui shell and
  a version check; weekly benchmark workflow; Dependabot.
- `SHA256SUMS` for every release asset; Authenticode signing through Azure
  Trusted Signing when the signing secrets are configured.
- CTest entry per test area plus one full-suite entry; per-test watchdog
  timeouts in the test harness.
- `tools/mcp_live_test.py` spawns and health-checks the engine itself, takes
  paths from argv/env and exits non-zero on failure.
- `examples/` Lua scripts (PS4 and generic) with a README.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, issue and pull-request templates.

### Changed

- `tools/sync_version.ps1` also checks the README version badge against `VERSION`.
- Every C/C++ dependency archive is pinned by SHA-256 and every git dependency
  by commit SHA; workflow actions are pinned by commit SHA.
- Tag releases are published only after all build, test and analysis lanes
  pass.
- `tools/build.ps1` regenerates build trees configured from another checkout
  location, `-FullClean` also clears `_ext\*-build` / `_ext\*-subbuild`, and
  log directories are pruned.

### Removed

- Unused frida-core devkit download and the `slop_frida.dll` CI artifact that
  no target produced.
- zlib's example programs and their CTest entries.

## [0.1.1]

- First tagged reverse-slop release: PS4 (ps4debug-NG) console connection,
  live memory, debugger, static analysis and decompiler, Tauri front end and
  MCP server.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/compare/v0.3.1...HEAD
[0.3.1]: https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1
[0.3.0]: https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/compare/v0.2.3...v0.3.0
[0.1.1]: https://github.com/NetVar1337/PS4-Slop/releases/tag/v0.1.1

`CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)

set(CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0091 NEW)
set(CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0090 NEW)
set(CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0141 NEW)

# Single version source: the VERSION file. tools/sync_version.ps1 copies it
# into app/package.json, app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json and Cargo.toml, and CI
# fails a tag build whose tag does not match it.
file(STRINGS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/VERSION" SLOP_VERSION LIMIT_COUNT 1)
string(STRIP "${SLOP_VERSION}" SLOP_VERSION)
if(NOT SLOP_VERSION MATCHES "^([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)$")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "VERSION must be MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, got '${SLOP_VERSION}'")
endif()
file(STRINGS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/magicmida-version.txt" SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION LIMIT_COUNT 1)
string(STRIP "${SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION}" SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION)
set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/VERSION"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/magicmida-version.txt")

# MASM only exists on Windows; elsewhere only the portable libraries build
set(_slop_languages C CXX)
if(CMAKE_HOST_WIN32)
    list(APPEND _slop_languages ASM_MASM)
endif()
project(reverse-slop VERSION ${SLOP_VERSION} LANGUAGES ${_slop_languages})

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
# compile_commands.json feeds clang-tidy (tools/clang_tidy.ps1) and IDEs
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)

set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>")
set(CMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT "$<$<CONFIG:Debug,RelWithDebInfo,Release>:Embedded>")

option(SLOP_BUILD_TEST_TARGET "Build SlopTarget.exe test target" ON)
option(SLOP_BUILD_TESTS "Build the core logic test harness" ON)
option(SLOP_BUILD_ENGINE "Build the headless engine host (Tauri front end backend)" ON)
option(SLOP_BUILD_UI "Build the legacy ImGui shell (reverse-slop.exe)" ON)
option(SLOP_ANALYZE "Run MSVC /analyze on first-party targets" OFF)
option(SLOP_BUILD_FUZZ "Build the libFuzzer targets in src/fuzz (needs SLOP_SANITIZE=address)" OFF)
set(SLOP_SANITIZE "" CACHE STRING "Sanitizer for every target: empty or 'address'")
set_property(CACHE SLOP_SANITIZE PROPERTY STRINGS "" "address")

if(MSVC)
    add_compile_definitions(UNICODE _UNICODE)
    # scoped to c and cxx so the vendored asm sources never see compiler switches
    add_compile_options(
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/permissive->"
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/Zc:__cplusplus>"
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/utf-8>"
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/GS>"
    )
    add_link_options(
        /DYNAMICBASE
        /HIGHENTROPYVA
        /NXCOMPAT
        # deliberately NOT /guard:cf + /GUARD:CF (CFG) and NOT /CETCOMPAT: the
        # Unicorn emulator executes code it generates at runtime, which is in no
        # CFG target table and does no shadow-stack bookkeeping, so either one
        # kills the first emulation run with STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN
        # (__fastfail). ASLR/DEP/stack cookies stay on; tools/check_binaries.ps1
        # verifies them on the release artifacts, SECURITY.md explains the two
        # omissions.
    )
endif()

if(SLOP_SANITIZE STREQUAL "address")
    if(NOT MSVC)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "SLOP_SANITIZE=address is wired for MSVC only")
    endif()
    # Applied before the dependencies are added: MSVC's STL container
    # annotations must match across every object in the link
    # (/FAILIFMISMATCH:annotate_*), so instrumentation is all-or-nothing.
    # /RTC and incremental linking are incompatible with ASan.
    foreach(_slop_flags_var CMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG)
        string(REGEX REPLACE "/RTC[1csu]+" "" ${_slop_flags_var} "${${_slop_flags_var}}")
    endforeach()
    add_compile_options("$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/fsanitize=address>")
    # instrumentation multiplies COMDAT sections; large tables (ps4_nid.cpp)
    # overflow the default object format
    add_compile_options("$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/bigobj>")
    add_link_options(/INCREMENTAL:NO)
    add_compile_definitions(SLOP_ASAN=1)
elseif(NOT SLOP_SANITIZE STREQUAL "")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "unsupported SLOP_SANITIZE='${SLOP_SANITIZE}' (use '' or 'address')")
endif()

list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake")
include(deps)

# Off Windows: the headless engine, its core and the portable test subset.
# The window shell (DX11/ImGui), the Win32 user-mode backend and the pieces
# that need Windows-only services (Schannel, CNG certificate minting, the
# Win32 debug API, the magicmida sidecar) are replaced by POSIX ports or
# gated out; docs/linux.md lists what runs and what does not.
if(NOT WIN32)
    add_compile_definitions(
        SLOP_VERSION_STRING="${PROJECT_VERSION}"
        SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION="${SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION}"
    )
    enable_testing()

    add_subdirectory(src/hyperion)
    add_subdirectory(src/core)

    if(SLOP_BUILD_ENGINE)
        add_subdirectory(src/engine)
    endif()

    if(SLOP_BUILD_TESTS)
        add_subdirectory(src/tests)
    endif()

    return()
endif()

include(slop_resources)

# Everything below is first-party: dependency targets were created above and
# never see these options.
add_compile_definitions(
    SLOP_VERSION_STRING="${PROJECT_VERSION}"
    SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION="${SLOP_MAGICMIDA_VERSION}"
)
if(MSVC AND SLOP_ANALYZE)
    # dependency headers come in through SYSTEM include dirs (/external:I),
    # /analyze:external- keeps the analysis on our own code.
    # /analyze:WX- keeps the findings advisory: the lane reports them in the run
    # summary instead of failing the build. The codebase carries a standing
    # backlog of C6xxx findings, so treating them as errors made the lane red
    # from the day it was added. /WX still applies to ordinary compiler warnings.
    add_compile_options(
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/analyze>"
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/analyze:external->"
        "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C,CXX>:/analyze:WX->"
    )
endif()

enable_testing()

add_subdirectory(src/hyperion)
add_subdirectory(src/core)

if(SLOP_BUILD_UI)
    add_subdirectory(src/ui)
    add_subdirectory(src/app)
endif()

if(SLOP_BUILD_ENGINE)
    add_subdirectory(src/engine)
endif()

if(SLOP_BUILD_TEST_TARGET)
    add_subdirectory(src/target)
endif()

if(SLOP_BUILD_TESTS)
    add_subdirectory(src/tests)
endif()

if(SLOP_BUILD_FUZZ)
    add_subdirectory(src/fuzz)
endif()

add_subdirectory(src/live)

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing to reverse-slop

Thanks for helping. This file covers how to build, test and ship changes; the
README covers what the tool does.

## Toolchain

- Windows 10/11 x64
- Visual Studio 2022 or newer with **Desktop development with C++** (MSVC, the
  bundled CMake/Ninja) and, for clang-tidy, **C++ Clang tools for Windows**
- Node.js 22 and the Rust toolchain (`rustup`) for the Tauri front end
- PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) for `tools/sync_version.ps1` and `tools/clang_tidy.ps1`

`tools/build.ps1` finds Visual Studio through `vswhere`; pass `-VsRoot <dir>` or
set `SLOP_VS_ROOT` for a non-standard install.

## Building

```powershell
powershell -File tools\build.ps1 -NoFrontend                 # C++ only (engine, ImGui shell, tests)
powershell -File tools\build.ps1                             # + Tauri front end, installer, portable dist
powershell -File tools\build.ps1 -NoFrontend -Test           # build, then every CTest test area
powershell -File tools\build.ps1 -NoFrontend -FullClean      # drop build\ and _ext\*-build|*-subbuild first
```

A build tree configured from a different checkout location (moved/copied repo)
is detected and regenerated automatically; downloaded sources in `_ext\*-src`
are kept.

`pwsh tools/clean.ps1` drops the generated trees (every `build*\` directory and
`_ext\*-build|*-subbuild`) and prints the space it frees; `-All` also removes
the downloaded dependency sources, `app\node_modules` and the cargo target
(the next build re-fetches them), `-DryRun` only lists them.

### Compiler cache (sccache)

CI wraps every compiler invocation in [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache);
a local build can do the same and skip most of the cold-build time:

```powershell
scoop install sccache            # or: cargo install sccache
$env:CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER   = 'sccache'
$env:CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER = 'sccache'
$env:RUSTC_WRAPPER               = 'sccache'   # frontend builds
powershell -File tools\build.ps1 -NoFrontend
sccache --show-stats
```

The launcher is read at configure time, so set it before the first configure of
a build tree (or re-run with `-FullClean`). sccache keeps working across
branches and checkouts; `sccache --zero-stats` resets the hit counters.

### CMake presets

| Configure preset | Binary dir | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ninja-msvc-release` | `build/` | Shipped configuration (deps in `_ext/`) |
| `ninja-msvc-debug` | `build-ninja-msvc-debug/` | Debug CRT, `/RTC1` |
| `ninja-msvc-asan` | `build-ninja-msvc-asan/` | RelWithDebInfo + `/fsanitize=address` on every target |
| `ninja-msvc-analyze` | `build-ninja-msvc-analyze/` | MSVC `/analyze` on first-party code |
| `ninja-msvc-fuzz` | `build-ninja-msvc-fuzz/` | RelWithDebInfo + `/fsanitize=address,fuzzer` for `src/fuzz` (no engine, UI or tests) |

`tools\build.ps1 -Preset <name>` builds any of them; each non-release preset
keeps its own dependency checkout under `<binary dir>/_deps`. Matching
`testPresets` exist (`ctest --preset ninja-msvc-release`).

CMake options: `SLOP_BUILD_UI` (legacy ImGui shell, default ON),
`SLOP_BUILD_ENGINE`, `SLOP_BUILD_TESTS`, `SLOP_BUILD_TEST_TARGET`,
`SLOP_SANITIZE=address`, `SLOP_ANALYZE`, `SLOP_BUILD_FUZZ` (default OFF, needs
`SLOP_SANITIZE=address`).

Every first-party target links with `/DYNAMICBASE`, `/NXCOMPAT`,
`/HIGHENTROPYVA`, `/GUARD:CF` and `/CETCOMPAT` (see `SECURITY.md`);
`tools/check_binaries.ps1` verifies the shipped engine carries all five.

## Tests

`slop_tests` is one executable; CTest registers one entry per test area (each
`src/tests/test_<area>.cpp`, label `area`) plus `slop_tests_all` (label `all`).

```powershell
ctest --test-dir build -L area --output-on-failure      # every area, one process each
$env:SLOP_TEST_AREA = 'network,memory'; build\tests\slop_tests.exe
$env:SLOP_TEST_FILTER = 'pe_parse'; build\tests\slop_tests.exe   # substring of the test name
```

Every test case runs under a watchdog (default 300 s, `SLOP_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC`
overrides it, `TEST_CASE_TIMEOUT(name, seconds)` sets it per test). A hung test
prints `[TIMEOUT] <name>` and the run exits with 124. New behavior needs a
regression test; tests must be deterministic and must not touch the real user
profile or certificate store.

`tools/mcp_live_test.py` drives a real engine over MCP:
`python tools/mcp_live_test.py --engine build\src\engine\reverse-slop-engine.exe`
(see `--help`).

## Fuzzing

`src/fuzz` holds one libFuzzer target per parser that eats untrusted input:
`elf_loader`, `pe_parser`, `macho_loader`, `ipa`, `zip_reader`, the ps4debug-NG
wire format and .NET metadata. They are MSVC-only and build with the
`ninja-msvc-fuzz` preset (ASan is part of the same instrumentation, so the whole
tree is instrumented).

```powershell
powershell -File tools\build.ps1 -Preset ninja-msvc-fuzz -NoFrontend -Targets "fuzz_elf,fuzz_zip"
pwsh tools/run_fuzzers.ps1 -Seconds 60                  # every target, 60 s each
pwsh tools/run_fuzzers.ps1 -Targets ps4 -Seconds 300    # one target, longer
```

The runner copies the committed seeds from `src/fuzz/corpus/<target>/` into a
scratch corpus (so the checkout stays clean) and fails on a crash, leaving the
reproducer in `fuzz-artifacts/<target>/`. Reproduce one with
`build-ninja-msvc-fuzz\fuzz\fuzz_<target>.exe <crash file>`.

Seeds are generated from the test fixtures:
`build-ninja-msvc-fuzz\fuzz\slop_fuzz_corpus.exe src/fuzz/corpus` (re-run after
a fixture or format change, then commit the files). A crash found by fuzzing
gets a regression test in the matching `src/tests/test_<area>.cpp`.

## Static analysis

- `pwsh tools/clang_tidy.ps1` runs clang-tidy (`.clang-tidy`) over first-party
  code using `build/compile_commands.json`. Error-level checks must stay clean.
- The `ninja-msvc-asan` and `ninja-msvc-analyze` presets back the `asan` and
  `analyze` CI lanes.

### Coverage and /analyze ratchets

- `docs/coverage-baseline.txt` holds the src/core line coverage the nightly
  lane must not drop more than 0.5 points below (`tools/coverage_ratchet.ps1`).
  The lane also runs on PRs that touch C++.
- `docs/analyze-baseline.txt` lists the accepted MSVC `/analyze` findings
  (`tools/analyze_ratchet.ps1`); a finding that is not listed fails the nightly
  analyze lane. After fixing or accepting one, re-baseline with `-Update`.

## Versioning and releases

- The product version lives only in `VERSION`. After changing it run
  `pwsh tools/sync_version.ps1` (updates `app/package.json`, `package-lock.json`,
  `tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`); CI fails on a mismatch and on a
  tag that differs from `VERSION`. CMake embeds it in the exe VERSIONINFO and
  manifests.
- Add a `## [x.y.z]` section to `CHANGELOG.md`; the release job publishes it as
  the release notes.
- Push tag `vX.Y.Z`. The release is published only after every CI lane passes,
  with `SHA256SUMS` for all assets. Binaries and the installer are
  Authenticode-signed through Azure Trusted Signing when the repository has the
  `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`,
  `AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_SIGNING_ACCOUNT` and `AZURE_SIGNING_PROFILE`
  secrets.
- The Magicmida release and its package hashes live in
  `tools/magicmida-version.txt` (CMake, `install_magicmida.ps1`, `build.ps1` and
  the CI cache key read it).

## Dependencies

- C/C++ dependencies are declared in `cmake/deps.cmake`, each archive pinned by
  `URL_HASH SHA256` and each git dependency by a full commit SHA. When bumping
  one, update URL and hash together (`tools/dep_hash.ps1 <url>` prints the hash).
- After adding or bumping any dependency (C/C++, npm or cargo) regenerate the
  notices: `python tools/gen_third_party_notices.py` (needs a configured build,
  `npm ci` in `app/`, and the cargo registry). `--check` reports a stale file.

## Benchmarks

See `docs/benchmarks/README.md` (`tools/run_benchmarks.ps1`, weekly CI run).

## Pull requests

- Keep changes focused; describe behavior changes and how you tested them.
- A PR that touches `src/**` or `app/src/**` must add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry
  (CI enforces it; label the PR `no-changelog` for a change that does not
  belong there).
- MSVC `/W4` must stay warning-free in first-party code.
- Frontend: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in `app/`.
- By contributing you agree that your contribution is licensed under the MIT
  license in `LICENSE`.

```

`README.md`:

```md
<p align="center">
  <img src="app/src-tauri/icons/256x256.png" width="128" alt="SlopStation logo" />
</p>

<h1 align="center">SlopStation</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>PS4 reverse-engineering workbench</b><br/>
  live memory, scanning and debugging over ps4debug-NG · static analysis of dumped modules ·
  a decompiler and x86-64 emulator · Lua scripting · a built-in MCP server for AI agents
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/actions/workflows/build.yml"><img alt="build" src="https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg"></a>
  <img alt="version" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.3.1-informational">

> [!WARNING]
> Use SlopStation only on consoles, games, and systems you own or are authorized to test.
> Live debugging and memory writes can crash the console or the game. Host-side packet
> capture needs administrator rights on the analysis PC.

![SlopStation workspace: host process list, value scanner and watchlist, disassembly of a loaded PE, inspector](docs/screenshots/workspace.png)

<sub>Screenshots were captured from the real UI against the bundled
[`SlopTarget`](src/target) fixture over the local user-mode backend — every address and
value is genuine runtime data. Console-only views are shown in their waiting state.</sub>

## What it is

SlopStation is a Windows workbench for PS4 reverse engineering and game research. It
speaks the [ps4debug-NG](https://github.com/Pharaoh2k/ps4debug-NG) wire protocol directly,
runs the same analysis stack against local Windows processes, and exposes everything —
live memory, the debugger, the scanner, the decompiler, the emulator, the network tools —
through one UI, one Lua surface and one MCP server.

| Area | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| **Console connection** | ps4debug-NG over TCP 744 plus the TCP 755 debug-event callback. Auto-discovery, auto-connect, reconnect with backoff, native/turbo scan and bulk writes. |
| **Live memory** | Regions, modules, threads, read/write/protect/alloc, Cheat Engine-style scans, AOB wildcards, pointer chains, snapshots and diffs, a shared watchlist with freeze/freeze-once/undo. |
| **Live debugging** | Software breakpoints (conditional, hit counts, log-only), DR0–DR3 watchpoints, continue/step/suspend, pushed stop events with registers, `.pdata` callstacks, FP/FS-GS, remote calls, continuous trace to JSONL, trace/find-write one-shots; the same surface on PS5 (ps5debug-NG) minus the on-console scan engine. |
| **On-console tooling** | Native scan/rescan, Turbo Scan, verified bulk writes, fork module/snapshot commands, Zydis disassembly, xrefs, Keystone assembly, ELF upload. |
| **Static analysis** | ELF64 with NID→name resolution, SELF, PE, Mach-O/`.ipa`, .NET; function/xref/string indexes; Xray passes; patching with a persisted journal; binary diffing; packer heuristics; FLIRT import; CFG graphs. |
| **Decompiler** | Hyperion p-code lifting, SSA, DCE, type inference and structuring to C-like output (SysV AMD64, Win64, AAPCS64). |
| **Emulation** | Isolated Unicorn x86-64 and ARM64 runs with demand paging from the loaded image or live memory, persistent sessions with snapshot/restore, tracing, byte-level taint, backward slicing, Orbis syscalls and devirtualization helpers. |
| **Automation** | Lua 5.4 against the shared session (snippets, `slop.api()`, wall-clock caps), plus an MCP server with action-based tools, resources/prompts, progress notifications, per-tool rate limits, task playbooks (`guide`), a JSONL audit log and an optional confirm gate. |
| **Payload host** | Built-in HTTP payload host with a sha256 `manifest.json`; UDP broadcast discovery; the bundled ps4debug-NG payload. |
| **Host network** | Raw-socket capture, DNS log, stream reassembly, PCAP export, and a localhost HTTP inspection proxy. |

Two desktop shells drive the same C++ core: the **Tauri v2 + React** app (the one that
ships) and a legacy **ImGui/DX11** shell. The engine also runs headless for MCP/HTTP
clients only.

## Install

### Installer (recommended)

Download `SlopStation_<version>_x64-setup.exe` from
[Releases](https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/releases/latest) and run it. The
installer is per-user — no administrator prompt — and installs the app, the engine, the
bundled ps4debug-NG payload and the optional Magicmida sidecars.

**Auto-update is on by default.** On launch the app checks the latest GitHub release,
downloads the signed installer in the background and offers **Install & restart** in the
banner. **Settings → Updates** shows the running version and a manual check. Updates are
verified against the embedded Tauri public key; the installer is Authenticode-signed when
the signing secrets are configured.

### Portable single file

`SlopStation.exe` from the release zip is self-contained: the engine is embedded in the
executable and extracted to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.slopstation.ui\engine` on first run. No
installer, no sidecar folder. The payload card can download the latest ps4debug-NG
release on demand.

### Requirements

| Needed for | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Running the app | Windows 10/11 x64, WebView2 runtime (bundled with Windows 11) |
| Headless engine on Linux | x86-64, CMake + Ninja + g++ + libssl-dev — see [`docs/linux.md`](docs/linux.md) |
| Console work | A PS4 on the same network running the ps4debug-NG payload |
| Building | Visual Studio 2022+ with _Desktop development with C++_, CMake ≥ 3.25, Ninja, Node.js + npm, Rust/Cargo |
| Optional | Administrator rights for host packet capture; Magicmida for Themida unpacking |

## Quick start

1. **Launch SlopStation.** The splash waits for the engine handshake (up to 180 s, which
   covers the UAC prompt on first run).
2. **Load the payload on the PS4.** In **Targets**, the *ps4debug-NG payload* card shows
   the bundled release. **Send to console** streams the `.bin` to BinLoader (port 9090)
   over TCP; **Save payload…** writes it wherever you want for FTP or a GoldHEN loader.
   **Check latest** compares the bundled build with the newest GitHub release;
   **Download** fetches a newer one. **Discover** in the connect form finds consoles on
   the LAN via UDP broadcast.
3. **Connect.** Enter the console IP (port 744) and press **Connect**, or let an agent do
   it in one call:

```json
{ "tool": "target", "action": "ps4_auto", "params": { "host": "192.168.1.50" } }
```

`ps4_auto` connects, authenticates the native scanner, picks the game process (the one
with `/app0/` modules, eboot-named preferred), attaches a session and the debug session,
and returns modules, threads and regions.

No console handy? Click **“List this PC’s processes instead”** in Targets and attach to
any local process — everything except the `ps4_*` actions works.

## Feature map

### Console connection (ps4debug-NG)

- `target.ps4_connect {host, port=744, pid?}`, `ps4_disconnect`, `ps4_reconnect`,
  `ps4_auto`, `ps4_discover` (UDP broadcast), `ps4_dump_module`.
- Reads are validated against the console VM map, so unmapped ranges fail instead of
  returning zeros. Windows `PAGE_*` constants are translated to FreeBSD `VM_PROT_*`.
- The port-755 listener accepts only the attached console and drains each connection on
  its own thread.

### Live memory

- Read/write in hex, UTF-8, integer and float formats; allocate, free, change protection.
- Initial and refined numeric scans: exact/range/changed/unchanged, signed/unsigned/float
  widths, rounding, region/protection/alignment filters, worker/chunk/result caps.
- AOB wildcard search, pointer-chain scans and verification, signature generation, live
  crypto-constant search.
- Memory snapshots with compare/list/free; `scan_save`/`scan_load` persist an address-list
  scan across restarts.
- `offsets_verify`: fingerprint-gated offset manifests. A manifest pins the build (title
  ID, app version, SHA-256 of the module's executable segment) and gives every offset an
  anchor signature that must match exactly once; any mismatch returns no addresses at all.
  Format in [`src/core/memory/offsets.hpp`](src/core/memory/offsets.hpp).
- Shared watchlist sampled about 10 Hz with freeze writes; UI and MCP edits appear in
  both. `watch_freeze_once` releases after the first write-back and `watch_undo` restores
  the captured value.

### Live debugging

| Group | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Session | `ps4_attach {pid}`, `ps4_detach`, `ps4_status` |
| Breakpoints | `ps4_bp_set {addr, condition?, hits?}`, `ps4_bp_clear`, `ps4_bp_list` (slots 0–29) |
| Watchpoints | `ps4_watch_set {addr, len, type}`, `ps4_watch_clear`, `ps4_watch_list` (DR0–DR3) |
| Run control | `ps4_continue`, `ps4_step`, `ps4_suspend`/`ps4_resume`, `ps4_process_stop` |
| Events | `ps4_wait {timeout_ms}`, `ps4_events {max, clear}` |
| Registers | `ps4_regs`, `ps4_set_reg`, `ps4_dbregs`, `ps4_set_dbregs`, `ps4_fpregs`, `ps4_fsgs` |
| Stack | `ps4_callstack`, `ps4_stack` |
| Remote calls | `ps4_call {addr, args[6]}` — installs the payload RPC stub once per process |
| Power actions | `ps4_until`, `ps4_find_write`, `ps4_trace_calls`, `ps4_trace_steps` |

### On-console tooling (runs inside the payload)

- **Turbo Scan & bulk writes**: `ps4_turbo_caps`, `ps4_turbo_regions`, `ps4_turbo_config`,
  `ps4_turbo_scan`, `ps4_turbo_rescan`, `ps4_turbo_results`, `ps4_turbo_cancel`,
  `ps4_turbo_end`, and `ps4_write_multi` (up to 65,535 verified writes in one round-trip).
- **Fork extensions**: `ps4_modules` (server-side module list) and `ps4_snapshot`
  (one-round-trip region stream); `target.modules` uses `CMD_PROC_MODULES` with a
  client-side fallback on upstream payloads.
- **Native scan** (unlocked by `ps4_auth`): `ps4_scan`, `ps4_rescan`, `ps4_scan_state`,
  `ps4_scan_reset`, `ps4_scan_all`, `ps4_scan_aob` (`??` wildcards).
- **Code analysis**: `ps4_disasm`, `ps4_xrefs`, `ps4_xrefs_to`.
- **Assembly**: `ps4_assemble {asm, base?, syntax?}` (payload-side Keystone).
- **ELF upload**: `ps4_elf_rpc {path}`, `ps4_elf_load {path}`.
- **Console**: `ps4_notify`, `ps4_print`, `ps4_app` (foreground pid, title ID, content ID).

### Static analysis

- ELF64 with **NID→name resolution** (built-in database, overridable via
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\nids.txt`) and relocation application; SELF header/segment
  extraction; PE headers/imports/exports; Mach-O thin/FAT and `.ipa`; .NET metadata.
- Fast Zydis function, xref and string indexes; Capstone for ARM64.
- Background Hyperion analysis (CFGs, globals, vtables, RTTI, names) and the decompiler
  for PE and Mach-O images; .NET assemblies list types, render C#, or dump IL.
- **Xray** (read-only): CFG and cyclomatic complexity, control-flow flattening and
  obfuscation scoring, string reconstruction, indirect-call recovery, anti-analysis
  patterns, hook checks, direct syscalls, API-hash resolution, entropy windows, page
  classification, crypto constants, ROP gadgets.
- **Patching** (loaded image only): junk-NOP cleanup, opaque predicates, anti-debug, XOR
  unpack, string decoding, byte writes, a patch journal with full revert, a combined pass,
  and re-indexing after edits.
- Binary-to-binary function diff, packer/protector indicators, RTTI/vtable recovery,
  dangerous-import callsites, library signatures, user structs/enums, comments and
  bookmarks. Names/comments/bookmarks persist per file hash and remap across bases.

### Emulation and devirtualization

- Unicorn x86-64 runs from bytes, loaded-image addresses or live target addresses, with
  demand paging, IAT stubs that log calls, custom registers/stack/memory, stop conditions,
  bounded traces and byte-granular taint.
- VM identification, handler discovery, opcode maps, trace/lift/pseudocode, CFG recovery,
  predicate proofs, invariants and IAT audits.
- Supervised Magicmida (Themida) jobs with architecture checks, cancellation and timeouts.

### Host network and proxy

- Raw-socket capture on the analysis PC (SIO_RCVALL, administrator): packet paging with
  text filters, DNS log, statistics, stream listing and reassembly, per-packet
  HTTP/TLS/DNS inspection, PCAP export.
- Independent localhost HTTP/1.1 proxy: start/stop, captured exchanges, replay. CONNECT
  tunnels record metadata and SNI only; TLS interception (`mitm_enable`) requires explicit
  consent, installs a local CA, and is fully reversible (`mitm_uninstall`).

### Persistence, filesystem and web

- SQLite session snapshots and key/value storage; Hyperion `.hdb` export/import.
- Host filesystem read/write/list/create/delete/search/grep (the engine data dir is
  refused).
- Outbound WinHTTP GET/POST without browser-cookie inheritance; private/loopback targets
  are denied unless explicitly allowed.

## Typical workflows

**Find and freeze a value**

1. Targets → connect → attach the game.
2. Scanner: choose a width (`u32`, `f32`, …), type the current value, **First**.
3. Change the value in game, type the new one, **Next** until a handful remain.
4. Add the hit to the watchlist and toggle **freeze**; the watch service writes it back
   about 10× per second.

**Find what writes an address**

```json
{
  "tool": "debugger",
  "action": "ps4_find_write",
  "params": { "addr": "0x200001000", "len": 4, "timeout_ms": 10000 }
}
```

Arms a write watchpoint, resumes, waits for the hit and returns the event with the
writer's callstack. `ps4_until`, `ps4_trace_calls` and `ps4_trace_steps` cover the other
common one-shot moves.

**Dump a module and analyze it offline**

```json
{
  "tool": "target",
  "action": "ps4_dump_module",
  "params": { "name": "eboot.bin", "path": "C:/dumps/eboot.bin", "load": true }
}
```

`load: true` opens an ELF dump in the Disassembly workspace (functions, xrefs, strings,
Xray, patching). The Debugger view has the same **dump+load** action.

**Let an agent drive**

Start the app (or `reverse-slop-engine.exe`) and point an MCP client at
`http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`. Supported clients are registered automatically on first
start. `guide list` / `guide get {topic}` return ready-to-run tool sequences such as
`ps4_setup`, `ps4_breakpoint`, `ps4_find_write`, `ps4_native_scan`, `find_health`.

## MCP and HTTP API

### Endpoints

The listener binds `127.0.0.1` only.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Liveness and version |
| `POST /mcp` | MCP JSON-RPC 2.0: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, `prompts/get` (protocol `2025-06-18`) |
| `GET /mcp` | MCP SSE endpoint: keepalive plus `notifications/progress` for a `tools/call` that carried `_meta.progressToken` |
| `POST /api/v1` | Direct frontend RPC; one request or an array |
| `POST /api` | Deprecated alias of `/api/v1` (answers with a `Deprecation` header) |
| `GET /api/v1/events` | Frontend SSE stream: `hello`, `output`, `boot.stage`, `target.changed`, `backend.changed`, `hype.progress`, `watch.list`, `watch.values`, `debugger.stop`, `debugger.state`, `debugger.log`, `types.changed`, `disasm.index_updated`, `app.quitting` |
| `GET /api/v1/events/ws` | The same event stream over RFC 6455 (text frames, ping/pong, close); the UI prefers it and falls back to SSE |
| `GET /events` | Deprecated alias of `/api/v1/events` |
| `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 descriptor generated from the MCP tool schemas |

`initialize` also returns `instructions` (a usage preamble) and `state` (backend badge,
attached target, debugger state, loaded image, analysis readiness). The same context is
available through `target.status` and `disasm.loaded`.

```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:8765/health

$body = @{ tool = 'target'; action = 'ps4_auto'; params = @{ host = '192.168.1.50' } } | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1 -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body

$body = @{ jsonrpc = '2.0'; id = 1; method = 'tools/call'
           params = @{ name = 'target'; arguments = @{ action = 'list' } } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body
```

### Configuration and security

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\settings.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp_enabled": true,
  "mcp_port": 8765,
  "mcp_token": "<auto>",
  "mcp_onboarded": false,
  "script_unsafe": false,
  "web_allow_private": false,
  "mcp_onboard_clients": [],
  "mcp_token_in_configs": false,
  "mcp_rate_limits": {},
  "events_max_streams": 64,
  "proxy_redact_secrets": true,
  "fs_root": []
}
```

- **A bearer token is generated automatically on first start** (`BCryptGenRandom`, 32
  bytes); every `/mcp` and `/api/v1` call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, loopback
  included. Regenerate it from Settings (`app.rotate_token`) — client configs and
  `engine.json` are updated in place. `SLOP_MCP_TOKEN` adds a per-process token without
  persisting anything. `--insecure-dev` accepts tokenless loopback requests for
  `npm run dev`; it is the only way to turn the check off.
- `--port <n>` overrides the port (it beats `SLOP_MCP_PORT` and the settings port). If the
  port is busy the engine takes an ephemeral port and skips onboarding, and a stale
  `engine.json` registration is probed and dropped instead of announced.
- The event stream (`/api/v1/events` or `/api/v1/events/ws`) authenticates with a
  **single-use ticket** from `app.events_ticket` — no token in URLs.
- Other settings: `script_unsafe` (full Lua `io`/`os`), `web_allow_private` /
  `web_allowlist` (deny loopback/LAN by default), `proxy_token`,
  `proxy_redact_secrets` (default on), `fs_root` (jails every `fs` action),
  `mcp_onboard_clients` (empty = Tern when installed, else every known client),
  `mcp_token_in_configs` (default off), `mcp_rate_limits`, `events_max_streams`.
- Request bodies are capped at 32 MiB. Every route validates `Host` and browser `Origin`
  (DNS-rebinding and cross-site JSON-RPC get 403).
- Treat `script.run` as code execution regardless of the sandbox — the `slop.*` surface
  writes memory and files.

### Tool index

Every tool takes an `action`; `tools/list` returns the exact schemas.

| `memory` | `read`, `write`, `scan`, `rescan`, `scan_state`, `scan_reset`, `scan_save`, `scan_load`, `scan_export`, `aob`, `pointerscan`, `pointerscan_verify`, `snapshot`, `snapshots`, `diff`, `snapshot_free`, `protect`, `alloc`, `free`, `siggen`, `live_crypto`, `watch_list`, `watch_add`, `watch_remove`, `watch_clear`, `watch_set`, `watch_undo`, `watch_freeze_once`, `watch_export_ct`, `watch_import_ct`, `offsets_verify`, `dissect` |
| `debugger` | `status` plus every `ps4_*` and `ps5_*` action above |

| `analyze` | `packer`, `signatures`, `diff`, `diff_start`, `diff_job`, `diff_cancel` |
| `re` | `rtti_scan`, `vftable`, `danger`, `libsig` (JSON sigsets or an IDA FLIRT `.sig`) |
| `types` | `declare`, `create_struct`, `get_struct`, `list_structs`, `add_member`, `remove_struct`, `create_enum`, `get_enum`, `list_enums`, `remove_enum`, `read_field`, `format_at` |

| `proxy` | `start`, `stop`, `status`, `entries`, `entry`, `replay`, `mitm_enable`, `mitm_disable`, `mitm_status`, `mitm_uninstall` |

| `web` | `fetch`, `post` |
| `script` | `run`, `api`, `list`, `save`, `load`, `delete` |
| `gdb` | `start` (loopback-only, `allow_writes` opt-in), `stop`, `status` — GDB Remote bridge sharing the console session |
| `host` | `start`, `stop`, `status`, `put`, `files`, `manifest` — HTTP payload host with sha256 `manifest.json`, token on non-loopback binds |
| `guide` | `list`, `get` |

`app` (`status`, `ping`, `output`, `output_clear`, `log`, `diag`, `diag_bundle`, `settings_get`, `settings_set`, `rotate_token`, `register_token`, `events_ticket`, `shutdown`) is frontend
plumbing, reachable through `/api` only and hidden from `tools/list`.

### Automatic MCP client registration

On the first successful start on the configured port, a `slopstation` HTTP entry is added
(existing entries are kept) to:

| Client | File |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `%USERPROFILE%\.claude.json` (user scope, `"type": "http"`) |
| Cursor | `%USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json` |
| Windsurf | `%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\mcp_config.json` |
| VS Code | `%APPDATA%\Code\User\settings.json` (`mcp.servers`) |
| OpenCode | `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\config.json` |

Stdio-only clients (Claude Desktop and others) run the engine with `--stdio`: JSON-RPC
arrives on stdin and leaves on stdout one message per line, logs go to stderr, and a
per-process token is generated automatically. If an engine is already running (the
desktop app), the stdio process bridges to it instead of starting a second one.

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "slopstation": {
    "command": "C:\\Users\\you\\AppData\\Local\\dev.slopstation.ui\\engine\\reverse-slop-engine.exe",
    "args": ["--stdio"] } } }
```

Unparseable config files are left untouched. **Tern** (`%APPDATA%\tern\settings.json`,
`agents.mcp`) is registered first when it is installed, and it is the only client written
when it exists; agents running inside Tern then receive the server over ACP. Configs get
`${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN}` by default (`mcp_token_in_configs` writes the literal token instead) —
**do not sync them publicly**. Run the engine with `--no-onboard` to skip registration;
set `mcp_onboarded` to `false` to request another pass.

## Lua scripting

Scripts run from the **Scripts** panel, the `script` MCP tool (`action=run`, `code`,
`timeout_ms`) or `/api`, against the same session as the UI — renames and comments made
in one surface show up in all of them. Returned values are appended as `return: <value>`.
Scripts are sandboxed by default (no `io`/`os` execution, memory and instruction caps, and
a wall-clock deadline that also covers a script stuck in native code); set `script_unsafe`
in Settings for the full standard library, or pass `unsafe:true, confirm:true` to one
`script.run` call. `slop.api()` lists every binding with its signature.

```lua
-- read the player struct on the console, then rank the dump's functions
local st = slop.target.status()
print("backend:", st.backend, st.name, st.pid)
local raw = slop.mem.read_bytes(0x200001000, 12)         -- raw bytes
local hp, ammo, lives = string.unpack("<i4i4i4", raw)
print("player: hp=" .. hp .. " ammo=" .. ammo .. " lives=" .. lives)

-- the debugger surface is scriptable too
slop.debugger.attach(st.pid)
slop.debugger.bp_set(0x484490, { hits = 2, log = "hit {rip}" })   -- or just (addr)
local ev = slop.debugger.wait(5000)
print(("stop: rip=0x%X thread=%s"):format(ev.rip, ev.thread))

local fns = slop.disasm.functions(4000)
table.sort(fns, function(a, b) return a.size > b.size end)
for i = 1, 5 do
  print(string.format("%X  %s  %d bytes", fns[i].va, fns[i].name, fns[i].size))
end
```

| Group | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Core | `slop.version()`, `slop.api()`, `slop.log(msg)`, `slop.log(level, msg)`, `slop.log.debug/info/warn/error(msg)` |
| Target | `slop.target.list()`, `attach(pid)`, `status()` |
| Memory | `slop.mem.read_hex(addr, len)`, `write_hex(addr, data)`, `scan(...)` |
| Image session | `slop.image.load(path[, base])`, `load_from_target`, `unload`, `status`, `wait_ready([ms])` |
| Instructions | `slop.disasm.decode(addr[, count])`, `bytes(addr[, len])`, `disassemble(...)` |
| Functions / xrefs | `slop.disasm.functions([limit])`, `function_at(va)`, `xrefs_to(va)` |
| Data | `slop.disasm.strings([min[, limit]])`, `slop.disasm.pe()` |
| Annotation | `slop.disasm.name/set_name/comment/set_comment`, `bookmark_toggle`, `bookmarks` |
| Decompiler | `slop.decomp.decompile(va)`, `blocks(va)`, `vtables()`, `globals()`, `rtti()` |
| Analysis | `slop.analyze.packer()` |
| Console | `slop.ps4.connect(host[, port])`, `auto(host[, port])`, `disconnect()`, `status()` |
| Debugger | `slop.debugger.status()`, `attach(pid)`, `detach()`, `bp_set(addr[, index\|opts])`, `bp_clear(addr)`, `bp_list()`, `watch_set(addr[, len[, type]])`, `watch_clear(addr)`, `watch_list()`, `continue([stop])`, `step([lwpid])`, `suspend(lwpid)`, `resume(lwpid)`, `wait([ms])`, `events([max])`, `regs([lwpid])`, `set_reg(lwpid, name, value)`, `callstack([lwpid[, depth]])`, `call(addr[, args[, pid]])`, `run_until(addr[, ms])`, `find_write(addr[, len[, ms]])`, `trace_calls(addr[, count[, ms]])`, `trace_start(mode, path[, opts])`, `trace_stop()`, `trace_status()`, `action(name, params)` |

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph PC["Analysis PC (Windows)"]
    UI["Tauri v2 + React<br/>app/"] -- "/api/v1, /api/v1/events (HTTP + SSE)" --> ENG
    AG["AI agent / MCP client"] -- "/mcp (JSON-RPC)" --> ENG
    IMGUI["ImGui / DX11 shell<br/>src/app + src/ui"] -- in-process --> CORE
    subgraph ENG["reverse-slop-engine.exe (src/engine)"]
      CORE["slop_core (src/core)<br/>process · memory · disasm · analysis<br/>emu · network · script · mcp"]
      HYPE["Hyperion<br/>src/hyperion"]
      CORE --- HYPE
    end
  end
  CORE -- "TCP 744 commands" --> PS4["PS4 running ps4debug-NG"]
  PS4 -- "TCP 755 debug events" --> CORE
```

- The Tauri supervisor (`app/src-tauri`) starts the engine as a sidecar, waits for the
  `SLOP_ENGINE_READY <port> <token>` handshake (up to 180 s, covering the UAC prompt),
  holds it in a kill-on-close job object and lets it shut down cleanly. Keeping the
  engine out of the Rust process avoids CRT mixing and isolates crashes.
- Both hosts share the lifecycle in `src/core/infra/lifecycle.cpp`: paths and worker
  queues → process/target services → settings and persistence → MCP/API server and
  onboarding → periodic target/watch/event servicing → orderly shutdown.
- Without a console, the active backend is the Win32 user-mode backend (`OpenProcess` /
  `ReadProcessMemory`) — the same one the test fixture drives.

```text
src/
├── app/       Win32 entry + DX11 loop (legacy shell)
├── engine/    headless host and parent-process contract
├── ui/        ImGui chrome, docking, theme, views
├── hyperion/  vendored analysis/decompiler engine (hype namespace)
├── core/
│   ├── infra/     lifecycle, jobs, settings, paths, events, onboarding
│   ├── runtime/   ps4debug-NG backend + Win32 user-mode backend
│   ├── process/   targets, processes, modules, threads, dumps
│   ├── memory/    scanner, AOB, pointer scan, snapshots, watch service
│   ├── debugger/  call-stack unwinding
│   ├── disasm/    image loading, Zydis/Capstone indexes, Hyperion bridge
│   ├── analysis/  packer, signatures, xray, patches, devirt, Magicmida
│   ├── emu/       Unicorn execution and taint
│   ├── network/   raw capture, traffic store, proxy, WinHTTP
│   ├── script/    Lua engine
│   ├── mcp/       JSON-RPC/SSE server and the action-based tool surface
│   ├── persist/   SQLite snapshots and key/value storage
│   └── util/      filesystem, zip, PE helpers
├── target/    SlopTarget fixture (test process)
└── tests/     CTest areas and the fake ps4debug-NG server
```

## Building

`tools/build.ps1` finds Visual Studio with `vswhere`, uses its bundled CMake and Ninja,
configures the `ninja-msvc-release` preset into `build/`, then builds the Tauri app.
First configure downloads pinned dependencies into `_ext/` (ImGui, FreeType, Zydis,
Capstone, Unicorn, nlohmann/json, cpp-httplib, SQLite, Lua, fmt, spdlog, zlib).

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation.git
cd SlopStation
powershell -File tools/build.ps1          # engine + Tauri app (portable + installer)
powershell -File tools/build.ps1 -NoFrontend   # C++ only, fastest loop
```

| Switch | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| _(none)_ | C++ engine + Tauri app: single-file portable (`dist\SlopStation\`) + per-user NSIS installer |
| `-NoFrontend` | C++ targets only |
| `-FullClean` | Delete `build/` before configuring |
| `-PlanOnly` | Configure without compiling |
| `-Preset <name>` | `ninja-msvc-debug`, `ninja-msvc-asan`, `ninja-msvc-analyze`, `ninja-msvc-fuzz` |
| `-Full` | Self-contained installer: embeds WebView2 and Magicmida |

The bundled payload is fetched from the latest ps4debug-NG release before packaging:

```powershell
powershell -File tools/fetch_ps4debug.ps1          # latest release -> build/ps4debug-ng
powershell -File tools/fetch_ps4debug.ps1 -Force   # re-download
```

First-party targets compile with `/W4 /WX`. The legacy ImGui shell is optional
(`SLOP_BUILD_UI=ON` in a local build, see [`docs/imgui-shell.md`](docs/imgui-shell.md) for what
it covers); CI builds the engine and the Tauri app.

| CMake option | Default | Builds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `SLOP_BUILD_ENGINE` | `ON` | headless engine |
| `SLOP_BUILD_UI` | `ON` | legacy ImGui shell |
| `SLOP_BUILD_FUZZ` | `OFF` | libFuzzer targets (`src/fuzz`, preset `ninja-msvc-fuzz`) |
| `SLOP_BUILD_TEST_TARGET` | `ON` | `SlopTarget.exe` fixture |
| `SLOP_BUILD_TESTS` | `ON` | `slop_tests.exe` |

Outputs:

```text
build\src\engine\reverse-slop-engine.exe                     headless engine
build\src\app\reverse-slop.exe                               legacy ImGui shell
dist\SlopStation\SlopStation.exe                            portable single file (engine embedded by CI)
app\src-tauri\target\release\bundle\nsis\...-setup.exe       per-user installer
app\src-tauri\target\release\bundle\nsis\...-setup.exe.sig   updater signature (when the signing key is set)
```

### Versioning

`VERSION` is the single product version; `tools/sync_version.ps1` copies it into the
frontend/Tauri manifests and the README badge, and CI verifies the tag matches.

### CI

- **PRs** run only the lanes their paths touch: C++ build/tests for `src/**`, frontend
  build/tests for `app/**`.
- **main** runs the build + test + frontend gate. ASan, `/analyze` and clang-tidy run
  nightly (and on manual dispatch), off the push critical path.
- **Tags** use a separate release workflow: it downloads the successful main build's
  engine and frontend artifacts for the same commit, then packages, signs and publishes
  the installer, the single-file portable zip, `SHA256SUMS` and `latest.json` — no
  rebuild on the release path.

## Tests

```powershell
.\build\tests\slop_tests.exe                       # full suite
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure         # registered CTest subsets
$env:SLOP_TEST_FILTER = 'ps4'; .\build\tests\slop_tests.exe; Remove-Item Env:SLOP_TEST_FILTER
```

The PS4 tests run the backend and the `ps4_*` MCP flows against a fake ps4debug-NG server
on loopback, including chaos modes (fragmented replies, mid-transfer disconnects) and the
reconnect/slot-restore flows. Other suites cover infrastructure, memory, disassembly, MCP
wire/schemas, analysis, emulation, the capture store, persistence, RTTI/types, Lua, module
dumping, Hyperion/decompilation, Mach-O/`.ipa`, Xray/patching and Magicmida supervision.
Weekly CI benchmarks guard the hot paths against regressions
([`docs/benchmarks`](docs/benchmarks)).

## Bundled ps4debug-NG

The installer and the app carry the [ps4debug-NG](https://github.com/Pharaoh2k/ps4debug-NG)
payload (GPLv3). The build always fetches the **latest release**:

- `tools/fetch_ps4debug.ps1` queries `releases/latest`, downloads the `.bin` asset and
  writes `build/ps4debug-ng/manifest.json` (tag, asset, URL, SHA-256, fetch time) plus the
  GPLv3 license text.
- The manifest and payload are bundled under `payloads/ps4debug-ng/`.
- The **Targets → ps4debug-NG payload** card shows the bundled/local tag, checks the
  latest release and downloads a newer payload to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.slopstation.ui\payloads\ps4debug-ng\`.
- **Send to console** streams the payload to the console's BinLoader over one fresh
  TCP connection (port 9090); **Save payload…** exports the `.bin` for FTP or a
  GoldHEN payload loader. The engine action is `target.ps4_send_payload {host, port,
  path?}`.

ps4debug-NG is a separate GPLv3 program, not linked into the MIT-licensed SlopStation
code; its source is at <https://github.com/Pharaoh2k/ps4debug-NG>.

## Security and qualification

- The engine binds `127.0.0.1` only and requires a bearer token on `/mcp` and `/api`.
  Mutating tools can require confirmation (`mcp_require_confirm`), and every call is
  written to a JSONL audit log with secrets redacted.
- Live writes and `script.run` are code execution against the target; a bad write can
  crash the console or the game. Read `SECURITY.md` and `docs/AUDIT.md` before running
  untrusted payloads or scripts.
- Host packet capture needs administrator rights; TLS interception is opt-in and
  reversible.
- The app's auto-updater verifies the installer against the embedded Tauri public key;
  the private key is a CI secret and never ships.

## License and credits

SlopStation is MIT-licensed (see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). Third-party components and their
licenses are listed in [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md); the bundled
ps4debug-NG payload is GPLv3 and ships with its license text.

Thanks to the ps4debug-NG maintainers, the Hyperion/Unicorn/Zydis/Capstone projects, and
the Tauri/React ecosystem.

`SECURITY.md`:

```md
# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's
[private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/NetVar1337/SlopStation/security/advisories/new)
(Security tab -> "Report a vulnerability"). Do not open a public issue for an
unfixed vulnerability.

Include the affected version (`VERSION` / the release tag), the component, a
description of the impact, and reproduction steps or a proof of concept. You
can expect an acknowledgement within 7 days and a fix or mitigation plan
within 30 days for confirmed issues; we will credit you in the release notes
unless you prefer otherwise.

## Supported versions

Only the latest release receives security fixes.

## Scope

In scope:

- The engine's local MCP/HTTP server (`127.0.0.1:8765`): authentication, origin
  and host checks, the SSE event stream, and every tool reachable through it
  (filesystem, web fetch, proxy, scripting, memory and debugger tools).
- The Tauri front end and its engine supervisor.
- Parsers that handle attacker-controlled input: executable/SELF/Mach-O
  loaders, `.hdb` databases, captured network traffic, the MITM proxy, the
  ps4debug wire protocol.
- Release integrity: installers, `SHA256SUMS`, signatures, the dependency
  pins in `cmake/deps.cmake`.

Out of scope: the intended capabilities of a debugging/reverse-engineering tool
used by its own operator (reading and writing memory of a process or console
you attached to, running Lua you supplied with `script_unsafe` enabled), and
vulnerabilities in third-party software analyzed with the tool.

## Binary hardening

Every first-party target (engine, legacy shell, test harness) is compiled and
linked with the Windows exploit mitigations below, and the release lane verifies
them on the artifact that actually ships (`tools/check_binaries.ps1`, which also
rejects an import or section the build does not expect):

| Mitigation | Flag | What it buys |
|---|---|---|
| ASLR | `/DYNAMICBASE` | the image is relocated to a random base |
| High-entropy ASLR | `/HIGHENTROPYVA` | 64-bit images get the full random range |
| DEP | `/NXCOMPAT` | no executable data pages |
| Stack cookies | `/GS` | stack buffer overruns are detected on return |

The mitigations are link-time, so they cover the whole image including the
vendored static libraries (Zydis, Capstone, Unicorn, spdlog, ...). Two are
deliberately **not** used, for the same reason: the Unicorn emulator executes
code it generates at runtime.

- `/guard:cf` + `/GUARD:CF` (Control Flow Guard) validates every indirect call
  against a compiler-emitted table; the JIT's generated code is not in that
  table, so the first emulation run dies with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`
  (`__fastfail(FAST_FAIL_CFG)`).
- `/CETCOMPAT` marks the image safe for hardware shadow stacks, but the JIT
  does no shadow-stack bookkeeping, so a CET-enforcing host faults the same way.

ASLR, high-entropy ASLR, DEP and stack cookies stay on for every first-party
target, and `tools/check_binaries.ps1` verifies them on the release artifacts.

## Handling untrusted input

Analyze untrusted samples in a disposable VM. The engine requests no elevation
by itself, but the shipped front end runs elevated.

```

they blur the distinction we usually make between modifying or adding to a
program and simply using it.  Linking a program with a library, without

Public License for libraries did not effectively promote software
sharing, because most developers did not use the libraries.  We
concluded that weaker conditions might promote sharing better.

users of those programs of all benefit from the free status of the
libraries themselves.  This Library General Public License is intended to

preserving your freedom as a user of such programs to change the free
libraries that are incorporated in them.  (We have not seen how to achieve
this as regards changes in header files, but we have achieved it as regards
changes in the actual functions of the Library.)  The hope is that this
will lead to faster development of free libraries.
