`app/README.md`:

```md
# reverse-slop UI (`app/`)

The desktop front end of reverse-slop: a React 18 + TypeScript single-page app
rendered by a Tauri v2 shell (`src-tauri/`). It has no business logic of its
own; every button drives the same engine tool actions an AI agent uses over
MCP, so whatever the UI does an agent can do, and vice versa.

```
┌──────────── Tauri shell (src-tauri) ─────────────┐
│ spawns reverse-slop-engine, supervises/restarts  │
│ it, hands the UI {port, token} via IPC           │
└───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                │ engine_endpoint / engine-crashed / engine-restarted
┌───────────────▼──────────────┐   POST /api/v1 (bearer token)   ┌─────────────────────┐
│ React UI (this directory)    │ ─────────────────────────────▶│ reverse-slop-engine │
│ zustand stores ◀── events ───│ ◀──── GET /events?ticket=… ───│ 127.0.0.1:<port>    │
└──────────────────────────────┘        (server-sent events)   └─────────────────────┘
```

## Architecture

- **Transport** (`src/lib/rpc.ts`): `call(tool, action, params)` posts
  `{tool, action, params}` to `/api/v1` and returns `data` or throws `ToolError`.
  Every request has a deadline (30 s default, longer for scans/dumps) so a
  wedged engine surfaces as a `TimeoutError` instead of a stuck spinner.
  `batch()` sends several actions in one round trip (the debugger view
  refreshes with one).
- **Events** (`src/lib/events.ts`): one `EventSource` on `/events`. With a
  token-protected engine the UI first asks `app.events_ticket` for a
  single-use, 60 s ticket and connects with `?ticket=`; the bearer token never
  appears in a URL. Drops reconnect with backoff (and, in the shell,
  re-resolve the endpoint first, a restarted engine may have a new port).
- **Stores** (`src/store/*`): zustand stores mirror engine state. Nothing polls
  except the Log tab: `target.changed`, `backend.changed`, `image.changed`,
  `hype.progress`, `watch.*` and `output` events keep them current, and every
  stream (re)open re-seeds them from `app.status`. A binary loaded or a process
  attached by an agent therefore shows up in the UI immediately.
- **Endpoint** (`src/lib/endpoint.ts`): in the shell the endpoint comes from
  the supervisor (`engine_endpoint`, blocking during a restart); startup waits
  for `/health` up to the supervisor's `startup_deadline_ms` (180 s, it covers
  the UAC prompt). Crash/restart events drive the Retry banner.
- **Layout** (`src/store/ui.ts`): rail, tabs, inspector visibility and
  splitter sizes persist in `localStorage` (`reverse-slop.layout`).

### Views

| View            | File                            | Purpose                                                                               |
| --------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Title bar       | `components/TitleBar.tsx`       | Menus (File/View/Window/Theme/Help), window buttons, insecure-dev badge               |
| Command palette | `components/CommandPalette.tsx` | Ctrl+K: jump to a function (server-side search) or address, switch views, run actions |
| Splash          | `components/Splash.tsx`         | Boot stages as the engine reports them, Retry on failure                              |
| Activity rail   | `components/ActivityRail.tsx`   | Targets / Modules / Scripts + Settings                                                |
| Targets         | `panels/TargetsPanel.tsx`       | Connect a PS4 (ps4debug-NG); console process list, attach/detach                      |
| Modules         | `panels/ModulesPanel.tsx`       | Modules of the attached process, dump + analyze                                       |
| Scripts         | `panels/ScriptsPanel.tsx`       | Lua scratchpad over `script.run`                                                      |
| Scanner         | `panels/ScannerPanel.tsx`       | Value scanner and watchlist (labels, freeze, poke)                                    |
| Disassembly     | `panels/DisassemblyView.tsx`    | Paged, server-filtered function list + listing                                        |
| Strings         | `panels/StringsView.tsx`        | String hits with xref-follow                                                          |
| Memory          | `panels/MemoryView.tsx`         | Region list + continuously scrolling hex editor                                       |
| Debugger        | `panels/DebuggerView.tsx`       | PS4 live debug: run control, regs, callstack, bp/wp, on-console scan                  |
| Image browser   | `panels/PeView.tsx`             | ELF/SELF/PE/Mach-O sections, imports, exports                                         |
| Output / Log    | `panels/OutputPanel.tsx`        | Engine output ring (streamed) and diag log (polled)                                   |
| Inspector       | `panels/InspectorPanel.tsx`     | Facts about the target and image                                                      |
| Settings        | `components/SettingsModal.tsx`  | Theme, motion, engine endpoints, MCP token, engine policy settings                    |

### Keyboard

| Keys                                   | Action                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ctrl+K, Ctrl+Shift+P, Ctrl+G           | Command palette                                           |
| Ctrl+O                                 | Open binary                                               |
| Ctrl+,                                 | Settings                                                  |
| Ctrl+1 … Ctrl+5                        | Disassembly / Strings / Memory / Debugger / Image browser |
| Ctrl+Alt+I                             | Toggle inspector                                          |
| Arrow keys on a focused splitter       | Resize (Shift = larger steps, Home/End = min/max)         |
| Arrow keys / Home / End in a tab strip | Switch tab                                                |

Themes: Obsidian, Nord-slop, Blood-orange (dark), Daylight (light) and High
contrast. On first run the OS `prefers-contrast` / `prefers-color-scheme`
picks between them. Motion defaults to "Auto" (follows the OS reduced-motion
setting).

## Running

Prerequisites: Node 20+, and for the shell a Rust toolchain plus a built
engine (`reverse-slop-engine.exe`, see the repository README).

```sh
npm install
npm run tauri dev     # the desktop app: Vite dev server + Tauri shell + engine
```

### Browser dev mode

`npm run dev` serves the UI on http://localhost:1420 without the shell. It
then connects to whatever engine listens on `127.0.0.1:8765` with no token and
no handshake, and the title bar shows an **insecure dev mode** badge: nothing
proves that listener is the engine. Start one yourself
(`reverse-slop-engine.exe` with the MCP server on its default port); its CORS
allow-list already includes `http://localhost:1420` and `http://127.0.0.1:1420`.
For an engine on another port or with an MCP token, put them in
`app/.env.local` (ignored by `app/.gitignore`; never commit a token):

```sh
VITE_SLOP_PORT=8765
VITE_SLOP_TOKEN=<the engine's mcp_token>
```

## Scripts

| Script                             | What it does                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`                      | Vite dev server (port 1420, fixed: the CSP and the engine's CORS allow-list name it)                                                                                  |
| `npm run build`                    | Typecheck, then a production bundle in `dist/` (no sourcemaps; `SOURCEMAP=1` or a Tauri debug build enables them)                                                     |
| `npm run typecheck`                | `tsc --noEmit` (strict)                                                                                                                                               |
| `npm run lint`                     | ESLint (TypeScript + React hooks rules), zero warnings allowed                                                                                                        |
| `npm run format` / `format:check`  | Prettier write / check                                                                                                                                                |
| `npm test`                         | The store-level smoke test (`scripts/test-app.mjs`) and the vitest suite                                                                                              |
| `npm run test:unit` / `test:watch` | vitest only (jsdom + Testing Library), once / watch                                                                                                                   |
| `npm run check:api`                | Cross-checks every `call(tool, action, {params})` in `src/` against a running engine's `tools/list` schema (`node scripts/check-api.mjs [port]`); needs a live engine |
| `npm run bench`                    | SSR render benchmark of the 4096-row output pane                                                                                                                      |
| `npm run icons`                    | Regenerates the app icons from `src/assets/reverse-slop-icon.png`                                                                                                     |
| `npm run tauri …`                  | The Tauri CLI                                                                                                                                                         |

## Tests

- `scripts/test-app.mjs` loads the real stores through Vite's SSR loader with
  a fake `EventSource`/`fetch`: output ring bounds and dedupe, watch teardown,
  function-list refresh on analysis completion, the native endpoint
  handshake, the ticketed event stream and startup/reconnect recovery.
- `src/**/*.test.ts(x)` (vitest, jsdom): component and store tests with a fake
  `/api/v1` (`src/test/api.ts`). Each fixed UI bug has a regression test there.

## Conventions

- Talk to the engine only through `call`/`batch`; add a new `app` action to
  `kAppActions` in `scripts/check-api.mjs`.
- Icon-only buttons use `IconButton` (its tooltip is also its accessible
  name); tab strips use `Tabs`; dialogs use `Modal`.
- Colours come from CSS variables in `src/styles/tokens.css`; never hard-code
  a colour that must work in the light and high-contrast themes.
- Dependencies are pinned to exact versions; `@tauri-apps/*` track the
  `tauri` crate's minor version in `src-tauri/Cargo.lock`.

```

`app/e2e/README.md`:

```md
# E2E driver

Drives the **real** stack end to end: spawns `reverse-slop-engine.exe` and the
`SlopTarget.exe` fixture, then either talks to the engine API directly
(`smoke`) or launches the Vite dev UI in headless Chrome/Edge and captures the
screenshots used in the top-level README (`screenshots`).

## Setup

```powershell
# engine + fixture must be built first
powershell -File tools/build.ps1 -NoFrontend
cd app
npm install            # vite for the screenshots mode
cd e2e
npm install            # playwright-core (drives your installed Chrome/Edge)
```

## Run

```powershell
npm run smoke          # API battery: health, attach, read, watchlist, script, detach
npm run screenshots    # regenerate docs/screenshots/*.png from the live UI
```

Useful overrides (env): `SLOP_E2E_PORT` (default 8791), `SLOP_E2E_TOKEN`,
`SLOP_E2E_ENGINE`, `SLOP_E2E_FIXTURE`, `SLOP_E2E_OUT`.

If another live engine is already advertised the engine coalesces onto it (by
product design); the driver then uses that endpoint and **leaves it running**
instead of shutting it down.

CI: the nightly `tests` lane of `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs `smoke` against the engine it just built. Screenshots
mode is not in CI (image-compare flakiness); run it by hand when the UI changes.

```

`app/e2e/run.mjs`:

```mjs
// app/e2e/run.mjs — end-to-end driver: real engine + SlopTarget fixture.
//
//   node run.mjs smoke         API-level e2e battery (no browser needed)
//   node run.mjs screenshots   regenerate docs/screenshots via the real UI
//
// Env overrides:
//   SLOP_E2E_PORT     requested engine port   (default 8791; the announce wins)
//   SLOP_E2E_TOKEN    bearer token            (default random)
//   SLOP_E2E_ENGINE   engine exe path         (default <repo>/build/src/engine/reverse-slop-engine.exe)
//   SLOP_E2E_FIXTURE  SlopTarget exe path     (default <repo>/build/src/app/SlopTarget.exe)
//   SLOP_E2E_OUT      screenshots output dir  (default <repo>/docs/screenshots)
//
// The product enforces one engine per session: if another engine (the desktop
// app, a ctest wave) is alive, ours coalesces onto it by registering our
// token; the driver then uses that endpoint and leaves it running. Engines
// with short lifetimes make the race real, so the spawn is retried and the
// port is always taken from the engine's own SLOP_ENGINE_READY announce.
import { spawn, spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import fs from "node:fs";
import net from "node:net";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const repo = path.resolve(here, "..", "..");
const mode = process.argv[2] ?? "smoke";

const PORT = Number(process.env.SLOP_E2E_PORT ?? 8791);
const TOKEN = process.env.SLOP_E2E_TOKEN ?? crypto.randomBytes(18).toString("hex");
const ENGINE =
  process.env.SLOP_E2E_ENGINE ?? path.join(repo, "build/src/engine/reverse-slop-engine.exe");
const FIXTURE = process.env.SLOP_E2E_FIXTURE ?? path.join(repo, "build/src/app/SlopTarget.exe");
const OUT = process.env.SLOP_E2E_OUT ?? path.join(repo, "docs/screenshots");

let healthPort = PORT;
let healthUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}`;
let failures = 0;
const ok = (what, detail = "") => console.log(`PASS  ${what.padEnd(40)} ${detail}`);
const fail = (what, detail = "") => {
  failures++;
  console.error(`FAIL  ${what.padEnd(40)} ${detail}`);
};

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

async function api(tool, action, params = {}) {
  const r = await fetch(`${healthUrl}/api/v1`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ tool, action, params }),
  });
  if (!r.ok) {
    const body = await r.text().catch(() => "");
    throw new Error(`http ${r.status} on ${tool}.${action}: ${body.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  const j = await r.json();
  if (j.ok === false)
    throw new Error(`${tool}.${action}: ${JSON.stringify(j.data ?? null).slice(0, 200)}`);
  return j.data;
}

const poll = async (fn, timeoutMs, stepMs = 400) => {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  for (;;) {
    try {
      const v = await fn();
      if (v) return v;
    } catch {
      // retry until the deadline
    }
    if (Date.now() - t0 > timeoutMs) throw new Error("poll timeout");
    await sleep(stepMs);
  }
};

const portOpen = (port) =>
  new Promise((resolve) => {
    const s = net.connect({ host: "localhost", port, timeout: 500 });
    s.on("connect", () => {
      s.end();
      resolve(true);
    });
    s.on("error", () => resolve(false));
    s.on("timeout", () => {
      s.destroy();
      resolve(false);
    });
  });

function killTree(pid) {
  if (pid) spawnSync("taskkill", ["/F", "/T", "/PID", String(pid)], { stdio: "ignore" });
}

function launch(cmd, args, env, cwd) {
  return spawn(cmd, args, {
    cwd,
    windowsHide: true,
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
    env,
  });
}

// wait until the child prints a SLOP_ENGINE_READY line or dies; returns
// { announced: port|null, alive: bool, coalesced: bool, log }.
// The engine prints SLOP_ENGINE_EXISTING right after READY when it coalesced
// onto another live engine — the unambiguous signal (no exit-event race).
async function awaitAnnounce(child, timeoutMs = 20_000) {
  let log = "";
  let announced = null;
  let dead = false;
  child.stdout.on("data", (d) => (log += d));
  child.stderr.on("data", (d) => (log += d));
  child.on("exit", () => (dead = true));
  const t0 = Date.now();
  while (!announced && !dead && Date.now() - t0 < timeoutMs) {
    const m = log.match(/SLOP_ENGINE_READY (\d+)/);
    if (m) announced = Number(m[1]);
    else await sleep(200);
  }
  await sleep(300); // let a trailing SLOP_ENGINE_EXISTING line arrive
  return { announced, alive: !dead, coalesced: /SLOP_ENGINE_EXISTING/.test(log), log };
}

const healthAnswers = () =>
  fetch(`${healthUrl}/health`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } })
    .then((r) => r.ok)
    .catch(() => false);

let engine = null; // owned engine child, if any
let enginePid = 0;
let fixturePid = 0;
let vite = null;
let fixtureOut = "";
let vitePid = 0;

async function main() {
  for (const [label, exe] of [
    ["engine", ENGINE],
    ["fixture", FIXTURE],
  ]) {
    if (!fs.existsSync(exe)) {
      console.error(
        `missing ${label}: ${exe}\nbuild first: powershell -File tools/build.ps1 -NoFrontend`,
      );
      process.exitCode = 2;
      return;
    }
  }

  // fixture first so the engine sees it in the process list
  // fixture quits on stdin EOF: keep a pipe open; it prints its value addresses
  const fixture = spawn(FIXTURE, [], {
    windowsHide: true,
    stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
    env: process.env,
  });
  fixture.stdout.on("data", (d) => (fixtureOut += d));
  fixturePid = fixture.pid;
  await sleep(800);

  let ready = false;
  let lastLog = "";
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 3 && !ready; attempt++) {
    engine = launch(ENGINE, ["--no-onboard", "--quiet", "--port", String(PORT)], {
      ...process.env,
      SLOP_MCP_TOKEN: TOKEN,
      SLOP_MCP_PORT: String(PORT),
    });
    enginePid = engine.pid;
    const a = await awaitAnnounce(engine);
    lastLog = a.log;

    if (a.announced) {
      // authoritative: trust the engine's own announce, not the requested port
      healthPort = a.announced;
      healthUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${a.announced}`;
      const healthy = await poll(healthAnswers, 10_000).catch(() => false);
      if (healthy) {
        ready = true;
        if (a.coalesced) {
          // not our process: never shut it down at the end
          enginePid = 0;
          ok("engine health", `${healthUrl} (coalesced onto an existing engine; left running)`);
        } else {
          ok("engine health", `${healthUrl} (owned)`);
        }
        break;
      }
      if (a.coalesced) {
        // a foreign engine owns the session and did not accept us; retrying
        // just coalesces onto it again
        console.error(
          `existing engine at ${healthUrl} did not accept this driver\n` +
            String(a.log).trim().slice(-300),
        );
        process.exitCode = 1;
        return;
      }
      console.log(`attempt ${attempt}: ${healthUrl} announced but did not answer, retrying...`);
    } else {
      const why = !a.alive ? "exited without a handshake" : "stayed silent";
      console.log(`attempt ${attempt}: engine ${why}, retrying...`);
      if (a.log.trim()) console.log("  engine said: " + JSON.stringify(a.log.trim().slice(-300)));
    }

    killTree(enginePid); // only reaches here on the owned path (coalesced resets enginePid)
    enginePid = 0;
    await sleep(3000);
  }

  if (!ready) {
    fail("engine health", "no healthy engine after 3 attempts");
    console.error(String(lastLog ?? "").slice(-2000));
    console.error(
      "hint: a stale %LOCALAPPDATA%\\reverse-slop\\engine.json can advertise dead engines",
    );
    return; // finally still cleans up
  }

  try {
    await run();
  } finally {
    killTree(fixturePid, "SlopTarget.exe");
    fixturePid = 0;
    if (vitePid) {
      killTree(vitePid);
      vitePid = 0;
    }
    // only shut the engine down when we own it; a coalesced foreign engine
    // keeps serving its owner
    if (enginePid) {
      await api("app", "shutdown").catch(() => {});
      await sleep(1500);
      killTree(enginePid);
      enginePid = 0;
    }
  }

  if (failures) {
    console.error(`\n${failures} failure(s)`);
    process.exitCode = 1;
  } else {
    console.log("\nall green");
  }
}

// ---- shared scenario state ------------------------------------------

let rwBase = 0n;

async function attachFixture() {
  const list = await api("target", "list");
  const proc = list.processes?.find((p) => /SlopTarget/i.test(p.name));
  if (!proc) throw new Error("SlopTarget not in target.list");
  await api("target", "attach", { pid: proc.pid });
  const regions = await api("target", "regions");
  const regs = regions.regions ?? [];
  // pick the largest committed RW region: small regions can sit next to guard
  // pages and short reads then fail with Win32 ERROR_PARTIAL_COPY (299)
  const rw =
    regs
      .filter((r) => /RW/.test(r.protect_str ?? "") && BigInt(r.size) >= 4096n)
      .sort((a, b) => Number(BigInt(b.size) - BigInt(a.size)))[0] ?? regs[1];
  rwBase = BigInt(rw.base_hex);
  ok("attach fixture", `pid ${proc.pid}, rw region ${rw.base_hex} (${rw.size} B)`);
}

const at = (off) => "0x" + (rwBase + BigInt(off)).toString(16);

// ---- smoke ------------------------------------------------------------

async function smoke() {
  await attachFixture();

  const read = await api("memory", "read", { addr: at(0), len: 16 });
  if (read.hex && read.hex.length === 32) ok("memory.read", "16 bytes");
  else fail("memory.read", JSON.stringify(read).slice(0, 120));

  await api("memory", "watch_clear").catch(() => {});
  const added = await api("memory", "watch_add", {
    addr: at(0x20),
    width: "u32",
    label: "e2e.probe",
  });
  const list = await api("memory", "watch_list");
  const hit = (list.entries ?? []).find((e) => e.label === "e2e.probe");
  if (hit) ok("watchlist roundtrip", `id ${hit.id}`);
  else fail("watchlist roundtrip", JSON.stringify(list).slice(0, 120));
  await api("memory", "watch_remove", { id: hit?.id ?? added.id }).catch(() => {});

  const ran = await api("script", "run", {
    code: 'return "e2e:" .. slop.version()',
    timeout_ms: 5000,
  });
  const text = JSON.stringify(ran);
  if (/reverse-slop/.test(text)) ok("script.run sandbox");
  else fail("script.run sandbox", text.slice(0, 120));

  await api("target", "detach").catch(() => {});
  ok("detach");
}

// ---- screenshots --------------------------------------------------------

const addrOf = (name) => {
  const m = fixtureOut.match(new RegExp(String.raw`values\.${name}:\s+(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)`));
  if (!m) throw new Error("fixture did not report values." + name);
  return m[1].toLowerCase();
};

async function shots() {
  await attachFixture();

  await api("memory", "watch_clear").catch(() => {});
  await api("memory", "watch_add", {
    addr: addrOf("health"),
    width: "u32",
    label: "player.health",
  });
  await api("memory", "watch_add", { addr: addrOf("speed"), width: "f32", label: "player.speed" });
  await api("memory", "watch_add", { addr: addrOf("gold"), width: "u64", label: "game.gold" });

  const cur = await api("disasm", "loaded").catch(() => null);
  if (!cur?.ready || !/SlopTarget/.test(cur.path ?? "")) {
    await api("disasm", "load", { path: FIXTURE });
  }
  await poll(async () => {
    const d = await api("disasm", "loaded");
    return d.hype?.ready || d.image?.hype?.ready ? d : null;
  }, 120_000);
  ok("image analyzed");

  // vite dev server on the engine's CORS allow-list port
  const viteBin = path.join(repo, "app/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js");
  if (!fs.existsSync(viteBin)) {
    console.error("vite not found; run npm install in app/ first");
    process.exitCode = 2;
    return;
  }
  vite = launch(
    process.execPath,
    [viteBin],
    {
      ...process.env,
      VITE_SLOP_PORT: String(healthPort),
      VITE_SLOP_TOKEN: TOKEN,
    },
    path.join(repo, "app"),
  );
  vitePid = vite.pid;
  await poll(() => portOpen(1420), 30_000);
  ok("vite dev server", "http://localhost:1420");

  const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
  let chromium;
  try {
    chromium = require("playwright-core").chromium;
  } catch {
    console.error("playwright-core not found; run npm ci in app/e2e first");
    process.exitCode = 2;
    return;
  }
  const browser = await chromium.launch({
    headless: true,
    channel: fs.existsSync("C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe")
      ? "chrome"
      : "msedge",
  });
  const page = await browser.newPage({
    viewport: { width: 1600, height: 900 },
    deviceScaleFactor: 1.5,
  });

  try {
    await page.goto("http://localhost:1420", { waitUntil: "networkidle" });
    await poll(
      async () => (await page.locator("text=waiting for the engine").count()) === 0,
      90_000,
    );
    await sleep(2500);
    // browser-only badge; not part of the shipped app
    await page.addStyleTag({ content: ".insecure-badge{display:none!important}" });

    const shot = (name) => page.screenshot({ path: path.join(OUT, `${name}.png`) });

    // never publish the real host process list: hide it before any capture
    await page
      .getByText("List this PC's processes instead")
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await sleep(800);
    await page
      .getByText("hide host list")
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await page.locator('input[placeholder="value"]').first().fill("1000");
    await page
      .getByRole("button", { name: /first/i })
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await sleep(1500);
    await shot("workspace");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+1");
    await sleep(1200);
    await page
      .locator(".fn-row", { hasText: "sub_140001600" })
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await page.locator(".insn-row").first().waitFor({ timeout: 15_000 });
    await sleep(1200);
    await shot("disassembly");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+2");
    await sleep(1500);
    await shot("strings");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+3");
    await sleep(2000);
    await shot("memory");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+4");
    await sleep(1200);
    await shot("debugger");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+5");
    await sleep(1500);
    await shot("pe");

    await page
      .getByRole("button", { name: /scripts/i })
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await sleep(800);
    await page
      .locator("textarea")
      .first()
      .fill(
        "-- live from the attached fixture process\n" +
          "local st = slop.target.status()\n" +
          'print("backend:", st.backend, st.name, "pid", st.pid)\n' +
          "return slop.version()",
      );
    await page.keyboard.press("Control+Enter");
    await sleep(2500);
    await shot("scripts");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+,");
    await sleep(1000);
    await shot("settings");

    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await sleep(400);
    await page.keyboard.press("Control+K");
    await sleep(700);
    await shot("command-palette");
    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");

    await page.keyboard.press("Control+,");
    await sleep(700);
    const nord = page.locator("button", { hasText: /^nord/i }).first();
    if (await nord.count()) {
      await nord.click();
      await sleep(400);
    }
    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await sleep(600);
    await page.keyboard.press("Control+1");
    await sleep(900);
    await page
      .locator(".fn-row", { hasText: "sub_140001600" })
      .first()
      .click()
      .catch(() => {});
    await page.locator(".insn-row").first().waitFor({ timeout: 15_000 });
    await sleep(1200);
    await shot("theme-nord");

    ok("10 screenshots", OUT);
  } finally {
    await browser.close().catch(() => {});
  }
}

async function run() {
  if (mode === "smoke") return smoke();
  if (mode === "screenshots") return shots();
  console.error(`unknown mode '${mode}' (smoke | screenshots)`);
  process.exitCode = 2;
}

main().then(
  () => process.exit(),
  (e) => {
    console.error(e.message ?? e);
    process.exit(1);
  },
);

`app/index.html`:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="obsidian">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <!-- No remote origins: everything ships in the bundle, and the only
         network target is the loopback engine. Source of truth is
         src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.security.csp; this copy serves plain
         browser dev, and src-tauri/build.rs fails the build if they drift. -->
    <meta
      http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"

`app/scripts/bench-ui.mjs`:

```mjs
// app/scripts/bench-ui.mjs
// frontend benchmarks: the Output panel's server-side render, and a
// 1,000,000-row virtualized list mounted in jsdom (mount, scroll frame and
// filter). Both are component work only, not browser frame time or RSS.

import { createServer } from "vite";
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { flushSync } from "react-dom";
import { renderToString } from "react-dom/server";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const server = await createServer({
  server: { middlewareMode: true },
  appType: "custom",
  optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: true, include: [] },
});

/** jsdom has no layout, so the virtualizer gets a fixed viewport from us. */
function installDom() {
  const dom = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><html><body></body></html>", {
    pretendToBeVisual: true,
  });
  const w = dom.window;
  const define = (key, value) =>
    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, key, { configurable: true, writable: true, value });
  define("window", w);
  for (const key of [
    "document",
    "navigator",
    "HTMLElement",
    "Element",
    "Node",
    "Event",
    "getComputedStyle",
    "requestAnimationFrame",
    "cancelAnimationFrame",
  ])
    define(key, w[key]);
  define(
    "ResizeObserver",
    class {
      observe() {}
      unobserve() {}
      disconnect() {}
    },
  );
  Object.defineProperty(w.HTMLElement.prototype, "clientHeight", {
    configurable: true,
    get: () => 600,
  });
  Object.defineProperty(w.HTMLElement.prototype, "clientWidth", {
    configurable: true,
    get: () => 800,
  });
  return w;
}

async function benchOutputPanel() {
  const { useOutput } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/store/output.ts");
  const { default: OutputPanel } = await server.ssrLoadModule(
    "/src/components/panels/OutputPanel.tsx",
  );
  const lines = Array.from({ length: 4096 }, (_, i) => ({
    seq: i + 1,
    ms: 1700000000000 + i,
    text: `line ${i} ${"x".repeat(80)}`,
  }));
  useOutput.setState({ lines, revision: 4096 });
  Object.assign(useOutput.getInitialState(), { lines, revision: 4096 });
  const run = () => renderToString(React.createElement(OutputPanel));
  run();
  const samples = [];
  let html;
  for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
    const start = performance.now();
    html = run();
    samples.push(performance.now() - start);
  }
  return {
    workload: "output_4096_rows_ssr",
    median_ms: [...samples].sort((a, b) => a - b)[3],
    samples_ms: samples,
    html_bytes: Buffer.byteLength(html),
    rendered_rows: (html.match(/class="log-row"/g) || []).length,
    note: "SSR component work only, not browser frame time or RSS",
  };
}

async function benchVirtualList() {
  const w = installDom();
  const { default: VirtualListBench, kBenchRows } = await server.ssrLoadModule(
    "/src/bench/VirtualListBench.tsx",
  );
  const host = w.document.createElement("div");
  w.document.body.appendChild(host);
  const root = createRoot(host);

  const ms = (fn) => {
    const start = performance.now();
    fn();
    return performance.now() - start;
  };

  const mount_ms = ms(() =>
    flushSync(() => root.render(React.createElement(VirtualListBench, { filter: "" }))),
  );

  // jsdom drops scrollTop unless the element scrolls, and the virtualizer reads
  // it back, so the offset lives on the element itself
  const scroller = host.firstElementChild;
  let offset = 0;
  Object.defineProperty(scroller, "scrollTop", {
    configurable: true,
    get: () => offset,
    set: (v) => {
      offset = v;
    },
  });
  scroller.getBoundingClientRect = () => ({
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    top: 0,
    left: 0,
    right: 800,
    bottom: 600,
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    toJSON: () => ({}),
  });

  // warm the render path first: the first frames pay for module/JIT setup and
  // would otherwise dominate the samples
  const total = kBenchRows * 20;
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    flushSync(() => {
      scroller.scrollTop = (total * i) / 11;
      scroller.dispatchEvent(new w.Event("scroll"));
    });
  }

  const scroll_samples_ms = [];
  for (let i = 1; i <= 60; i++) {
    scroll_samples_ms.push(
      ms(() =>
        flushSync(() => {
          scroller.scrollTop = (total * i) / 61;
          scroller.dispatchEvent(new w.Event("scroll"));
        }),
      ),
    );
  }

  const filter_ms = ms(() =>
    flushSync(() => root.render(React.createElement(VirtualListBench, { filter: "sub_1400000" }))),
  );

  const rows = host.querySelectorAll("div > div > div").length;
  root.unmount();
  host.remove();

  const sorted = [...scroll_samples_ms].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  return {
    workload: "virtual_list_1m_rows",
    rows: kBenchRows,
    mount_ms,
    // the tenth percentile: the fastest frames still carry the real render
    // cost, while a busy machine only inflates the rest
    scroll_frame_ms: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 10)],
    scroll_median_ms: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)],
    scroll_samples_ms,
    filter_ms,
    visible_rows: rows,
    note: "jsdom render work only, not browser frame time or RSS",
  };
}

try {
  const result = {
    workloads: [await benchOutputPanel(), await benchVirtualList()],
  };
  console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
  if (process.argv[2]) writeFileSync(process.argv[2], JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + "\n");
} finally {
  await server.close();
}

`app/scripts/check-api.mjs`:

```mjs
// app/scripts/check-api.mjs
//
// Cross-checks every (tool, action, param) the front end sends against the
// engine's own tools/list schema
//
// This exists because `target.dump_module` was called with `output_path` when the
// schema says `path`: the request was well-formed JSON, the tool rejected it at
// runtime, and nothing before the user clicking Dump could have caught it
// Types cannot help here, the wire contract lives in C++
//
//   node scripts/check-api.mjs [port]      (SLOP_MCP_TOKEN = the engine's bearer token)
//
// Exits non-zero on any unknown tool, action, or parameter

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { globSync } from "node:fs";

const port = process.argv[2] ?? "8765";
const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

// `app` is reachable over /api only and deliberately absent from tools/list, so
// its surface is declared here instead
const kAppActions = {
  status: [],
  ping: [],
  output: ["since"],
  output_clear: [],
  log: ["text"],
  diag: ["since_revision", "limit"],
  diag_bundle: ["path"],
  shutdown: ["reason"],
  settings_get: [],
  settings_set: ["key", "value"],
  rotate_token: [],
  events_ticket: [],
};

const auth = process.env.SLOP_MCP_TOKEN
  ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SLOP_MCP_TOKEN}` }
  : {};

async function schemas() {
  const res = await fetch(`${base}/mcp`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", ...auth },
    body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" }),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`tools/list failed: HTTP ${res.status}`);
  const body = await res.json();
  const out = new Map();
  for (const t of body.result.tools) {
    const props = t.inputSchema?.properties ?? {};
    out.set(t.name, {
      actions: new Set(props.action?.enum ?? []),
      params: new Set(Object.keys(props)),
    });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * /api/v1/openapi.json is generated from the same tool schemas, so a tool
 * missing there means the two surfaces drifted apart.
 */
async function openapi() {
  const res = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/openapi.json`, { headers: auth });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`openapi.json failed: HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res.json();
}

/** Pull `call("tool", "action", { a, b })` triples out of the sources. */
function callSites() {
  const sites = [];
  const files = globSync("src/**/*.{ts,tsx}");
  const re =
    /call<[^>]*>\(\s*"([a-z]+)"\s*,\s*"([a-z_0-9]+)"\s*(?:,\s*\{([^}]*)\})?|call\(\s*"([a-z]+)"\s*,\s*"([a-z_0-9]+)"\s*(?:,\s*\{([^}]*)\})?/g;
  for (const file of files) {
    const src = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
    for (const m of src.matchAll(re)) {
      const tool = m[1] ?? m[4];
      const action = m[2] ?? m[5];
      const blob = m[3] ?? m[6] ?? "";
      sites.push({ file, tool, action, params: objectKeys(blob) });
    }
  }
  return sites;
}

/**
 * Keys of an inline object literal. Splitting on top-level commas and taking
 * what precedes `:` matters: a naive scan treats the *value* in `addr: va` as a
 * key and reports `va` as an unknown parameter.
 */
function objectKeys(blob) {
  const keys = [];
  let depth = 0;
  let part = "";
  const flush = () => {
    const text = part.trim();
    part = "";
    if (text === "") return;
    // Spread of a conditional, e.g. `...(label ? { label } : {})`, recurse
    if (text.startsWith("...")) {
      for (const inner of text.matchAll(/\{([^}]*)\}/g)) keys.push(...objectKeys(inner[1]));
      return;
    }
    const colon = text.indexOf(":");
    const name = (colon === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, colon)).trim();
    if (/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(name)) keys.push(name);
  };
  for (const ch of blob) {
    if (ch === "(" || ch === "[" || ch === "{") depth++;
    else if (ch === ")" || ch === "]" || ch === "}") depth--;
    if (ch === "," && depth === 0) {
      flush();
      continue;
    }
    part += ch;
  }
  flush();
  return keys;
}

const known = await schemas();
const sites = callSites();
let bad = 0;

for (const s of sites) {
  const spec =
    s.tool === "app"
      ? {
          actions: new Set(Object.keys(kAppActions)),
          params: new Set(Object.values(kAppActions).flat()),
        }
      : known.get(s.tool);

  if (spec === undefined) {
    console.log(`  UNKNOWN TOOL   ${s.tool}.${s.action}  (${s.file})`);
    bad++;
    continue;
  }
  if (!spec.actions.has(s.action)) {
    console.log(`  UNKNOWN ACTION ${s.tool}.${s.action}  (${s.file})`);
    bad++;
    continue;
  }
  for (const p of s.params) {
    if (p === "action") continue;
    if (!spec.params.has(p)) {
      console.log(`  UNKNOWN PARAM  ${s.tool}.${s.action} -> "${p}"  (${s.file})`);
      bad++;
    }
  }
}

const doc = await openapi();
const openapiSchemas = doc.components?.schemas ?? {};
for (const name of known.keys()) {
  if (!(name in openapiSchemas)) {
    console.log(`  MISSING OPENAPI SCHEMA ${name}`);
    bad++;
  }
}
if (!doc.paths?.["/api/v1"]) {
  console.log("  MISSING OPENAPI PATH /api/v1");
  bad++;
}

console.log(
  `\nchecked ${sites.length} call sites against ${known.size} tool schemas: ` +
    (bad === 0 ? "all valid" : `${bad} problem(s)`),
);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);

`app/scripts/gen-icons.mjs`:

```mjs
// app/scripts/gen-icons.mjs
//
// Generates the bundle icons from the brand source image at
// src/assets/reverse-slop-icon.png. Tauri needs a set of PNGs plus an ICO at
// build time; `tauri icon` requires the tauri CLI to fetch its own tooling, so
// the resampling happens here: the source is decoded, area-averaged down to
// each target size, and re-encoded, all with node:zlib, no image library
//
// Run with: npm run icons

import { deflateSync, inflateSync } from "node:zlib";
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const scriptDir = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const sourcePath = join(scriptDir, "..", "src", "assets", "reverse-slop-icon.png");
const outDir = join(scriptDir, "..", "src-tauri", "icons");
mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });

const kSig = Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a]);

const crcTable = (() => {
  const t = new Int32Array(256);
  for (let n = 0; n < 256; n++) {
    let c = n;
    for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
    t[n] = c;
  }
  return t;
})();

function crc32(buf) {
  let c = 0xffffffff;
  for (const b of buf) c = crcTable[(c ^ b) & 0xff] ^ (c >>> 8);
  return (c ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
}

function chunk(type, data) {
  const len = Buffer.alloc(4);
  len.writeUInt32BE(data.length);
  const body = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(type, "ascii"), data]);
  const crc = Buffer.alloc(4);
  crc.writeUInt32BE(crc32(body));
  return Buffer.concat([len, body, crc]);
}

// decoding

/** Decode an 8-bit non-interlaced PNG (colour types 2 RGB and 6 RGBA) to RGBA. */
function decodePng(buf) {
  if (!buf.subarray(0, 8).equals(kSig)) throw new Error("source is not a PNG");

  let width = 0;
  let height = 0;
  let bitDepth = 0;
  let colorType = 0;
  let interlace = 0;
  const idat = [];

  let off = 8;
  while (off < buf.length) {
    const len = buf.readUInt32BE(off);
    const type = buf.toString("ascii", off + 4, off + 8);
    const data = buf.subarray(off + 8, off + 8 + len);
    if (type === "IHDR") {
      width = data.readUInt32BE(0);
      height = data.readUInt32BE(4);
      bitDepth = data[8];
      colorType = data[9];
      interlace = data[12];
    } else if (type === "IDAT") {
      idat.push(data);
    } else if (type === "IEND") {
      break;
    }
    off += 12 + len;
  }

  if (bitDepth !== 8) throw new Error(`unsupported bit depth ${bitDepth} (need 8)`);
  if (interlace !== 0) throw new Error("interlaced PNGs are not supported");
  const channels = colorType === 2 ? 3 : colorType === 6 ? 4 : 0;
  if (!channels) throw new Error(`unsupported colour type ${colorType} (need RGB/RGBA)`);

  const raw = inflateSync(Buffer.concat(idat));
  const stride = width * channels;
  const out = Buffer.alloc(width * height * 4);
  const row = Buffer.alloc(stride);
  const prev = Buffer.alloc(stride);

  const paeth = (a, b, c) => {
    const p = a + b - c;
    const pa = Math.abs(p - a);
    const pb = Math.abs(p - b);
    const pc = Math.abs(p - c);
    return pa <= pb && pa <= pc ? a : pb <= pc ? b : c;
  };

  for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    const filter = raw[y * (stride + 1)];
    raw.copy(row, 0, y * (stride + 1) + 1, (y + 1) * (stride + 1));
    for (let i = 0; i < stride; i++) {
      const left = i >= channels ? row[i - channels] : 0;
      const up = prev[i];
      const upLeft = i >= channels ? prev[i - channels] : 0;
      if (filter === 1) row[i] = (row[i] + left) & 0xff;
      else if (filter === 2) row[i] = (row[i] + up) & 0xff;
      else if (filter === 3) row[i] = (row[i] + ((left + up) >> 1)) & 0xff;
      else if (filter === 4) row[i] = (row[i] + paeth(left, up, upLeft)) & 0xff;
    }
    for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
      const s = x * channels;
      const d = (y * width + x) * 4;
      out[d] = row[s];
      out[d + 1] = row[s + 1];
      out[d + 2] = row[s + 2];
      out[d + 3] = channels === 4 ? row[s + 3] : 255;
    }
    row.copy(prev);
  }
  return { width, height, rgba: out };
}

// resampling

/** Area-average downscale: each destination pixel averages the source pixels
 *  it covers, with fractional weights at the box edges. */
function resample(src, sw, sh, dw, dh) {
  const dst = Buffer.alloc(dw * dh * 4);
  const sx = sw / dw;
  const sy = sh / dh;
  for (let dy = 0; dy < dh; dy++) {
    const y0 = dy * sy;
    const y1 = y0 + sy;
    for (let dx = 0; dx < dw; dx++) {
      const x0 = dx * sx;
      const x1 = x0 + sx;
      let r = 0;
      let g = 0;
      let b = 0;
      let a = 0;
      let wsum = 0;
      for (let yy = Math.floor(y0); yy < Math.min(Math.ceil(y1), sh); yy++) {
        const wy = Math.min(y1, yy + 1) - Math.max(y0, yy);
        if (wy <= 0) continue;
        for (let xx = Math.floor(x0); xx < Math.min(Math.ceil(x1), sw); xx++) {
          const wx = Math.min(x1, xx + 1) - Math.max(x0, xx);
          if (wx <= 0) continue;
          const w = wx * wy;
          const i = (yy * sw + xx) * 4;
          r += src[i] * w;
          g += src[i + 1] * w;
          b += src[i + 2] * w;
          a += src[i + 3] * w;
          wsum += w;
        }
      }
      const d = (dy * dw + dx) * 4;
      dst[d] = Math.round(r / wsum);
      dst[d + 1] = Math.round(g / wsum);
      dst[d + 2] = Math.round(b / wsum);
      dst[d + 3] = Math.round(a / wsum);
    }
  }
  return dst;
}

// encoding

function png(size, px) {
  const stride = size * 4;
  const filtered = Buffer.alloc((stride + 1) * size);
  for (let y = 0; y < size; y++) {
    filtered[y * (stride + 1)] = 0; // filter type: none
    px.copy(filtered, y * (stride + 1) + 1, y * stride, (y + 1) * stride);
  }
  const ihdr = Buffer.alloc(13);
  ihdr.writeUInt32BE(size, 0);
  ihdr.writeUInt32BE(size, 4);
  ihdr[8] = 8; // bit depth
  ihdr[9] = 6; // colour type: RGBA
  return Buffer.concat([
    kSig,
    chunk("IHDR", ihdr),
    chunk("IDAT", deflateSync(filtered, { level: 9 })),
    chunk("IEND", Buffer.alloc(0)),
  ]);
}

function ico(frames) {
  const header = Buffer.alloc(6);
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 2);
  header.writeUInt16LE(frames.length, 4);

  let offset = 6 + 16 * frames.length;
  const entries = frames.map(({ size, data }) => {
    const e = Buffer.alloc(16);
    e[0] = size >= 256 ? 0 : size; // 0 encodes 256
    e[1] = size >= 256 ? 0 : size;
    e.writeUInt16LE(1, 4); // planes
    e.writeUInt16LE(32, 6); // bit count
    e.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 8);
    e.writeUInt32LE(offset, 12);
    offset += data.length;
    return e;
  });
  return Buffer.concat([header, ...entries, ...frames.map((f) => f.data)]);
}

// generate

const source = decodePng(readFileSync(sourcePath));
console.log(`source: ${source.width}x${source.height} ${sourcePath}`);

const sizes = [32, 128, 256, 512];
const rendered = new Map(
  sizes.map((s) => [s, resample(source.rgba, source.width, source.height, s, s)]),
);
for (const s of [16, 48, 64])
  rendered.set(s, resample(source.rgba, source.width, source.height, s, s));

const written = [];
for (const size of sizes) {
  const name = size === 512 ? "icon.png" : `${size}x${size}.png`;
  writeFileSync(join(outDir, name), png(size, rendered.get(size)));
  written.push(name);
}
writeFileSync(join(outDir, "128x128@2x.png"), png(256, rendered.get(256)));
written.push("128x128@2x.png");
writeFileSync(
  join(outDir, "icon.ico"),
  ico([16, 32, 48, 64, 128, 256].map((s) => ({ size: s, data: png(s, rendered.get(s)) }))),
);
written.push("icon.ico");

console.log(`wrote ${written.length} icons to src-tauri/icons: ${written.join(", ")}`);

`app/scripts/test-app.mjs`:

```mjs
// app/scripts/test-app.mjs
// Store-level smoke test run under Vite's SSR loader in plain node (no DOM):
// the event stream, output ring, watch mirror, function-list refresh, native
// endpoint handshake and startup/reconnect recovery. Component and store unit
// tests live in src/**/*.test.ts(x) and run under vitest (npm test runs both)

import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createServer } from "vite";

const server = await createServer({
  server: { middlewareMode: true },
  appType: "custom",
  optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: true, include: [] },
});

class FakeSource {
  static current;
  handlers = new Map();
  constructor(url) {
    this.url = url;
    FakeSource.current = this;
  }
  addEventListener(name, fn) {
    this.handlers.set(name, fn);
  }
  close() {}
  emit(name, data) {
    this.handlers.get(name)?.({ data: JSON.stringify(data) });
  }
}

// The UI tries the websocket stream first and falls back to SSE when the
// socket closes before opening (an engine without the route). This fake always
// takes that path, so the SSE assertions below also cover the fallback.
class FakeSocket {
  static urls = [];
  static throws = false;
  constructor(url) {
    // WebView2 throws here when the CSP's connect-src has no ws: source
    if (FakeSocket.throws) throw new DOMException("blocked by CSP", "SecurityError");
    this.url = url;
    FakeSocket.urls.push(url);
    setTimeout(() => this.onclose?.(), 0);
  }
  close() {}
}

const tick = () => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
const until = async (pred) => {
  for (let i = 0; i < 100 && !pred(); i++) await tick();
};
const reply = (data) => ({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ ok: true, data }) });

globalThis.EventSource = FakeSource;
globalThis.WebSocket = FakeSocket;
globalThis.fetch = async () => reply({ revision: 0, lines: [] });
// Node's own localStorage needs --localstorage-file and warns without it; the
// stores only need a session-scoped one
const memoryStorage = new Map();
Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "localStorage", {
  configurable: true,
  value: {
    getItem: (k) => (memoryStorage.has(k) ? memoryStorage.get(k) : null),
    setItem: (k, v) => memoryStorage.set(k, String(v)),
    removeItem: (k) => memoryStorage.delete(k),
    clear: () => memoryStorage.clear(),
  },
});

try {
  const events = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/lib/events.ts");
  const { useOutput } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/store/output.ts");
  const { useWatch } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/store/watch.ts");
  events.connect();
  await until(() => FakeSource.current !== undefined);
  assert.ok(FakeSocket.urls.at(-1).endsWith("/api/v1/events/ws"), "websocket tried first");
  const send = (name, data) => FakeSource.current.emit(name, data);
  let detach = useOutput.getState().attach();
  detach();
  detach = useOutput.getState().attach();
  for (let seq = 1; seq <= 5000; seq++) send("output", { seq, ms: seq, text: `line ${seq}` });
  // Streamed lines are batched; commit the burst before inspecting it
  useOutput.getState().flush();
  assert.equal(useOutput.getState().lines.length, 4096);
  assert.equal(useOutput.getState().lines[0].seq, 905);
  send("output", { seq: 5000, ms: 0, text: "duplicate" });
  useOutput.getState().flush();
  assert.equal(useOutput.getState().lines.at(-1).text, "line 5000");
  detach();
  send("output", { seq: 5001, ms: 0, text: "detached" });
  assert.equal(useOutput.getState().revision, 5000);
  let notifications = 0;
  const stop = useWatch.subscribe(() => notifications++);
  let off = useWatch.getState().attach();
  off();
  off = useWatch.getState().attach();
  send("watch.values", { attached: true, values: [] });
  assert.equal(notifications, 1);
  off();
  send("watch.values", { attached: false, values: [] });
  assert.equal(notifications, 1);
  stop();

  // Function list must fill in once background (hyperion) analysis completes.
  // At load the list is seeded from the fast native index; for a .NET/IL image
  // that index holds only the entry stub, and every managed method appears only
  // after analysis finishes and the engine streams hype.progress ready=true.
  // Regression guard for the "shows 1 function" .NET bug.
  {
    const { useDisasm, rowAt } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/store/disasm.ts");
    let analysisReady = false;
    const nativeOnly = {
      functions: [{ va: 0x1000, size: 6, name: "entry_point" }],
      total: 1,
      matched: 1,
    };
    const managed = {
      functions: [
        { va: 0x1000, size: 6, name: "entry_point" },
        { va: 0x2000, size: 10, name: "App::Main" },
        { va: 0x3000, size: 10, name: "App::Run" },
      ],
      total: 3,
      matched: 3,
    };
    globalThis.fetch = async (url, opts) => {
      if (String(url).endsWith("/health")) return { ok: true, json: async () => ({ ok: true }) };
      const { tool, action } = JSON.parse(opts.body);
      if (tool === "disasm" && action === "load") return reply({ ok: true, ready: true });
      if (tool === "disasm" && action === "loaded")
        return reply({
          ready: true,
          name: "net.exe",
          entry_va: 0x1000,
          functions: analysisReady ? 3 : 1,
          hype: { available: true, ready: analysisReady, progress: analysisReady ? 1 : 0.5 },
        });
      if (tool === "disasm" && action === "functions")
        return reply(analysisReady ? managed : nativeOnly);
      if (tool === "disasm" && action === "disassemble") return reply({ instructions: [] });
      return reply({});
    };

    await useDisasm.getState().loadFile("net.exe");
    // Analysis still running: only the native entry stub is known.
    assert.equal(useDisasm.getState().matched, 1);
    assert.equal(useDisasm.getState().total, 1);
    assert.equal(useDisasm.getState().selected, 0x1000);

    // Engine reports analysis complete; the store must re-pull the full list.
    analysisReady = true;
    useDisasm.getState().onHypeProgress(true, true);
    await until(() => useDisasm.getState().total === 3);
    assert.equal(useDisasm.getState().total, 3);
    assert.equal(useDisasm.getState().matched, 3);
    assert.equal(rowAt(useDisasm.getState(), 2).name, "App::Run");

    // A second ready event on the same edge must not thrash / re-fetch.
    let calls = 0;
    const base = globalThis.fetch;
    globalThis.fetch = async (u, o) => {
      calls++;
      return base(u, o);
    };
    useDisasm.getState().onHypeProgress(true, true);
    await tick();
    assert.equal(calls, 0);
  }

  // Release builds omit window.__TAURI__. The SDK bridge must still wait for
  // the native handshake and preserve its port/token rather than use 8765.
  {
    const { resolveEndpoint } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/lib/endpoint.ts");
    const { getEndpoint } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/lib/rpc.ts");
    let resolveReply;
    let invokes = 0;
    globalThis.window = {
      isTauri: true,
      __TAURI_INTERNALS__: {
        invoke: async (cmd) => {
          assert.equal(cmd, "engine_endpoint");
          invokes++;
          return new Promise((resolve) => {
            resolveReply = resolve;
          });
        },
      },
    };
    // the SDK reads globalThis.isTauri; in the webview globalThis is window
    globalThis.isTauri = true;
    const pending = resolveEndpoint();
    assert.equal(invokes, 1);
    resolveReply({ port: 43123, token: "handshake-test" });
    assert.deepEqual(await pending, { port: 43123, token: "handshake-test" });
    assert.deepEqual(getEndpoint(), { port: 43123, token: "handshake-test" });
    for (const invalid of [
      null,
      { port: 0, token: "" },
      { port: 65536, token: "" },
      { port: 1.5, token: "" },
      { port: 43123, token: null },
    ]) {
      globalThis.window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke = async () => invalid;
      await assert.rejects(resolveEndpoint(), /invalid engine endpoint/);
      assert.deepEqual(getEndpoint(), { port: 43123, token: "handshake-test" });
    }
    globalThis.window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke = async () => {
      throw new Error("native bridge failed");
    };
    await assert.rejects(resolveEndpoint(), /native bridge failed/);
    globalThis.window = {};
    delete globalThis.isTauri;
    assert.deepEqual(await resolveEndpoint(), { port: 8765, token: "" });
  }

  // A token-protected engine: the stream authenticates with a single-use
  // ticket from app.events_ticket, never with the bearer token in the URL.
  {
    const { setEndpoint } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/lib/rpc.ts");
    setEndpoint({ port: 43123, token: "secret-token" });
    let auth = null;
    globalThis.fetch = async (url, opts) => {
      const { tool, action } = JSON.parse(opts.body);
      assert.equal(`${tool}.${action}`, "app.events_ticket");
      auth = opts.headers.Authorization;
      return reply({ ticket: "t-123" });
    };
    const before = FakeSource.current;
    events.connect();
    await until(() => FakeSource.current !== before);
    assert.equal(auth, "Bearer secret-token");
    assert.equal(FakeSocket.urls.at(-1), "ws://127.0.0.1:43123/api/v1/events/ws?ticket=t-123");
    assert.equal(FakeSource.current.url, "http://127.0.0.1:43123/api/v1/events?ticket=t-123");
    assert.ok(!FakeSource.current.url.includes("secret-token"));
    events.disconnect();
    // A websocket the page may not open must still reach SSE, on the same
    // unspent ticket, instead of retrying the blocked socket forever (0.3.0)
    let tickets = 0;
    globalThis.fetch = async () => reply({ ticket: `t-${++tickets}` });
    FakeSocket.throws = true;
    const blocked = FakeSource.current;
    events.connect();
    await until(() => FakeSource.current !== blocked);
    FakeSocket.throws = false;
    assert.equal(tickets, 1);
    assert.equal(FakeSource.current.url, "http://127.0.0.1:43123/api/v1/events?ticket=t-1");
    events.disconnect();
    setEndpoint({ port: 8765, token: "" });
  }

  // A failed initial snapshot must not leave stage 0/user forever after the
  // stream connects. Reconnects also re-seed state missed while disconnected.
  {
    const { useEngine } = await server.ssrLoadModule("/src/store/engine.ts");
    const priorSource = FakeSource.current;
    globalThis.window = {
      isTauri: true,
      __TAURI_INTERNALS__: {
        invoke: async () => {
          throw new Error("native bridge failed");
        },
      },
    };
    globalThis.isTauri = true;
    await useEngine.getState().start();
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().startupError, "native bridge failed");
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().connected, false);
    assert.equal(FakeSource.current, priorSource);
    globalThis.window = {};
    delete globalThis.isTauri;
    let available = false;
    let backend = "ps4";
    let statusReads = 0;
    globalThis.fetch = async (url, opts) => {
      if (String(url).endsWith("/health")) return { ok: true, json: async () => ({ ok: true }) };
      const { tool, action } = JSON.parse(opts.body);
      if (tool !== "app" || action !== "status") return reply({});
      statusReads++;
      if (!available) throw new Error("startup snapshot failed");
      return reply({ backend, target: { attached: false } });
    };
    await useEngine.getState().start();
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().boot.done, false);
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().startupError, null);
    assert.equal(statusReads, 0);
    FakeSource.current.onopen();
    await until(() => useEngine.getState().startupError !== null);
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().startupError, "startup snapshot failed");
    available = true;
    FakeSource.current.onopen();
    await until(() => useEngine.getState().boot.done);
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().connected, true);
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().boot.done, true);
    assert.deepEqual(useEngine.getState().backend, { badge: "ps4", ps4: true });
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().startupError, null);
    backend = "user";
    FakeSource.current.onopen();
    await until(() => !useEngine.getState().backend.ps4);
    assert.deepEqual(useEngine.getState().backend, { badge: "user", ps4: false });
    // The engine's badge is upper-case "PS4": still a console (item 80)
    backend = "PS4";
    FakeSource.current.onopen();
    await until(() => useEngine.getState().backend.ps4);
    assert.deepEqual(useEngine.getState().backend, { badge: "PS4", ps4: true });
    send("boot.stage", { stage: 5, total: 5, label: "ready", done: true });
    assert.equal(useEngine.getState().boot.done, true);
    delete globalThis.window;
  }

  events.disconnect();
  console.log(
    "PASS: bounded batched output, duplicate frames, output/watch teardown and remount, function-list refresh on analysis-complete, native endpoint handshake and validation, ticketed event stream, SSE when the websocket is blocked, startup snapshot recovery, reconnect and PS4 badge case",
  );
} finally {
  await server.close();
}

[package]
name = "reverse-slop-ui"
version = "0.3.1"
description = "SlopStation workbench front end"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.77"
publish = false

[lib]
name = "reverse_slop_ui_lib"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]

[build-dependencies]
# keep tauri-build / tauri / tauri-plugin-dialog on the same minors as the npm
# side (@tauri-apps/cli 2.12.x, @tauri-apps/api 2.12.x, plugin-dialog 2.8.x);
# the tauri CLI refuses mismatched major.minor pairs
tauri-build = { version = "~2.7.4", features = [] }
# build.rs parses tauri.conf.json to keep index.html's CSP in lockstep
serde_json = "1"

[dependencies]
# no "devtools" feature: tauri enables devtools in debug builds on its own,
# release builds ship without them
tauri = { version = "~2.12.5", features = [] }
tauri-plugin-dialog = "~2.8.4"
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"
tauri-plugin-process = "2"
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls"] }
sha2 = "0.10"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
# Job object (kill-on-close), the adopted-engine process wait, and the OS RNG
# for the per-launch engine token. The supervisor stops the engine gracefully
# on exit; the job object is the OS-enforced backstop so a wedged engine can
# never outlive the UI and keep holding the MCP port and console sockets.
windows-sys = { version = "0.61", features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_Security",
    "Win32_Security_Cryptography",
    "Win32_System_JobObjects",
    "Win32_System_Threading",
] }

[features]
# Keeps `tauri build --features custom-protocol` working with the default setup.
custom-protocol = ["tauri/custom-protocol"]

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
lto = true
# unwind, not abort: a panic on a helper thread (log tee, engine supervisor)
# must not take the whole window down; the supervisor catches its own panics
# and reports them to the UI as a failed engine
panic = "unwind"
strip = true

`app/src-tauri/build.rs`:

```rs
fn main() {
    csp::check();

    // Release ships requireAdministrator: host packet capture (SIO_RCVALL raw
    // sockets) needs it, and the engine sidecar (asInvoker) inherits the
    // elevated token so only one UAC prompt appears for the whole app.
    //
    // Debug builds are asInvoker instead. An elevated exe cannot be launched by
    // an ordinary terminal, so requiring it here would mean `tauri dev` only
    // works from an elevated shell, and front-end work does not need capture:
    // an unelevated engine just reports capture as unavailable.
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let dev = std::env::var("PROFILE").is_ok_and(|p| p == "debug");
        let manifest = if dev {
            include_str!("app.dev.manifest")
        } else {
            include_str!("app.manifest")
        };
        let attrs = tauri_build::WindowsAttributes::new().app_manifest(manifest);
        tauri_build::try_build(tauri_build::Attributes::new().windows_attributes(attrs))
            .expect("failed to run tauri-build");
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    tauri_build::build();
}

/// One CSP, two carriers: tauri.conf.json `app.security.csp` is the source of
/// truth (Tauri injects it into the bundled pages), and app/index.html repeats
/// it as a <meta> tag so plain browser dev on the Vite server gets the same
/// policy. The build fails when they drift apart.
mod csp {
    use std::path::Path;

    pub fn check() {
        let conf_path = Path::new("tauri.conf.json");
        let html_path = Path::new("../index.html");
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", conf_path.display());
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", html_path.display());

        let conf = std::fs::read_to_string(conf_path).expect("read tauri.conf.json");
        let html = std::fs::read_to_string(html_path).expect("read ../index.html");
        let conf: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&conf).expect("parse tauri.conf.json");
        let from_conf = conf
            .pointer("/app/security/csp")
            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
            .expect("tauri.conf.json app.security.csp must be a string");
        let from_html = meta_csp(&html)
            .expect("index.html must carry a Content-Security-Policy <meta> tag");

        if normalize(from_conf) != normalize(from_html) {
            panic!(
                "CSP drift: app/index.html and app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json disagree\n  \
                 tauri.conf.json: {from_conf}\n  index.html:      {from_html}\n\
                 tauri.conf.json is the source of truth; copy it into index.html's <meta>"
            );
        }
    }

    /// content attribute of the http-equiv=Content-Security-Policy meta tag
    fn meta_csp(html: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        let lower = html.to_ascii_lowercase();
        let marker = lower.find("http-equiv=\"content-security-policy\"")?;
        let tag_start = lower[..marker].rfind('<')?;
        let tag_end = marker + lower[marker..].find('>')?;
        let tag = &html[tag_start..tag_end];
        let attr = tag.to_ascii_lowercase().find("content=\"")? + "content=\"".len();
        let len = tag[attr..].find('"')?;
        Some(&tag[attr..attr + len])
    }

    /// directive order and whitespace don't change meaning
    fn normalize(csp: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut directives: Vec<String> = csp
            .split(';')
            .map(|d| d.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" "))
            .filter(|d| !d.is_empty())
            .collect();
        directives.sort();
        directives
    }
}

```

// app/src-tauri/src/engine_log.rs
//
// persistent log for the engine sidecar, release builds run under the windows
// subsystem so stdout and stderr go nowhere, everything the engine and the
// supervisor say lands in %LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\logs\engine.log instead
// the file rotates by size so a chatty engine can never fill the disk

use std::fs::{self, File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::Write;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Mutex, PoisonError, TryLockError};
use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

/// rotate once the live file passes this size
pub const MAX_BYTES: u64 = 4 << 20;
/// engine.1.log .. engine.N.log are kept, older ones are dropped
pub const KEEP: u32 = 3;

struct Sink {
    file: Option<File>,
    size: u64,
}

pub struct EngineLog {
    path: PathBuf,
    max_bytes: u64,
    sink: Mutex<Sink>,
}

impl EngineLog {
    /// the standard location, falls back to the temp dir when LOCALAPPDATA is
    /// missing (service accounts, stripped environments)
    pub fn default_location() -> Self {
        let base = std::env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA")
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .unwrap_or_else(std::env::temp_dir);
        Self::at(base.join("reverse-slop").join("logs").join("engine.log"), MAX_BYTES)
    }

    pub fn at(path: PathBuf, max_bytes: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            path,
            max_bytes,
            sink: Mutex::new(Sink { file: None, size: 0 }),
        }
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.path
    }

    /// one line, timestamped and tagged with where it came from
    /// failures to write are swallowed on purpose, logging must never take the
    /// supervisor down with it
    pub fn line(&self, source: &str, text: &str) {
        let entry = format!("{} [{source}] {}\n", timestamp(SystemTime::now()), text.trim_end());
        if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
            eprint!("{entry}");
        }
        let mut sink = self.sink.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner);
        self.append(&mut sink, &entry);
    }

    /// same as line but gives up instead of blocking when the log is busy,
    /// for the panic hook, which may fire while this thread holds the lock
    pub fn try_line(&self, source: &str, text: &str) {
        let entry = format!("{} [{source}] {}\n", timestamp(SystemTime::now()), text.trim_end());
        if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
            eprint!("{entry}");
        }
        let mut sink = match self.sink.try_lock() {
            Ok(guard) => guard,
            Err(TryLockError::Poisoned(p)) => p.into_inner(),
            Err(TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return,
        };
        self.append(&mut sink, &entry);
    }

    fn append(&self, sink: &mut Sink, entry: &str) {
        if sink.file.is_none() {
            self.open(sink);
        }
        if sink.file.is_some() && sink.size > 0 && sink.size + entry.len() as u64 > self.max_bytes {
            sink.file = None;
            rotate(&self.path, KEEP);
            self.open(sink);
        }
        if let Some(file) = sink.file.as_mut() {
            if file.write_all(entry.as_bytes()).is_ok() {
                sink.size += entry.len() as u64;
            } else {
                // drop the handle so the next line retries a fresh open
                sink.file = None;
            }
        }
    }

    fn open(&self, sink: &mut Sink) {
        if let Some(dir) = self.path.parent() {
            let _ = fs::create_dir_all(dir);
        }
        // an oversized file left by a previous run rotates before we append
        if fs::metadata(&self.path).is_ok_and(|m| m.len() >= self.max_bytes) {
            rotate(&self.path, KEEP);
        }
        match OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&self.path) {
            Ok(file) => {
                sink.size = file.metadata().map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);
                sink.file = Some(file);
            }
            Err(_) => sink.file = None,
        }
    }
}

/// engine.log -> engine.1.log -> engine.2.log ..., the oldest falls off
fn rotate(path: &Path, keep: u32) {
    let numbered = |n: u32| -> PathBuf {
        let stem = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("engine");
        let ext = path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("log");
        path.with_file_name(format!("{stem}.{n}.{ext}"))
    };
    if keep == 0 {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(path);
        return;
    }
    let _ = fs::remove_file(numbered(keep));
    for n in (1..keep).rev() {
        let from = numbered(n);
        if from.exists() {
            let _ = fs::rename(&from, numbered(n + 1));
        }
    }
    let _ = fs::rename(path, numbered(1));
}

/// utc, iso 8601 with milliseconds, no date crate needed for one format
pub fn timestamp(now: SystemTime) -> String {
    let since = now.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default();
    let secs = since.as_secs();
    let millis = since.subsec_millis();
    let days = (secs / 86_400) as i64;
    let rem = secs % 86_400;
    let (y, m, d) = civil_from_days(days);
    format!(
        "{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}.{millis:03}Z",
        rem / 3600,
        (rem % 3600) / 60,
        rem % 60
    )
}

/// howard hinnant's days -> civil date
fn civil_from_days(z: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32) {
    let z = z + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32;
    (if m <= 2 { y + 1 } else { y }, m, d)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::time::Duration;

    fn scratch(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "slop-engine-log-test-{name}-{}",
            std::process::id()
        ));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        dir
    }

    #[test]
    fn timestamp_formats_known_instants() {
        assert_eq!(timestamp(UNIX_EPOCH), "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z");
        let t = UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_millis(1_709_164_800_123); // 2024-02-29
        assert_eq!(timestamp(t), "2024-02-29T00:00:00.123Z");
        let t = UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(4_102_444_799); // 2099-12-31T23:59:59
        assert_eq!(timestamp(t), "2099-12-31T23:59:59.000Z");
    }

    #[test]
    fn writes_tagged_lines_and_creates_directories() {
        let dir = scratch("write");
        let log = EngineLog::at(dir.join("logs").join("engine.log"), MAX_BYTES);
        log.line("stdout", "hello");
        log.line("stderr", "world\r\n");
        let text = fs::read_to_string(log.path()).unwrap();
        let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 2);
        assert!(lines[0].ends_with(" [stdout] hello"));
        assert!(lines[1].ends_with(" [stderr] world"));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rotates_by_size_and_keeps_bounded_history() {
        let dir = scratch("rotate");
        let path = dir.join("engine.log");
        let log = EngineLog::at(path.clone(), 200);
        for i in 0..200 {
            log.line("stderr", &format!("line {i:04} padding padding padding"));
        }
        assert!(fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len() <= 200);
        for n in 1..=KEEP {
            assert!(dir.join(format!("engine.{n}.log")).is_file(), "missing engine.{n}.log");
        }
        assert!(!dir.join(format!("engine.{}.log", KEEP + 1)).exists());
        // the newest line is in the live file, the history is in order
        let live = fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(live.contains("line 0199"));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn oversized_file_from_previous_run_rotates_on_open() {
        let dir = scratch("reopen");
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("engine.log");
        fs::write(&path, vec![b'x'; 512]).unwrap();
        let log = EngineLog::at(path.clone(), 256);
        log.line("supervisor", "fresh");
        assert_eq!(fs::metadata(dir.join("engine.1.log")).unwrap().len(), 512);
        assert!(fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap().contains("fresh"));
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
