```ts
describe("struct catalog store (item 114)", () => {
  it("re-reads the catalog after a mutation and flags the decompiler cache", async () => {
    const fields = [{ name: "hp", type: "u32", offset: 0, size: 4, array_count: 0 }];
    const def = () => ({
      name: "Player",
      size: fields.length * 4,
      packed: false,
      fields: [...fields],
    });
    const { calls } = mockApi(({ action, params }) => {
      if (action === "list_structs") return { structs: [def()] };
      if (action === "list_enums") return { enums: [] };
      if (action === "get_struct") return def();
      if (action === "add_member") {
        fields.push({
          name: String(params.field),
          type: String(params.type),
          offset: 4,
          size: 4,
          array_count: 0,
        });
        return def();
      }
      if (action === "declare") {
        fields.splice(0, fields.length);
        return { declared: 1 };
      }
      return {};
    });

    await useTypes.getState().load();
    expect(useTypes.getState().selected).toBe("Player");

    expect(
      await useTypes
        .getState()
        .addMember({ name: "mp", type: "u32", offset: 0, size: 0, array_count: 0 }),
    ).toBe(true);
    expect(useTypes.getState().invalidated).toBe(1);
    expect(useTypes.getState().structs[0].fields.map((f) => f.name)).toEqual(["hp", "mp"]);

    // removal is a declare rebuild: no remove_member action exists
    await useTypes.getState().removeMember("hp");
    expect(
      calls.some((c) => c.action === "declare" && c.params.decl === "struct Player { u32 mp; };"),
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

`app/src/store/targets.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/targets.ts
// process list and attach flow, refresh is explicit and the target mirror
// arrives over events

import { create } from "zustand";
import { call, errorText } from "@/lib/rpc";

export type ProcessRow = {
  pid: number;
  name: string;
  arch: string;
  path?: string;
  /** "user" | "admin" | "system" | "unknown" from target.list. */
  elevation?: string;
};

export type ModuleRow = {
  name: string;
  base: number;
  size: number;
  path?: string;
};

export type Ps4Info = {
  endpoint: string;
  branding: string;
};

/** Per-console profile restored by target.consoles_switch. */
export type ConsoleProfile = {
  watchlist: string;
  scan_width: string;
  scan_kind: string;
};

/** One saved endpoint from target.consoles_list. */
export type ConsoleRow = {
  name: string;
  host: string;
  port: number;
  notes: string;
  default_pid: number;
  title_filter: string;
  auto_connect: boolean;
  profile: ConsoleProfile;
  /** Filled in by the engine on connect/switch (fw/caps from ps4_status). */
  last_seen_ms: number;
  last_fw: string;
  last_branding: string;
  last_caps: string;
  active: boolean;
};

const kShowHostKey = "reverse-slop.show-host-processes";

/** The remembered backend choice (audit #82), read once at store creation. */
export function readShowHost(): boolean {
  try {
    return localStorage.getItem(kShowHostKey) === "1";
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

type TargetsStore = {
  processes: ProcessRow[];
  modules: ModuleRow[];
  filter: string;
  loading: boolean;
  error: string | null;
  ps4: Ps4Info | null;
  /**
   * The engine falls back to the local usermode backend when no console is
   * connected. Its process list is this PC's, which is not what a PS4
   * workbench should show by default; listing it is an explicit opt-in.
   */
  showHost: boolean;
  /** Saved endpoints (multi-console manager) and the active one. */
  consoles: ConsoleRow[];
  activeConsole: string;
  setFilter: (v: string) => void;
  setShowHost: (v: boolean) => void;
  refresh: () => Promise<void>;
  refreshModules: () => Promise<void>;
  /** Re-read the console endpoint after a backend change (MCP or UI). */
  syncPs4: (ps4Active: boolean) => Promise<void>;
  attach: (pid: number) => Promise<boolean>;
  detach: () => Promise<void>;
  connectPs4: (host: string, port: number) => Promise<boolean>;
  disconnectPs4: () => Promise<void>;
  loadConsoles: () => Promise<void>;
  saveConsole: (c: {
    name: string;
    host: string;
    port?: number;
    notes?: string;
    default_pid?: number;
    title_filter?: string;
    auto_connect?: boolean;
    profile?: Partial<ConsoleProfile>;
  }) => Promise<boolean>;
  removeConsole: (name: string) => Promise<void>;
  /** Disconnect the current console and connect the saved one. */
  switchConsole: (name: string) => Promise<boolean>;
};

export const useTargets = create<TargetsStore>((set, get) => ({
  processes: [],
  modules: [],
  filter: "",
  loading: false,
  error: null,
  ps4: null,
  consoles: [],
  activeConsole: "",
  showHost: readShowHost(),

  setFilter: (filter) => set({ filter }),

  setShowHost: (showHost) => {
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(kShowHostKey, showHost ? "1" : "0");
    } catch {
      // storage unavailable: the choice just does not persist
    }
    set({ showHost });
    if (showHost) void get().refresh();
    else if (get().ps4 === null) set({ processes: [] });
  },

  refresh: async () => {
    set({ loading: true, error: null });
    try {
      const res = await call<{ processes: ProcessRow[] }>("target", "list");
      const processes = [...(res.processes ?? [])].sort((a, b) =>
        a.name.localeCompare(b.name, undefined, { sensitivity: "base" }),
      );
      set({ processes, loading: false });
    } catch (e) {
      set({ loading: false, error: errorText(e) });
    }
  },

  refreshModules: async () => {
    try {
      const res = await call<{ modules: ModuleRow[] }>("target", "modules");
      set({ modules: res.modules ?? [] });
    } catch {
      set({ modules: [] });
    }
  },

  syncPs4: async (ps4Active) => {
    if (!ps4Active) {
      set({ ps4: null });
      return;
    }
    try {
      const res = await call<{ ps4?: { endpoint?: string; branding?: string } }>(
        "target",
        "status",
      );
      if (res.ps4 !== undefined)
        set({ ps4: { endpoint: res.ps4.endpoint ?? "", branding: res.ps4.branding ?? "" } });
    } catch {
      // the badge alone still says PS4; the banner just lacks the endpoint
    }
  },

  attach: async (pid) => {
    try {
      await call("target", "attach", { pid });
      await get().refreshModules();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
      return false;
    }
  },

  detach: async () => {
    try {
      await call("target", "detach");
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
    } finally {
      set({ modules: [] });
    }
  },

  connectPs4: async (host, port) => {
    set({ error: null });
    try {
      const res = await call<{ endpoint?: string; branding?: string }>("target", "ps4_connect", {
        host,
        port,
      });
      set({ ps4: { endpoint: res.endpoint ?? `${host}:${port}`, branding: res.branding ?? "" } });
      await get().refresh();
      // connecting to a saved endpoint makes it the active console
      await get().loadConsoles();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
      return false;
    }
  },

  disconnectPs4: async () => {
    try {
      await call("target", "ps4_disconnect");
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
    } finally {
      // The engine is back on the local backend: its list is this PC's
      // processes, shown only when the user opted in
      set({ ps4: null, modules: [] });
      if (get().showHost) await get().refresh();
      else set({ processes: [] });
    }
  },

  loadConsoles: async () => {
    try {
      const res = await call<{ consoles?: ConsoleRow[]; active?: string }>(
        "target",
        "consoles_list",
      );
      set({ consoles: res.consoles ?? [], activeConsole: res.active ?? "" });
    } catch {
      // keep the last list; the panel already shows the engine error
    }
  },

  saveConsole: async (c) => {
    set({ error: null });
    try {
      await call("target", "consoles_save", c);
      await get().loadConsoles();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
      return false;
    }
  },

  removeConsole: async (name) => {
    try {
      await call("target", "consoles_remove", { name });
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
    }
    await get().loadConsoles();
  },

  switchConsole: async (name) => {
    set({ error: null });
    try {
      const res = await call<{ endpoint?: string; branding?: string; attached?: boolean }>(
        "target",
        "consoles_switch",
        { name },
      );
      set({ ps4: { endpoint: res.endpoint ?? "", branding: res.branding ?? "" } });
      await get().loadConsoles();
      await get().refresh();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
      // the engine may have fallen back to the previous console
      await get().loadConsoles();
      return false;
    }
  },
}));

/** Name-or-pid substring match, same rule as NameFilterMatch() in the ImGui view. */
export function matchesFilter(row: ProcessRow, filter: string): boolean {
  if (filter === "") return true;
  const needle = filter.toLowerCase();
  return row.name.toLowerCase().includes(needle) || String(row.pid) === needle;
}
```

`app/src/store/theme.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/theme.ts
// theme pick, palettes are css, this only picks the live block and remembers.
// The theme editor writes the same custom properties inline on <html>, and
// named custom themes are a base palette plus those overrides

import { create } from "zustand";
import type { Key } from "@/i18n/en";

export type ThemeName = "obsidian" | "nord-slop" | "blood-orange" | "daylight" | "high-contrast";

export const kThemes: readonly { id: ThemeName; labelKey: Key; scheme: "dark" | "light" }[] = [
  { id: "obsidian", labelKey: "theme.obsidian", scheme: "dark" },
  { id: "nord-slop", labelKey: "theme.nordSlop", scheme: "dark" },
  { id: "blood-orange", labelKey: "theme.bloodOrange", scheme: "dark" },
  { id: "daylight", labelKey: "theme.daylight", scheme: "light" },
  { id: "high-contrast", labelKey: "theme.highContrast", scheme: "dark" },
];

/** Palette tokens the theme editor exposes. All are opaque hex in every
 *  palette, so a native color input can round-trip them. */
export const kThemeTokens = [
  { id: "--bg-0", labelKey: "token.bg0" },
  { id: "--bg-1", labelKey: "token.bg1" },
  { id: "--bg-2", labelKey: "token.bg2" },
  { id: "--border", labelKey: "token.border" },
  { id: "--border-soft", labelKey: "token.borderSoft" },
  { id: "--text", labelKey: "token.text" },
  { id: "--text-dim", labelKey: "token.textDim" },
  { id: "--text-faint", labelKey: "token.textFaint" },
  { id: "--accent", labelKey: "token.accent" },
  { id: "--success", labelKey: "token.success" },
  { id: "--warning", labelKey: "token.warning" },
  { id: "--danger", labelKey: "token.danger" },
] as const satisfies readonly { id: string; labelKey: Key }[];

export type ThemeToken = (typeof kThemeTokens)[number]["id"];

/** Overrides for a subset of the palette tokens. */
export type ThemeColors = Partial<Record<ThemeToken, string>>;

export type CustomTheme = { name: string; base: ThemeName; colors: ThemeColors };

const kStorageKey = "reverse-slop.theme";
const kCustomKey = "reverse-slop.custom-themes";
const kHex = /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i;

function initialTheme(): ThemeName {
  const saved = localStorage.getItem(kStorageKey);
  if (kThemes.some((t) => t.id === saved)) return saved as ThemeName;
  // First run: follow an explicit OS contrast / light preference
  if (window.matchMedia?.("(prefers-contrast: more)").matches) return "high-contrast";
  if (window.matchMedia?.("(prefers-color-scheme: light)").matches) return "daylight";
  return "obsidian";
}

function validColors(input: unknown): ThemeColors {
  const out: ThemeColors = {};
  if (typeof input !== "object" || input === null) return out;
  for (const { id } of kThemeTokens) {
    const value = (input as Record<string, unknown>)[id];
    if (typeof value === "string" && kHex.test(value)) out[id] = value;
  }
  return out;
}

function readCustom(): { themes: CustomTheme[]; active: string | null } {
  try {
    const raw = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(kCustomKey) ?? "{}") as {
      themes?: unknown;
      active?: unknown;
    };
    const themes = Array.isArray(raw.themes)
      ? raw.themes.flatMap((t): CustomTheme[] => {
          const item = t as Partial<CustomTheme> | null;
          if (typeof item?.name !== "string" || item.name === "") return [];
          const base = kThemes.some((b) => b.id === item.base) ? (item.base as ThemeName) : null;
          return base === null ? [] : [{ name: item.name, base, colors: validColors(item.colors) }];
        })
      : [];
    const active =
      typeof raw.active === "string" && themes.some((t) => t.name === raw.active)
        ? raw.active
        : null;
    return { themes, active };
  } catch {
    return { themes: [], active: null };
  }
}

function persist(theme: ThemeName, themes: CustomTheme[], active: string | null): void {
  localStorage.setItem(kStorageKey, theme);
  localStorage.setItem(kCustomKey, JSON.stringify({ themes, active }));
}

function applyBase(name: ThemeName): void {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  root.setAttribute("data-theme", name);
  // Native form controls and scrollbars follow color-scheme
  root.style.colorScheme = kThemes.find((t) => t.id === name)?.scheme ?? "dark";
}

/** Write (or clear) the palette overrides on <html>. */
function applyColors(colors: ThemeColors | null): void {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  for (const { id } of kThemeTokens) {
    const value = colors?.[id];
    if (value === undefined) root.style.removeProperty(id);
    else root.style.setProperty(id, value);
  }
}

type ThemeStore = {
  theme: ThemeName;
  customThemes: CustomTheme[];
  /** Name of the applied custom theme, or null for a plain base palette. */
  activeCustom: string | null;
  setTheme: (name: ThemeName) => void;
  /** Live preview while editing; null restores the active theme. */
  previewColors: (colors: ThemeColors | null) => void;
  /** Create or replace a named theme; returns it, or null for an empty name. */
  saveCustom: (name: string, base: ThemeName, colors: ThemeColors) => CustomTheme | null;
  applyCustom: (name: string) => void;
  deleteCustom: (name: string) => void;
  /** JSON for one custom theme, or null when it does not exist. */
  exportCustom: (name: string) => string | null;
  /** Parse and store a theme JSON; returns it, or null when invalid. */
  importCustom: (json: string) => CustomTheme | null;
};

export const useTheme = create<ThemeStore>((set, get) => {
  const { themes, active } = readCustom();
  const theme = initialTheme();
  const activeTheme = themes.find((t) => t.name === active);
  applyBase(theme);
  applyColors(activeTheme?.colors ?? null);

  return {
    theme,
    customThemes: themes,
    activeCustom: activeTheme?.name ?? null,

    setTheme: (name) => {
      applyBase(name);
      applyColors(null);
      persist(name, get().customThemes, null);
      set({ theme: name, activeCustom: null });
    },

    previewColors: (colors) => {
      const current = get().customThemes.find((t) => t.name === get().activeCustom);
      applyColors(colors ?? current?.colors ?? null);
    },

    saveCustom: (name, base, colors) => {
      const trimmed = name.trim();
      if (trimmed === "") return null;
      const saved: CustomTheme = { name: trimmed, base, colors: validColors(colors) };
      const themes = [...get().customThemes.filter((t) => t.name !== trimmed), saved];
      persist(get().theme, themes, get().activeCustom);
      set({ customThemes: themes });
      return saved;
    },

    applyCustom: (name) => {
      const custom = get().customThemes.find((t) => t.name === name);
      if (custom === undefined) return;
      applyBase(custom.base);
      applyColors(custom.colors);
      persist(custom.base, get().customThemes, name);
      set({ theme: custom.base, activeCustom: name });
    },

    deleteCustom: (name) => {
      const themes = get().customThemes.filter((t) => t.name !== name);
      const active = get().activeCustom === name ? null : get().activeCustom;
      if (active === null) applyColors(null);
      persist(get().theme, themes, active);
      set({ customThemes: themes, activeCustom: active });
    },

    exportCustom: (name) => {
      const custom = get().customThemes.find((t) => t.name === name);
      return custom === undefined ? null : JSON.stringify(custom, null, 2);
    },

    importCustom: (json) => {
      let raw: { name?: unknown; base?: unknown; colors?: unknown };
      try {
        raw = JSON.parse(json) as { name?: unknown; base?: unknown; colors?: unknown };
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
      if (typeof raw.name !== "string" || raw.name.trim() === "") return null;
      if (!kThemes.some((t) => t.id === raw.base)) return null;
      const imported: CustomTheme = {
        name: raw.name.trim(),
        base: raw.base as ThemeName,
        colors: validColors(raw.colors),
      };
      const themes = [...get().customThemes.filter((t) => t.name !== imported.name), imported];
      persist(get().theme, themes, get().activeCustom);
      set({ customThemes: themes });
      return imported;
    },
  };
});
```

`app/src/store/types.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/types.ts
// Struct/enum catalog mirror for the struct editor. The engine owns the
// catalog (types tool) and persists it per binary hash; every mutation bumps
// its generation, which invalidates decompiled functions, so the store keeps
// a counter the editor shows as "decompiler cache invalidated"

import { create } from "zustand";
import { parseAddress } from "@/lib/format";
import { call, errorText } from "@/lib/rpc";

export type StructField = {
  name: string;
  type: string;
  offset: number;
  size: number;
  array_count: number;
};

export type StructDef = {
  name: string;
  size: number;
  packed: boolean;
  fields: StructField[];
};

export type EnumValue = { name: string; value: number };

export type EnumDef = { name: string; underlying: string; values: EnumValue[] };

/** types.read_field result: every width is a coercion of the same bytes. */
export type FieldValue = {
  hex: string;
  uint: number;
  int: number;
  double: number;
  source: string;
};

export type FieldRead = FieldValue | { error: string };

/** The engine has no remove_member/rename_member: rebuild the struct with declare. */
export function declOf(name: string, fields: readonly StructField[], packed: boolean): string {
  const body = fields
    .map((f) => `${f.type} ${f.name}${f.array_count > 0 ? `[${f.array_count}]` : ""};`)
    .join(" ");
  return `struct ${name} { ${body} }${packed ? " packed" : ""};`;
}

/** "A=1, B=0x10" / one per line -> enum values. Invalid entries are dropped. */
export function parseEnumValues(text: string): EnumValue[] {
  const out: EnumValue[] = [];
  for (const part of text.split(/[,;\n]/)) {
    const [name, value] = part.split("=").map((s) => s.trim());
    if (!name) continue;
    const n = value === undefined || value === "" ? 0 : Number(value);
    if (!Number.isFinite(n)) continue;
    out.push({ name, value: n });
  }
  return out;
}

type TypesStore = {
  structs: StructDef[];
  enums: EnumDef[];
  /** Struct whose members the editor shows, and whose type format_at renders. */
  selected: string | null;
  selectedEnum: string | null;
  /** Address the live value column reads from, as typed. */
  addr: string;
  values: Record<string, FieldRead>;
  busy: boolean;
  error: string | null;
  /** Bumped by every catalog mutation: decompiled functions are stale. */
  invalidated: number;
  load: () => Promise<void>;
  select: (name: string | null) => void;
  selectEnum: (name: string | null) => void;
  setAddr: (text: string) => void;
  readValues: () => Promise<void>;
  createStruct: (name: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  deleteStruct: (name: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  addMember: (field: StructField) => Promise<boolean>;
  removeMember: (name: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  renameMember: (from: string, to: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  saveEnum: (def: EnumDef) => Promise<boolean>;
  deleteEnum: (name: string) => Promise<boolean>;
};

export const useTypes = create<TypesStore>((set, get) => {
  /** Run a catalog mutation, then re-read the catalog and the live values. */
  const mutate = async (fn: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<boolean> => {
    set({ busy: true });
    try {
      await fn();
      set((s) => ({ busy: false, error: null, invalidated: s.invalidated + 1 }));
      await get().load();
      await get().readValues();
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ busy: false, error: errorText(e) });
      return false;
    }
  };

  const current = (): StructDef | undefined => get().structs.find((s) => s.name === get().selected);

  return {
    structs: [],
    enums: [],
    selected: null,
    selectedEnum: null,
    addr: "",
    values: {},
    busy: false,
    error: null,
    invalidated: 0,

    load: async () => {
      try {
        const [structs, enums] = await Promise.all([
          call<{ structs: StructDef[] }>("types", "list_structs"),
          call<{ enums: EnumDef[] }>("types", "list_enums"),
        ]);
        set((s) => {
          const list = structs.structs ?? [];
          const keep = list.some((x) => x.name === s.selected)
            ? s.selected
            : (list[0]?.name ?? null);
          const enumList = enums.enums ?? [];
          const keepEnum = enumList.some((x) => x.name === s.selectedEnum)
            ? s.selectedEnum
            : (enumList[0]?.name ?? null);
          return {
            structs: list,
            enums: enumList,
            selected: keep,
            selectedEnum: keepEnum,
            error: null,
          };
        });
      } catch (e) {
        set({ error: errorText(e) });
      }
    },

    select: (selected) => {
      set({ selected, values: {} });
      void get().readValues();
    },
    selectEnum: (selectedEnum) => set({ selectedEnum }),
    setAddr: (addr) => {
      set({ addr, values: {} });
      void get().readValues();
    },

    readValues: async () => {
      const { selected, addr, structs } = get();
      const def = structs.find((s) => s.name === selected);
      const base = parseAddress(addr);
      if (!def || base === null) {
        set({ values: {} });
        return;
      }
      const entries = await Promise.all(
        def.fields.map(async (f): Promise<[string, FieldRead]> => {
          try {
            const v = await call<FieldValue>("types", "read_field", {
              struct: def.name,
              field: f.name,
              addr: base,
            });
            return [f.name, v];
          } catch (e) {
            return [f.name, { error: errorText(e) }];
          }
        }),
      );
      // a newer address or struct selection wins over this reply
      if (get().addr !== addr || get().selected !== def.name) return;
      set({ values: Object.fromEntries(entries) });
    },

    createStruct: (name) =>
      mutate(() => call("types", "declare", { decl: `struct ${name} {};` })).then((ok) => {
        if (ok) set({ selected: name });
        return ok;
      }),

    deleteStruct: (name) =>
      mutate(() => call("types", "remove_struct", { name })).then((ok) => {
        if (ok && get().selected === name) set({ selected: null, values: {} });
        return ok;
      }),

    addMember: (field) => {
      const def = current();
      if (!def) return Promise.resolve(false);
      return mutate(() =>
        call("types", "add_member", {
          name: def.name,
          field: field.name,
          type: field.type,
          array_count: field.array_count,
        }),
      );
    },

    removeMember: (name) => {
      const def = current();
      if (!def) return Promise.resolve(false);
      const fields = def.fields.filter((f) => f.name !== name);
      return mutate(() => call("types", "declare", { decl: declOf(def.name, fields, def.packed) }));
    },

    renameMember: (from, to) => {
      const def = current();
      if (!def) return Promise.resolve(false);
      const fields = def.fields.map((f) => (f.name === from ? { ...f, name: to } : f));
      return mutate(() => call("types", "declare", { decl: declOf(def.name, fields, def.packed) }));
    },

    saveEnum: (def) =>
      mutate(() =>
        call("types", "create_enum", {
          name: def.name,
          underlying: def.underlying,
          values: def.values,
        }),
      ),

    deleteEnum: (name) =>
      mutate(() => call("types", "remove_enum", { name })).then((ok) => {
        if (ok && get().selectedEnum === name) set({ selectedEnum: null });
        return ok;
      }),
  };
});

```

`app/src/store/ui.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/ui.ts
// Shell-level UI state more than one component needs: dialogs, which left
// panel the rail selected, the active tabs and the splitter sizes. The layout
// half is persisted so a reload (or the next launch) comes back the same

import { create } from "zustand";
import { kMotionOptions, useMotion, type MotionPref } from "@/store/motion";
import { kThemes, useTheme, type ThemeName } from "@/store/theme";

export type RailView = "targets" | "modules" | "scripts";
export type WorkspaceTab =
  | "disassembly"
  | "decomp"
  | "strings"
  | "memory"
  | "debugger"
  | "pe"
  | "structs"
  | "unpacker"
  | "xray"
  | "patch"
  | "network"
  | "emulate";
export type OutputTab = "output" | "log";

/** Splitter-driven CSS variables and their defaults (px), see app.css. */
export const kLayoutVars = {
  "--left-w": 300,
  "--scan-w": 316,
  "--bottom-h": 260,
  "--right-w": 320,
} as const;
export type LayoutVar = keyof typeof kLayoutVars;

type Layout = {
  rail: RailView;
  workspaceTab: WorkspaceTab;
  outputTab: OutputTab;
  inspectorOpen: boolean;
  sizes: Partial<Record<LayoutVar, number>>;
};

const kStorageKey = "reverse-slop.layout";

const kDefaultLayout: Layout = {
  rail: "targets",
  workspaceTab: "disassembly",
  outputTab: "output",
  inspectorOpen: true,
  sizes: {},
};

const kRails: readonly RailView[] = ["targets", "modules", "scripts"];
const kWorkspaceTabs: readonly WorkspaceTab[] = [
  "disassembly",
  "decomp",
  "strings",
  "memory",
  "debugger",
  "pe",
  "structs",
  "unpacker",
  "xray",
  "patch",
  "network",
  "emulate",
];

/** Parse persisted layout defensively: a hand-edited or stale blob must not break boot. */
export function parseLayout(raw: string | null): Layout {
  if (raw === null) return kDefaultLayout;
  try {
    const v = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<Layout>;
    return {
      rail: kRails.includes(v.rail as RailView) ? (v.rail as RailView) : kDefaultLayout.rail,
      workspaceTab: kWorkspaceTabs.includes(v.workspaceTab as WorkspaceTab)
        ? (v.workspaceTab as WorkspaceTab)
        : kDefaultLayout.workspaceTab,
      outputTab: v.outputTab === "log" ? "log" : "output",
      inspectorOpen: v.inspectorOpen !== false,
      sizes: parseSizes(v.sizes),
    };
  } catch {
    return kDefaultLayout;
  }
}

/** Splitter sizes that survive a round trip: finite, positive, sane pixels. */
function parseSizes(raw: unknown): Partial<Record<LayoutVar, number>> {
  const sizes: Partial<Record<LayoutVar, number>> = {};
  if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null) return sizes;
  for (const key of Object.keys(kLayoutVars) as LayoutVar[]) {
    const n = (raw as Record<string, unknown>)[key];
    if (typeof n === "number" && Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 && n < 4000)
      sizes[key] = Math.round(n);
  }
  return sizes;
}

/** Bumped when the exported shape changes; an older file is refused, not guessed at. */
export const kLayoutFileVersion = 1;

/** What Settings writes: layout vars, rail, workspace tab, theme and motion. */
export type LayoutFile = {
  version: number;
  sizes: Partial<Record<LayoutVar, number>>;
  rail: RailView;
  workspaceTab: WorkspaceTab;
  theme: ThemeName;
  motion: MotionPref;
};

/** The live shell state as an export file. */
export function layoutFile(): LayoutFile {
  const s = useUi.getState();
  return {
    version: kLayoutFileVersion,
    sizes: s.sizes,
    rail: s.rail,
    workspaceTab: s.workspaceTab,
    theme: useTheme.getState().theme,
    motion: useMotion.getState().motion,
  };
}

/**
 * Validate an imported file. Throws naming the offending field: a support
 * hand-off must never half-apply a file that was meant for another build.
 */
export function parseLayoutFile(raw: string): LayoutFile {
  let v: Partial<LayoutFile>;
  try {
    v = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<LayoutFile>;
  } catch {
    throw new Error("not a JSON file");
  }
  if (typeof v !== "object" || v === null) throw new Error("not a JSON object");
  if (v.version !== kLayoutFileVersion)
    throw new Error(
      `unsupported version ${JSON.stringify(v.version)} (expected ${kLayoutFileVersion})`,
    );
  if (!kRails.includes(v.rail as RailView))
    throw new Error(`unknown rail ${JSON.stringify(v.rail)}`);
  if (!kWorkspaceTabs.includes(v.workspaceTab as WorkspaceTab))
    throw new Error(`unknown workspace tab ${JSON.stringify(v.workspaceTab)}`);
  if (!kThemes.some((t) => t.id === v.theme))
    throw new Error(`unknown theme ${JSON.stringify(v.theme)}`);
  if (!kMotionOptions.some((o) => o.id === v.motion))
    throw new Error(`unknown motion ${JSON.stringify(v.motion)}`);
  return {
    version: kLayoutFileVersion,
    sizes: parseSizes(v.sizes),
    rail: v.rail as RailView,
    workspaceTab: v.workspaceTab as WorkspaceTab,
    theme: v.theme as ThemeName,
    motion: v.motion as MotionPref,
  };
}

/** One line per field an import changes; empty when the file matches the shell. */
export function layoutChanges(before: LayoutFile, after: LayoutFile): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  if (before.theme !== after.theme) out.push(`theme ${before.theme} → ${after.theme}`);
  if (before.motion !== after.motion) out.push(`motion ${before.motion} → ${after.motion}`);
  if (before.rail !== after.rail) out.push(`rail ${before.rail} → ${after.rail}`);
  if (before.workspaceTab !== after.workspaceTab)
    out.push(`tab ${before.workspaceTab} → ${after.workspaceTab}`);
  for (const key of Object.keys(kLayoutVars) as LayoutVar[]) {
    const a = before.sizes[key];
    const b = after.sizes[key];
    if (a !== b) out.push(`${key} ${a ?? "default"} → ${b ?? "default"}`);
  }
  return out;
}

function load(): Layout {
  try {
    return parseLayout(localStorage.getItem(kStorageKey));
  } catch {
    return kDefaultLayout;
  }
}

function save(layout: Layout): void {
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(kStorageKey, JSON.stringify(layout));
  } catch {
    // storage unavailable: layout just does not persist
  }
}

type UiStore = Layout & {
  settingsOpen: boolean;
  paletteOpen: boolean;
  setRail: (rail: RailView) => void;
  setWorkspaceTab: (tab: WorkspaceTab) => void;
  setOutputTab: (tab: OutputTab) => void;
  setInspectorOpen: (open: boolean) => void;
  setSize: (key: LayoutVar, px: number) => void;
  resetLayout: () => void;
  importLayout: (file: LayoutFile) => void;
  openSettings: () => void;
  closeSettings: () => void;
  setPaletteOpen: (open: boolean) => void;
};

export const useUi = create<UiStore>((set, get) => {
  const update = (patch: Partial<Layout>) => {
    set(patch);
    const s = get();
    save({
      rail: s.rail,
      workspaceTab: s.workspaceTab,
      outputTab: s.outputTab,
      inspectorOpen: s.inspectorOpen,
      sizes: s.sizes,
    });
  };

  return {
    ...load(),
    settingsOpen: false,
    paletteOpen: false,
    setRail: (rail) => update({ rail }),
    setWorkspaceTab: (workspaceTab) => update({ workspaceTab }),
    setOutputTab: (outputTab) => update({ outputTab }),
    setInspectorOpen: (inspectorOpen) => update({ inspectorOpen }),
    setSize: (key, px) => update({ sizes: { ...get().sizes, [key]: Math.round(px) } }),
    resetLayout: () => update({ ...kDefaultLayout, sizes: {} }),
    importLayout: (file) => {
      useTheme.getState().setTheme(file.theme);
      useMotion.getState().setMotion(file.motion);
      update({ rail: file.rail, workspaceTab: file.workspaceTab, sizes: file.sizes });
    },
    openSettings: () => set({ settingsOpen: true, paletteOpen: false }),
    closeSettings: () => set({ settingsOpen: false }),
    setPaletteOpen: (paletteOpen) => set({ paletteOpen }),
  };
});
```

`app/src/store/updater.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/updater.ts
// Tauri updater bridge: check on boot, download + install, relaunch. Browser
// dev has no updater plugin, so every entry point is a no-op there.

import { create } from "zustand";
import type { DownloadEvent } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-updater";
import { isTauri } from "@/lib/endpoint";

export type UpdatePhase = "idle" | "checking" | "available" | "downloading" | "ready" | "error";

type PendingUpdate = {
  version: string;
  body: string;
  downloadAndInstall: (onEvent: (event: DownloadEvent) => void) => Promise<void>;
};

type UpdaterStore = {
  phase: UpdatePhase;
  version: string;
  notes: string;
  /** 0..1 while downloading, -1 when the server sent no length. */
  progress: number;
  error: string | null;
  dismissed: boolean;
  check: (manual?: boolean) => Promise<void>;
  install: () => Promise<void>;
  dismiss: () => void;
};

let pending: PendingUpdate | null = null;

async function plugins() {
  const [updater, process] = await Promise.all([
    import("@tauri-apps/plugin-updater"),
    import("@tauri-apps/plugin-process"),
  ]);
  return { check: updater.check, relaunch: process.relaunch };
}

export const useUpdater = create<UpdaterStore>((set, get) => ({
  phase: "idle",
  version: "",
  notes: "",
  progress: 0,
  error: null,
  dismissed: false,

  check: async (manual = false) => {
    if (!isTauri()) return;
    const phase = get().phase;
    if (phase === "checking" || phase === "downloading" || phase === "ready") return;
    set({ phase: "checking", error: null, dismissed: false });
    try {
      const { check } = await plugins();
      const update = await check();
      if (update === null) {
        set({ phase: "idle", version: "", notes: "", progress: 0 });
        return;
      }
      pending = {
        version: update.version,
        body: update.body ?? "",
        downloadAndInstall: (onEvent) => update.downloadAndInstall(onEvent),
      };
      set({ phase: "available", version: update.version, notes: update.body ?? "" });
      void manual;
    } catch (e) {
      // An offline launch must not nag; only a manual check surfaces the error.
      if (manual) {
        set({ phase: "error", error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) });
      } else {
        set({ phase: "idle", error: null });
      }
    }
  },

  install: async () => {
    if (!isTauri() || pending === null) return;
    set({ phase: "downloading", progress: 0, error: null });
    let total = 0;
    let done = 0;
    try {
      await pending.downloadAndInstall((event) => {
        if (event.event === "Started") {
          total = event.data.contentLength ?? 0;
        } else if (event.event === "Progress") {
          done += event.data.chunkLength;
          set({ progress: total > 0 ? Math.min(done / total, 1) : -1 });
        } else if (event.event === "Finished") {
          set({ phase: "ready", progress: 1 });
        }
      });
      // NSIS installs and exits on its own; relaunch is the explicit path for
      // installers that return control to us.
      const { relaunch } = await plugins();
      await relaunch();
    } catch (e) {
      set({ phase: "error", error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) });
    }
  },

  dismiss: () => set({ dismissed: true }),
}));

```

`app/src/store/watch.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/watch.ts
// watchlist mirror, the list lives in core and the app tick services it, a
// watch added over mcp shows up here and vice versa

import { create } from "zustand";
import * as events from "@/lib/events";
import { call, errorText } from "@/lib/rpc";
import type { WatchEntry, WatchValue } from "@/lib/events";

type WatchStore = {
  entries: WatchEntry[];
  values: Map<number, WatchValue>;
  attached: boolean;
  /** Last failed action, shown above the watchlist until the next success. */
  error: string | null;
  attach: () => () => void;
  load: () => Promise<void>;
  add: (addr: number, width: string, label?: string, intervalMs?: number) => Promise<boolean>;
  remove: (id: number) => Promise<boolean>;
  setFreeze: (id: number, freeze: boolean) => Promise<boolean>;
  poke: (id: number, value: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  /** Write the list as a Cheat Engine .CT table. */
  exportCt: (path: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  /** Append the entries of a .CT table to the list. */
  importCt: (path: string) => Promise<boolean>;
  clear: () => Promise<boolean>;
};

export const useWatch = create<WatchStore>((set) => {
  /** Every watch action reports through `error` instead of rejecting. */
  const run = async (fn: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<boolean> => {
    try {
      await fn();
      set({ error: null });
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      set({ error: errorText(e) });
      return false;
    }
  };

  return {
    entries: [],
    values: new Map(),
    attached: false,
    error: null,

    attach: () => {
      const offList = events.on("watch.list", ({ entries }) => set({ entries }));
      const offValues = events.on("watch.values", ({ attached, values }) =>
        set({ attached, values: new Map(values.map((v) => [v.id, v])) }),
      );
      return () => {
        offList();
        offValues();
      };
    },

    load: async () => {
      await run(async () => {
        const res = await call<{ entries: WatchEntry[]; values: WatchValue[] }>(
          "memory",
          "watch_list",
        );
        set({
          entries: res.entries ?? [],
          values: new Map((res.values ?? []).map((v) => [v.id, v])),
        });
      });
    },

    add: (addr, width, label, intervalMs) =>
      run(() =>
        call("memory", "watch_add", {
          addr,
          width,
          ...(label ? { label } : {}),
          ...(intervalMs !== undefined && intervalMs !== 100 ? { interval_ms: intervalMs } : {}),
        }),
      ),

    remove: (id) => run(() => call("memory", "watch_remove", { id })),

    setFreeze: (id, freeze) => run(() => call("memory", "watch_set", { id, freeze })),

    // Text form so f32/f64 and signed widths round-trip through the same
    // parse_value_text() the scanner's value box used
    poke: (id, value) => run(() => call("memory", "watch_set", { id, value })),

    exportCt: (path) => run(() => call("memory", "watch_export_ct", { path })),

    importCt: (path) => run(() => call("memory", "watch_import_ct", { path })),

    clear: () => run(() => call("memory", "watch_clear")),
  };
});

```

`app/src/store/xray.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/store/xray.ts
// Read-only xray passes over the loaded image or one function. One pass runs
// at a time; the engine reply is flattened into a table the panel can render
// and, for cfg, the shared CfgGraph component

import { create } from "zustand";
import { call, errorText } from "@/lib/rpc";
import type { CfgGraphData } from "@/store/decomp";

export const kXrayPasses = [
  "cfg",
  "complexity",
  "cff",
  "obfuscation",
  "strings_recon",
  "indirect_calls",
  "anti_analysis",
  "hooks",
  "syscalls",
  "apihash",
  "entropy",
  "pages",
  "crypto_range",
  "gadgets",
] as const;
export type XrayPass = (typeof kXrayPasses)[number];

/** Passes that take a function-start VA; the rest scan the whole image. */
export const kFunctionPasses: readonly XrayPass[] = [
  "cfg",
  "complexity",
  "cff",
  "obfuscation",
  "strings_recon",
  "indirect_calls",
  "anti_analysis",
];

export const kHashAlgorithms = ["ror13", "djb2", "crc32", "fnv1a", "sdbm"] as const;

export type Severity = "ok" | "warn" | "bad";
export type XrayRow = { addr?: number; cells: string[]; severity?: Severity };
export type XrayTable = { columns: string[]; rows: XrayRow[] };

export type XrayParams = {
  addr?: number;
  size?: number;
  limit?: number;
  algorithm?: string;
  hash?: string;
};

type XrayReply = {
  image?: string;
  graph?: CfgGraphData;
  blocks?: { start: number; end: number; instructions: number; successors: number[] }[];
  block_count?: number;
  edge_count?: number;
  back_edges?: number;
  cyclomatic_complexity?: number;
  instruction_count?: number;
  basic_block_count?: number;
  call_count?: number;
  branch_count?: number;
  return_count?: number;
  arithmetic_ops?: number;
  memory_accesses?: number;
  string_operations?: number;
  unique_operators?: number;
  unique_operands?: number;
  complexity_rating?: string;
  flattened?: boolean;
  dispatcher?: number;
  dispatcher_backedges?: number;
  state_variable?: string;
  state_blocks?: { start: number; end: number; next_state?: number | null; assign_addr: number }[];
  state_block_count?: number;
  patterns?: { type: string; address: number; detail: string }[];
  opaque_predicates?: number;
  dead_heads?: number;
  junk_sequences?: number;
  indirect_jumps?: number;
  push_ret?: number;
  privileged?: number;
  obfuscation_score_pct?: number;
  warning?: string;
  candidates?: {
    type: string;
    address: number;
    reconstructed?: string;
    xor_key?: number;
    length: number;
  }[];
  count?: number;
  indirect_calls?: {
    address: number;
    text: string;
    classification: string;
    base_register?: string;
    offset?: number;
    target?: number;
  }[];
  total?: number;
  detections?: { type: string; address: number; detail: string }[];
  anti_debug?: number;
  anti_vm?: number;
  timing_checks?: number;
  traps?: number;
  anti_analysis_score_pct?: number;
  functions_checked?: number;
  hooks_found?: number;
  hooks?: { address: number; hook_type: string; target: number; prologue_bytes: string }[];
  source?: string;
  abi?: string;
  syscalls_found?: number;
  syscalls?: { address: number; syscall_number: number; pattern: string; name?: string | null }[];
  algorithm?: string;
  total_queried?: number;
  resolved_count?: number;
  resolved?: { hash: number; api: string; dll: string }[];
  name_inputs?: { name: string; hash: number }[];
  hint?: string;
  overall_entropy?: number;
  min_window_entropy?: number;
  max_window_entropy?: number;
  window_size?: number;
  verdict?: string;
  truncated?: boolean;
  total_windows?: number;
  windows?: { offset: number; entropy: number; verdict: string }[];
  scan_base?: number;
  scan_size?: number;
  total_pages?: number;
  summary?: Record<string, number>;
  pages?: {
    address: number;
    size: number;
    class: string;
    entropy: number;
    insn_ratio: number;
    zero_ratio: number;
    string_ratio: number;
  }[];
  matches?: { va: number; algorithm: string; constant: string; value: number; source: string }[];
  gadgets?: { address: number; text: string }[];
  note?: string;
};

type XrayView = { table: XrayTable; summary: string; graph: CfgGraphData | null };

const kHex = (v: number | undefined) =>
  v === undefined ? "-" : `0x${v.toString(16).toUpperCase()}`;
const kNum = (v: number | undefined) => (v === undefined ? "-" : String(v));
const kPct = (v: number | undefined) => (v === undefined ? "-" : `${v}%`);

function entropySeverity(verdict: string | undefined): Severity {
  if (verdict === "encrypted_or_compressed") return "bad";
  if (verdict === "high_entropy") return "warn";
  return "ok";
}

function pageSeverity(klass: string): Severity {
  if (klass === "encrypted_or_compressed" || klass === "single_byte_encrypted") return "bad";
  if (klass === "mixed") return "warn";
  return "ok";
}

/** Flatten one engine reply into the panel's table + summary. */
function viewFor(action: XrayPass, r: XrayReply): XrayView {
  switch (action) {
    case "cfg":
      return {
        graph: r.graph ?? null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.block_count)} blocks · ${kNum(r.edge_count)} edges · ${kNum(
          r.back_edges,
        )} back edges · cyclomatic ${kNum(r.cyclomatic_complexity)}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Block", "End", "Insns", "Successors"],
          rows: (r.blocks ?? []).map((b) => ({
            addr: b.start,
            cells: [
              kHex(b.start),
              kHex(b.end),
              kNum(b.instructions),
              b.successors.map((s) => kHex(s)).join(", ") || "-",
            ],
          })),
        },
      };
    case "complexity":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `rating ${r.complexity_rating ?? "-"}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Metric", "Value"],
          rows: [
            ["Instructions", r.instruction_count],
            ["Basic blocks", r.basic_block_count],
            ["Edges", r.edge_count],
            ["Cyclomatic", r.cyclomatic_complexity],
            ["Calls", r.call_count],
            ["Branches", r.branch_count],
            ["Returns", r.return_count],
            ["Arithmetic ops", r.arithmetic_ops],
            ["Memory accesses", r.memory_accesses],
            ["String ops", r.string_operations],
            ["Unique operators", r.unique_operators],
            ["Unique operands", r.unique_operands],
          ].map(([label, value]) => ({
            cells: [String(label), kNum(value as number | undefined)],
          })),
        },
      };
    case "cff":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: r.flattened
          ? `flattened · dispatcher ${kHex(r.dispatcher)} · ${
              r.dispatcher_backedges ?? 0
            } backedges · state ${r.state_variable ?? "-"}`
          : "not flattened (no dispatcher)",
        table: {
          columns: ["State block", "End", "Next state", "Assign at"],
          rows: (r.state_blocks ?? []).map((b) => ({
            addr: b.start,
            cells: [
              kHex(b.start),
              kHex(b.end),
              kHex(b.next_state ?? undefined),
              kHex(b.assign_addr),
            ],
            severity: "warn",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "obfuscation":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `score ${kPct(r.obfuscation_score_pct)} · opaque ${kNum(
          r.opaque_predicates,
        )} · junk ${kNum(r.junk_sequences)} · indirect jumps ${kNum(r.indirect_jumps)}${
          r.warning !== undefined ? ` · ${r.warning}` : ""
        }`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Pattern", "Address", "Detail"],
          rows: (r.patterns ?? []).map((p) => ({
            addr: p.address,
            cells: [p.type, kHex(p.address), p.detail],
            severity: "bad",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "strings_recon":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.count)} candidates`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Type", "Length", "XOR key", "Reconstructed"],
          rows: (r.candidates ?? []).map((c) => ({
            addr: c.address,
            cells: [
              kHex(c.address),
              c.type,
              kNum(c.length),
              c.xor_key === undefined ? "-" : kHex(c.xor_key),
              c.reconstructed ?? "-",
            ],
            severity: c.reconstructed !== undefined ? "warn" : "ok",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "indirect_calls":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.total)} indirect calls`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Classification", "Base", "Target", "Instruction"],
          rows: (r.indirect_calls ?? []).map((c) => ({
            addr: c.address,
            cells: [
              kHex(c.address),
              c.classification,
              c.base_register === undefined
                ? "-"
                : `${c.base_register}${c.offset === undefined ? "" : `+${kHex(c.offset)}`}`,
              kHex(c.target),
              c.text,
            ],
            severity: "warn",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "anti_analysis":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `score ${kPct(r.anti_analysis_score_pct)} · anti-debug ${kNum(
          r.anti_debug,
        )} · anti-VM ${kNum(r.anti_vm)} · timing ${kNum(r.timing_checks)} · traps ${kNum(r.traps)}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Type", "Address", "Detail"],
          rows: (r.detections ?? []).map((d) => ({
            addr: d.address,
            cells: [d.type, kHex(d.address), d.detail],
            severity: "bad",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "hooks":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.hooks_found)} hooks in ${kNum(r.functions_checked)} functions (${
          r.source ?? "index"
        })`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Hook", "Target", "Prologue"],
          rows: (r.hooks ?? []).map((h) => ({
            addr: h.address,
            cells: [kHex(h.address), h.hook_type, kHex(h.target), h.prologue_bytes],
            severity: "bad",
          })),
        },
      };
    case "syscalls":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.syscalls_found)} syscalls · abi ${r.abi ?? "-"}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Number", "Name", "Pattern"],
          rows: (r.syscalls ?? []).map((s) => ({
            addr: s.address,
            cells: [kHex(s.address), kNum(s.syscall_number), s.name ?? "-", s.pattern],
          })),
        },
      };
    case "apihash":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.resolved_count)} / ${kNum(r.total_queried)} resolved · ${
          r.algorithm ?? "-"
        }${r.hint !== undefined ? ` · ${r.hint}` : ""}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Hash", "API", "DLL"],
          rows: (r.resolved ?? []).map((h) => ({
            cells: [kHex(h.hash), h.api, h.dll],
          })),
        },
      };
    case "entropy":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `overall ${r.overall_entropy?.toFixed(3) ?? "-"} · min ${
          r.min_window_entropy?.toFixed(3) ?? "-"
        } · max ${r.max_window_entropy?.toFixed(3) ?? "-"} · ${
          r.verdict ?? "-"
        } · ${kNum(r.total_windows)} windows of ${kNum(r.window_size)} B`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Offset", "Entropy", "Verdict"],
          rows: (r.windows ?? []).map((w) => ({
            cells: [kHex(w.offset), w.entropy.toFixed(3), w.verdict],
            severity: entropySeverity(w.verdict),
          })),
        },
      };
    case "pages":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.total_pages)} pages · ${Object.entries(r.summary ?? {})
          .map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${v}`)
          .join(" · ")}`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Size", "Class", "Entropy", "Code", "Zero", "Strings"],
          rows: (r.pages ?? []).map((p) => ({
            addr: p.address,
            cells: [
              kHex(p.address),
              kNum(p.size),
              p.class,
              p.entropy.toFixed(2),
              `${Math.round(p.insn_ratio * 100)}%`,
              `${Math.round(p.zero_ratio * 100)}%`,
              `${Math.round(p.string_ratio * 100)}%`,
            ],
            severity: pageSeverity(p.class),
          })),
        },
      };
    case "crypto_range":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.count)} constant matches`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Algorithm", "Constant", "Value", "Source"],
          rows: (r.matches ?? []).map((m) => ({
            addr: m.va,
            cells: [kHex(m.va), m.algorithm, m.constant, kHex(m.value), m.source],
          })),
        },
      };
    case "gadgets":
      return {
        graph: null,
        summary: `${kNum(r.count)} gadgets`,
        table: {
          columns: ["Address", "Gadget"],
          rows: (r.gadgets ?? []).map((g) => ({
            addr: g.address,
            cells: [kHex(g.address), g.text],
          })),
        },
      };
  }
}

type XrayStore = {
  action: XrayPass | null;
  table: XrayTable | null;
  summary: string;
  graph: CfgGraphData | null;
  note: string;
  busy: boolean;
  error: string | null;
  run: (action: XrayPass, params?: XrayParams) => Promise<void>;
  reset: () => void;
};

export const useXray = create<XrayStore>((set) => ({
  action: null,
  table: null,
  summary: "",
  graph: null,
  note: "",
  busy: false,
  error: null,

  run: async (action, params = {}) => {
    set({ busy: true, error: null, note: "" });
    try {
      const reply = await call<XrayReply>("xray", action, params);
      const view = viewFor(action, reply);
      set({
        action,
        table: view.table,
        summary: view.summary,
        graph: view.graph,
        note: reply.note ?? "",
        busy: false,
      });
    } catch (e) {
      set({ action, table: null, summary: "", graph: null, error: errorText(e), busy: false });
    }
  },

  reset: () =>
    set({
      action: null,
      table: null,
      summary: "",
      graph: null,
      note: "",
      error: null,
      busy: false,
    }),
}));

```

```css
/* --- scrollbars ----------------------------------------------------------- */
/* WebView2 ships Chromium's default chunky light scrollbar, which reads as a
 * different application bolted onto the side of the panels. Thin, dark, and
 * accent-on-drag instead. `scrollbar-gutter: stable` keeps content from
 * shifting sideways when a list crosses the overflow threshold */

* {
  scrollbar-width: thin;
  scrollbar-color: var(--border) transparent;
}

.panel-body,
.modal-body,
.code-area {
  scrollbar-gutter: stable;
}

::-webkit-scrollbar {
  width: 11px;
  height: 11px;
  background: transparent;
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
  background: transparent;
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
  /* Border trick: a transparent border with background-clip gives the thumb
     inset padding without a wrapper element, so it floats clear of the edge */
  background: var(--border);
  background-clip: padding-box;
  border: 3px solid transparent;
  border-radius: 6px;
  transition: background-color 120ms ease-out;
}

::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover {
  background: var(--text-faint);

/* --- motion --------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* One timing scale for the whole app so nothing feels out of step. Short
 * enough that a workbench never feels like it is waiting on an animation */

:root {
  --ease: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0.2, 1);
  --fast: 90ms;
  --med: 190ms;
  --slow: 260ms;
}

@keyframes view-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(7px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: none;
  }
}

/* Panels slide in from the rail side rather than upward, the horizontal motion
   reads as "this replaced the thing next to the rail" */
@keyframes panel-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateX(-10px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: none;
  }
}

@keyframes pop-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: scale(0.97);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: none;
  }
}

@keyframes tip-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(3px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: none;
  }
}

     placement, so only opacity moves */

  }
  to {

  }

}

/* Panels are keyed by the activity rail, so this replays on every rail switch
   as well as on first paint */

}

   (a scrolling .panel-body, a table body) and just need the enter transition */

}

.empty {

/* --- press feedback ------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Every clickable surface acknowledges the press. Scale is deliberately tiny
 * (2-3%), enough to feel mechanical, not enough to look bouncy */

.menu-button,
.win-button,
.rail-button,
.icon-button,
.row-action,
.tab,
.hex-cell,
.insn-target,
.select,
.link {

    background-color var(--fast) var(--ease),
    color var(--fast) var(--ease),
    border-color var(--fast) var(--ease),
    transform var(--fast) var(--ease),
    opacity var(--fast) var(--ease);
}

.row-action:active:not(:disabled),
.rail-button:active,
.hex-cell:active,
.insn-target:active {

}

.menu-button:active,

}

.icon-button:disabled {

}

    background-color var(--fast) var(--ease),
    color var(--fast) var(--ease);
}

/* Rows are hovered constantly while scanning a list; keep theirs even shorter
   so the highlight tracks the cursor instead of trailing it */
.fn-row,
.insn-row,
.hex-row,
.table tbody tr {
  transition: background-color 60ms linear;
}

/* The rail's active marker grows from the centre rather than popping in */
.rail-button::before {
  transform: scaleY(0);
  transition: transform var(--med) var(--ease);
}

.rail-button[data-active="true"]::before {
  transform: scaleY(1);
}

/* The tab underline slides its width in from the active edge */
.tab::after {
  transform: scaleX(0);
  transform-origin: center;
  transition: transform var(--med) var(--ease);
}

.tab[data-active="true"]::after {
  transform: scaleX(1);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  /* Only when the user has not explicitly asked for motion. This machine's
     Windows animation setting is off, which Chromium reports here, honouring it
     unconditionally meant the app could never animate at all */
  html:not([data-motion="on"]) *,
  html:not([data-motion="on"]) *::before,
  html:not([data-motion="on"]) *::after {
    animation-duration: 1ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: 1ms !important;
  }
}

html[data-motion="off"] *,
html[data-motion="off"] *::before,
html[data-motion="off"] *::after {
  animation-duration: 1ms !important;
  animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
  transition-duration: 1ms !important;
}
```

`app/src/test/api.ts`:

```ts
// app/src/test/api.ts
// Fake engine /api for tests: routes single and batched tool calls to a
// handler and records every call. A handler may return data, throw (tool
// failure), or return a promise that never settles (wedged engine)

import { vi } from "vitest";

export type ApiCall = { tool: string; action: string; params: Record<string, unknown> };
export type ApiHandler = (call: ApiCall) => unknown;

type Body = { tool: string; action: string; params?: Record<string, unknown>; id?: number };

async function envelope(handler: ApiHandler, b: Body, calls: ApiCall[]) {
  const call = { tool: b.tool, action: b.action, params: b.params ?? {} };
  calls.push(call);
  try {
    const data = await handler(call);
    return { ok: true, data: data ?? {}, ...(b.id !== undefined ? { id: b.id } : {}) };
  } catch (e) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      data: { error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) },
      ...(b.id !== undefined ? { id: b.id } : {}),
    };
  }
}

/** Install a fetch stub for the engine. Returns the recorded calls. */
export function mockApi(handler: ApiHandler): {
  calls: ApiCall[];
  fetch: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
} {
  const calls: ApiCall[] = [];
  const fetch = vi.fn(async (url: string, init?: RequestInit) => {
    if (String(url).endsWith("/health")) return { ok: true, json: async () => ({ ok: true }) };
    const body = JSON.parse(String(init?.body)) as Body | Body[];
    const signal = init?.signal;
    const work = Array.isArray(body)
      ? Promise.all(body.map((b) => envelope(handler, b, calls)))
      : envelope(handler, body, calls);
    const result = await new Promise<unknown>((resolve, reject) => {
      signal?.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(new DOMException("aborted", "AbortError")));
      work.then(resolve, reject);
    });
    return { ok: true, json: async () => result };
  });
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", fetch);
  return { calls, fetch };
}

/** Let pending promise continuations run. */
export async function flushPromises(rounds = 5): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < rounds; i++) await Promise.resolve();
}

```

```ts
// app/src/test/setup.ts
// jsdom gaps the components rely on, plus Testing Library matchers/cleanup

import "@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest";
import { cleanup } from "@testing-library/react";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, vi } from "vitest";

// Node >= 25 ships its own global localStorage that is undefined without
// --localstorage-file and shadows jsdom's; give tests a working Storage
class MemoryStorage implements Storage {
  private map = new Map<string, string>();
  get length(): number {
    return this.map.size;
  }
  clear(): void {
    this.map.clear();
  }
  getItem(key: string): string | null {
    return this.map.get(key) ?? null;
  }
  key(index: number): string | null {
    return [...this.map.keys()][index] ?? null;
  }
  removeItem(key: string): void {
    this.map.delete(key);
  }
  setItem(key: string, value: string): void {
    this.map.set(key, String(value));
  }
}
Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "localStorage", {
  configurable: true,
  value: new MemoryStorage(),
});

// Virtualized lists measure their scroll element; jsdom reports 0x0, which
// would render no rows at all
Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect = function getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect {
  return {
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    top: 0,
    left: 0,
    bottom: 600,
    right: 800,
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    toJSON: () => ({}),
  } as DOMRect;
};
Object.defineProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, "offsetHeight", {
  configurable: true,
  get: () => 600,
});
Object.defineProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, "offsetWidth", { configurable: true, get: () => 800 });
// @tanstack/virtual-core >= 3.19 measures via clientWidth/clientHeight rather
// than getBoundingClientRect, and jsdom leaves both at 0
Object.defineProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, "clientHeight", {
  configurable: true,
  get: () => 600,
});
Object.defineProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, "clientWidth", { configurable: true, get: () => 800 });

class ResizeObserverStub {
  observe(): void {}
  unobserve(): void {}
  disconnect(): void {}
}
globalThis.ResizeObserver = ResizeObserverStub as unknown as typeof ResizeObserver;

export class EventSourceStub {
  static instances: EventSourceStub[] = [];
  onopen: (() => void) | null = null;
  onerror: (() => void) | null = null;
  private listeners = new Map<string, (ev: MessageEvent<string>) => void>();
  constructor(readonly url: string) {
    EventSourceStub.instances.push(this);
  }
  addEventListener(name: string, fn: (ev: MessageEvent<string>) => void): void {
    this.listeners.set(name, fn);
  }
  /** Deliver one server-sent event, as the engine would. */
  emit(name: string, data: unknown): void {
    this.listeners.get(name)?.(new MessageEvent(name, { data: JSON.stringify(data) }));
  }
  close(): void {}
}
globalThis.EventSource = EventSourceStub as unknown as typeof EventSource;

/** The engine's /events websocket, driven by hand from the tests. */
export class WebSocketStub {
  static instances: WebSocketStub[] = [];
  onopen: (() => void) | null = null;
  onmessage: ((ev: MessageEvent<string>) => void) | null = null;
  onclose: (() => void) | null = null;
  onerror: (() => void) | null = null;
  readyState = 0;
  constructor(readonly url: string) {
    WebSocketStub.instances.push(this);
  }
  close(): void {
    this.readyState = 3;
  }
  /** Deliver one frame, as the engine would. */
  emit(name: string, data: unknown): void {
    this.onmessage?.(new MessageEvent("message", { data: JSON.stringify({ event: name, data }) }));
  }
}
globalThis.WebSocket = WebSocketStub as unknown as typeof WebSocket;

/** The stream the engine just opened: websocket first, sse after a fallback. */
export function lastStream(): Promise<EventSourceStub | WebSocketStub> {
  return vi.waitFor(() => {
    const stream = WebSocketStub.instances.at(-1) ?? EventSourceStub.instances.at(-1);
    if (stream === undefined) throw new Error("no stream opened");
    return stream;
  });
}

if (window.matchMedia === undefined) {
  window.matchMedia = (query: string) =>
    ({
      matches: false,
      media: query,
      onchange: null,
      addEventListener: () => undefined,
      removeEventListener: () => undefined,
      addListener: () => undefined,
      removeListener: () => undefined,
      dispatchEvent: () => false,
    }) as MediaQueryList;
}

Element.prototype.scrollTo = function scrollTo(): void {};
Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = function scrollIntoView(): void {};

beforeEach(() => {
  localStorage.clear();
});

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  vi.useRealTimers();
});
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { fileURLToPath, URL } from "node:url";

// `tauri build --debug` (and `tauri dev`) export TAURI_ENV_DEBUG=true. Release
// bundles ship without sourcemaps: the installer would otherwise carry the
// complete TypeScript sources. SOURCEMAP=1 forces them on for local profiling.
const debugBuild = process.env.TAURI_ENV_DEBUG === "true" || process.env.SOURCEMAP === "1";

// Tauri drives this: it starts `npm run dev` and points the webview at
// devUrl. The fixed port matters because tauri.conf.json and the engine's
// CORS allow-list both name it explicitly.
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  resolve: {
    alias: { "@": fileURLToPath(new URL("./src", import.meta.url)) },
  },
  clearScreen: false,
  server: {
    port: 1420,
    strictPort: true,
    watch: { ignored: ["**/src-tauri/**"] },
  },
  build: {
    target: "chrome110",
    sourcemap: debugBuild,
  },
});
```

```cmake
include_guard(GLOBAL)
include(FetchContent)

# Downloaded dependency sources plus their sub-builds/binary dirs. The primary
# build/ tree uses _ext/ (cached by CI); the other presets (debug, asan,
# analyze) point this into their own binary dir because a dependency's binary
# dir under here belongs to exactly one build tree.
set(SLOP_DEPS_DIR "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/_ext" CACHE PATH "FetchContent base dir for dependency sources and builds")
set(FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR "${SLOP_DEPS_DIR}" CACHE PATH "" FORCE)
set(FETCHCONTENT_QUIET OFF)
set(FETCHCONTENT_UPDATES_DISCONNECTED ON)

# Every archive is pinned by SHA-256 and every git dependency by a full commit
# SHA, so a moved tag or a tampered download fails the configure instead of
# being compiled into the shipped engine. Bumping a dep means updating both
# the URL and its hash (tools/dep_hash.ps1 prints the hash of a URL).
# Dear ImGui v1.92.1-docking (tag object e0b5968) -> commit 44aa9a4
set(SLOP_IMGUI_COMMIT "44aa9a4b3a6f27d09a4eb5770d095cbd376dfc4b")

# reverse-slop's own tests

set(FT_DISABLE_PNG TRUE CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

set(CAPSTONE_BUILD_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

set(CAPSTONE_ARM_SUPPORT ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(CAPSTONE_ARM64_SUPPORT ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

FetchContent_Declare(fmt
    URL https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt/archive/refs/tags/11.1.4.zip
    URL_HASH SHA256=7e85cbf6125a76daa0f83cd9240eff863d988aca68cd5f66c01ff7b59fa886b6
    SYSTEM

# Unicorn's qemu util defines crc32() with the same CRC-32 algorithm zlib
# exports (same table, same complement convention). Enabling the aarch64
# target makes the ARM CRC32 helpers reference crc32c(), which pulls
# qemu/util/crc32c.c in and with it a second crc32 definition. The two are
# behaviourally identical, so let the linker accept the duplicate instead of
# renaming a symbol that also feeds the generated TCG helper names
if(MSVC AND TARGET unicorn)
    target_link_options(unicorn INTERFACE /FORCE:MULTIPLE)
elseif(TARGET unicorn)
    # same duplicate crc32 as the MSVC case above; ELF has no /FORCE:MULTIPLE
    target_link_options(unicorn INTERFACE -Wl,--allow-multiple-definition)
endif()

# zlib builds both a shared and a static lib, we only want the static one so
# the exes stay freestanding
if(NOT TARGET ZLIB::ZLIB)
    add_library(ZLIB::ZLIB ALIAS zlibstatic)
endif()

    "${sqlite_SOURCE_DIR}/sqlite3.c"

)

endif()

# Lua must build as C++: LUAI_THROW then raises a real C++ exception, so a
```

`cmake/slop_resources.cmake`:

```cmake
include_guard(GLOBAL)

# slop_add_win_resources(<target> DESCRIPTION <text> MANIFEST <manifest.in>)
#
# Configures <manifest.in> (assemblyIdentity version from PROJECT_VERSION) and
# a resource script carrying that manifest plus a VERSIONINFO block into the
# target's binary dir, then compiles it into <target>. The exe name comes from
# the target's OUTPUT_NAME (or the target name).
function(slop_add_win_resources target)
    cmake_parse_arguments(PARSE_ARGV 1 arg "" "DESCRIPTION;MANIFEST" "")
    if(NOT arg_DESCRIPTION OR NOT arg_MANIFEST)
        message(FATAL_ERROR "slop_add_win_resources: DESCRIPTION and MANIFEST are required")
    endif()
    get_target_property(_name ${target} OUTPUT_NAME)
    if(NOT _name)
        set(_name ${target})
    endif()

    set(_out "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}_res")
    get_filename_component(_manifest_name "${arg_MANIFEST}" NAME)
    string(REGEX REPLACE "\\.in$" "" _manifest_name "${_manifest_name}")
    configure_file("${arg_MANIFEST}" "${_out}/${_manifest_name}" @ONLY)

    set(SLOP_RC_MANIFEST "${_out}/${_manifest_name}")
    set(SLOP_RC_DESCRIPTION "${arg_DESCRIPTION}")
    set(SLOP_RC_NAME "${_name}")
    configure_file("${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/win_resources.rc.in" "${_out}/${target}.rc" @ONLY)

    target_sources(${target} PRIVATE "${_out}/${target}.rc")
    # the manifest is embedded as RT_MANIFEST by the .rc, keep the linker's own
    # manifest machinery out of it entirely (CMP0090 NEW)
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE "/MANIFEST:NO")
endfunction()

```

`cmake/win_resources.rc.in`:

```in
// Generated by cmake/slop_resources.cmake from cmake/win_resources.rc.in.
// Embeds the application manifest (RT_MANIFEST, ID 1) and a VERSIONINFO block
// derived from the root VERSION file.
#include <winres.h>

1 24 "@SLOP_RC_MANIFEST@"

VS_VERSION_INFO VERSIONINFO
 FILEVERSION     @PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR@,@PROJECT_VERSION_MINOR@,@PROJECT_VERSION_PATCH@,0
 PRODUCTVERSION  @PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR@,@PROJECT_VERSION_MINOR@,@PROJECT_VERSION_PATCH@,0
 FILEFLAGSMASK   VS_FFI_FILEFLAGSMASK
 FILEFLAGS       0x0L
 FILEOS          VOS_NT_WINDOWS32
 FILETYPE        VFT_APP
 FILESUBTYPE     VFT2_UNKNOWN
BEGIN
    BLOCK "StringFileInfo"
    BEGIN
        BLOCK "040904B0"
        BEGIN
            VALUE "CompanyName",      "NetVar1337"
            VALUE "FileDescription",  "@SLOP_RC_DESCRIPTION@"
            VALUE "FileVersion",      "@PROJECT_VERSION@"
            VALUE "InternalName",     "@SLOP_RC_NAME@"
            VALUE "LegalCopyright",   "Copyright (c) 2026 NetVar1337. MIT License."
            VALUE "OriginalFilename", "@SLOP_RC_NAME@.exe"
            VALUE "ProductName",      "reverse-slop"
            VALUE "ProductVersion",   "@PROJECT_VERSION@"
        END
    END
    BLOCK "VarFileInfo"
    BEGIN
        VALUE "Translation", 0x0409, 1200
    END
END
```

`docs/AUDIT.md`:

```md
# reverse-slop — Full Audit

Date: 2026-11-11 · Scope: whole repo (`src/`, `app/`, `tools/`, CI, docs) · Baseline: v0.1.1, ~36.4k lines of first-party C++ (280 files), ~7.5k lines of TypeScript/React, 455 C++ test cases, 50 frontend tests.

## Verdict up front

This is an unusually healthy codebase: pinned dependencies, ASAN + `/analyze` + clang-tidy CI lanes, a deterministic live-fixture test target, chaos-mode protocol tests, benchmark baselines with CI regression gating, signed releases with SHA256SUMS, a sandboxed Lua surface, loopback-only HTTP with bearer tokens and DNS-rebinding guards. There are **no confirmed critical defects** in the audited state. The findings below are dominated by _feature gaps and hardening opportunities_, plus a small number of concrete issues.

**Top 5 things to act on first:**

1. **Unfinished merge in the working tree** — `git status` shows an in-progress merge with conflicts in `src/core/mcp/mcp_tools.cpp`, `src/core/runtime/backend_ps4.cpp`, `src/tests/test_ps4.cpp` (and staged edits in `backend_ps4.hpp`, `ps4_protocol.hpp`). The tree does not build in this state and the conflicted hunks contain typos (`INTALL`, `intall`, `ths`, `clen`). Resolve, commit or abort before anything else.
2. **No fuzzing** of the ELF/PE/Mach-O/IPA/packet parsers that consume untrusted dumps and captures.
3. **No code-coverage reporting** in CI — 455 tests exist, but nobody measures what they reach.
4. **No e2e/UI tests** for the Tauri app — only component/store unit tests; nothing drives a real engine.
5. **README/docs drift risk** — version badge is hardcoded, deep reference tables duplicate the code, and the README is 36 KB (reworked separately in this pass).

Severity legend: **P0** fix now · **P1** next milestone · **P2** roadmap · **P3** nice-to-have.

---

## 1. Repository / process

| #   | Sev    | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **P0** | Unresolved merge conflicts (`UU` files) left in the working tree; build is broken until resolved.                                                                                         |
| 2   | P2     | `.cache/` (clangd index) is not in `.gitignore`; it sits untracked in the working tree.                                                                                                   |
| 3   | P2     | Two stale build trees (`build/`, `build-ninja-msvc-asan/`) live in the checkout; documented, but a `tools/clean.ps1` convenience would help.                                              |
| 4   | P3     | No `CODEOWNERS`; review routing is implicit.                                                                                                                                              |
| 5   | P3     | No `FUNDING.yml` / sponsorship metadata.                                                                                                                                                  |
| 6   | P2     | No `ROADMAP.md`; intended direction (PS5? Switch? Linux host?) is discoverable only from issues.                                                                                          |
| 7   | P3     | `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is 609 KB generated noise in the repo root; generate at packaging time instead and keep a checksum.                                                              |
| 8   | P3     | Git history mixes `feat:`/`refactor:` conventional commits with free-form ones; add commitlint only if you care — currently cosmetic.                                                     |
| 9   | P2     | Release notes are auto-cut from CHANGELOG by tag; CHANGELOG `Unreleased` section is healthy but make `tools/sync_version.ps1` also verify the badge version in README (currently manual). |

## 2. Build / CI

| #   | Sev | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 10  | P1  | No code-coverage lane (OpenCPPCoverage/`/cs`-style or llvm-cov) — add one and gate PRs on core modules.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 11  | P1  | No fuzz targets. libFuzzer harnesses for `elf_loader`, `pe_parser`, `macho_loader`, `ipa`, `zip_reader`, and the ps4debug-NG packet parser would pay for themselves (these eat untrusted dumps).                                                                            |

### Runtime / PS4 backend

| #   | Sev | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Summary counts

- **P0:** 1 (merge conflicts in working tree)
- **P1:** 14 (fuzzing, coverage, e2e, conditional breakpoints, unknown-value scans, encrypted-SELF strategy, SELF-decrypt, secret redaction in proxy, MITM key handling, MCP annotations/versioning, UI telemetry/export parity, README)
- **P2:** ~55 items across runtime, memory, debugger, decompiler, network, MCP, frontend, docs, security hardening, platform ports
- **P3:** ~45 polish/parity/community items

**Theme of the audit:** the _engineering floor_ (build, CI, tests, pinning, signing) is already better than most commercial tooling; the leverage is now in (a) closing the test-visibility gap (coverage, fuzz, e2e), (b) debugger/scanner parity with Cheat Engine-class expectations (conditions, counts, unknown-value, pointer chains), (c) agent-facing upgrades to the MCP surface (annotations, versioning, rate limits, elicitation), and (d) deciding the fate of the ImGui shell and the multi-console roadmap.

## Addendum — implementation pass (same day)

Landed from this audit:

- Items 2, 4, 6, 9: `.gitignore` covers `.cache/`; `CODEOWNERS`; `ROADMAP.md`;
  `tools/sync_version.ps1` also validates the README version badge.
- Items 80 + 97: `app/e2e` driver (smoke + screenshots modes), `tools/screenshots.ps1`,
  nightly `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`. Both modes verified green against the real
  engine + fixture, with no leaked processes.
- README: new screenshots regenerated through the committed driver; Tests section
  documents the e2e lane; screenshot disclaimer updated.
- CHANGELOG updated under Unreleased.

New findings surfaced while building the e2e harness:

- **P2 — `--port` ignored by the current build.** The engine announces/binds the
  settings port even with `--port <n>` on the command line; the `SLOP_MCP_PORT`
  environment variable works. Either the checked-in binary predates the flag or the
  flag plumbing regressed; rebuild and re-test (the e2e driver passes both and trusts
  the engine's own `SLOP_ENGINE_READY` announce instead of the requested port).
- **P2 — spawner can report a dead endpoint.** Under process churn, `engine.json` can
  name a pid that is alive-but-not-serving (or reused); a spawner then prints
  `SLOP_ENGINE_READY <port>` for an endpoint that 401s/times out. The e2e driver works
  around it (probes health + detects `SLOP_ENGINE_EXISTING`); the engine should verify
  the registration round-trip before announcing (or liveness-probe the endpoint).
- **P3 — `/health` is unauthenticated** (liveness, by design) — automation must treat
  the first `/api` call as the real readiness gate.
```
