```hpp
namespace slop::core::compat {

// "pid N (name)" of the process listening on `port`, from /proc/net/tcp* and
// the socket inode -> fd symlinks; empty when nobody listens there
inline std::string tcp_listener_owner(uint16_t port) {
    std::FILE* f = std::fopen("/proc/net/tcp", "r");
    if (!f) return {};
    char line[512];
    std::string inode;
    if (!std::fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) { std::fclose(f); return {}; }
    while (std::fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
        // sl local_address rem_address st tx:rx tr:when retrnsmt uid timeout inode
        unsigned local_port = 0, state = 0;
        unsigned long ino = 0;
        char local[64]{};
        if (std::sscanf(line, " %*d: %63[0-9A-Fa-f]:%x %*63s %x %*s %*s %*s %*u %*u %lu",
                        local, &local_port, &state, &ino) < 4)
            continue;
        if (local_port == port && state == 0x0A) { inode = std::to_string(ino); break; }
    }
    std::fclose(f);
    if (inode.empty()) return {};
    const std::string want = "socket:[" + inode + "]";
    // true when /proc/<pid>/fd holds the listening socket
    const auto owns = [&want](const std::string& pid) {
        DIR* d = ::opendir(("/proc/" + pid + "/fd").c_str());
        if (!d) return false;
        bool hit = false;
        while (dirent* e = ::readdir(d)) {
            if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;
            char target[512];
            const std::string path = "/proc/" + pid + "/fd/" + e->d_name;
            const ssize_t n = ::readlink(path.c_str(), target, sizeof(target) - 1);
            if (n <= 0) continue;
            target[n] = '\0';
            if (want == target) { hit = true; break; }
        }
        ::closedir(d);
        return hit;
    };
    const auto describe = [](const std::string& pid) {
        std::string who = "pid " + pid;
        char name[512];
        const ssize_t n = ::readlink(("/proc/" + pid + "/exe").c_str(), name, sizeof(name) - 1);
        if (n > 0) {
            name[n] = '\0';
            const std::string s = name;
            const size_t slash = s.find_last_of('/');
            who += " (" + (slash == std::string::npos ? s : s.substr(slash + 1)) + ")";
        }
        return who;
    };
    // the common case (our own stale listener) first, labelled like the Win32 path
    const std::string self = std::to_string(::getpid());
    if (owns(self)) return "pid " + self + " (this process)";
    // then only the pids that exist, not the whole pid_max range
    DIR* proc = ::opendir("/proc");
    if (!proc) return {};
    std::string found;
    while (dirent* e = ::readdir(proc)) {
        const char* n = e->d_name;
        if (*n < '1' || *n > '9') continue;
        bool numeric = true;
        for (const char* c = n; *c; ++c) numeric = numeric && *c >= '0' && *c <= '9';
        if (!numeric || self == n || !owns(n)) continue;
        found = describe(n);
        break;
    }
    ::closedir(proc);
    return found;
}
```

`src/core/debugger/callstack.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/debugger/callstack.cpp

#include "core/debugger/callstack.hpp"

#include <cstring>
#include <set>

namespace slop::core::debugger::unwind {

namespace {

constexpr uint64_t kUserMax = 0x7FFFFFFEFFFFull;   // highest user VA

bool plausible_code(disasm::engine_t& eng, reader_t& rdr, uint64_t va) {
    if (va == 0 || va > kUserMax) return false;
    uint8_t buf[16]{};
    if (!rdr.read(va, buf, sizeof(buf))) return false;
    auto in = eng.decode(va, buf, sizeof(buf));
    return in.has_value() && in->length > 0;
}

} // namespace

std::vector<frame_t> walk_stack(disasm::engine_t& eng, reader_t& rdr,
                                uint64_t /*rip*/, uint64_t rsp, uint64_t rbp,
                                size_t max_frames) {
    std::vector<frame_t> out;
    if (max_frames == 0) return out;

    // Frame 0: the return address at [rsp] is the caller of the paused site
    uint64_t ret = 0;
    if (rdr.read(rsp, &ret, 8) && ret != 0 && ret <= kUserMax) {
        frame_t f;
        f.ret_addr = ret;
        uint8_t buf[16];
        if (rdr.read(ret, buf, sizeof(buf))) {
            if (auto in = eng.decode(ret, buf, sizeof(buf))) f.snippet = in->text;
        }
        out.push_back(std::move(f));
        if (out.size() >= max_frames) return out;
    }

    // RBP-chain walk with sanity gates
    std::set<uint64_t> seen;
    uint64_t fp = rbp;
    for (size_t guard = 0; guard < max_frames * 4 + 32; ++guard) {
        if (fp == 0 || fp > kUserMax || !seen.insert(fp).second) break;
        uint64_t saved_rbp = 0, saved_ret = 0;
        if (!rdr.read(fp, &saved_rbp, 8)) break;
        if (!rdr.read(fp + 8, &saved_ret, 8)) break;

        const bool ok_chain =
            saved_rbp == 0 ||
            (saved_rbp > fp && saved_rbp <= kUserMax);
        if (!ok_chain) break;

        frame_t f;
        f.frame_ptr = fp;
        f.ret_addr  = saved_ret;
        uint8_t buf[16];
        if (saved_ret && saved_ret <= kUserMax && rdr.read(saved_ret, buf, sizeof(buf))) {
            if (auto in = eng.decode(saved_ret, buf, sizeof(buf)))
                f.snippet = in->text;
            else
                f.ret_addr = 0;   // not code: drop frame
        }
        if (f.ret_addr) {
            // Frame 0 already reported [rsp]; skip a duplicate
            if (!(out.size() == 1 && out[0].ret_addr == f.ret_addr &&
                  out[0].frame_ptr == 0))
                out.push_back(std::move(f));
        }
        if (saved_rbp == 0) break;
        fp = saved_rbp;
        if (out.size() >= max_frames) break;
    }

    // Scan fallback when the chain died early
    if (out.size() < 3) {
        constexpr size_t kScanBytes = 0x800;
        std::set<uint64_t> known;
        for (const auto& f : out) known.insert(f.ret_addr);

        for (size_t off = 8; off < kScanBytes && out.size() < max_frames; off += 8) {
            uint64_t cand = 0;
            if (!rdr.read(rsp + off, &cand, 8)) break;
            if (cand <= rsp || cand > kUserMax || known.count(cand)) continue;

            // Memory-query gate proxy: readable via our reader, decodes as
            // an instruction start, and sits above the current stack top
            // (a real return address points back into code)
            if (!plausible_code(eng, rdr, cand)) continue;

            bool dup = false;
            for (const auto& f : out)
                if (f.ret_addr == cand) { dup = true; break; }
            if (dup) continue;

            frame_t f;
            f.ret_addr = cand;
            f.scanned  = true;
            uint8_t buf[16];
            if (rdr.read(cand, buf, sizeof(buf))) {
                if (auto in = eng.decode(cand, buf, sizeof(buf))) f.snippet = in->text;
            }
            out.push_back(std::move(f));
        }
    }
    return out;
}

seh_result_t seh_chain(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t teb_addr) {
    seh_result_t res;
    if (teb_addr == 0) {
        res.note = "no TEB address available";
        return res;
    }

    // NT_TIB at TEB+0: ExceptionList (x86), plus ExpectedDfr / etc. On x64
    // the list must be empty (-1); walk it only if it isn't
    uint64_t head = 0;
    if (!rdr.read(teb_addr, &head, 8)) {
        res.note = "TEB read failed";
        return res;
    }

    constexpr uint64_t kSentinel = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull;
    std::set<uint64_t> seen;
    while (head != kSentinel && head != 0) {
        if (head > kUserMax || !seen.insert(head).second) {
            res.note = "chain stop reason: implausible or cyclic entry";
            break;
        }
        // _EXCEPTION_REGISTRATION_RECORD { Next; Handler; }
        uint64_t next = 0, handler = 0;
        if (!rdr.read(head, &next, 8) || !rdr.read(head + 8, &handler, 8)) {
            res.note = "chain stop reason: unreadable record";
            break;
        }
        seh_entry_t e;
        e.handler = handler;
        e.filter  = 0;
        e.frame   = head;
        res.chain.push_back(e);
        head = next;
        if (res.chain.size() >= 32) {
            res.note = "chain truncated at 32 entries";
            break;
        }
    }
    if (head == kSentinel)
        res.chain_empty_proven = res.chain.empty();

    // x64 framed-handler candidates: scan the stack for values that look
    // like code pointers (heuristic parity with the reference viewer)
    return res;
}

// ---- PE x64 unwind info ---------------------------------------------------

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kUnwFlagChainInfo = 0x4;
constexpr uint32_t kAllCodes = 0xFFFFFFFFu;   // apply every code (past the prologue)
constexpr uint32_t kMaxChainDepth = 8;

bool read_u16(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t addr, uint16_t& v) {
    return rdr.read(addr, &v, sizeof(v));
}

bool read_u32(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t addr, uint32_t& v) {
    return rdr.read(addr, &v, sizeof(v));
}

bool read_u64(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t addr, uint64_t& v) {
    return rdr.read(addr, &v, sizeof(v));
}

struct pe_dir_t {
    uint32_t pdata_rva = 0;
    uint32_t pdata_size = 0;
};

// exception directory (data directory 3) of the PE mapped at base
bool pe_exception_dir(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t base, pe_dir_t& out) {
    uint16_t mz = 0;
    if (!read_u16(rdr, base, mz) || mz != 0x5A4D) return false;
    uint32_t lfanew = 0;
    if (!read_u32(rdr, base + 0x3C, lfanew)) return false;
    uint32_t sig = 0;
    if (!read_u32(rdr, base + lfanew, sig) || sig != 0x00004550) return false;
    const uint64_t opt = base + lfanew + 4 + 20;
    uint16_t magic = 0;
    if (!read_u16(rdr, opt, magic) || magic != 0x20B) return false;   // PE32+
    uint32_t nrva = 0;
    if (!read_u32(rdr, opt + 108, nrva) || nrva <= 3) return false;
    const uint64_t dir = opt + 112 + 3 * 8;
    if (!read_u32(rdr, dir, out.pdata_rva) || !read_u32(rdr, dir + 4, out.pdata_size))
        return false;
    return out.pdata_rva != 0 && out.pdata_size >= 12;
}

struct runtime_function_t {
    uint32_t begin = 0;
    uint32_t end = 0;
    uint32_t unwind_rva = 0;
};

bool read_runtime_function(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t at, runtime_function_t& rf) {
    uint8_t buf[12];
    if (!rdr.read(at, buf, sizeof(buf))) return false;
    std::memcpy(&rf.begin, buf, 4);
    std::memcpy(&rf.end, buf + 4, 4);
    std::memcpy(&rf.unwind_rva, buf + 8, 4);
    return true;
}

// .pdata is sorted by BeginAddress: binary search the entry covering rva
bool find_runtime_function(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t base, const pe_dir_t& dir, uint32_t rva,
                           runtime_function_t& out) {
    size_t lo = 0, hi = dir.pdata_size / 12;
    while (lo < hi) {
        const size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        runtime_function_t rf;
        if (!read_runtime_function(rdr, base + dir.pdata_rva + mid * 12, rf)) return false;
        if (rva < rf.begin) hi = mid;
        else if (rva >= rf.end) lo = mid + 1;
        else { out = rf; return true; }
    }
    return false;
}

// unwind register numbering: 0 rax, 1 rcx, 2 rdx, 3 rbx, 4 rsp, 5 rbp,
// 6 rsi, 7 rdi, 8..15 r8..r15
struct uw_ctx_t {
    uint64_t reg[16]{};
    uint64_t rip = 0;
};

void load_ctx(const runtime::thread_context_t& c, uw_ctx_t& u) {
    u.reg[0] = c.rax; u.reg[1] = c.rcx; u.reg[2] = c.rdx; u.reg[3] = c.rbx;
    u.reg[4] = c.rsp; u.reg[5] = c.rbp; u.reg[6] = c.rsi; u.reg[7] = c.rdi;
    u.reg[8] = c.r8;  u.reg[9] = c.r9;  u.reg[10] = c.r10; u.reg[11] = c.r11;
    u.reg[12] = c.r12; u.reg[13] = c.r13; u.reg[14] = c.r14; u.reg[15] = c.r15;
    u.rip = c.rip;
}

// apply one UNWIND_INFO block; codes are ordered by decreasing code offset,
// so a forward walk is the reverse of the prologue (the RtlVirtualUnwind
// order). offset_in_func skips prologue ops that have not run yet.
bool apply_unwind_info(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t base, uint32_t unwind_rva, uw_ctx_t& u,
                       uint32_t offset_in_func, uint32_t depth) {
    if (depth > kMaxChainDepth) return false;
    const uint64_t info = base + unwind_rva;
    uint8_t hdr[4];
    if (!rdr.read(info, hdr, sizeof(hdr))) return false;
    const uint8_t flags = hdr[0] >> 3;
    const uint8_t count = hdr[2];
    const uint8_t frame_reg = hdr[3] & 0xF;
    const uint32_t frame_off = static_cast<uint32_t>(hdr[3] >> 4) * 16u;
    const uint64_t codes = info + 4;

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        uint16_t code = 0;
        if (!read_u16(rdr, codes + i * 2, code)) return false;
        const uint8_t off = static_cast<uint8_t>(code & 0xFF);
        const uint8_t op = static_cast<uint8_t>((code >> 8) & 0xF);
        const uint8_t op_info = static_cast<uint8_t>(code >> 12);
        if (offset_in_func != kAllCodes && off > offset_in_func) {
            // not executed yet, but its operand slots still occupy the array
            if (op == 1) i += op_info == 0 ? 1 : 2;
            else if (op == 4) i += 1;
            else if (op == 5) i += 2;
            else if (op == 8) i += 1;
            else if (op == 9) i += 2;
            continue;
        }
        switch (op) {
        case 0:   // push nonvolatile register
            if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4], u.reg[op_info])) return false;
            u.reg[4] += 8;
            break;
        case 1: { // alloc large
            uint32_t size = 0;
            if (op_info == 0) {
                uint16_t slots = 0;
                if (!read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 1) * 2, slots)) return false;
                size = static_cast<uint32_t>(slots) * 8u;
                i += 1;
            } else {
                uint16_t lo = 0, hi = 0;
                if (!read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 1) * 2, lo) ||
                    !read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 2) * 2, hi))
                    return false;
                size = static_cast<uint32_t>(lo) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(hi) << 16);
                i += 2;
            }
            u.reg[4] += size;
            break;
        }
        case 2:   // alloc small
            u.reg[4] += static_cast<uint32_t>(op_info) * 8u + 8u;
            break;
        case 3:   // set frame pointer
            if (frame_reg == 0 || frame_reg >= 16) return false;
            u.reg[4] = u.reg[frame_reg] - frame_off;
            break;
        case 4: { // save nonvolatile
            uint16_t slots = 0;
            if (!read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 1) * 2, slots)) return false;
            if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4] + static_cast<uint64_t>(slots) * 8u, u.reg[op_info]))
                return false;
            i += 1;
            u.reg[4] += 8;
            break;
        }
        case 5: { // save nonvolatile far
            uint16_t lo = 0, hi = 0;
            if (!read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 1) * 2, lo) ||
                !read_u16(rdr, codes + (i + 2) * 2, hi))
                return false;
            const uint32_t disp = static_cast<uint32_t>(lo) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(hi) << 16);
            if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4] + disp, u.reg[op_info])) return false;
            i += 2;
            u.reg[4] += 8;
            break;
        }
        case 8:   // save xmm128
            i += 1;
            u.reg[4] += 16;
            break;
        case 9:   // save xmm128 far
            i += 2;
            u.reg[4] += 16;
            break;
        case 10: {   // push machine frame
            if (op_info) u.reg[4] += 8;
            uint64_t new_rip = 0, new_rsp = 0;
            if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4], new_rip)) return false;
            if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4] + 24, new_rsp)) return false;
            u.rip = new_rip;
            u.reg[4] = new_rsp;
            break;
        }
        default:
            break;
        }
    }

    if (flags & kUnwFlagChainInfo) {
        // the chained RUNTIME_FUNCTION follows the codes, 4-byte aligned
        runtime_function_t chain;
        if (!read_runtime_function(rdr, codes + (((count + 1u) & ~1u) * 2u), chain))
            return false;
        return apply_unwind_info(rdr, base, chain.unwind_rva, u, kAllCodes, depth + 1);
    }
    return true;
}

// one frame: rip -> the caller's rip/rsp/regs
bool unwind_one(reader_t& rdr, const module_of_fn& module_of, uw_ctx_t& u) {
    module_span_t m;
    if (!module_of(u.rip, m)) return false;
    pe_dir_t dir;
    if (!pe_exception_dir(rdr, m.base, dir)) return false;
    const uint32_t rva = static_cast<uint32_t>(u.rip - m.base);
    runtime_function_t rf;
    if (!find_runtime_function(rdr, m.base, dir, rva, rf)) {
        // leaf function: the return address sits at rsp
        uint64_t ret = 0;
        if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4], ret)) return false;
        u.reg[4] += 8;
        u.rip = ret;
        return true;
    }
    if (!apply_unwind_info(rdr, m.base, rf.unwind_rva, u, rva - rf.begin, 0)) return false;
    uint64_t ret = 0;
    if (!read_u64(rdr, u.reg[4], ret)) return false;
    u.reg[4] += 8;
    u.rip = ret;
    return true;
}

} // namespace

bool pe_unwind(reader_t& rdr, const runtime::thread_context_t& ctx, size_t max_frames,
               const module_of_fn& module_of, std::vector<frame_t>& out, std::string* note) {
    out.clear();
    if (max_frames == 0) return false;
    uw_ctx_t u;
    load_ctx(ctx, u);

    // frame 0 is the paused site itself, the same shape rbp_frames returns
    frame_t first;
    first.ret_addr = ctx.rip;
    first.frame_ptr = ctx.rbp;
    out.push_back(first);

    std::set<uint64_t> seen;
    seen.insert(u.rip);
    std::string why = "no .pdata for the first frame";
    while (out.size() < max_frames && u.rip != 0) {
        if (!unwind_one(rdr, module_of, u)) {
            why = "unwind stopped at " + std::to_string(u.rip);
            break;
        }
        if (u.rip == 0) break;
        if (!seen.insert(u.rip).second) {
            why = "unwind cycle at " + std::to_string(u.rip);
            break;
        }
        frame_t f;
        f.ret_addr = u.rip;
        f.frame_ptr = u.reg[5];
        out.push_back(f);
    }
    if (note) *note = why;
    return out.size() > 1;   // only the paused site: no unwind info was usable
}

} // namespace slop::core::debugger::unwind
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/debugger/callstack.hpp
// pure unwinding and seh chain walking over a reader callback, rbp chain
// first with a stack scan fallback, no os calls so it tests against
// synthetic stacks

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/disasm/engine.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"

namespace slop::core::debugger::unwind {

struct reader_t {
    virtual ~reader_t() = default;
    virtual bool read(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) = 0;
};

struct frame_t {
    uint64_t    ret_addr  = 0;      // return address into the caller
    uint64_t    frame_ptr = 0;      // rbp of this frame (chain walk) or 0
    std::string snippet;            // disassembly at ret_addr (best effort)
    bool        scanned  = false;   // found by scan fallback, not rbp chain
};

// Walk up to max_frames frames starting from the given context
std::vector<frame_t> walk_stack(disasm::engine_t& eng, reader_t& rdr,
                                uint64_t rip, uint64_t rsp, uint64_t rbp,
                                size_t max_frames = 32);

// ---- PE x64 unwind info (.pdata) ------------------------------------------
// The local usermode backend is Windows x64: every non-leaf function carries a
// RUNTIME_FUNCTION in the module's .pdata, so the callstack does not need a
// frame pointer. The tables are read from target memory, no OS unwind helper.

struct module_span_t {
    uint64_t base = 0;
    uint64_t size = 0;
};

// true when addr belongs to a module (fills its load base and size)
using module_of_fn = std::function<bool(uint64_t addr, module_span_t& out)>;

// Frame 0 is ctx.rip itself (same shape as rbp_frames), then every caller
// resolved through RUNTIME_FUNCTION/UNWIND_INFO. Returns false when the first
// frame's module has no usable .pdata (caller falls back to walk_stack).
bool pe_unwind(reader_t& rdr, const runtime::thread_context_t& ctx, size_t max_frames,
               const module_of_fn& module_of, std::vector<frame_t>& out,
               std::string* note = nullptr);

struct seh_entry_t {
    uint64_t handler = 0;
    uint64_t filter  = 0;
    uint64_t frame   = 0;
};

struct seh_result_t {
    std::vector<seh_entry_t> chain;
    std::vector<uint64_t>    scan_candidates;   // framed-handler candidates
    bool chain_empty_proven = false;            // sentinel reached (x64 norm)
    std::string note;
};

// teb_addr is the threads teb base, the x64 exception list is normally
// the minus one sentinel, anything else gets walked
seh_result_t seh_chain(reader_t& rdr, uint64_t teb_addr);

} // namespace slop::core::debugger::unwind
```

`src/core/debugger/composite.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/debugger/composite.cpp

#include "core/debugger/composite.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace slop::core::debugger {

namespace {

namespace infra = slop::core::infra;

std::string io_text(const char* what, const runtime::io_result_t& io) {
    return std::string(what) + ": " + runtime::ps4::io_error_str(io.error);
}

int remaining_ms(int64_t deadline) {
    const int64_t left = deadline - infra::steady_ms();
    return left <= 0 ? 0 : static_cast<int>(left);
}

} // namespace

std::vector<frame_rec_t> rbp_frames(debug_target_t& t, const runtime::thread_context_t& ctx,
                                    size_t depth) {
    std::vector<frame_rec_t> out;
    if (depth == 0) return out;
    out.push_back({ctx.rip, ctx.rbp});
    uint64_t rbp = ctx.rbp;
    for (size_t i = 1; i < depth && rbp != 0; ++i) {
        uint64_t pair[2] = {0, 0};   // saved rbp, return address
        if (!t.read(rbp, pair, sizeof(pair))) break;
        out.push_back({pair[1], rbp});
        if (pair[0] == 0 || pair[0] <= rbp) break;   // 0 = top; the chain must ascend
        rbp = pair[0];
    }
    return out;
}

bool stop_at(const stop_event_t& ev, uint64_t addr) {
    return ev.ctx.rip == addr || ev.ctx.rip == addr + 1;
}

until_result_t run_until(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, int timeout_ms) {
    until_result_t r;
    if (!t.attached()) { r.error = "no debug session"; return r; }
    auto io = t.bp_arm(addr, r.index, r.reused);
    if (!io.ok) { r.error = io_text("cannot arm breakpoint", io); return r; }
    const int64_t deadline = infra::steady_ms() + std::max(timeout_ms, 0);
    // resume only a debuggee that is actually held: a running target needs no
    // resume, and resuming after the bp stop already landed would consume the
    // very stop we are waiting for (the event would still look like a hit)
    if (t.stopped()) {
        io = t.resume();
        if (!io.ok) {
            if (!r.reused) t.bp_disarm(addr);
            r.error = io_text("resume failed", io);
            return r;
        }
    }
    r.ok = true;
    for (;;) {
        stop_event_t ev;
        if (!t.wait_event(ev, remaining_ms(deadline))) break;
        if (stop_at(ev, addr)) { r.halted = true; r.ev = ev; break; }
        if (ev.reason == "exit") { r.ev = ev; break; }
        // a stop that is not ours (another breakpoint, a step, a signal):
        // let the debuggee go on toward addr
        ++r.skipped;
        if (!t.resume().ok) break;
    }
    if (!r.reused) t.bp_disarm(addr);
    return r;
}

find_write_result_t find_write(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, uint32_t len,
                               int timeout_ms, size_t depth) {
    find_write_result_t r;
    if (!t.attached()) { r.error = "no debug session"; return r; }
    if (len != 1 && len != 2 && len != 4 && len != 8) { r.error = "len must be 1, 2, 4 or 8"; return r; }
    auto io = t.wp_arm(addr, len, kWatchWrite, r.index, r.reused);
    if (!io.ok) { r.error = io_text("cannot arm watchpoint", io); return r; }
    if (t.stopped()) {
        io = t.resume();
        if (!io.ok) {
            if (!r.reused) t.wp_disarm(addr);
            r.error = io_text("resume failed", io);
            return r;
        }
    }
    r.ok = true;
    stop_event_t ev;
    if (t.wait_event(ev, std::max(timeout_ms, 0)) && ev.reason != "exit") {
        r.halted = true;
        r.ev = ev;
        r.frames = rbp_frames(t, ev.ctx, depth);
    }
    if (!r.reused) t.wp_disarm(addr);
    return r;
}

trace_calls_result_t trace_calls(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, size_t count, int timeout_ms) {
    trace_calls_result_t r;
    if (!t.attached()) { r.error = "no debug session"; return r; }
    auto io = t.bp_arm(addr, r.index, r.reused);
    if (!io.ok) { r.error = io_text("cannot arm breakpoint", io); return r; }
    r.ok = true;
    r.stop_reason = "count_reached";
    // the first wait needs a resume only when the debuggee is held; after any
    // consumed stop it is held again
    bool need_resume = t.stopped();
    while (r.hits.size() < count) {
        if (need_resume && !t.resume().ok) { r.stop_reason = "continue_failed"; break; }
        need_resume = true;
        // the per-hit timeout covers foreign stops resumed past on the way
        const int64_t deadline = infra::steady_ms() + std::max(timeout_ms, 0);
        bool got = false;
        for (;;) {
            stop_event_t ev;
            if (!t.wait_event(ev, remaining_ms(deadline))) break;
            if (ev.reason == "exit") { r.stop_reason = "process_exited"; break; }
            if (stop_at(ev, addr)) { r.hits.push_back(ev); got = true; break; }
            ++r.skipped;
            if (!t.resume().ok) { r.stop_reason = "continue_failed"; break; }
        }
        if (!got) {
            if (r.stop_reason == "count_reached") r.stop_reason = "timeout";
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!r.reused) t.bp_disarm(addr);
    return r;
}

trace_steps_result_t trace_steps(debug_target_t& t, uint32_t tid, size_t count, int timeout_ms) {
    trace_steps_result_t r;
    if (!t.attached()) { r.error = "no debug session"; return r; }
    r.ok = true;
    r.stop_reason = "count_reached";
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        if (!t.step(tid).ok) { r.stop_reason = "step_failed"; break; }
        stop_event_t ev;
        if (!t.wait_event(ev, std::max(timeout_ms, 0))) { r.stop_reason = "timeout"; break; }
        if (ev.reason == "exit") { r.stop_reason = "process_exited"; break; }
        step_rec_t s;
        s.tid = ev.tid;
        s.rip = ev.ctx.rip;
        if (t.read(s.rip, s.bytes, sizeof(s.bytes))) s.nbytes = sizeof(s.bytes);
        r.steps.push_back(s);
        if (tid == 0) tid = ev.tid;   // keep stepping the thread that stopped
    }
    return r;
}

} // namespace slop::core::debugger
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/debugger/composite.hpp
// One-call debugger workflows over any debug_target_t (PS4 console or the
// local Win32 debugger): run until an address, find the writer of an address,
// log every call to a function, and single-step trace a thread.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/debugger/debug_target.hpp"

namespace slop::core::debugger {

struct frame_rec_t {
    uint64_t ret_addr  = 0;
    uint64_t frame_ptr = 0;
};

// rbp chain from a stop context; frame 0 is rip itself
std::vector<frame_rec_t> rbp_frames(debug_target_t& t, const runtime::thread_context_t& ctx,
                                    size_t depth);

// does a breakpoint stop belong to addr? (rip at the breakpoint, or one past
// the int3 on payloads that report the trap address)
bool stop_at(const stop_event_t& ev, uint64_t addr);

struct until_result_t {
    bool         ok = false;        // false = could not even arm/resume (see error)
    std::string  error;
    bool         halted = false;    // stopped at addr before the timeout
    stop_event_t ev;
    uint32_t     index = 0;         // breakpoint slot used
    bool         reused = false;    // addr was already armed (slot left armed)
    uint32_t     skipped = 0;       // other stops resumed past while waiting
};
// arm a one-shot breakpoint at addr (unless one is already there), resume,
// wait for the stop at addr (other stops are resumed past), disarm
until_result_t run_until(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, int timeout_ms);

struct find_write_result_t {
    bool         ok = false;
    std::string  error;
    bool         halted = false;
    stop_event_t ev;
    uint32_t     index = 0;         // watchpoint slot used
    bool         reused = false;
    std::vector<frame_rec_t> frames;
};
// write watchpoint on [addr, addr+len), resume, wait, callstack of the writer
find_write_result_t find_write(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, uint32_t len,
                               int timeout_ms, size_t depth);

struct trace_calls_result_t {
    bool         ok = false;
    std::string  error;
    std::vector<stop_event_t> hits;
    std::string  stop_reason;       // count_reached | timeout | continue_failed
    uint32_t     index = 0;
    bool         reused = false;
    uint32_t     skipped = 0;
};
// breakpoint at addr, then resume+wait count times recording every hit (the
// debuggee stays stopped at the last hit)
trace_calls_result_t trace_calls(debug_target_t& t, uint64_t addr, size_t count, int timeout_ms);

struct step_rec_t {
    uint32_t tid = 0;
    uint64_t rip = 0;
    uint8_t  bytes[16]{};
    size_t   nbytes = 0;            // bytes read at rip (0 = unreadable)
};
struct trace_steps_result_t {
    bool         ok = false;
    std::string  error;
    std::vector<step_rec_t> steps;
    std::string  stop_reason;       // count_reached | timeout | step_failed
};
// single-step tid count times recording rip and the code bytes there
trace_steps_result_t trace_steps(debug_target_t& t, uint32_t tid, size_t count, int timeout_ms);

} // namespace slop::core::debugger
```

`src/core/debugger/debug_target.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/debugger/debug_target.hpp
// The small surface the composite debugger flows (run-until, find-writer,
// call tracing, step tracing) need, implemented by the PS4 console debugger
// (ps4debug-NG over the wire) and by the local Win32 debugger. Semantics
// follow the console: a stop event freezes the debuggee until resume() or
// step(); breakpoints are software, watchpoints are the DR0-DR3 slots.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"

namespace slop::core::debugger {

// watchpoint types (same values as ps4::kWp*)
constexpr uint32_t kWatchExec      = 0;
constexpr uint32_t kWatchWrite     = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kWatchReadWrite = 3;

struct stop_event_t {
    uint32_t    tid = 0;            // lwpid on the console, thread id locally
    int         signal = 0;         // 5 (SIGTRAP) for breakpoint/step/watch stops
    uint64_t    status = 0;         // raw wait4 status (PS4) / exception code (local)
    std::string reason;             // breakpoint | single_step | watchpoint | exception | signal | exit
    std::string thread;             // thread name when known
    runtime::thread_context_t ctx{};
    uint64_t    dr[16]{};           // debug registers at the stop when known (dr[6] = DR6)
};

class debug_target_t {
public:
    virtual ~debug_target_t() = default;

    virtual const char* kind() const noexcept = 0;   // "ps4" | "user"
    virtual bool attached() const = 0;

    // true while a stop event is holding the debuggee (run_until/trace_* must
    // only resume() from this state; a running target needs no resume)
    virtual bool stopped() const = 0;

    // arm a software breakpoint at addr; reuses the slot already armed there
    // (reused = true) so callers know whether they own the slot
    virtual runtime::io_result_t bp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t& index, bool& reused) = 0;
    virtual runtime::io_result_t bp_disarm(uint64_t addr) = 0;
    // arm a hardware watchpoint (len 1/2/4/8, type kWatch*)
    virtual runtime::io_result_t wp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t len, uint32_t type,
                                        uint32_t& index, bool& reused) = 0;
    virtual runtime::io_result_t wp_disarm(uint64_t addr) = 0;

    // let the stopped debuggee run / single-step one thread (0 = the thread
    // of the last stop)
    virtual runtime::io_result_t resume() = 0;
    virtual runtime::io_result_t step(uint32_t tid) = 0;

    // next stop event, false on timeout
    virtual bool wait_event(stop_event_t& out, int timeout_ms) = 0;

    // debuggee memory as the program sees it (software breakpoints hidden)
    virtual bool read(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) = 0;
};

} // namespace slop::core::debugger

```

`src/core/debugger/local_debugger.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/debugger/local_debugger.cpp
// Win32 debug loop on a dedicated thread (WaitForDebugEvent/ContinueDebugEvent
// must run on the thread that called DebugActiveProcess). Callers talk to it
// through a small command queue; stop events flow back through a queue.

#include "core/debugger/local_debugger.hpp"

#include <windows.h>

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/context.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstring>
#include <deque>
#include <future>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <set>
#include <thread>

namespace slop::core::debugger {

namespace {

namespace infra = slop::core::infra;
namespace ps4 = slop::core::runtime::ps4;
using runtime::io_result_t;

constexpr DWORD kWx86Breakpoint = 0x4000001F;   // STATUS_WX86_BREAKPOINT
constexpr DWORD kWx86SingleStep = 0x4000001E;   // STATUS_WX86_SINGLE_STEP
constexpr uint64_t kTrapFlag    = 0x100;
constexpr uint64_t kResumeFlag  = 0x10000;

io_result_t ok_result() { return io_result_t{true, 0, 0}; }
io_result_t err_result(uint32_t code) { return io_result_t{false, 0, code}; }
io_result_t last_error() { return io_result_t{false, 0, GetLastError()}; }

std::string win32_text(DWORD code) {
    return ps4::io_error_str(code);
}

} // namespace

struct local_debugger_t::impl_t {
    std::thread loop_thread; // the debug loop
    std::atomic<bool>     alive{false};    // attached and the loop runs
    std::atomic<bool>     quit{false};
    std::atomic<bool>     held{false};     // a stop event holds the process
    std::atomic<uint32_t> pid{0};
    std::atomic<HANDLE>   proc{nullptr};   // our own handle (not the event's)

    // commands executed on the debug thread
    std::mutex cmd_mu;
    std::condition_variable cmd_cv;
    std::deque<std::packaged_task<io_result_t()>> cmds;

    // stop events
    std::mutex ev_mu;
    std::condition_variable ev_cv;
    std::deque<stop_event_t> evq;

    // newest stop context, for callstacks taken while the process is held
    mutable std::mutex last_mu;
    runtime::thread_context_t last_ctx;
    uint32_t last_tid = 0;
    bool last_valid = false;

    // slots (read by callers, written on the debug thread)
    struct bp_t { bool used = false; uint64_t addr = 0; uint8_t orig = 0; };
    struct wp_t { bool used = false; uint64_t addr = 0; uint32_t len = 0, type = 0; };
    mutable std::mutex slot_mu;
    std::array<bp_t, kMaxBreakpoints> bps{};
    std::array<wp_t, kMaxWatchpoints> wps{};

    // ---- debug-thread-only state -------------------------------------
    std::map<DWORD, HANDLE> threads;          // event-owned handles, never closed by us
    DEBUG_EVENT pending{};                    // the held stop
    DWORD       pending_cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
    int         pending_bp = -1;              // slot the held stop sits on
    bool        pending_exec_watch = false;   // resume needs RF set
    bool        initial_bp_seen = false;
    std::map<DWORD, uint64_t> stepping_over;  // tid -> bp addr to re-insert after TF trap
    std::set<DWORD> user_step;                // tids with a requested single step

    ~impl_t() { stop_thread(); }

    // ---- queue plumbing ----------------------------------------------
    io_result_t post(std::function<io_result_t()> fn) {
        std::packaged_task<io_result_t()> task(std::move(fn));
        auto fut = task.get_future();
        {
            // alive flips under cmd_mu at teardown, so nothing is queued
            // after the loop dropped its queue
            std::lock_guard lk(cmd_mu);
            if (!alive.load()) return err_result(ps4::kErrNotAttached);
            cmds.push_back(std::move(task));
        }
        cmd_cv.notify_all();
        if (fut.wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(15)) != std::future_status::ready)
            return err_result(ps4::kErrTimeout);
        try {
            return fut.get();
        } catch (const std::future_error&) {
            return err_result(ps4::kErrNotAttached);   // dropped at teardown
        }
    }

    void run_cmds() {
        std::deque<std::packaged_task<io_result_t()>> batch;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(cmd_mu);
            batch.swap(cmds);
        }
        for (auto& t : batch) t();
    }

    // teardown: stop accepting commands; queued ones are dropped (their
    // waiters see a broken promise and report "not attached")
    void close_queue() {
        std::deque<std::packaged_task<io_result_t()>> batch;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(cmd_mu);
            alive = false;
            batch.swap(cmds);
        }
    }

    void push_event(stop_event_t ev) {
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(ev_mu);
            if (evq.size() >= 4096) evq.pop_front();
            evq.push_back(std::move(ev));
        }
        ev_cv.notify_all();
    }

    // ---- thread contexts ---------------------------------------------
    HANDLE thread_handle(DWORD tid) {
        auto it = threads.find(tid);
        return it == threads.end() ? nullptr : it->second;
    }

    static bool get_ctx(HANDLE worker, CONTEXT& c, DWORD flags) {
        std::memset(&c, 0, sizeof(c));
        c.ContextFlags = flags;
        return GetThreadContext(worker, &c) != FALSE;
    }

    stop_event_t make_event(DWORD tid, const char* reason, int signal, uint64_t code) {
        stop_event_t ev;
        ev.tid = tid;
        ev.reason = reason;
        ev.signal = signal;
        ev.status = code;
        if (HANDLE worker = thread_handle(tid)) {
            alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
            // CONTEXT_FULL and CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS share the CONTEXT_AMD64
            // base bit; the OR is intentional (adds the debug-register set).
            // NOLINTNEXTLINE(misc-redundant-expression)
            if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_FULL | CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS)) {
                runtime::context_from_win(ev.ctx, c);
                ev.dr[0] = c.Dr0; ev.dr[1] = c.Dr1; ev.dr[2] = c.Dr2; ev.dr[3] = c.Dr3;
                ev.dr[6] = c.Dr6; ev.dr[7] = c.Dr7;
                std::lock_guard lk(last_mu);
                last_ctx = ev.ctx;
                last_tid = tid;
                last_valid = true;
            }
        }
        return ev;
    }

    bool set_flags(HANDLE worker, uint64_t set_bits, uint64_t clear_bits) {
        alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
        if (!get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_CONTROL)) return false;
        c.EFlags = static_cast<DWORD>((c.EFlags | set_bits) & ~clear_bits);
        return SetThreadContext(worker, &c) != FALSE;
    }

    // DR0-DR3/DR7 of one thread from the watchpoint table
    void apply_drs(HANDLE worker) {
        std::array<wp_t, kMaxWatchpoints> w;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
            w = wps;
        }
        const DWORD sus = SuspendThread(worker);
        alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
        if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS)) {
            DWORD64 dr7 = 0;
            DWORD64* drs[4] = {&c.Dr0, &c.Dr1, &c.Dr2, &c.Dr3};
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxWatchpoints; ++i) {
                if (!w[i].used) { *drs[i] = 0; continue; }
                *drs[i] = w[i].addr;
                const DWORD64 rw = w[i].type == kWatchExec ? 0 : (w[i].type == kWatchWrite ? 1 : 3);
                const DWORD64 ln = w[i].type == kWatchExec ? 0
                                 : w[i].len == 1 ? 0 : w[i].len == 2 ? 1 : w[i].len == 8 ? 2 : 3;
                dr7 |= DWORD64{1} << (2 * i);
                dr7 |= rw << (16 + 4 * i);
                dr7 |= ln << (18 + 4 * i);
            }
            c.Dr7 = dr7;
            c.Dr6 = 0;
            SetThreadContext(worker, &c);
        }
        if (sus != static_cast<DWORD>(-1)) ResumeThread(worker);
    }

    void apply_drs_all() {
        for (const auto& [tid, worker] : threads) apply_drs(worker);
    }

    // ---- code patching -----------------------------------------------
    bool write_byte(uint64_t addr, uint8_t v) {
        HANDLE h = proc.load();
        SIZE_T n = 0;
        if (WriteProcessMemory(h, reinterpret_cast<LPVOID>(addr), &v, 1, &n) && n == 1) {
            FlushInstructionCache(h, reinterpret_cast<LPCVOID>(addr), 1);
            return true;
        }
        DWORD old = 0;
        if (!VirtualProtectEx(h, reinterpret_cast<LPVOID>(addr), 1, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &old))
            return false;
        const BOOL ok = WriteProcessMemory(h, reinterpret_cast<LPVOID>(addr), &v, 1, &n);
        DWORD tmp = 0;
        VirtualProtectEx(h, reinterpret_cast<LPVOID>(addr), 1, old, &tmp);
        FlushInstructionCache(h, reinterpret_cast<LPCVOID>(addr), 1);
        return ok && n == 1;
    }

    int bp_slot_at(uint64_t addr) const {
        std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxBreakpoints; ++i)
            if (bps[i].used && bps[i].addr == addr) return static_cast<int>(i);
        return -1;
    }

    // ---- event handling ----------------------------------------------
    // returns true when the event is held as a stop
    bool on_exception(const DEBUG_EVENT& de, DWORD& cont) {
        const auto& er = de.u.Exception.ExceptionRecord;
        const DWORD code = er.ExceptionCode;
        const uint64_t at = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(er.ExceptionAddress);
        const DWORD tid = de.dwThreadId;

        if (code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT || code == kWx86Breakpoint) {
            const int slot = bp_slot_at(at);
            if (slot >= 0) {
                // rewind past the int3 so the stop shows (and resumes at) addr
                if (HANDLE worker = thread_handle(tid)) {
                    alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
                    if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_CONTROL)) {
                        c.Rip = at;
                        SetThreadContext(worker, &c);
                    }
                }
                pending_bp = slot;
                pending_exec_watch = false;
                cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
                push_event(make_event(tid, "breakpoint", 5, code));
                return true;
            }
            if (!initial_bp_seen) {   // the attach break-in thread
                initial_bp_seen = true;
                cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
                return false;
            }
            cont = DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED;   // the program's own int3
            return false;
        }

        if (code == EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP || code == kWx86SingleStep) {
            bool ours = false, report = false, exec_watch = false;
            const char* reason = "single_step";
            if (auto it = stepping_over.find(tid); it != stepping_over.end()) {
                const uint64_t bp_addr = it->second;
                stepping_over.erase(it);
                if (bp_slot_at(bp_addr) >= 0) write_byte(bp_addr, 0xCC);   // re-insert
                ours = true;
            }
            if (user_step.erase(tid)) { ours = true; report = true; }
            if (HANDLE worker = thread_handle(tid)) {
                alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
                if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS) && (c.Dr6 & 0xF)) {
                    std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
                    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxWatchpoints; ++i) {
                        if (!(c.Dr6 & (DWORD64{1} << i)) || !wps[i].used) continue;
                        ours = true;
                        report = true;
                        reason = "watchpoint";
                        if (wps[i].type == kWatchExec) exec_watch = true;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (!ours) { cont = DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED; return false; }
            cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
            if (!report) return false;   // silent step-over finished
            stop_event_t ev = make_event(tid, reason, 5, code);
            if (HANDLE worker = thread_handle(tid)) {   // DR6 is sticky: clear it
                alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
                if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_DEBUG_REGISTERS)) { c.Dr6 = 0; SetThreadContext(worker, &c); }
            }
            pending_bp = -1;
            pending_exec_watch = exec_watch;
            push_event(std::move(ev));
            return true;
        }

        // the program's own exceptions: first chance goes to its handlers,
        // a second chance (about to crash) is reported and held
        cont = DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED;
        if (de.u.Exception.dwFirstChance) return false;
        pending_bp = -1;
        pending_exec_watch = false;
        push_event(make_event(tid, "exception", 0, code));
        return true;
    }

    // release the held stop; step_tid != 0 single-steps that thread
    io_result_t continue_held(DWORD step_tid) {
        if (!held.load()) return ok_result();
        if (step_tid && !thread_handle(step_tid)) return err_result(ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER);
        const DWORD tid = pending.dwThreadId;
        HANDLE worker = thread_handle(tid);
        if (pending_bp >= 0 && worker) {
            uint64_t addr = 0;
            uint8_t orig = 0;
            bool used = false;
            {
                std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
                used = bps[static_cast<size_t>(pending_bp)].used;
                addr = bps[static_cast<size_t>(pending_bp)].addr;
                orig = bps[static_cast<size_t>(pending_bp)].orig;
            }
            if (used) {
                // step over the breakpoint: original byte back, one TF trap,
                // then the int3 is re-inserted (see on_exception)
                write_byte(addr, orig);
                set_flags(worker, kTrapFlag, 0);
                stepping_over[tid] = addr;
            }
        }
        if (pending_exec_watch && worker) set_flags(worker, kResumeFlag, 0);   // skip the DR0-3 exec fault once
        if (step_tid) {
            HANDLE sth = thread_handle(step_tid);
            if (!sth) return err_result(ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER);
            set_flags(sth, kTrapFlag, 0);
            user_step.insert(step_tid);
        }
        if (!ContinueDebugEvent(pending.dwProcessId, tid, pending_cont)) return last_error();
        held = false;
        pending_bp = -1;
        pending_exec_watch = false;
        return ok_result();
    }

    // ---- teardown ------------------------------------------------------
    void unpatch_everything(std::set<uint64_t>& removed) {
        std::array<bp_t, kMaxBreakpoints> b;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
            b = bps;
            for (auto& x : bps) x = bp_t{};
            for (auto& x : wps) x = wp_t{};
        }
        for (const auto& x : b) {
            if (!x.used) continue;
            write_byte(x.addr, x.orig);
            removed.insert(x.addr);
        }
        for (const auto& [tid, worker] : threads) {
            apply_drs(worker);                     // all slots empty now
            set_flags(worker, 0, kTrapFlag);       // no step trap may outlive us
        }
        stepping_over.clear();
        user_step.clear();
    }

    // events already queued for breakpoints we just removed would leave a
    // thread one byte past the original instruction: rewind and swallow them
    void drain_after_unpatch(const std::set<uint64_t>& removed) {
        const int64_t until = infra::steady_ms() + 100;
        while (infra::steady_ms() < until) {
            DEBUG_EVENT de{};
            if (!WaitForDebugEvent(&de, 10)) continue;
            DWORD cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
            if (de.dwDebugEventCode == EXCEPTION_DEBUG_EVENT) {
                const auto& er = de.u.Exception.ExceptionRecord;
                const uint64_t at = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(er.ExceptionAddress);
                const DWORD code = er.ExceptionCode;
                if ((code == EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT || code == kWx86Breakpoint) && removed.count(at)) {
                    if (HANDLE worker = thread_handle(de.dwThreadId)) {
                        alignas(16) CONTEXT c;
                        if (get_ctx(worker, c, CONTEXT_CONTROL)) { c.Rip = at; SetThreadContext(worker, &c); }
                    }
                } else if (code == EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP || code == kWx86SingleStep) {
                    cont = DBG_CONTINUE;   // a leftover TF trap of ours
                } else {
                    cont = DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED;
                }
            } else if (de.dwDebugEventCode == CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT &&
                       de.u.CreateProcessInfo.hFile) {
                CloseHandle(de.u.CreateProcessInfo.hFile);
            } else if (de.dwDebugEventCode == LOAD_DLL_DEBUG_EVENT && de.u.LoadDll.hFile) {
                CloseHandle(de.u.LoadDll.hFile);
            } else if (de.dwDebugEventCode == CREATE_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT) {
                threads[de.dwThreadId] = de.u.CreateThread.hThread;
            } else if (de.dwDebugEventCode == EXIT_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT) {
                threads.erase(de.dwThreadId);
            }
            ContinueDebugEvent(de.dwProcessId, de.dwThreadId, cont);
        }
    }

    // ---- the loop ------------------------------------------------------
    void loop(uint32_t target, std::promise<std::string> ready) {
        if (!DebugActiveProcess(target)) {
            ready.set_value("DebugActiveProcess(" + std::to_string(target) + ") failed: " +
                            win32_text(GetLastError()));
            return;
        }
        DebugSetProcessKillOnExit(FALSE);
        bool ready_sent = false;
        bool exited = false;
        const int64_t attach_deadline = infra::steady_ms() + 10000;
        while (!quit.load()) {
            run_cmds();
            if (quit.load()) break;
            if (held.load()) {
                std::unique_lock lk(cmd_mu);
                cmd_cv.wait_for(lk, std::chrono::milliseconds(20),
                                [this] { return !cmds.empty() || quit.load(); });
                continue;
            }
            DEBUG_EVENT de{};
            if (!WaitForDebugEvent(&de, 20)) {
                if (!ready_sent && infra::steady_ms() > attach_deadline) {
                    // no break-in arrived: treat the attach as done anyway
                    initial_bp_seen = true;
                    alive = true;
                    ready.set_value("");
                    ready_sent = true;
                }
                continue;
            }
            DWORD cont = DBG_CONTINUE;
            bool hold = false;
            switch (de.dwDebugEventCode) {
            case CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT:
                threads[de.dwThreadId] = de.u.CreateProcessInfo.hThread;
                if (de.u.CreateProcessInfo.hFile) CloseHandle(de.u.CreateProcessInfo.hFile);
                break;
            case CREATE_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT:
                threads[de.dwThreadId] = de.u.CreateThread.hThread;
                apply_drs(de.u.CreateThread.hThread);
                break;
            case EXIT_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT:
                threads.erase(de.dwThreadId);
                stepping_over.erase(de.dwThreadId);
                user_step.erase(de.dwThreadId);
                break;
            case LOAD_DLL_DEBUG_EVENT:
                if (de.u.LoadDll.hFile) CloseHandle(de.u.LoadDll.hFile);
                break;
            case EXIT_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT: {
                stop_event_t ev;
                ev.tid = de.dwThreadId;
                ev.reason = "exit";
                ev.status = de.u.ExitProcess.dwExitCode;
                push_event(std::move(ev));
                exited = true;
                break;
            }
            case EXCEPTION_DEBUG_EVENT:
                hold = on_exception(de, cont);
                break;
            default:
                break;
            }
            if (hold) {
                pending = de;
                pending_cont = cont;
                held = true;
                continue;
            }
            ContinueDebugEvent(de.dwProcessId, de.dwThreadId, cont);
            if (!ready_sent && initial_bp_seen) {
                alive = true;
                ready.set_value("");
                ready_sent = true;
            }
            if (exited) break;
        }

        // teardown on the debug thread; no new commands from here on
        close_queue();
        if (!exited) {
            std::set<uint64_t> removed;
            unpatch_everything(removed);
            if (held.load()) {
                ContinueDebugEvent(pending.dwProcessId, pending.dwThreadId,
                                   pending_cont == DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED ? DBG_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
                                                                             : DBG_CONTINUE);
                held = false;
            }
            drain_after_unpatch(removed);
            DebugActiveProcessStop(target);
        }
        held = false;
        if (!ready_sent) ready.set_value(exited ? "process exited during attach" : "attach aborted");
        threads.clear();
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(slot_mu);
            for (auto& x : bps) x = bp_t{};
            for (auto& x : wps) x = wp_t{};
        }
        ev_cv.notify_all();
    }

    void stop_thread() {
        quit = true;
        cmd_cv.notify_all();
        if (loop_thread.joinable()) loop_thread.join();
        if (HANDLE h = proc.exchange(nullptr)) CloseHandle(h);
        pid = 0;
    }
};

local_debugger_t::local_debugger_t() : m_(std::make_unique<impl_t>()) {}

local_debugger_t::~local_debugger_t() {
    detach();
}

bool local_debugger_t::attach(uint32_t pid, std::string& err) {
    if (attached()) {
        if (m_->pid.load() == pid) return true;
        detach();
    }
    m_->stop_thread();   // a previous loop that ended on its own (exit)
    m_->quit = false;
    m_->held = false;
    m_->initial_bp_seen = false;
    m_->pending_bp = -1;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(m_->ev_mu);
        m_->evq.clear();
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(m_->last_mu);
        m_->last_valid = false;
        m_->last_tid = 0;
    }
    HANDLE h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION |
                           PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, FALSE, pid);
    if (!h) {
        err = "OpenProcess(" + std::to_string(pid) + ") failed: " + win32_text(GetLastError());
        return false;
    }
    m_->proc = h;
    std::promise<std::string> ready;
    auto fut = ready.get_future();
    m_->loop_thread = std::thread([this, pid, p = std::move(ready)]() mutable { m_->loop(pid, std::move(p)); });
    if (fut.wait_for(std::chrono::seconds(15)) != std::future_status::ready) {
        err = "attach timed out";
        m_->stop_thread();
        return false;
    }
    err = fut.get();
    if (!err.empty()) {
        m_->stop_thread();
        return false;
    }
    m_->pid = pid;
    return true;
}

void local_debugger_t::detach() {
    m_->stop_thread();
    std::lock_guard lk(m_->ev_mu);
    m_->evq.clear();
}

uint32_t local_debugger_t::pid() const noexcept {
    return attached() ? m_->pid.load() : 0;
}

bool local_debugger_t::stopped() const noexcept {
    return m_->held.load();
}

bool local_debugger_t::last_stop_context(uint32_t tid, runtime::thread_context_t& out) const {
    std::lock_guard lk(m_->last_mu);
    if (!m_->last_valid || (tid != 0 && tid != m_->last_tid)) return false;
    out = m_->last_ctx;
    return true;
}

bool local_debugger_t::attached() const {
    return m_->alive.load();
}

std::vector<local_debugger_t::slot_t> local_debugger_t::breakpoints() const {
    std::lock_guard lk(m_->slot_mu);
    std::vector<slot_t> out;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxBreakpoints; ++i)
        if (m_->bps[i].used) out.push_back({i, m_->bps[i].addr, 0, 0});
    return out;
}

std::vector<local_debugger_t::slot_t> local_debugger_t::watchpoints() const {
    std::lock_guard lk(m_->slot_mu);
    std::vector<slot_t> out;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxWatchpoints; ++i)
        if (m_->wps[i].used) out.push_back({i, m_->wps[i].addr, m_->wps[i].len, m_->wps[i].type});
    return out;
}

// the debug-thread lambdas hand the slot back in io_result_t.bytes (index,
// bit 8 = reused) so nothing on the caller's stack is captured by reference
constexpr size_t kReusedBit = 0x100;

io_result_t local_debugger_t::bp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t& index, bool& reused) {
    reused = false;
    if (addr == 0) return err_result(ps4::kErrBadArg);
    io_result_t r = m_->post([this, addr]() -> io_result_t {
        auto& m = *m_;
        int free_slot = -1;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxBreakpoints; ++i) {
                if (m.bps[i].used && m.bps[i].addr == addr) return io_result_t{true, i | kReusedBit, 0};
                if (!m.bps[i].used && free_slot < 0) free_slot = static_cast<int>(i);
            }
        }
        if (free_slot < 0) return err_result(ps4::kErrNoSlot);
        uint8_t orig = 0;
        SIZE_T n = 0;
        if (!ReadProcessMemory(m.proc.load(), reinterpret_cast<LPCVOID>(addr), &orig, 1, &n) || n != 1)
            return last_error();
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            m.bps[static_cast<size_t>(free_slot)] = impl_t::bp_t{true, addr, orig};
        }
        if (!m.write_byte(addr, 0xCC)) {
            const DWORD e = GetLastError();
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            m.bps[static_cast<size_t>(free_slot)] = impl_t::bp_t{};
            return err_result(e);
        }
        return io_result_t{true, static_cast<size_t>(free_slot), 0};
    });
    if (r.ok) {
        index  = static_cast<uint32_t>(r.bytes & 0xFF);
        reused = (r.bytes & kReusedBit) != 0;
        r.bytes = 0;
    }
    return r;
}

io_result_t local_debugger_t::bp_disarm(uint64_t addr) {
    return m_->post([this, addr]() -> io_result_t {
        auto& m = *m_;
        impl_t::bp_t rec{};
        int slot = -1;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxBreakpoints; ++i)
                if (m.bps[i].used && m.bps[i].addr == addr) { slot = static_cast<int>(i); rec = m.bps[i]; break; }
            if (slot < 0) return err_result(ps4::kErrNotArmed);
            m.bps[static_cast<size_t>(slot)] = impl_t::bp_t{};
        }
        if (m.pending_bp == slot) m.pending_bp = -1;   // the held thread already sits on addr
        if (!m.write_byte(rec.addr, rec.orig)) return last_error();
        return ok_result();
    });
}

io_result_t local_debugger_t::wp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t len, uint32_t type,
                                     uint32_t& index, bool& reused) {
    reused = false;
    if (len != 1 && len != 2 && len != 4 && len != 8) return err_result(ps4::kErrBadArg);
    if (type != kWatchExec && type != kWatchWrite && type != kWatchReadWrite)
        return err_result(ps4::kErrBadArg);
    if (type != kWatchExec && (addr % len) != 0) return err_result(ps4::kErrBadArg);   // DR alignment
    io_result_t r = m_->post([this, addr, len, type]() -> io_result_t {
        auto& m = *m_;
        size_t out = 0;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            int slot = -1;
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxWatchpoints; ++i)
                if (m.wps[i].used && m.wps[i].addr == addr) { slot = static_cast<int>(i); out |= kReusedBit; break; }
            if (slot < 0)
                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kMaxWatchpoints; ++i)
                    if (!m.wps[i].used) { slot = static_cast<int>(i); break; }
            if (slot < 0) return err_result(ps4::kErrNoSlot);
            m.wps[static_cast<size_t>(slot)] = impl_t::wp_t{true, addr, len, type};
            out |= static_cast<size_t>(slot);
        }
        m.apply_drs_all();
        return io_result_t{true, out, 0};
    });
    if (r.ok) {
        index  = static_cast<uint32_t>(r.bytes & 0xFF);
        reused = (r.bytes & kReusedBit) != 0;
        r.bytes = 0;
    }
    return r;
}

io_result_t local_debugger_t::wp_disarm(uint64_t addr) {
    return m_->post([this, addr]() -> io_result_t {
        auto& m = *m_;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(m.slot_mu);
            bool found = false;
            for (auto& w : m.wps)
                if (w.used && w.addr == addr) { w = impl_t::wp_t{}; found = true; break; }
            if (!found) return err_result(ps4::kErrNotArmed);
        }
        m.apply_drs_all();
        return ok_result();
    });
}

io_result_t local_debugger_t::resume() {
    return m_->post([this]() { return m_->continue_held(0); });
}

io_result_t local_debugger_t::step(uint32_t tid) {
    return m_->post([this, tid]() -> io_result_t {
        auto& m = *m_;
        if (!m.held.load())
            return err_result(ERROR_INVALID_STATE);   // stepping needs a stopped debuggee
        const DWORD t = tid ? tid : m.pending.dwThreadId;
        return m.continue_held(t);
    });
}

bool local_debugger_t::wait_event(stop_event_t& out, int timeout_ms) {
    std::unique_lock lk(m_->ev_mu);
    if (m_->evq.empty())
        m_->ev_cv.wait_for(lk, std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms > 0 ? timeout_ms : 0),
                           [this] { return !m_->evq.empty(); });
    if (m_->evq.empty()) return false;
    out = std::move(m_->evq.front());
    m_->evq.pop_front();
    return true;
}

bool local_debugger_t::read(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) {
    HANDLE h = m_->proc.load();
    if (!h || len == 0) return false;
    SIZE_T n = 0;
    if (!ReadProcessMemory(h, reinterpret_cast<LPCVOID>(addr), dst, len, &n) || n != len)
        return false;
    // show the program's bytes, not our int3s
    std::lock_guard lk(m_->slot_mu);
    auto* out = static_cast<uint8_t*>(dst);
    for (const auto& b : m_->bps)
        if (b.used && b.addr >= addr && b.addr < addr + len) out[b.addr - addr] = b.orig;
    return true;
}

} // namespace slop::core::debugger
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/debugger/local_debugger.hpp
// Win32 debugger for the user-mode backend (the internal test lab): one
// debuggee at a time, software int3 breakpoints with transparent step-over,
// DR0-DR3 hardware watchpoints on every thread, single-step. It mirrors the
// console debugger's stop semantics (a stop freezes the process until
// resume()/step()), so the composite flows run unchanged on both.

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/debugger/debug_target.hpp"

namespace slop::core::debugger {

class local_debugger_t final : public debug_target_t {
public:
    local_debugger_t();
    ~local_debugger_t() override;   // detaches, the debuggee keeps running

    local_debugger_t(const local_debugger_t&) = delete;
    local_debugger_t& operator=(const local_debugger_t&) = delete;

    // DebugActiveProcess on a dedicated debug thread; returns once the
    // attach break-in has been consumed and the process runs again
    bool     attach(uint32_t pid, std::string& err);
    // remove every breakpoint/watchpoint, release a held stop, stop debugging
    void     detach();
    uint32_t pid() const noexcept;
    bool     stopped() const noexcept;   // a stop event is holding the process

    // register context of the newest stop (tid 0 = any thread); false when no
    // stop was seen yet. Used by the callstack (.pdata unwind) path.
    bool     last_stop_context(uint32_t tid, runtime::thread_context_t& out) const;

    static constexpr uint32_t kMaxBreakpoints = 30;
    static constexpr uint32_t kMaxWatchpoints = 4;
    struct slot_t {
        uint32_t index = 0;
        uint64_t addr  = 0;
        uint32_t len   = 0;
        uint32_t type  = 0;
    };
    std::vector<slot_t> breakpoints() const;
    std::vector<slot_t> watchpoints() const;

    // debug_target_t
    const char* kind() const noexcept override { return "user"; }
    bool attached() const override;
    runtime::io_result_t bp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t& index, bool& reused) override;
    runtime::io_result_t bp_disarm(uint64_t addr) override;
    runtime::io_result_t wp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t len, uint32_t type,
                                uint32_t& index, bool& reused) override;
    runtime::io_result_t wp_disarm(uint64_t addr) override;
    runtime::io_result_t resume() override;
    runtime::io_result_t step(uint32_t tid) override;
    bool wait_event(stop_event_t& out, int timeout_ms) override;
    bool read(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) override;

private:
    struct impl_t;
    std::unique_ptr<impl_t> m_;
};

} // namespace slop::core::debugger
```

```cpp
// records, DR0-DR3). Nothing here pretends to debug: attach() reports that the

// backends. A ptrace implementation is the natural follow-up.

    "the local debugger is a Win32 debug-API feature; use a console backend on this platform";

    return r;

    return false;
```

`src/core/debugger/ps4_debug_target.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/debugger/ps4_debug_target.cpp

#include "core/debugger/ps4_debug_target.hpp"

#include "core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp"

#include <cstring>

namespace slop::core::debugger {

stop_event_t ps4_debug_target_t::from_ps4(const runtime::ps4_event_t& e) {
    stop_event_t s;
    s.tid    = e.lwpid;
    s.signal = e.signal;
    s.status = e.status;
    s.thread = e.thread_name;
    s.ctx    = e.ctx;
    std::memcpy(s.dr, e.dr, sizeof(s.dr));
    switch (e.signal) {
    case 5:  s.reason = "breakpoint"; break;   // SIGTRAP: bp, step or DR trap
    case 9:  s.reason = "exit";       break;   // SIGKILL tears the session down
    default: s.reason = "signal";     break;
    }
    // DR6 bits 0-3 name the hardware slot that fired, BS (bit 14) a step
    if (e.signal == 5) {
        if (e.dr[6] & (1ull << 14)) s.reason = "single_step";
        else if (e.dr[6] & 0xF)     s.reason = "watchpoint";
    }
    return s;
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::bp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t& index, bool& reused) {
    return p_.ps4_bp_arm(addr, runtime::backend_ps4_t::kAutoSlot, index, &reused);
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::bp_disarm(uint64_t addr) {
    return p_.ps4_bp_disarm_addr(addr);
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::wp_arm(uint64_t addr, uint32_t len, uint32_t type,
                                                uint32_t& index, bool& reused) {
    return p_.ps4_wp_arm(addr, len, type, runtime::backend_ps4_t::kAutoSlot, index, &reused);
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::wp_disarm(uint64_t addr) {
    return p_.ps4_wp_disarm_addr(addr);
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::resume() {
    return p_.ps4_continue(runtime::ps4::kStopResume);
}

runtime::io_result_t ps4_debug_target_t::step(uint32_t tid) {
    return p_.ps4_step(tid);
}

bool ps4_debug_target_t::wait_event(stop_event_t& out, int timeout_ms) {
    runtime::ps4_event_t e{};
    if (!p_.ps4_wait_event(e, timeout_ms)) return false;
    out = from_ps4(e);
    return true;
}

bool ps4_debug_target_t::read(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) {
    if (!s_ || !s_->valid()) return false;
    const auto io = s_->read(static_cast<uintptr_t>(addr), dst, len);
    return io.ok && io.bytes == len;
}

} // namespace slop::core::debugger
```
