```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/diag.hpp
// little tagged log ring the engines push into

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstddef>
#include <limits>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::infra::diag {

enum class level_t : uint8_t { trace = 0, info, warn, error };

struct entry_t {
    int64_t     timestamp_ms = 0;
    level_t     level        = level_t::info;
    std::string tag;         // "boot", "scanner", "attach", "pointer", etc
    std::string message;
};

void init();
void shutdown();

void log(level_t level, std::string_view tag, std::string_view message);

inline void trace(std::string_view tag, std::string_view msg) { log(level_t::trace, tag, msg); }
inline void info (std::string_view tag, std::string_view msg) { log(level_t::info,  tag, msg); }
inline void warn (std::string_view tag, std::string_view msg) { log(level_t::warn,  tag, msg); }
inline void error(std::string_view tag, std::string_view msg) { log(level_t::error, tag, msg); }

// snapshot of everything newer than the given revision
struct snapshot_t {
    std::vector<entry_t> entries;
    uint64_t             revision = 0;
};
// Limit selects the newest entries, without copying older discarded messages.
snapshot_t snapshot(uint64_t since_revision = 0,
                    size_t limit = std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max());

uint64_t revision() noexcept;

} // namespace slop::core::infra::diag
```

`src/core/infra/event_bus.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/infra/event_bus.cpp

#include "core/infra/event_bus.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"

#include <atomic>
#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <deque>
#include <mutex>
#include <unordered_map>

namespace slop::core::infra::event_bus {

namespace {

using json = nlohmann::json;

constexpr size_t kMaxOutput      = 4096;   // lines retained for replay
constexpr size_t kMaxQueueFrames = 512;    // per-subscriber backlog

std::mutex                  g_out_mu;
std::deque<output_line_t>   g_out;
uint64_t                    g_out_seq = 0;

std::atomic<bool>           g_open{true};

std::mutex                                   g_last_mu;
std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string> g_last;   // type -> last payload

// frames are shared so a publish is one allocation no matter how many listeners
using frame_t = std::shared_ptr<const std::string>;

} // namespace

struct subscriber_t::impl_t {
    std::mutex              mu;
    std::condition_variable cv;
    std::deque<frame_t>     q;
    uint64_t                dropped = 0;
    bool                    closed  = false;

    void push(const frame_t& f) {
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(mu);
            if (closed) return;
            if (q.size() >= kMaxQueueFrames) {
                q.pop_front();     // drop oldest: fresh state beats stale
                ++dropped;
            }
            q.push_back(f);
        }
        cv.notify_one();
    }

    void close() {
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(mu);
            closed = true;
        }
        cv.notify_all();
    }
};

namespace {

std::mutex                                          g_sub_mu;
std::vector<std::weak_ptr<subscriber_t::impl_t>>    g_subs;

// one sse frame, bytes can be junk so bad utf8 gets swapped not thrown
frame_t make_frame(std::string_view type, std::string_view encoded) {
    std::string s;
    s.reserve(16 + type.size() + encoded.size());
    s += "event: ";
    s.append(type.data(), type.size());
    s += "\ndata: ";
    s += encoded;
    s += "\n\n";
    return std::make_shared<const std::string>(std::move(s));
}

void fan_out(const frame_t& f) {
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<subscriber_t::impl_t>> live;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
        live.reserve(g_subs.size());
        for (auto it = g_subs.begin(); it != g_subs.end();) {
            if (auto sp = it->lock()) {
                live.push_back(std::move(sp));
                ++it;
            } else {
                it = g_subs.erase(it);   // reap dead subscribers lazily
            }
        }
    }
    // push outside the registry lock so publishes never stack up
    for (const auto& sp : live) sp->push(f);
}

} // namespace

// app output ring

void output(std::string_view line) {
    output_line_t rec;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
        rec.seq  = ++g_out_seq;
        rec.ms   = wall_ms();
        rec.text.assign(line);
        if (g_out.size() >= kMaxOutput) g_out.pop_front();
        g_out.push_back(rec);
    }
    publish("output", json{{"seq", rec.seq}, {"ms", rec.ms}, {"text", rec.text}});
}

std::vector<output_line_t> output_since(uint64_t since) {
    std::vector<output_line_t> out;
    std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
    const auto first = std::upper_bound(g_out.begin(), g_out.end(), since,
        [](uint64_t seq, const output_line_t& line) { return seq < line.seq; });
    out.assign(first, g_out.end());
    return out;
}

uint64_t output_revision() noexcept {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
    return g_out_seq;
}

void output_clear() {
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
        g_out.clear();
    }
    publish("output.cleared", json::object());
}

void output_visit(const std::function<void(const output_line_t&)>& fn) {
    if (!fn) return;
    std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
    for (const auto& l : g_out) fn(l);
}

// event fan out

void publish(std::string_view type, const json& data) {
    if (!g_open.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
        if (g_subs.empty()) return;    // nobody listening: skip serialization
    }
    try {
        fan_out(make_frame(type, data.dump(-1, ' ', false, json::error_handler_t::replace)));
    } catch (...) {
        // a publish must never take down whoever called it
    }
}

void publish_changed(std::string_view type, const json& data) {
    if (!g_open.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return;
    std::string encoded;
    try {
        encoded = data.dump(-1, ' ', false, json::error_handler_t::replace);
    } catch (...) {
        return;
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_last_mu);
        auto [it, inserted] = g_last.try_emplace(std::string(type), encoded);
        if (!inserted) {
            if (it->second == encoded) return;   // unchanged: stay silent
            it->second = encoded;
        }
    }
    try {
        // Reuse the serialization used for change detection.
        std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
        if (g_subs.empty()) return;
    } catch (...) { return; }
    try { fan_out(make_frame(type, encoded)); } catch (...) {}
}

// subscriber

subscriber_t::subscriber_t(std::shared_ptr<impl_t> impl) : impl_(std::move(impl)) {}

subscriber_t::~subscriber_t() {
    if (impl_) impl_->close();
}

bool subscriber_t::wait(std::string& out, uint32_t timeout_ms) {
    out.clear();
    if (!impl_) return false;

    std::deque<frame_t> batch;
    {
        std::unique_lock lk(impl_->mu);
        if (impl_->q.empty() && !impl_->closed) {
            impl_->cv.wait_for(lk, std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms),
                               [this] { return !impl_->q.empty() || impl_->closed; });
        }
        batch.swap(impl_->q);
        if (batch.empty() && impl_->closed) return false;
    }
    // squash the backlog into one write, way cheaper than a send per frame
    size_t total = 0;
    for (const auto& f : batch) total += f->size();
    out.reserve(total);
    for (const auto& f : batch) out += *f;
    return true;
}

uint64_t subscriber_t::dropped() const noexcept {
    if (!impl_) return 0;
    std::lock_guard lk(impl_->mu);
    return impl_->dropped;
}

std::shared_ptr<subscriber_t> subscribe() {
    auto impl = std::make_shared<subscriber_t::impl_t>();
    if (!g_open.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) impl->closed = true;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
        g_subs.emplace_back(impl);
    }
    return std::make_shared<subscriber_t>(std::move(impl));
}

size_t subscriber_count() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
    size_t n = 0;
    for (const auto& w : g_subs)
        if (!w.expired()) ++n;
    return n;
}

void shutdown() {
    g_open.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<subscriber_t::impl_t>> live;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_sub_mu);
        for (const auto& w : g_subs)
            if (auto sp = w.lock()) live.push_back(std::move(sp));
        g_subs.clear();
    }
    for (const auto& sp : live) sp->close();
}

void reset() {
    shutdown();
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_out_mu);
        g_out.clear();
        g_out_seq = 0;
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_last_mu);
        g_last.clear();
    }
    g_open.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
}

} // namespace slop::core::infra::event_bus

```

`src/core/infra/event_bus.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/event_bus.hpp
// event hub for the front end plus the app output ring
// the ring keeps numbered lines so a late connection can catch up and
// the fan out pushes frames to everyone without waiting on slow readers

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

namespace slop::core::infra::event_bus {

// app output ring

struct output_line_t {
    uint64_t    seq = 0;   // monotonic, never reused
    int64_t     ms  = 0;   // wall clock at append
    std::string text;
};

// one output line, also goes out as an event
void output(std::string_view line);

// everything after the given seq, 0 for the whole ring
std::vector<output_line_t> output_since(uint64_t since);

// newest seq so far, 0 when empty
uint64_t output_revision() noexcept;

void output_clear();

// zero copy walk of the ring, keep it short and never re enter
void output_visit(const std::function<void(const output_line_t&)>& fn);

// event fan out

// serialize once, queue everywhere, never blocks
void publish(std::string_view type, const nlohmann::json& data);

// only sends when the payload actually changed so an idle engine stays quiet
void publish_changed(std::string_view type, const nlohmann::json& data);

class subscriber_t {
public:
    ~subscriber_t();

    subscriber_t(const subscriber_t&)            = delete;
    subscriber_t& operator=(const subscriber_t&) = delete;

    // drain queued frames, false once the bus is dead, empty means timeout
    bool wait(std::string& out, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    // frames dropped when the queue was full
    uint64_t dropped() const noexcept;

    struct impl_t;
    explicit subscriber_t(std::shared_ptr<impl_t> impl);

private:
    std::shared_ptr<impl_t> impl_;
};

std::shared_ptr<subscriber_t> subscribe();

size_t subscriber_count();

// wake everyone and close up shop
void shutdown();

// reset everything so tests can reuse the bus
void reset();

} // namespace slop::core::infra::event_bus
```

`src/core/infra/jobs.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/limits.hpp"
#include "core/infra/published.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::infra {

// job internals

struct job_context_t::impl_t {
    uint64_t           id = 0;
    cancel_source_t    cancel_src;
    cancel_token_t     tok;
    std::atomic<float> progress{-1.0f};
    std::mutex         mu;
    std::string        stage;
    std::string        error;
    job_state_t        state = job_state_t::queued;
    int64_t            started_ms  = 0;
    int64_t            finished_ms = 0;
    std::string        label;
    std::string        owner;
    bool               cancellable = true;
    std::thread        thread;
    std::atomic<bool>  exited{false};          // the thread body returned, join is instant
    bool               joined = false;         // guarded by jobs g_mu
    bool               join_claimed = false;   // guarded by jobs g_mu, one joiner only

    impl_t() : tok(cancel_src.token()) {}

    // A joinable std::thread destroyed without join/detach calls std::terminate.
    // A job context can outlive any explicit reap - e.g. g_jobs is torn down at
    // process exit when jobs::shutdown() was never called - so settle the thread
    // here. Finished bodies join instantly; a still-running one (or self, when
    // the body's own captured ref is last) is detached, matching shutdown().
    ~impl_t() {
        if (!thread.joinable()) return;
        if (thread.get_id() == std::this_thread::get_id()) thread.detach();
        else if (exited.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) thread.join();
        else thread.detach();
    }
};

const cancel_token_t& job_context_t::cancel() const noexcept { return impl_->tok; }
bool job_context_t::cancelled() const noexcept { return impl_->tok.cancelled(); }
uint64_t job_context_t::id() const noexcept { return impl_->id; }

void job_context_t::set_stage(std::string s) {
    std::lock_guard lk(impl_->mu);
    impl_->stage = std::move(s);
}

void job_context_t::set_progress(float p) {
    impl_->progress.store(p, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

void job_context_t::set_progress(uint64_t done, uint64_t total) {
    if (total == 0) return;
    set_progress(static_cast<float>(done) / static_cast<float>(total));
}

void job_context_t::fail(std::string message) {
    std::lock_guard lk(impl_->mu);
    impl_->error = std::move(message);
    impl_->state = job_state_t::failed;
}

// the jobs namespace

namespace jobs {

namespace {

std::mutex                                       g_mu;
std::vector<std::shared_ptr<job_context_t::impl_t>> g_jobs;
std::atomic<uint64_t>                            g_next_id{1};
published_t<jobs_view_t>                         g_published;
std::atomic<bool>                                g_shutting_down{false};

void rebuild_snapshot() {
    auto view = std::make_shared<jobs_view_t>();
    view->reserve(g_jobs.size());
    for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
        job_snapshot_t s;
        s.id          = j->id;
        s.label       = j->label;
        s.owner       = j->owner;
        s.cancellable = j->cancellable;
        s.progress    = j->progress.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        s.started_ms  = j->started_ms;
        s.finished_ms = j->finished_ms;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(j->mu);
            s.stage = j->stage;
            s.error = j->error;
            s.state = j->state;
        }
        view->push_back(std::move(s));
    }
    g_published.publish(std::move(view));
}

} // namespace

uint64_t submit(job_desc_t d) {
    if (g_shutting_down.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return 0;

    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    // count live jobs
    size_t live = 0;
    for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
        std::lock_guard jlk(j->mu);
        if (j->state == job_state_t::queued || j->state == job_state_t::running)
            ++live;
    }
    if (live >= limits::max_live_jobs) return 0;

    auto impl        = std::make_shared<job_context_t::impl_t>();
    impl->id         = g_next_id.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    impl->label      = std::move(d.label);
    impl->owner      = std::move(d.owner);
    impl->cancellable = d.cancellable;

    const uint64_t job_id = impl->id;
    auto body = std::move(d.body);

    impl->thread = std::thread([impl, body = std::move(body)]() mutable {
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(impl->mu);
            impl->state      = job_state_t::running;
            impl->started_ms = steady_ms();
        }
        job_context_t ctx(impl.get());
        body(ctx);
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(impl->mu);
            if (impl->state == job_state_t::running) {
                impl->state = impl->tok.cancelled()
                    ? job_state_t::cancelled
                    : job_state_t::succeeded;
            }
            impl->finished_ms = steady_ms();
        }
        impl->exited.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    });

    g_jobs.push_back(std::move(impl));
    rebuild_snapshot();
    return job_id;
}

bool cancel(uint64_t id) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
        if (j->id == id && j->cancellable) {
            j->cancel_src.request();
            return true;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

bool alive(uint64_t id) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
        if (j->id != id) continue;
        std::lock_guard jlk(j->mu);
        return j->state == job_state_t::queued || j->state == job_state_t::running;
    }
    return false;
}

std::shared_ptr<const jobs_view_t> snapshot() {
    return g_published.get();
}

namespace {

// fail() marks a job failed while its body may still run, so joinability
// keys off the thread having actually returned
bool finished(const job_context_t::impl_t& j) {
    return j.exited.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
}

} // namespace

void reap() {
    // claim finished jobs under the lock, join them without it: a job body that
    // calls submit/cancel/alive while finishing would otherwise deadlock here
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<job_context_t::impl_t>> to_join;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
        for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
            if (j->joined || j->join_claimed || !finished(*j)) continue;
            j->join_claimed = true;
            to_join.push_back(j);
        }
    }
    for (auto& j : to_join)
        if (j->thread.joinable()) j->thread.join();

    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    bool changed = !to_join.empty();
    for (auto& j : to_join) j->joined = true;
    // keep the last 32 finished jobs
    while (g_jobs.size() > 32) {
        auto it = std::find_if(g_jobs.begin(), g_jobs.end(), [](auto& j) { return j->joined; });
        if (it == g_jobs.end()) break;
        g_jobs.erase(it);
        changed = true;
    }
    if (changed) rebuild_snapshot();
}

void reset() {
    // let tests reuse the coordinator
    g_shutting_down.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
}

void shutdown(uint32_t deadline_ms) {
    g_shutting_down.store(true, std::memory_order_release);

    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<job_context_t::impl_t>> mine;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
        for (auto& j : g_jobs) {
            j->cancel_src.request();
            if (j->joined || j->join_claimed) continue;   // a concurrent reap owns it
            j->join_claimed = true;
            mine.push_back(j);
        }
        g_jobs.clear();
        rebuild_snapshot();
    }

    // the deadline bounds the whole sweep: wait for each body to finish, join the
    // finished ones, detach whatever is still running when time is up (the thread
    // keeps its impl alive through the captured shared_ptr)
    const int64_t deadline = steady_ms() + static_cast<int64_t>(deadline_ms);
    for (auto& j : mine) {
        if (!j->thread.joinable()) continue;
        while (!finished(*j) && steady_ms() < deadline)
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2));
        if (finished(*j)) j->thread.join();
        else j->thread.detach();
    }
}

} // namespace jobs
} // namespace slop::core::infra
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/jobs.hpp
// long jobs each get their own thread so they cant starve the pool

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/infra/cancel.hpp"

namespace slop::core::infra {

enum class job_state_t : uint8_t { queued, running, succeeded, cancelled, failed };

struct job_snapshot_t {
    uint64_t    id          = 0;
    std::string label;
    std::string owner;
    std::string stage;
    std::string error;
    float       progress    = -1.0f;   // -1 = indeterminate
    job_state_t state       = job_state_t::queued;
    bool        cancellable = false;
    int64_t     started_ms  = 0;
    int64_t     finished_ms = 0;
};

class job_context_t {
public:
    const cancel_token_t& cancel() const noexcept;
    bool  cancelled() const noexcept;
    void  set_stage(std::string s);
    void  set_progress(float p);
    void  set_progress(uint64_t done, uint64_t total);
    void  fail(std::string message);
    uint64_t id() const noexcept;

    // internals, hands off
    struct impl_t;
    explicit job_context_t(impl_t* p) : impl_(p) {}
private:
    impl_t* impl_ = nullptr;
};

struct job_desc_t {
    std::string label;
    std::string owner;
    bool        cancellable = true;
    std::function<void(job_context_t&)> body;
};

using jobs_view_t = std::vector<job_snapshot_t>;

namespace jobs {

uint64_t submit(job_desc_t d);          // 0 = rejected (cap reached)
bool     cancel(uint64_t id);
bool     alive(uint64_t id);

std::shared_ptr<const jobs_view_t> snapshot();

// call once a frame to join finished jobs
void reap();

// cancel all and join what we can
void shutdown(uint32_t deadline_ms = 3000);

// clear the shutdown flag for tests
void reset();

} // namespace jobs
} // namespace slop::core::infra
```

```cpp
// src/core/infra/lifecycle.cpp

#include "core/infra/lifecycle.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <dpapi.h>
#else
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif

#include <httplib.h>
#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "core/disasm/binary_state.hpp"
#include "core/infra/app_control.hpp"
#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/event_bus.hpp"
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/mcp_onboard.hpp"
#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"
#include "core/infra/settings.hpp"
#include "core/infra/text_format.hpp"
#include "core/infra/work_queue.hpp"
#include "core/mcp/mcp_server.hpp"
#include "core/memory/watch_service.hpp"
#include "core/process/target_service.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#pragma comment(lib, "crypt32.lib")
#endif

namespace slop::core::infra::lifecycle {

namespace {

using json = nlohmann::json;
namespace bus = event_bus;

// Auto-reconnect a dropped console on a worker thread: reconnect() opens a TCP
// socket and can block for seconds, so it must not run on the 10 ms tick.
std::thread       g_auto_thread;
std::atomic<bool> g_auto_stop{false};

struct state_t {
    std::mutex        mu;
    config_t          cfg;
    boot_result_t     result;
    std::atomic<int>  stage{0};
    std::atomic<bool> started{false};
    std::atomic<bool> torn_down{false};
    int64_t           last_tick_ms = 0;
};

state_t& st() {
    static state_t s;
    return s;
}

std::string g_endpoint_override;   // tests: scratch registration file

std::string endpoint_file() {
    if (!g_endpoint_override.empty()) return g_endpoint_override;
    const std::string& dir = paths::app_data();
    if (dir.empty()) return {};
    return dir + "\\engine.json";
}

// the token never lands on disk in the clear: DPAPI (current user) blob as
// hex on Windows; on POSIX the endpoint file is 0600 and the token is stored
// as-is (there is no per-user key service to borrow)
std::string protect(const std::string& plain) {
    if (plain.empty()) return {};
#ifdef _WIN32
    DATA_BLOB in{static_cast<DWORD>(plain.size()),
                 reinterpret_cast<BYTE*>(const_cast<char*>(plain.data()))};
    DATA_BLOB out{};
    if (!::CryptProtectData(&in, L"reverse-slop engine token", nullptr, nullptr, nullptr,
                            CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, &out))
        return {};
    std::string hex = fmt::format_hex_packed({out.pbData, out.cbData});
    ::LocalFree(out.pbData);
    return hex;
#else
    return plain;
#endif
}

#ifdef _WIN32
std::string unprotect(const std::string& hex) {
    std::vector<uint8_t> blob;
    std::string err;
    if (hex.empty() || !fmt::parse_hex(hex, blob, err)) return {};
    DATA_BLOB in{static_cast<DWORD>(blob.size()), blob.data()};
    DATA_BLOB out{};
    if (!::CryptUnprotectData(&in, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr,
                              CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, &out))
        return {};
    std::string plain(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(out.pbData), out.cbData);
    ::SecureZeroMemory(out.pbData, out.cbData);
    ::LocalFree(out.pbData);
    return plain;
}
#endif

#ifdef _WIN32
std::wstring image_path_of(HANDLE process) {
    wchar_t buf[MAX_PATH * 2]{};
    DWORD n = static_cast<DWORD>(std::size(buf));
    if (!::QueryFullProcessImageNameW(process, 0, buf, &n)) return {};
    return std::wstring(buf, n);
}
#else
std::string image_path_of(uint32_t pid) {
    char link[64], buf[4096];
    std::snprintf(link, sizeof(link), "/proc/%u/exe", pid);
    const ssize_t n = ::readlink(link, buf, sizeof(buf) - 1);
    if (n <= 0) return {};
    buf[n] = '\0';
    return buf;
}
#endif

#ifdef _WIN32
std::string utf8(const std::wstring& w) {
    if (w.empty()) return {};
    const int n = ::WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w.data(), static_cast<int>(w.size()),
                                        nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr);
    std::string out(static_cast<size_t>(n), '\0');
    ::WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w.data(), static_cast<int>(w.size()), out.data(), n,
                          nullptr, nullptr);
    return out;
}

std::wstring wide(const std::string& s) {
    if (s.empty()) return {};
    const int n = ::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.data(), static_cast<int>(s.size()),
                                        nullptr, 0);
    std::wstring out(static_cast<size_t>(n), L'\0');
    ::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.data(), static_cast<int>(s.size()), out.data(), n);
    return out;
}
#endif

void write_endpoint(uint16_t p, const std::string& token) {
    const std::string path = endpoint_file();
    if (path.empty()) return;
#ifdef _WIN32
    const json doc{{"pid", static_cast<uint32_t>(::GetCurrentProcessId())},
                   {"port", p},
                   {"exe", utf8(image_path_of(::GetCurrentProcess()))},
                   {"token_dpapi", protect(token)}};
#else
    const json doc{{"pid", static_cast<uint32_t>(::getpid())},
                   {"port", p},
                   {"exe", image_path_of(static_cast<uint32_t>(::getpid()))},
                   {"token", protect(token)}};
#endif
    if (!paths::write_file_atomic(path, doc.dump(2))) return;
#ifndef _WIN32
    ::chmod(path.c_str(), 0600);   // the bearer token is plaintext here
#endif
}

void remove_endpoint() {
    endpoint_t existing;
    // only delete the file if it is still ours
#ifdef _WIN32
    const uint32_t self = static_cast<uint32_t>(::GetCurrentProcessId());
#else
    const uint32_t self = static_cast<uint32_t>(::getpid());
#endif
    if (read_endpoint(existing) && existing.pid != self) return;
    const std::string path = endpoint_file();
    if (path.empty()) return;
    std::error_code ec;
    std::filesystem::remove(path, ec);
}

void set_stage(stage_t s) {
    st().stage.store(static_cast<int>(s), std::memory_order_release);
    bus::publish("boot.stage",
                 json{{"stage", static_cast<int>(s)},
                      {"total", kStageCount},
                      {"label", stage_label(s)},
                      {"done", s == stage_t::done}});
}

void start_mcp() {
    state_t& s = st();
    if (!settings::mcp_enabled()) return;

    mcp::server_config_t cfg;
    cfg.token = settings::mcp_token();
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
        cfg.port = resolve_mcp_port(s.cfg.mcp_port, std::getenv("SLOP_MCP_PORT"),
                                    settings::mcp_port());
    }
    cfg.max_streams = settings::events_max_streams();
    // a spawner (tauri supervisor, test harness) brings its own per-launch token
    // so the persisted one never has to travel over stdout
    if (const char* env_tok = std::getenv("SLOP_MCP_TOKEN"); env_tok && *env_tok)
        cfg.extra_tokens.emplace_back(env_tok);
    if (cfg.token.empty() && cfg.extra_tokens.empty()) {
        // Fail closed. An empty token used to mean "no auth" (the server
        // accepted any local process); generate and persist one instead, and
        // refuse to start rather than expose an open endpoint if that fails.
        const std::string tok = settings::generate_token();
        if (tok.empty() || !settings::set("mcp_token", tok)) {
            bus::output("mcp_token is empty and could not be generated; refusing to start "
                        "an unauthenticated MCP server");
            return;
        }
        cfg.token = tok;
        bus::output("mcp_token was empty; generated a new bearer token");
    }

    // port taken means fall back to an ephemeral one and skip onboarding so clients stay pointed at the owner
    bool ephemeral = false;
    if (!mcp::start(cfg)) {
        const uint16_t wanted = cfg.port;
        cfg.port  = 0;
        ephemeral = mcp::start(cfg);
        if (!ephemeral) {
            bus::output("mcp server failed to bind port " + std::to_string(wanted));
            return;
        }
        bus::output("mcp port " + std::to_string(wanted) +
                    " busy, bound ephemeral port " + std::to_string(mcp::port()));
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
        s.result.mcp_ok   = true;
        s.result.mcp_port = mcp::port();
    }
    bus::output("mcp server ready: http://127.0.0.1:" +
                std::to_string(mcp::port()) + "/mcp");
    write_endpoint(mcp::port(), cfg.token);

    bool onboard = false;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
        onboard = s.cfg.mcp_onboarding;
    }
    if (!onboard || ephemeral) return;

    // first run registers everywhere; later runs only refresh entries we already
    // wrote so a changed port or rotated token never leaves a client stale
    const bool first = !settings::mcp_onboarded();
    const auto results = first ? mcp_onboard::install_all(mcp::port(), cfg.token)
                               : mcp_onboard::refresh_existing(mcp::port(), cfg.token);
    for (const auto& r : results) {
        if (r.installed)
            bus::output(std::string(first ? "mcp registered: " : "mcp entry refreshed: ") +
                        r.client + " -> " + r.path);
        else if (!r.error.empty())
            bus::output("mcp onboard skip (" + r.client + "): " + r.error);
    }
    if (first) {
        settings::set_mcp_onboarded(true);
        bus::output("note: client configs now hold the mcp bearer token; do not sync them "
                    "to public dotfile repos");
    }
}

} // namespace

const char* stage_label(stage_t s) noexcept {
    switch (s) {
    case stage_t::runtime_pool:     return "runtime pool & job queue";
    case stage_t::process_services: return "process / target services";
    case stage_t::settings:         return "settings & session store";
    case stage_t::mcp_server:       return "mcp server";
    case stage_t::frontend:         return "interface";
    case stage_t::done:             return "ready";
    }
    return "?";
}

const char* stage_status(stage_t row) noexcept {
    const int cur = st().stage.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    const int idx = static_cast<int>(row);
    if (idx < cur) return "ok";
    if (idx == cur) return "run";
    return "wait";
}

stage_t stage() noexcept {
    return static_cast<stage_t>(st().stage.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
}

bool booted() noexcept { return stage() == stage_t::done; }

boot_result_t result() {
    state_t& s = st();
    std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
    return s.result;
}

void begin(config_t cfg) {
    state_t& s = st();
    if (s.started.exchange(true)) return;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
        s.cfg = std::move(cfg);
    }

    // init paths first or settings save renames onto nothing and drops temp files everywhere
    paths::init();

    pool::start();
    set_stage(stage_t::process_services);

    process::target_init();
    runtime::registry_init();
    set_stage(stage_t::settings);
}

stage_t advance() {
    state_t& s = st();

    if (stage() == stage_t::settings) {
        // probe before load creates the file or every run looks like the first
        const bool fresh = !std::filesystem::exists(paths::settings_file());
        settings::load();
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(s.mu);
            s.result.first_run = fresh;
        }
        set_stage(stage_t::mcp_server);
    }

    if (stage() == stage_t::mcp_server) {
        start_mcp();
        set_stage(stage_t::frontend);
    }

    if (stage() == stage_t::frontend) {
        bus::output("memory suite ready (scanner / aob / pointer scan / snapshots)");
        bus::output("disasm suite ready (zydis / functions / xrefs / strings / pe)");
        bus::output("analysis suites ready (emulation+taint / packer / signatures / decompiler)");
        bus::output("recon ready (rtti / vtables / danger imports / libsig / symbols)");
        bus::output("network ready (raw-socket capture / proxy / pcap), persistence + scripting live");
        bus::output("ps4 toolkit ready: connect a console with target ps4_auto, then debugger ps4_* / guide get ps4_setup.");
        set_stage(stage_t::done);
    }

    return stage();
}

void tick() {
    state_t& s = st();

    process::target_tick();
    jobs::reap();
    memory::watch::tick();

    // A dropped console comes back on its own with exponential backoff; the
    // session, breakpoints and slots are restored by reconnect(). Opt out with
    // ps4_auto_reconnect=false. disconnect() clears "lost", so an intentional
    // disconnect is never undone.
    const auto console_lost = [] {
        return runtime::registry_ps4_lost() || runtime::registry_ps5_lost();
    };
    if (!g_auto_thread.joinable() &&
        settings::get<bool>("ps4_auto_reconnect", true) &&
        console_lost()) {
        g_auto_stop.store(false);
        g_auto_thread = std::thread([] {
            int backoff_ms = 1000;
            while (!g_auto_stop.load() &&
                   (runtime::registry_ps4_lost() || runtime::registry_ps5_lost())) {
                std::string err;
                const bool back = runtime::registry_ps4_selected()
                    ? runtime::registry_ps4_reconnect(err)
                    : runtime::registry_ps5_reconnect(err);
                if (back) break;
                for (int waited = 0; waited < backoff_ms && !g_auto_stop.load(); waited += 100)
                    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(100));
                backoff_ms = (std::min)(backoff_ms * 2, 30000);
            }
        });
    }
    if (g_auto_thread.joinable() && !console_lost()) {
        g_auto_stop.store(true);
        g_auto_thread.join();
    }

    // mirror state at 10hz for the stream since polling over a socket isnt free anymore
    const int64_t now = steady_ms();
    if (now - s.last_tick_ms < 100) return;
    s.last_tick_ms = now;

    json target{{"attached", false}};
    if (auto sess = process::active_session(); sess && sess->valid()) {
        target["attached"] = true;
        target["pid"]      = sess->pid();
        target["name"]     = sess->name();
    }
    bus::publish_changed("target.changed", target);

    bus::publish_changed("backend.changed",
                         json{{"badge", runtime::active_badge()},
                              {"ps4", runtime::registry_ps4_active()},
                              {"ps5", runtime::registry_ps5_active()}});

    const auto hs = disasm::binary_state::hype_status();
    bus::publish_changed("hype.progress",
                         json{{"has_image", hs.has_image},
                              {"image", hs.image},
                              {"present", hs.engine_present},
                              {"ready", hs.ready},
                              {"running", hs.running},
                              {"progress", hs.progress},
                              {"error", hs.engine_error}});
}

void shutdown() {
    state_t& s = st();
    if (s.torn_down.exchange(true)) return;

    g_auto_stop.store(true);
    if (g_auto_thread.joinable()) g_auto_thread.join();

    remove_endpoint();
    mcp::stop();
    jobs::shutdown(1000);
    pool::stop(1000);
    memory::watch::shutdown();
    process::target_shutdown();
    settings::save();

    bus::shutdown();
}

const std::string& endpoint_path() {
    static const std::string path = [] {
        paths::init();
        return endpoint_file();
    }();
    return path;
}

void refresh_endpoint() {
    // only the booted engine owns engine.json; a bare mcp::start (tests) never writes it
    if (!st().started.load() || st().torn_down.load() || !mcp::running()) return;
    write_endpoint(mcp::port(), settings::mcp_token());
}

bool read_endpoint(endpoint_t& out) {
    const std::string path = endpoint_file();
    if (path.empty()) return false;

    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) return false;
    json doc = json::parse(f, nullptr, false);
    if (doc.is_discarded() || !doc.is_object()) return false;

    endpoint_t ep;
    ep.pid   = doc.value("pid", uint32_t{0});
    ep.port  = doc.value("port", uint16_t{0});
#ifdef _WIN32
    ep.token = unprotect(doc.value("token_dpapi", std::string{}));
#else
    ep.token = doc.value("token", std::string{});
#endif
    const std::string exe = doc.value("exe", std::string{});
    if (ep.pid == 0 || ep.port == 0) return false;

#ifdef _WIN32
    // a crash leaves the file behind, treat a dead pid as no endpoint
    HANDLE h = ::OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, ep.pid);
    if (h == nullptr) return false;
    DWORD exit_code = 0;
    const bool alive = ::GetExitCodeProcess(h, &exit_code) && exit_code == STILL_ACTIVE;
    // pid reuse: the live process must still be the image that wrote the file
    const std::wstring image = alive ? image_path_of(h) : std::wstring{};
    ::CloseHandle(h);
    if (!alive) return false;
    if (exe.empty() || image.empty() ||
        ::CompareStringOrdinal(image.c_str(), -1, wide(exe).c_str(), -1, TRUE) != CSTR_EQUAL)
        return false;
#else
    if (::kill(static_cast<pid_t>(ep.pid), 0) != 0) return false;
    const std::string image = image_path_of(ep.pid);
    if (exe.empty() || image.empty() || image != exe) return false;
#endif

    out = std::move(ep);
    return true;
}

uint16_t resolve_mcp_port(uint16_t cli_port, const char* env_port, uint16_t settings_port) {
    uint16_t port = settings_port;
    if (env_port != nullptr) {
        const int p = std::atoi(env_port);
        if (p > 0 && p < 65536) port = static_cast<uint16_t>(p);
    }
    if (cli_port != 0) port = cli_port;
    return port;
}

bool endpoint_serving(const endpoint_t& ep, int timeout_ms) {
    if (ep.port == 0) return false;
    httplib::Client cli("127.0.0.1", ep.port);
    cli.set_connection_timeout(std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms));
    cli.set_read_timeout(std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms));
    cli.set_write_timeout(std::chrono::milliseconds(timeout_ms));
    httplib::Headers h;
    if (ep.token.empty()) {
        // no usable token blob (other user, missing): liveness is all we can check
        const auto health = cli.Get("/health");
        return health && health->status == 200;
    }
    h.emplace("Authorization", "Bearer " + ep.token);
    const json body = {{"tool", "app"}, {"action", "status"}};
    const auto res = cli.Post("/api", h, body.dump(), "application/json");
    if (!res || res->status != 200) return false;
    const json reply = json::parse(res->body, nullptr, false);
    return reply.is_object() && reply.value("ok", false);
}

bool drop_stale_endpoint() {
    const std::string path = endpoint_file();
    if (path.empty()) return false;
    endpoint_t ep;
    if (read_endpoint(ep) && endpoint_serving(ep)) return false;
    std::error_code ec;
    return std::filesystem::remove(path, ec);
}

void set_endpoint_path_for_testing(std::string path) { g_endpoint_override = std::move(path); }

} // namespace slop::core::infra::lifecycle
```

`src/core/infra/lifecycle.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/lifecycle.hpp
// the boot and shutdown state machine, any shell can drive it

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

namespace slop::core::infra::lifecycle {

enum class stage_t : int {
    runtime_pool = 0,
    process_services,
    settings,
    mcp_server,
    // not interface because windows.h defines it as a macro and it wrecks the enum
    frontend,
    done,
};

inline constexpr int kStageCount = static_cast<int>(stage_t::done);

// label for the splash
const char* stage_label(stage_t s) noexcept;

// ok, run or wait for a row
const char* stage_status(stage_t row) noexcept;

struct config_t {
    // register the mcp endpoint into ai clients on first run
    bool mcp_onboarding = true;
    // --port <n>: wins over SLOP_MCP_PORT and the persisted mcp_port setting
    uint16_t mcp_port = 0;
};

struct boot_result_t {
    bool        mcp_ok           = false;
    uint16_t    mcp_port         = 0;
    bool        first_run        = false;   // no prior settings on disk
};

// starts the sequence
void begin(config_t cfg);

// call once per loop, done means booted
stage_t advance();

stage_t stage() noexcept;
bool    booted() noexcept;

// copy by value, another thread writes these
boot_result_t result();

// the per loop tick, heartbeat, job reaping, watchlist, change events
void tick();

// teardown in the old order, safe to call twice
void shutdown();

// endpoint advertisement
// the running instance writes pid, port, its image path and the DPAPI (current
// user) protected token to engine.json so a front end / second engine can find it

struct endpoint_t {
    uint32_t    pid  = 0;
    uint16_t    port = 0;
    std::string token;   // decrypted; empty when the blob is missing or not ours
};

const std::string& endpoint_path();

// false when the file is missing, the pid is dead or now runs another image
bool read_endpoint(endpoint_t& out);

// authenticated app.status round trip against the advertised endpoint; false
// when nothing answers (alive-but-not-serving pid, reused port, stale token).
// Probes /api on purpose: the deprecated alias also answers on engines that
// predate /api/v1, so a handover to an older build still verifies.
bool endpoint_serving(const endpoint_t& ep, int timeout_ms = 1500);

// removes engine.json when it does not serve; true when the file was removed
bool drop_stale_endpoint();

// --port beats SLOP_MCP_PORT beats the settings port (0 = unset)
uint16_t resolve_mcp_port(uint16_t cli_port, const char* env_port, uint16_t settings_port);

// tests point the registration at a scratch file
void set_endpoint_path_for_testing(std::string path);

// rewrites engine.json with the current port and settings token (token rotation)
void refresh_endpoint();

} // namespace slop::core::infra::lifecycle
```

`src/core/infra/mcp_onboard.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/infra/mcp_onboard.cpp
// drops the SlopStation mcp entry into every ai client config we know about
// runs once on first boot and skips anything that already has us registered
//
// every client wants a slightly different entry shape:
//  - Claude Code: ~/.claude.json "mcpServers" entry with "type":"http", it
//    reads an entry with a url but no type as stdio and skips it
//  - Claude Desktop: stdio only, remote servers go through the connectors ui
//  - Cursor / Windsurf / OpenCode: bare "url" entries
//  - VS Code: settings.json "mcp.servers" entry with "type":"http"

#include "core/infra/mcp_onboard.hpp"
#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"
#include "core/infra/settings.hpp"

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <shlobj.h>
#else
#include <cstdlib>
#endif

#include <algorithm>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>

namespace slop::core::infra::mcp_onboard {

namespace fs = std::filesystem;
using json = nlohmann::json;

namespace {

// path helpers

std::string env_or(const char* var, const std::string& fallback) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    char buf[MAX_PATH]{};
    const DWORD n = GetEnvironmentVariableA(var, buf, MAX_PATH);
    if (n == 0 || n >= MAX_PATH) return fallback;
    return std::string(buf, n);
#else
    const char* v = std::getenv(var);
    return (v && *v) ? std::string(v) : fallback;
#endif
}

#ifdef _WIN32
std::string localappdata() { return env_or("LOCALAPPDATA", ""); }
std::string appdata()      { return env_or("APPDATA", ""); }
std::string userprofile()  { return env_or("USERPROFILE", ""); }
#else
std::string userprofile()  { return env_or("HOME", ""); }
[[maybe_unused]] std::string localappdata() {
    return env_or("XDG_DATA_HOME", userprofile() + "/.local/share");
}
std::string appdata()      { return env_or("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", userprofile() + "/.config"); }
#endif

// json helpers

// parse result, a file we cant read never gets written back over
enum class read_t { ok, missing, corrupt };

read_t read_json_file(const std::string& path, json& out) {
    std::error_code ec;
    if (!fs::exists(path, ec) || ec) return read_t::missing;
    std::ifstream f(path);
    if (!f.is_open()) return read_t::corrupt;
    try {
        f >> out;
        return read_t::ok;
    } catch (...) {
        return read_t::corrupt;
    }
}

bool write_json_file(const std::string& path, const json& j) {
    return paths::write_file_atomic(path, j.dump(2));
}

// entry builder

constexpr const char* kServerName = "slopstation";
#ifdef _WIN32
constexpr const char* kSep = "\\";
#else
constexpr const char* kSep = "/";
#endif

// Configs reference the env var by default so a rotated token never leaves
// plaintext behind in a dotfile repo; mcp_token_in_configs opts into plaintext
// for clients that cannot expand ${VAR}.
constexpr const char* kTokenEnvRef = "Bearer ${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN}";

std::string auth_header(const std::string& token) {
    return infra::settings::mcp_token_in_configs() && !token.empty()
               ? "Bearer " + token
               : std::string(kTokenEnvRef);
}

// bare url entry, no "transport" key since nobody reads one
json make_mcp_entry(uint16_t port, const std::string& token) {
    json entry;
    entry["url"] = "http://127.0.0.1:" + std::to_string(port) + "/mcp";
    entry["headers"] = json::object({{"Authorization", auth_header(token)}});
    return entry;
}

// Tern keeps every MCP server centrally in one array and always gets the env
// reference: its config is the one users share/sync most
std::string tern_path() { return appdata() + kSep + "tern" + kSep + "settings.json"; }

json make_tern_entry(uint16_t port) {
    return {{"name", kServerName},
            {"transport", "http"},
            {"url", "http://127.0.0.1:" + std::to_string(port) + "/mcp"},
            {"headers", json::object({{"Authorization", kTokenEnvRef}})},
            {"agents", json::array()},
            {"enabled", true}};
}

// per client installers

// Each returns {client_name, installed, path, error}

// shared installer, keeps every other key and bails on a config it cant parse
// true when an existing entry already points at this port with this token
bool entry_current(const json& existing, const json& wanted) {
    if (!existing.is_object()) return false;
    for (const char* k : {"url", "headers", "type"}) {
        const bool has_w = wanted.contains(k);
        const bool has_e = existing.contains(k);
        if (has_w != has_e) return false;
        if (has_w && existing.at(k) != wanted.at(k)) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// writes or refreshes our entry inside container[servers_key]; keeps every
// other key. a stale entry (old port/token) is rewritten in place, and in
// update_only mode a missing entry is left missing
install_result_t upsert_entry(const char* client, const std::string& path, json& cfg,
                              json& container, const char* servers_key, json entry,
                              bool update_only) {
    if (!container.contains(servers_key) || !container.at(servers_key).is_object()) {
        if (update_only) return {client, false, path, ""};
        container[servers_key] = json::object();
    }
    json& servers = container[servers_key];
    if (servers.contains(kServerName)) {
        json& existing = servers[kServerName];
        if (entry_current(existing, entry)) return {client, false, path, ""};
        // keep user additions (env, disabled flags...) and refresh only what we own
        if (existing.is_object()) {
            existing.erase("headers");
            for (auto& [k, v] : entry.items()) existing[k] = v;
        } else {
            existing = std::move(entry);
        }
    } else {
        if (update_only) return {client, false, path, ""};
        servers[kServerName] = std::move(entry);
    }
    if (!write_json_file(path, cfg))
        return {client, false, path, "write failed"};
    return {client, true, path, ""};
}

// shared installer, keeps every other key and bails on a config it cant parse
install_result_t install_url_entry(const char* client, const std::string& path,
                                   uint16_t port, const std::string& token,
                                   bool with_type, bool update_only) {
    json cfg;
    switch (read_json_file(path, cfg)) {
    case read_t::corrupt:
        return {client, false, path, "config unparseable, left untouched"};
    case read_t::missing:
        if (update_only) return {client, false, path, ""};
        cfg = json::object();
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
    if (!cfg.is_object())
        return {client, false, path, "config root is not an object, left untouched"};

    json entry = make_mcp_entry(port, token);
    if (with_type) entry["type"] = "http";
    return upsert_entry(client, path, cfg, cfg, "mcpServers", std::move(entry), update_only);
}

// old builds wrote a dead entry into ~/.claude/settings.json, wipe just ours
void remove_legacy_claude_code_settings_entry() {
    const std::string path = userprofile() + kSep + ".claude" + kSep + "settings.json";
    json settings;
    if (read_json_file(path, settings) != read_t::ok) return;
    if (!settings.contains("mcpServers") ||
        !settings.at("mcpServers").is_object() ||
        !settings.at("mcpServers").contains(kServerName))
        return;
    settings["mcpServers"].erase(kServerName);
    if (settings.at("mcpServers").empty()) settings.erase("mcpServers");
    write_json_file(path, settings);
}

install_result_t do_claude_code_global(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    // ~/.claude.json is claude codes state file so only add our key and touch nothing else
    remove_legacy_claude_code_settings_entry();   // old builds wrote there
    return install_url_entry("Claude Code (global)", userprofile() + kSep + ".claude.json",
                             port, token, /*with_type=*/true, update_only);
}

install_result_t do_claude_desktop(uint16_t port, const std::string& token) {
    (void)port;
    (void)token;
    // desktop config only does stdio servers so all we can do here is clean up
    const std::string path = appdata() + kSep + "Claude" + kSep + "claude_desktop_config.json";
    json cfg;
    if (read_json_file(path, cfg) == read_t::ok &&
        cfg.contains("mcpServers") && cfg.at("mcpServers").is_object() &&
        cfg.at("mcpServers").contains(kServerName)) {
        const json& e = cfg.at("mcpServers").at(kServerName);
        if (!e.contains("command")) {   // ours, a url entry a stdio client cant load
            cfg["mcpServers"].erase(kServerName);
            if (cfg.at("mcpServers").empty()) cfg.erase("mcpServers");
            write_json_file(path, cfg);
        }
    }
    return {"Claude Desktop", false, path,
            "desktop config is stdio-only; add remote MCP via the Connectors UI"};
}

install_result_t do_cursor(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    return install_url_entry("Cursor", userprofile() + kSep + ".cursor" + kSep + "mcp.json",
                             port, token, /*with_type=*/false, update_only);
}

install_result_t do_windsurf(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    return install_url_entry("Windsurf",
                             userprofile() + kSep + ".codeium" + kSep + "windsurf" + kSep + "mcp_config.json",
                             port, token, /*with_type=*/false, update_only);
}

install_result_t do_vscode(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    // vs code tucks servers under mcp.servers
    const std::string path = appdata() + kSep + "Code" + kSep + "User" + kSep + "settings.json";

    json settings;
    switch (read_json_file(path, settings)) {
    case read_t::corrupt:
        return {"VS Code", false, path, "config unparseable, left untouched"};
    case read_t::missing:
        if (update_only) return {"VS Code", false, path, ""};
        settings = json::object();
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
    if (!settings.is_object())
        return {"VS Code", false, path, "config root is not an object, left untouched"};

    // VS Code uses "mcp" -> "servers" -> { name: { ... } }; a non-object "mcp"
    // is the user's business, never overwrite it
    if (!settings.contains("mcp")) {
        if (update_only) return {"VS Code", false, path, ""};
        settings["mcp"] = json::object();
    }
    if (!settings.at("mcp").is_object())
        return {"VS Code", false, path, "\"mcp\" is not an object, left untouched"};

    json entry = make_mcp_entry(port, token);
    entry["type"] = "http";
    return upsert_entry("VS Code", path, settings, settings["mcp"], "servers",
                        std::move(entry), update_only);
}

install_result_t do_opencode(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    // ~/.config/opencode/config.json  (XDG on Linux; %USERPROFILE%\.config on Win)
    return install_url_entry("OpenCode",
                             userprofile() + kSep + ".config" + kSep + "opencode" + kSep + "config.json",
                             port, token, /*with_type=*/false, update_only);
}

// Tern: agents.mcp is an array of flat entries, matched by name. "agents" is
// the user's scope choice, so it is written once and never refreshed.
constexpr const char* kTernOwnedKeys[] = {"name", "transport", "url", "headers", "enabled"};

bool tern_entry_current(const json& existing, const json& wanted) {
    if (!existing.is_object()) return false;
    for (const char* k : kTernOwnedKeys) {
        const bool has_w = wanted.contains(k);
        const bool has_e = existing.contains(k);
        if (has_w != has_e) return false;
        if (has_w && existing.at(k) != wanted.at(k)) return false;
    }
    return true;
}

install_result_t do_tern(uint16_t port, bool update_only) {
    const std::string path = tern_path();
    json cfg;
    switch (read_json_file(path, cfg)) {
    case read_t::missing:
        // only users who already run Tern get an entry; never create %APPDATA%\tern
        return {"Tern", false, path, ""};
    case read_t::corrupt:
        return {"Tern", false, path, "config unparseable, left untouched"};
    default:
        break;
    }
    if (!cfg.is_object())
        return {"Tern", false, path, "config root is not an object, left untouched"};

    // a non-object agents / non-array mcp is the user's business, never overwrite it
    if (!cfg.contains("agents")) {
        if (update_only) return {"Tern", false, path, ""};
        cfg["agents"] = json::object();
    }
    if (!cfg.at("agents").is_object())
        return {"Tern", false, path, "\"agents\" is not an object, left untouched"};
    json& agents = cfg["agents"];
    if (!agents.contains("mcp")) {
        if (update_only) return {"Tern", false, path, ""};
        agents["mcp"] = json::array();
    }
    if (!agents.at("mcp").is_array())
        return {"Tern", false, path, "agents.mcp is not an array, left untouched"};

    json& servers = agents["mcp"];
    json entry = make_tern_entry(port);
    for (auto& e : servers) {
        if (!e.is_object() || e.value("name", std::string{}) != kServerName) continue;
        if (tern_entry_current(e, entry)) return {"Tern", false, path, ""};
        // keep user additions (a scoped agents list, extra keys) and refresh ours
        for (const char* k : kTernOwnedKeys) e[k] = entry.at(k);
        if (!write_json_file(path, cfg)) return {"Tern", false, path, "write failed"};
        return {"Tern", true, path, ""};
    }
    if (update_only) return {"Tern", false, path, ""};
    servers.push_back(std::move(entry));
    if (!write_json_file(path, cfg)) return {"Tern", false, path, "write failed"};
    return {"Tern", true, path, ""};
}

} // namespace

// public api

namespace {

// one bad config must never abort the sweep (or the boot that runs it)
template <class Fn>
install_result_t guarded(const char* client, Fn&& fn) {
    try {
        return fn();
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        return {client, false, "", std::string("installer failed: ") + e.what()};
    } catch (...) {
        return {client, false, "", "installer failed"};
    }
}

std::vector<install_result_t> sweep(uint16_t port, const std::string& token, bool update_only) {
    std::vector<install_result_t> results;
    std::vector<std::string> clients = infra::settings::mcp_onboard_clients();
    if (clients.empty()) clients = default_clients();
    results.reserve(clients.size());
    for (const std::string& client : clients) {
        const char* c = client.c_str();
        if (client == "Tern") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_tern(port, update_only); }));
        } else if (client == "Claude Code (global)") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] {
                return do_claude_code_global(port, token, update_only);
            }));
        } else if (client == "Claude Desktop") {
            if (!update_only)
                results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_claude_desktop(port, token); }));
        } else if (client == "Cursor") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_cursor(port, token, update_only); }));
        } else if (client == "Windsurf") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_windsurf(port, token, update_only); }));
        } else if (client == "VS Code") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_vscode(port, token, update_only); }));
        } else if (client == "OpenCode") {
            results.push_back(guarded(c, [&] { return do_opencode(port, token, update_only); }));
        }
    }
    return results;
}

} // namespace

std::vector<install_result_t> install_all(uint16_t port, const std::string& token) {
    return sweep(port, token, /*update_only=*/false);
}

std::vector<install_result_t> refresh_existing(uint16_t port, const std::string& token) {
    return sweep(port, token, /*update_only=*/true);
}

std::vector<install_result_t> uninstall_all() {
    std::vector<install_result_t> results;

    auto remove_key = [&](const char* client, const std::string& path,
                          const char* servers_key, const char* parent_key = nullptr) {
        json cfg;
        switch (read_json_file(path, cfg)) {
        case read_t::missing:
            results.push_back({client, false, path, "file not found"});
            return;
        case read_t::corrupt:
            results.push_back({client, false, path, "config unparseable, left untouched"});
            return;
        default:
            break;
        }

        json* container = &cfg;
        if (parent_key && cfg.contains(parent_key))
            container = &cfg[parent_key];

        if (!container->contains(servers_key) ||
            !(*container)[servers_key].contains(kServerName)) {
            results.push_back({client, false, path, ""});
            return;
        }

        (*container)[servers_key].erase(kServerName);
        if (write_json_file(path, cfg))
            results.push_back({client, true, path, ""});
        else
            results.push_back({client, false, path, "write failed"});
    };

    remove_key("Claude Code (global)",
               userprofile() + kSep + ".claude.json", "mcpServers");
    // Pre-fix builds wrote into settings.json instead of .claude.json  
    // clean both so uninstall actually removes what install wrote
    remove_key("Claude Code (legacy settings)",
               userprofile() + kSep + ".claude" + kSep + "settings.json", "mcpServers");
    remove_key("Claude Desktop",
               appdata() + kSep + "Claude" + kSep + "claude_desktop_config.json", "mcpServers");
    remove_key("Cursor",
               userprofile() + kSep + ".cursor" + kSep + "mcp.json", "mcpServers");
    remove_key("Windsurf",
               userprofile() + kSep + ".codeium" + kSep + "windsurf" + kSep + "mcp_config.json", "mcpServers");
    remove_key("VS Code",
               appdata() + kSep + "Code" + kSep + "User" + kSep + "settings.json", "servers", "mcp");
    remove_key("OpenCode",
               userprofile() + kSep + ".config" + kSep + "opencode" + kSep + "config.json", "mcpServers");

    // Tern keeps servers in an array, so it needs its own removal
    {
        const std::string path = tern_path();
        json cfg;
        switch (read_json_file(path, cfg)) {
        case read_t::missing:
            results.push_back({"Tern", false, path, "file not found"});
            break;
        case read_t::corrupt:
            results.push_back({"Tern", false, path, "config unparseable, left untouched"});
            break;
        default:
            if (!cfg.is_object() || !cfg.contains("agents") || !cfg.at("agents").is_object() ||
                !cfg.at("agents").contains("mcp") || !cfg.at("agents").at("mcp").is_array()) {
                results.push_back({"Tern", false, path, ""});
                break;
            }
            {
                json& servers = cfg["agents"]["mcp"];
                const size_t before = servers.size();
                servers.erase(std::remove_if(servers.begin(), servers.end(),
                                             [](const json& e) {
                                                 return e.is_object() &&
                                                        e.value("name", std::string{}) ==
                                                            kServerName;
                                             }),
                              servers.end());
                if (servers.size() == before)
                    results.push_back({"Tern", false, path, ""});
                else if (write_json_file(path, cfg))
                    results.push_back({"Tern", true, path, ""});
                else
                    results.push_back({"Tern", false, path, "write failed"});
            }
            break;
        }
    }

    return results;
}

std::vector<std::string> default_clients() {
    std::error_code ec;
    if (fs::exists(tern_path(), ec) && !ec) return {"Tern"};
    return {"Claude Code (global)", "Claude Desktop", "Cursor", "Windsurf", "VS Code", "OpenCode"};
}

std::vector<std::string> plaintext_token_clients() {
    std::vector<std::string> out;

    // a literal bearer is anything that is not the ${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN} reference
    auto literal = [](const json& entry) {
        if (!entry.is_object() || !entry.contains("headers") || !entry.at("headers").is_object())
            return false;
        const json& h = entry.at("headers");
        if (!h.contains("Authorization") || !h.at("Authorization").is_string()) return false;
        return h.at("Authorization").get<std::string>().find("${") == std::string::npos;
    };

    auto check = [&](const char* client, const std::string& path, const char* servers_key,
                     const char* parent_key = nullptr) {
        json cfg;
        if (read_json_file(path, cfg) != read_t::ok || !cfg.is_object()) return;
        const json* container = &cfg;
        if (parent_key) {
            if (!cfg.contains(parent_key) || !cfg.at(parent_key).is_object()) return;
            container = &cfg.at(parent_key);
        }
        if (!container->contains(servers_key) || !(*container)[servers_key].is_object()) return;
        const json& servers = (*container)[servers_key];
        if (servers.contains(kServerName) && literal(servers.at(kServerName)))
            out.push_back(client);
    };

    check("Claude Code (global)", userprofile() + kSep + ".claude.json", "mcpServers");
    check("Cursor", userprofile() + kSep + ".cursor" + kSep + "mcp.json", "mcpServers");
    check("Windsurf", userprofile() + kSep + ".codeium" + kSep + "windsurf" + kSep + "mcp_config.json", "mcpServers");
    check("VS Code", appdata() + kSep + "Code" + kSep + "User" + kSep + "settings.json", "servers", "mcp");
    check("OpenCode", userprofile() + kSep + ".config" + kSep + "opencode" + kSep + "config.json", "mcpServers");

    json tern;
    if (read_json_file(tern_path(), tern) == read_t::ok && tern.is_object() &&
        tern.contains("agents") && tern.at("agents").is_object() &&
        tern.at("agents").contains("mcp") && tern.at("agents").at("mcp").is_array()) {
        for (const auto& e : tern.at("agents").at("mcp"))
            if (e.is_object() && e.value("name", std::string{}) == kServerName && literal(e)) {
                out.push_back("Tern");
                break;
            }
    }
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::infra::mcp_onboard
```

```cpp
#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <shlobj.h>
#else
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#endif

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <utility>

namespace slop::core::infra::paths {

namespace {
std::string g_app_data;
std::string g_settings_file;
std::string g_sessions_dir;
std::string g_crashes_dir;
} // namespace

void init() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    char buf[MAX_PATH]{};
    const DWORD n = GetEnvironmentVariableA("LOCALAPPDATA", buf, MAX_PATH);
    if (n == 0 || n >= MAX_PATH) {
        // fall back to the working dir
        g_app_data = ".\\reverse-slop";
    } else {
        g_app_data = std::string(buf, n) + "\\reverse-slop";
    }
    const char sep = '\\';
#else
    // XDG: $XDG_DATA_HOME, else ~/.local/share
    const char* xdg = std::getenv("XDG_DATA_HOME");
    std::string base;
    if (xdg && *xdg) {
        base = xdg;
    } else if (const char* home = std::getenv("HOME"); home && *home) {
        base = std::string(home) + "/.local/share";
    } else {
        base = ".";
    }
    g_app_data = base + "/reverse-slop";
    const char sep = '/';
#endif

    g_settings_file = g_app_data + sep + "settings.json";
    g_sessions_dir  = g_app_data + sep + "sessions";
    g_crashes_dir   = g_app_data + sep + "crashes";

    // make sure the folders exist
    std::error_code ec;
    std::filesystem::create_directories(g_app_data, ec);
    std::filesystem::create_directories(g_sessions_dir, ec);
    std::filesystem::create_directories(g_crashes_dir, ec);
}

// lazy: a host that never calls init() (the test binary, a library embedder)
// still gets the platform default instead of an empty path
const std::string& app_data() {
    if (g_app_data.empty()) init();
    return g_app_data;
}
const std::string& settings_file() { return g_settings_file; }
const std::string& sessions_dir()  { return g_sessions_dir; }
const std::string& crashes_dir()   { return g_crashes_dir; }

void set_app_data_for_testing(std::string dir) {
    g_app_data = std::move(dir);
#ifdef _WIN32
    const char sep = '\\';
#else
    const char sep = '/';
#endif
    g_settings_file = g_app_data + sep + "settings.json";
    g_sessions_dir  = g_app_data + sep + "sessions";
    g_crashes_dir   = g_app_data + sep + "crashes";
    std::error_code ec;
    std::filesystem::create_directories(g_app_data, ec);
}

bool write_file_atomic(const std::string& path, std::string_view data) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    std::error_code ec;
    const fs::path dst(path);
    if (dst.has_parent_path()) fs::create_directories(dst.parent_path(), ec);

    const fs::path tmp(path + ".tmp");
    {
        std::ofstream f(tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
        if (!f.is_open()) return false;
        f.write(data.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(data.size()));
        f.flush();
        if (!f) {
            f.close();
            fs::remove(tmp, ec);
            return false;
        }
    }
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!::MoveFileExW(tmp.c_str(), dst.c_str(),
                       MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)) {
        fs::remove(tmp, ec);
        return false;
    }
#else
    // POSIX rename() replaces atomically and is durable once the file is closed
    if (::rename(tmp.c_str(), dst.c_str()) != 0) {
        fs::remove(tmp, ec);
        return false;
    }
#endif
    return true;
}

} // namespace slop::core::infra::paths
```

`src/core/infra/published.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/published.hpp
// one writer many readers snapshot, readers just copy the pointer

#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>

namespace slop::core::infra {

template <class T>
class published_t {
public:
    published_t() {
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        slot_ = std::make_shared<const T>();
    }

    std::shared_ptr<const T> get() const {
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        return slot_;
    }

    void publish(std::shared_ptr<const T> v) {
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        slot_ = std::move(v);
        rev_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }

    uint64_t revision() const noexcept {
        return rev_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    }

private:
    mutable std::mutex          mu_;
    std::shared_ptr<const T>    slot_;
    std::atomic<uint64_t>       rev_{0};
};

} // namespace slop::core::infra
```

`src/core/infra/settings.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/infra/settings.hpp"
#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <bcrypt.h>
#else
#include <openssl/rand.h>
#endif

#include <chrono>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <mutex>
#include <sstream>

#ifdef _WIN32
#pragma comment(lib, "bcrypt.lib")
#endif

namespace slop::core::infra::settings {

namespace {

constexpr uint16_t kDefaultPort = 8765;

std::mutex      g_mu;
nlohmann::json  g_data = nlohmann::json::object();
std::string     g_file;          // empty = paths::settings_file()

const std::string& path_locked() {
    return g_file.empty() ? paths::settings_file() : g_file;
}

bool save_locked() {
    const std::string& p = path_locked();
    if (p.empty()) return false;
    return paths::write_file_atomic(p, g_data.dump(2));
}

// keep the unreadable original around so a hand edit with a typo is recoverable
void backup_corrupt_locked(const std::string& p) {
    const auto ms = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
                        std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
                        .count();
    std::error_code ec;
    std::filesystem::copy_file(p, p + ".corrupt-" + std::to_string(ms),
                               std::filesystem::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
}

} // namespace

std::string generate_token() {
    unsigned char buf[32]{};
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!BCRYPT_SUCCESS(::BCryptGenRandom(nullptr, buf, sizeof(buf),
                                          BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG)))
        return {};
#else
    if (::RAND_bytes(buf, sizeof(buf)) != 1) return {};
#endif
    static constexpr char kHex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    std::string out;
    out.reserve(sizeof(buf) * 2);
    for (unsigned char b : buf) {
        out.push_back(kHex[b >> 4]);
        out.push_back(kHex[b & 0xF]);
    }
    return out;
}

void load() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    const std::string& p = path_locked();
    g_data = nlohmann::json::object();
    bool dirty = false;

    std::ifstream f(p, std::ios::binary);
    if (f.is_open()) {
        std::stringstream ss;
        ss << f.rdbuf();
        f.close();
        nlohmann::json parsed = nlohmann::json::parse(ss.str(), nullptr, false);
        if (!parsed.is_discarded() && parsed.is_object()) {
            g_data = std::move(parsed);
        } else {
            backup_corrupt_locked(p);
            dirty = true;
        }
    }

    // first run (or a wiped token) gets a fresh bearer token so the server is never open by default
    const auto tok = g_data.find("mcp_token");
    if (tok == g_data.end() || !tok->is_string() || tok->get_ref<const std::string&>().empty()) {
        const std::string t = generate_token();
        if (!t.empty()) {
            g_data["mcp_token"] = t;
            dirty = true;
        }
    }
    if (dirty) save_locked();
}

bool save() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    return save_locked();
}

void set_file_for_testing(std::string path) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    g_file = std::move(path);
    g_data = nlohmann::json::object();
}

const std::string& file() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    return path_locked();
}

nlohmann::json get_json(std::string_view key) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    const auto it = g_data.find(key);
    return it == g_data.end() ? nlohmann::json() : *it;
}

bool set(std::string_view key, nlohmann::json value) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    if (value.is_null())
        g_data.erase(std::string(key));
    else
        g_data[std::string(key)] = std::move(value);
    return save_locked();
}

nlohmann::json snapshot() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_mu);
    return g_data;
}

bool mcp_enabled() { return get<bool>("mcp_enabled", true); }

uint16_t mcp_port() {
    const int64_t p = get<int64_t>("mcp_port", kDefaultPort);
    if (p < 1 || p > 65535) return kDefaultPort;
    return static_cast<uint16_t>(p);
}

std::string mcp_token() { return get<std::string>("mcp_token", {}); }

bool mcp_onboarded() { return get<bool>("mcp_onboarded", false); }

void set_mcp_onboarded(bool v) { set("mcp_onboarded", v); }

std::vector<std::string> mcp_onboard_clients() {
    return get<std::vector<std::string>>("mcp_onboard_clients", {});
}

bool mcp_token_in_configs() { return get<bool>("mcp_token_in_configs", false); }

bool mcp_audit_enabled() { return get<bool>("mcp_audit_enabled", true); }

std::string mcp_audit_path() {
    const std::string p = get<std::string>("mcp_audit_path", {});
    if (!p.empty()) return p;
    const std::string& ad = paths::app_data();
    if (ad.empty()) return {};
    return ad + "\\mcp_audit.jsonl";
}

bool mcp_require_confirm() { return get<bool>("mcp_require_confirm", false); }

size_t events_max_streams() {
    const int64_t n = get<int64_t>("events_max_streams", 64);
    if (n < 1) return 1;
    if (n > 1024) return 1024;
    return static_cast<size_t>(n);
}

} // namespace slop::core::infra::settings
```

`src/core/infra/settings.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/infra/settings.hpp
// persistent engine settings (%LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\settings.json)
//
// every setter persists immediately through an atomic replace so a crash never
// loses a change and never leaves a half written file behind

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

namespace slop::core::infra::settings {

// loads settings_file(); a parseable non-object or unparseable file is backed up
// to settings.json.corrupt-<ms> and replaced by an empty object. generates the
// mcp_token on first run when it is empty
void load();
// atomic write of the current state; returns false when the write failed
bool save();

// tests point the store at a scratch file; load() reads from it afterwards
void set_file_for_testing(std::string path);
const std::string& file();

// raw value or null when absent
nlohmann::json get_json(std::string_view key);

// typed read with a fallback for missing keys and type mismatches
template <class T>
T get(std::string_view key, T def) {
    const nlohmann::json j = get_json(key);
    if (j.is_null()) return def;
    try {
        return j.get<T>();
    } catch (...) {
        return def;
    }
}

// sets (null erases) and persists immediately; false when the write failed
bool set(std::string_view key, nlohmann::json value);

// copy of the whole settings object
nlohmann::json snapshot();

// MCP server
bool        mcp_enabled();
uint16_t    mcp_port();                 // out of range values fall back to 8765
std::string mcp_token();
std::string generate_token();           // 32 random bytes as 64 hex chars

// first run registration into ai clients
bool mcp_onboarded();
void set_mcp_onboarded(bool v);

// which clients the onboarder touches; empty = auto (Tern when installed,
// else every known client)
std::vector<std::string> mcp_onboard_clients();
// false (default): client configs reference ${SLOP_MCP_TOKEN} instead of the
// plaintext bearer
bool mcp_token_in_configs();

// MCP audit trail + confirm gate (ps4debug-mcp safety model): every tool call
// is appended as one JSONL line to mcp_audit_path(); when mcp_require_confirm
// is on, mutating console/target actions refuse to run without "confirm": true
bool        mcp_audit_enabled();      // default true
std::string mcp_audit_path();         // default <app_data>\mcp_audit.jsonl, "" disables
bool        mcp_require_confirm();    // default false (opt-in)

// concurrent GET /events + GET /mcp streams the server accepts (default 64,
// clamped to 1..1024); read once at boot
size_t      events_max_streams();

} // namespace slop::core::infra::settings
```
