`src/core/persist/session_store.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/persist/session_store.cpp

#include "core/persist/session_store.hpp"
#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#endif

#include <sqlite3.h>

#include <ctime>

namespace slop::core::persist {

namespace {

std::string now_iso_utc() {
    std::time_t t = std::time(nullptr);
    std::tm tm{};
#ifdef _WIN32
    gmtime_s(&tm, &t);
#else
    gmtime_r(&t, &tm);
#endif
    char buf[32];
    std::strftime(buf, sizeof(buf), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", &tm);
    return buf;
}

// Ordered, append-only migration steps: step N takes the schema from N-1 to N.
// Never edit a released step, add the next one and bump kSchemaVersion.
const char* migration_sql(int version) {
    switch (version) {
    case 1:
        // IF NOT EXISTS keeps files written before versioning (user_version 0,
        // tables already present) migratable in place
        return "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions("
               " id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,"
               " name TEXT NOT NULL,"
               " created_at TEXT NOT NULL,"
               " data TEXT NOT NULL);"
               "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv("
               " key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);";
    default:
        return nullptr;
    }
}

bool user_version(sqlite3* db, int* out, std::string* error) {
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, "PRAGMA user_version", -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK) {
        if (error) *error = sqlite3_errmsg(db);
        return false;
    }
    const bool row = sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_ROW;
    if (row) *out = sqlite3_column_int(st, 0);
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    if (!row && error) *error = "cannot read the schema version";
    return row;
}

// one step, one transaction: a failure leaves the file at the old version
bool apply_migration(sqlite3* db, int version, std::string* error) {
    const char* sql = migration_sql(version);
    if (!sql) {
        if (error) *error = "no migration for schema version " + std::to_string(version);
        return false;
    }
    const std::string script = "BEGIN IMMEDIATE;" + std::string(sql) +
                               "PRAGMA user_version = " + std::to_string(version) +
                               ";COMMIT;";
    char* msg = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_exec(db, script.c_str(), nullptr, nullptr, &msg) != SQLITE_OK) {
        if (error) *error = msg ? msg : "migration failed";
        sqlite3_free(msg);
        sqlite3_exec(db, "ROLLBACK", nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

} // namespace

session_store_t::~session_store_t() { close(); }

bool session_store_t::open(const std::string& path, std::string* error) {
    close();
    sqlite3* db = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_open_v2(path.c_str(), &db,
                        SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE,
                        nullptr) != SQLITE_OK) {
        if (error) *error = db ? sqlite3_errmsg(db) : "cannot open store";
        if (db) sqlite3_close(db);
        return false;
    }
    db_ = db;
    int version = 0;
    if (!user_version(db, &version, error)) {
        close();
        return false;
    }
    if (version > kSchemaVersion) {
        // never touch a file a newer build owns: its tables may mean anything
        if (error) *error = "sessions.db schema version " + std::to_string(version) +
                            " is newer than this build supports (" +
                            std::to_string(kSchemaVersion) +
                            "); upgrade reverse-slop or use another store path";
        close();
        return false;
    }
    for (int next = version + 1; next <= kSchemaVersion; ++next) {
        if (!apply_migration(db, next, error)) {
            close();
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

void session_store_t::close() {
    if (db_) {
        sqlite3_close(static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_));
        db_ = nullptr;
    }
}

int session_store_t::schema_version() const {
    if (!ok()) return -1;
    int v = -1;
    user_version(static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_), &v, nullptr);
    return v;
}

std::optional<uint64_t> session_store_t::save_session(
    const std::string& name, const std::string& json_data,
    std::string* error) {
    if (!ok()) {
        if (error) *error = "store not open";
        return std::nullopt;
    }
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db,
            "INSERT INTO sessions(name, created_at, data) VALUES(?,?,?)",
            -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK) {
        if (error) *error = sqlite3_errmsg(db);
        return std::nullopt;
    }
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 1, name.c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 2, now_iso_utc().c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 3, json_data.c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    const bool done = sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_DONE;
    if (!done && error) *error = sqlite3_errmsg(db);
    const uint64_t id = done
        ? static_cast<uint64_t>(sqlite3_last_insert_rowid(db))
        : 0;
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    if (!done) return std::nullopt;
    return id;
}

std::vector<session_meta_t> session_store_t::list_sessions() const {
    std::vector<session_meta_t> out;
    if (!ok()) return out;
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db,
            "SELECT id, name, created_at FROM sessions ORDER BY id DESC",
            -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK)
        return out;
    while (sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_ROW) {
        session_meta_t m;
        m.id         = static_cast<uint64_t>(sqlite3_column_int64(st, 0));
        m.name       = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 1));
        m.created_at = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 2));
        out.push_back(std::move(m));
    }
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    return out;
}

std::optional<session_store_t::row_t> session_store_t::load_session(
    uint64_t id) const {
    if (!ok()) return std::nullopt;
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db,
            "SELECT id, name, created_at, data FROM sessions WHERE id=?",
            -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK)
        return std::nullopt;
    sqlite3_bind_int64(st, 1, static_cast<sqlite3_int64>(id));
    std::optional<row_t> out;
    if (sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_ROW) {
        row_t r;
        r.id         = static_cast<uint64_t>(sqlite3_column_int64(st, 0));
        r.name       = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 1));
        r.created_at = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 2));
        r.data       = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 3));
        out = std::move(r);
    }
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    return out;
}

bool session_store_t::delete_session(uint64_t id) {
    if (!ok()) return false;
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, "DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id=?",
                           -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK)
        return false;
    sqlite3_bind_int64(st, 1, static_cast<sqlite3_int64>(id));
    const bool ok = sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_DONE &&
                    sqlite3_changes(db) > 0;
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    return ok;
}

bool session_store_t::kv_set(const std::string& key, const std::string& value) {
    if (!ok()) return false;
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db,
            "INSERT INTO kv(key,value) VALUES(?,?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value",
            -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK)
        return false;
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 1, key.c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 2, value.c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    const bool ok = sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_DONE;
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    return ok;
}

std::optional<std::string> session_store_t::kv_get(
    const std::string& key) const {
    if (!ok()) return std::nullopt;
    sqlite3* db = static_cast<sqlite3*>(db_);
    sqlite3_stmt* st = nullptr;
    if (sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, "SELECT value FROM kv WHERE key=?",
                           -1, &st, nullptr) != SQLITE_OK)
        return std::nullopt;
    sqlite3_bind_text(st, 1, key.c_str(), -1, SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
    std::optional<std::string> out;
    if (sqlite3_step(st) == SQLITE_ROW)
        out = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(sqlite3_column_text(st, 0));
    sqlite3_finalize(st);
    return out;
}

std::string default_store_path() {
    // paths::init creates the app data folder; tests may reach here before boot
    if (infra::paths::app_data().empty()) infra::paths::init();
    const std::string& dir = infra::paths::app_data();
    if (dir.empty()) return {};
    return dir + "\\sessions.db";
}

} // namespace slop::core::persist
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// sqlite session snapshots plus a kv table, symbols keep their per hash
// json store

#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::persist {

struct session_meta_t {
    uint64_t    id = 0;
    std::string name;
    std::string created_at;
};

class session_store_t {
public:
    // schema generations this build knows. open() migrates an older file up
    // and refuses one written by a newer build instead of guessing
    static constexpr int kSchemaVersion = 1;

    session_store_t() = default;
    ~session_store_t();

    session_store_t(const session_store_t&)            = delete;
    session_store_t& operator=(const session_store_t&) = delete;

    bool open(const std::string& path, std::string* error = nullptr);
    void close();
    bool ok() const { return db_ != nullptr; }
    // PRAGMA user_version of the open store, -1 when it is not open
    int schema_version() const;

    // sessions
    std::optional<uint64_t> save_session(const std::string& name,
                                         const std::string& json_data,
                                         std::string* error = nullptr);
    struct row_t : session_meta_t {
        std::string data;
    };
    std::vector<session_meta_t> list_sessions() const;
    std::optional<row_t> load_session(uint64_t id) const;
    bool delete_session(uint64_t id);

    // key/value (layouts etc.)
    bool kv_set(const std::string& key, const std::string& value);
    std::optional<std::string> kv_get(const std::string& key) const;

private:
    void* db_ = nullptr;   // sqlite3*
};

std::string default_store_path();   // %LOCALAPPDATA%\reverse-slop\sessions.db

} // namespace slop::core::persist
```

`src/core/process/handle_table.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/process/handle_table.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/published.hpp"
#include "core/process/target_service.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

infra::published_t<handle_table_t> g_handles;

} // namespace

uint64_t refresh_handles() {
    // the job holds the session (see refresh_threads)
    auto s = active_session();
    if (!s || !s->valid()) return 0;
    return infra::jobs::submit({
        "Enumerate handles", "handle_table", false,
        [s](infra::job_context_t& ctx) {
            auto r = s->backend()->enum_handles(s->pid());
            auto snap = std::make_shared<handle_table_t>();
            snap->sampled_ms = infra::wall_ms();
            if (r.ok) snap->items = std::move(r.items);
            if (ctx.cancelled() || active_session() != s) return;
            g_handles.publish(std::move(snap));
        }});
}

std::shared_ptr<const handle_table_t> cached_handles() {
    return g_handles.get();
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

`src/core/process/heap_list.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/process/heap_list.cpp

#include "core/process/heap_list.hpp"

#include <windows.h>
#include <tlhelp32.h>

namespace slop::core::process {

std::vector<heap_info_t> list_heaps(uint32_t pid, std::string* error) {
    std::vector<heap_info_t> out;
    HANDLE snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPHEAPLIST, pid);
    if (snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        if (error) *error = "snapshot failed";
        return out;
    }
    HEAPLIST32 hl{};
    hl.dwSize = sizeof(hl);
    if (Heap32ListFirst(snap, &hl)) {
        do {
            heap_info_t h;
            h.base  = hl.th32HeapID;
            h.flags = hl.dwFlags;
            // Per-heap size: sum of blocks is expensive; report the list
            // entry's committed range via the block walk lazily instead
            HEAPENTRY32 he{};
            he.dwSize = sizeof(he);
            uint64_t max_end = 0;
            if (Heap32First(&he, pid, hl.th32HeapID)) {
                do {
                    const uint64_t end =
                        static_cast<uint64_t>(he.dwAddress) +
                        he.dwBlockSize;
                    if (end > max_end) max_end = end;
                    ++h.entries_used_hint;
                } while (Heap32Next(&he) &&
                         h.entries_used_hint < 200000);
            }
            h.size = static_cast<uint32_t>(
                max_end > h.base ? max_end - h.base : 0);
            out.push_back(std::move(h));
        } while (Heap32ListNext(snap, &hl));
    }
    CloseHandle(snap);
    return out;
}

std::vector<heap_block_t> walk_heap_blocks(uint32_t pid, uint64_t heap_base,
                                           std::string* error,
                                           size_t max_blocks) {
    std::vector<heap_block_t> out;
    HANDLE snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPHEAPLIST, pid);
    if (snap == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        if (error) *error = "snapshot failed";
        return out;
    }
    HEAPLIST32 hl{};
    hl.dwSize = sizeof(hl);
    if (Heap32ListFirst(snap, &hl)) {
        do {
            if (hl.th32HeapID != heap_base) continue;
            HEAPENTRY32 he{};
            he.dwSize = sizeof(he);
            if (Heap32First(&he, pid, hl.th32HeapID)) {
                do {
                    if (out.size() >= max_blocks) break;
                    heap_block_t b;
                    b.address = he.dwAddress;
                    b.size    = static_cast<uint32_t>(he.dwBlockSize);
                    b.flags   = he.dwFlags;
                    out.push_back(std::move(b));
                } while (Heap32Next(&he));
            }
            break;
        } while (Heap32ListNext(snap, &hl));
    }
    CloseHandle(snap);
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::process

```

`src/core/process/module_dump.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/process/module_dump.hpp"

#include "core/disasm/pe_parser.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/session.hpp"

#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <unistd.h>

// The PE structs module_dump walks come from <windows.h> on Windows. These are
// the same layouts, only the fields this file reads.
#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct IMAGE_DOS_HEADER {
    uint16_t e_magic;
    uint16_t e_cblp, e_cp, e_crlc, e_cparhdr, e_minalloc, e_maxalloc, e_ss, e_sp;
    uint16_t e_csum, e_ip, e_cs, e_lfarlc, e_ovno;
    uint16_t e_res[4];
    uint16_t e_oemid, e_oeminfo;
    uint16_t e_res2[10];
    int32_t  e_lfanew;
};
struct IMAGE_FILE_HEADER {
    uint16_t Machine, NumberOfSections;
    uint32_t TimeDateStamp, PointerToSymbolTable, NumberOfSymbols;
    uint16_t SizeOfOptionalHeader, Characteristics;
};
struct IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER {
    uint8_t  Name[8];
    uint32_t VirtualSize, VirtualAddress, SizeOfRawData, PointerToRawData;
    uint32_t PointerToRelocations, PointerToLinenumbers;
    uint16_t NumberOfRelocations, NumberOfLinenumbers;
    uint32_t Characteristics;
};
struct IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER32 {
    uint16_t Magic;
    uint8_t  MajorLinkerVersion, MinorLinkerVersion;
    uint32_t SizeOfCode, SizeOfInitializedData, SizeOfUninitializedData;
    uint32_t AddressOfEntryPoint, BaseOfCode, BaseOfData;
    uint32_t ImageBase, SectionAlignment, FileAlignment;
    uint16_t MajorOperatingSystemVersion, MinorOperatingSystemVersion;
    uint16_t MajorImageVersion, MinorImageVersion;
    uint16_t MajorSubsystemVersion, MinorSubsystemVersion;
    uint32_t Win32VersionValue, SizeOfImage, SizeOfHeaders, CheckSum;
    uint16_t Subsystem, DllCharacteristics;
    uint32_t SizeOfStackReserve, SizeOfStackCommit, SizeOfHeapReserve, SizeOfHeapCommit;
    uint32_t LoaderFlags, NumberOfRvaAndSizes;
    uint8_t  DataDirectory[16 * 8];
};
struct IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 {
    uint16_t Magic;
    uint8_t  MajorLinkerVersion, MinorLinkerVersion;
    uint32_t SizeOfCode, SizeOfInitializedData, SizeOfUninitializedData;
    uint32_t AddressOfEntryPoint, BaseOfCode;
    uint64_t ImageBase;
    uint32_t SectionAlignment, FileAlignment;
    uint16_t MajorOperatingSystemVersion, MinorOperatingSystemVersion;
    uint16_t MajorImageVersion, MinorImageVersion;
    uint16_t MajorSubsystemVersion, MinorSubsystemVersion;
    uint32_t Win32VersionValue, SizeOfImage, SizeOfHeaders, CheckSum;
    uint16_t Subsystem, DllCharacteristics;
    uint64_t SizeOfStackReserve, SizeOfStackCommit, SizeOfHeapReserve, SizeOfHeapCommit;
    uint32_t LoaderFlags, NumberOfRvaAndSizes;
    uint8_t  DataDirectory[16 * 8];
};
#pragma pack(pop)

inline constexpr uint16_t IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE = 0x5A4D;
inline constexpr uint32_t IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE = 0x00004550;
inline constexpr uint16_t IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR32_MAGIC = 0x10B;
inline constexpr uint16_t IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC = 0x20B;
#endif

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <limits>
#include <system_error>

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

constexpr size_t kMaxHeaderBytes = 4u * 1024u * 1024u;
constexpr size_t kMaxOutputBytes = 512u * 1024u * 1024u;
constexpr uint16_t kMaxSections = 256;

bool add_fits(size_t a, size_t b, size_t limit, size_t& sum) {
    if (a > limit || b > limit - a) return false;
    sum = a + b;
    return true;
}

bool read_exact(const module_read_fn_t& read, uintptr_t address, void* dst,
                size_t size, size_t chunk_size) {
    auto* out = static_cast<uint8_t*>(dst);
    size_t done = 0;
    const size_t chunk = std::max<size_t>(chunk_size, 4096);
    while (done < size) {
        const size_t take = std::min(chunk, size - done);
        const auto io = read(address + done, out + done, take);
        if (!io.ok || io.bytes != take) return false;
        done += take;
    }
    return true;
}

bool write_atomic(const std::string& output_path,
                  const std::vector<uint8_t>& data, std::string& error) {
#ifndef _WIN32
    // same contract: temp file, flushed, renamed over the destination
    const std::string tmp = output_path + ".slop-tmp-" + std::to_string(::getpid());
    {
        std::FILE* f = std::fopen(tmp.c_str(), "wb");
        if (!f) {
            error = "failed to create temporary dump file";
            return false;
        }
        const size_t n = std::fwrite(data.data(), 1, data.size(), f);
        const bool flushed = std::fflush(f) == 0;
        std::fclose(f);
        if (n != data.size() || !flushed) {
            std::remove(tmp.c_str());
            error = "failed to write dump file";
            return false;
        }
    }
    if (std::rename(tmp.c_str(), output_path.c_str()) != 0) {
        std::remove(tmp.c_str());
        error = "failed to replace the dump file";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
#else
    const std::filesystem::path final_path{output_path};
    if (final_path.empty()) {
        error = "output path is empty";
        return false;
    }

    const auto temporary = final_path.wstring() + L".slop-tmp-" +
        std::to_wstring(GetCurrentProcessId()) + L"-" +
        std::to_wstring(GetTickCount64());
    HANDLE file = CreateFileW(temporary.c_str(), GENERIC_WRITE, 0, nullptr,
                              CREATE_NEW, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY |
                              FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH, nullptr);
    if (file == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        error = "failed to create temporary dump file (error " +
                std::to_string(GetLastError()) + ")";
        return false;
    }

    bool ok = true;
    size_t written_total = 0;
    while (written_total < data.size()) {
        const DWORD take = static_cast<DWORD>(std::min<size_t>(
            data.size() - written_total, 1u * 1024u * 1024u));
        DWORD written = 0;
        if (!WriteFile(file, data.data() + written_total, take, &written,
                       nullptr) || written != take) {
            ok = false;
            break;
        }
        written_total += written;
    }
    if (ok) ok = FlushFileBuffers(file) != FALSE;
    CloseHandle(file);

    if (ok) {
        ok = MoveFileExW(temporary.c_str(), final_path.c_str(),
                         MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) != FALSE;
    }
    if (!ok) {
        const DWORD code = GetLastError();
        DeleteFileW(temporary.c_str());
        error = "failed to write dump file (error " + std::to_string(code) + ")";
    }
    return ok;
#endif
}

} // namespace

module_dump_result_t reconstruct_mapped_pe(
    uintptr_t module_base, uint32_t module_size, const module_read_fn_t& read,
    std::vector<uint8_t>& output, const module_dump_options_t& options) {
    module_dump_result_t result;
    result.module_base = module_base;
    output.clear();

    if (module_base == 0 || module_size < sizeof(IMAGE_DOS_HEADER) || !read) {
        result.error = "invalid module range or reader";
        return result;
    }

    IMAGE_DOS_HEADER dos{};
    if (!read_exact(read, module_base, &dos, sizeof(dos), options.chunk_size)) {
        result.error = "failed to read DOS header";
        return result;
    }
    if (dos.e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE || dos.e_lfanew <= 0 ||
        static_cast<size_t>(dos.e_lfanew) > kMaxHeaderBytes) {
        result.error = "module does not contain a valid DOS header";
        return result;
    }

    const size_t nt_offset = static_cast<size_t>(dos.e_lfanew);
    size_t coff_end = 0;
    if (!add_fits(nt_offset, sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(IMAGE_FILE_HEADER),
                  kMaxHeaderBytes, coff_end)) {
        result.error = "PE header offset is out of range";
        return result;
    }
    std::vector<uint8_t> prefix(coff_end);
    if (!read_exact(read, module_base, prefix.data(), prefix.size(),
                    options.chunk_size)) {
        result.error = "failed to read PE header";
        return result;
    }
    uint32_t signature = 0;
    IMAGE_FILE_HEADER file_header{};
    std::memcpy(&signature, prefix.data() + nt_offset, sizeof(signature));
    std::memcpy(&file_header, prefix.data() + nt_offset + sizeof(signature),
                sizeof(file_header));
    if (signature != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE || file_header.NumberOfSections == 0 ||
        file_header.NumberOfSections > kMaxSections) {
        result.error = "module does not contain a valid PE header";
        return result;
    }
    if (file_header.SizeOfOptionalHeader < sizeof(uint16_t)) {
        result.error = "PE optional header is truncated";
        return result;
    }

    size_t optional_offset = coff_end;
    size_t section_table = 0;
    size_t section_table_end = 0;
    if (!add_fits(optional_offset, file_header.SizeOfOptionalHeader,
                  kMaxHeaderBytes, section_table) ||
        !add_fits(section_table,
                  static_cast<size_t>(file_header.NumberOfSections) *
                      sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER),
                  kMaxHeaderBytes, section_table_end)) {
        result.error = "PE section table is out of range";
        return result;
    }

    std::vector<uint8_t> tables(section_table_end);
    if (!read_exact(read, module_base, tables.data(), tables.size(),
                    options.chunk_size)) {
        result.error = "failed to read PE section table";
        return result;
    }

    uint16_t optional_magic = 0;
    std::memcpy(&optional_magic, tables.data() + optional_offset,
                sizeof(optional_magic));
    uint32_t size_of_image = 0;
    uint32_t size_of_headers = 0;
    if (optional_magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC) {
        if (file_header.SizeOfOptionalHeader < sizeof(IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64)) {
            result.error = "PE32+ optional header is truncated";
            return result;
        }
        IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 optional{};
        std::memcpy(&optional, tables.data() + optional_offset, sizeof(optional));
        size_of_image = optional.SizeOfImage;
        size_of_headers = optional.SizeOfHeaders;
    } else if (optional_magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR32_MAGIC) {
        if (file_header.SizeOfOptionalHeader < sizeof(IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER32)) {
            result.error = "PE32 optional header is truncated";
            return result;
        }
        IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER32 optional{};
        std::memcpy(&optional, tables.data() + optional_offset, sizeof(optional));
        size_of_image = optional.SizeOfImage;
        size_of_headers = optional.SizeOfHeaders;
    } else {
        result.error = "unsupported PE optional-header magic";
        return result;
    }

    if (size_of_image == 0 || size_of_headers < section_table_end ||
        size_of_headers > kMaxHeaderBytes) {
        result.error = "PE image/header sizes are invalid";
        return result;
    }
    if (module_size < size_of_image) {
        result.warnings.push_back("enumerated module size is smaller than SizeOfImage");
    }

    std::vector<IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER> sections(file_header.NumberOfSections);
    std::memcpy(sections.data(), tables.data() + section_table,
                sections.size() * sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER));

    size_t output_size = size_of_headers;
    for (const auto& section : sections) {
        size_t end = 0;
        if (!add_fits(section.PointerToRawData, section.SizeOfRawData,
                      kMaxOutputBytes, end)) {
            result.error = "PE section raw range is out of bounds";
            return result;
        }
        output_size = std::max(output_size, end);
    }
    if (output_size < 1024 || output_size > kMaxOutputBytes) {
        result.error = "reconstructed PE size is invalid";
        return result;
    }

    output.assign(output_size, 0);
    if (!read_exact(read, module_base, output.data(), size_of_headers,
                    options.chunk_size)) {
        result.error = "failed to read complete PE headers";
        output.clear();
        return result;
    }

    bool complete = true;
    for (const auto& section : sections) {
        if (section.SizeOfRawData == 0) continue;

        const uint64_t section_end = static_cast<uint64_t>(section.VirtualAddress) +
                                     section.SizeOfRawData;
        size_t readable = section.SizeOfRawData;
        if (section.VirtualAddress >= size_of_image) {
            readable = 0;
        } else if (section_end > size_of_image) {
            readable = size_of_image - section.VirtualAddress;
        }

        if (readable != 0 && !read_exact(
                read, module_base + section.VirtualAddress,
                output.data() + section.PointerToRawData, readable,
                options.chunk_size)) {
            if (options.strict_reads) {
                result.error = "failed to read section " +
                    std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(section.Name),
                                strnlen(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(section.Name), 8));
                output.clear();
                return result;
            }
            std::fill_n(output.data() + section.PointerToRawData, readable, 0);
            complete = false;
        }
        if (readable < section.SizeOfRawData) {
            complete = false;
            result.warnings.push_back("section data extends beyond SizeOfImage and was zero-filled");
        }
    }

    const auto parsed = disasm::pe_parse(output.data(), output.size());
    if (!parsed.ok || parsed.sections.size() != sections.size()) {
        result.error = "reconstructed image failed PE validation";
        output.clear();
        return result;
    }

    result.ok = true;
    result.complete = complete;
    result.bytes_written = output.size();
    result.section_count = sections.size();
    return result;
}

module_dump_result_t dump_module_pe(
    runtime::session_t& session, const runtime::module_info_t& module,
    const std::string& output_path, const module_dump_options_t& options) {
    std::vector<uint8_t> image;
    auto result = reconstruct_mapped_pe(
        module.base, module.size,
        [&session](uintptr_t address, void* destination, size_t size) {
            return session.read(address, destination, size);
        },
        image, options);
    result.output_path = output_path;
    if (!result.ok) return result;

    if (!write_atomic(output_path, image, result.error)) {
        result.ok = false;
        result.bytes_written = 0;
        return result;
    }
    return result;
}

namespace {

constexpr uint64_t kElfPage = 0x4000;   // PS4 page size; also a multiple of 4 KiB

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct elf64_ehdr_t {
    uint8_t  e_ident[16];
    uint16_t e_type;
    uint16_t e_machine;
    uint32_t e_version;
    uint64_t e_entry;
    uint64_t e_phoff;
    uint64_t e_shoff;
    uint32_t e_flags;
    uint16_t e_ehsize;
    uint16_t e_phentsize;
    uint16_t e_phnum;
    uint16_t e_shentsize;
    uint16_t e_shnum;
    uint16_t e_shstrndx;
};
struct elf64_phdr_t {
    uint32_t p_type;
    uint32_t p_flags;
    uint64_t p_offset;
    uint64_t p_vaddr;
    uint64_t p_paddr;
    uint64_t p_filesz;
    uint64_t p_memsz;
    uint64_t p_align;
};
#pragma pack(pop)
static_assert(sizeof(elf64_ehdr_t) == 64);
static_assert(sizeof(elf64_phdr_t) == 56);

uint64_t align_up(uint64_t v, uint64_t a) { return (v + a - 1) & ~(a - 1); }

// copy [start, end) through read into dst; unreadable chunks zero-fill (non
// strict) or fail. Returns false only on a strict failure
bool read_segment(const module_read_fn_t& read, uint64_t start, uint64_t end, uint8_t* dst,
                  const module_dump_options_t& options, module_dump_result_t& result) {
    const size_t chunk = std::max<size_t>(options.chunk_size, 4096);
    uint64_t failed_from = 0, failed_bytes = 0;
    auto flush_warning = [&] {
        if (!failed_bytes) return;
        char b[96];
        std::snprintf(b, sizeof(b), "unreadable 0x%llX..0x%llX zero-filled",
                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(failed_from),
                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(failed_from + failed_bytes));
        result.warnings.emplace_back(b);
        failed_bytes = 0;
    };
    for (uint64_t a = start; a < end;) {
        const size_t take = static_cast<size_t>(std::min<uint64_t>(chunk, end - a));
        uint8_t* out = dst + (a - start);
        const auto io = read(static_cast<uintptr_t>(a), out, take);
        if (!io.ok || io.bytes != take) {
            if (options.strict_reads) {
                char b[96];
                std::snprintf(b, sizeof(b), "read failed at 0x%llX (%zu bytes)",
                              static_cast<unsigned long long>(a), take);
                result.error = b;
                return false;
            }
            std::memset(out, 0, take);
            result.complete = false;
            if (!failed_bytes) failed_from = a;
            failed_bytes += take;
        } else {
            flush_warning();
        }
        a += take;
    }
    flush_warning();
    return true;
}

bool validate_segments(const std::vector<mapped_segment_t>& segs, std::string& error) {
    if (segs.empty()) { error = "no segments to dump"; return false; }
    uint64_t total = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < segs.size(); ++i) {
        const auto& s = segs[i];
        if (s.end <= s.start) { error = "empty or inverted segment"; return false; }
        if (i > 0 && s.start < segs[i - 1].end) { error = "segments overlap or are unsorted"; return false; }
        total += s.end - s.start;
        if (total > kMaxOutputBytes) { error = "module larger than the dump cap (512 MiB)"; return false; }
    }
    return true;
}

} // namespace

module_dump_result_t reconstruct_elf_from_segments(
    const std::vector<mapped_segment_t>& segments, const module_read_fn_t& read,
    std::vector<uint8_t>& output, const module_dump_options_t& options,
    elf_rebuild_info_t* info) {
    module_dump_result_t result;
    output.clear();
    elf_rebuild_info_t meta;
    if (!validate_segments(segments, result.error)) return result;
    if (segments.size() >= 0xFFFF) {
        result.error = "too many segments for one ELF program header table";
        return result;
    }
    const uint64_t base = segments.front().start;
    const uint64_t end  = segments.back().end;
    result.module_base = base;
    result.complete = true;

    // layout: ehdr, phdrs, then every segment at a page-aligned offset whose
    // residue matches its vaddr (p_offset % p_align == p_vaddr % p_align)
    const size_t n = segments.size();
    uint64_t off = align_up(sizeof(elf64_ehdr_t) + n * sizeof(elf64_phdr_t), kElfPage);
    std::vector<uint64_t> offsets(n);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        off += (segments[i].start - off) & (kElfPage - 1);   // match the residue
        offsets[i] = off;
        off += segments[i].end - segments[i].start;
    }
    if (off > kMaxOutputBytes) {
        result.error = "reconstructed ELF larger than the dump cap (512 MiB)";
        return result;
    }
    output.assign(static_cast<size_t>(off), 0);

    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (!read_segment(read, segments[i].start, segments[i].end,
                          output.data() + offsets[i], options, result)) {
            output.clear();
            result.complete = false;
            return result;
        }
    }

    // an in-memory ELF header (rare on PS4: the SELF loader maps only the
    // segments) tells us the entry point and the original type
    const uint8_t* first = output.data() + offsets[0];
    const uint64_t first_len = segments[0].end - segments[0].start;
    if (first_len >= sizeof(elf64_ehdr_t) && std::memcmp(first, "\x7f" "ELF", 4) == 0 &&
        first[4] == 2 /*ELFCLASS64*/) {
        elf64_ehdr_t src{};
        std::memcpy(&src, first, sizeof(src));
        meta.had_header = true;
        meta.source_type = src.e_type;
        const uint64_t span = end - base;
        if (src.e_entry >= base && src.e_entry < end) meta.entry = src.e_entry;          // absolute
        else if (src.e_entry != 0 && src.e_entry < span) meta.entry = base + src.e_entry; // PIE-relative
    }

    elf64_ehdr_t eh{};
    const uint8_t ident[16] = {0x7F, 'E', 'L', 'F', 2 /*64-bit*/, 1 /*LE*/, 1 /*version*/,
                               9 /*FreeBSD*/, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
    std::memcpy(eh.e_ident, ident, sizeof(ident));
    eh.e_type      = 2;      // ET_EXEC: p_vaddr are the runtime addresses
    eh.e_machine   = 62;     // EM_X86_64
    eh.e_version   = 1;
    eh.e_entry     = meta.entry;
    eh.e_phoff     = sizeof(elf64_ehdr_t);
    eh.e_shoff     = 0;
    eh.e_ehsize    = sizeof(elf64_ehdr_t);
    eh.e_phentsize = sizeof(elf64_phdr_t);
    eh.e_phnum     = static_cast<uint16_t>(n);
    eh.e_shentsize = 64;
    eh.e_shnum     = 0;
    eh.e_shstrndx  = 0;
    std::memcpy(output.data(), &eh, sizeof(eh));
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const auto& s = segments[i];
        elf64_phdr_t ph{};
        ph.p_type   = 1;   // PT_LOAD
        ph.p_flags  = ((s.prot & 1) ? 4u : 0u) | ((s.prot & 2) ? 2u : 0u) | ((s.prot & 4) ? 1u : 0u);
        ph.p_offset = offsets[i];
        ph.p_vaddr  = s.start;
        ph.p_paddr  = s.start;
        ph.p_filesz = s.end - s.start;
        ph.p_memsz  = s.end - s.start;
        ph.p_align  = kElfPage;
        std::memcpy(output.data() + sizeof(eh) + i * sizeof(ph), &ph, sizeof(ph));
    }
    meta.segments = n;
    result.ok = true;
    result.bytes_written = output.size();
    result.section_count = n;
    if (!meta.had_header)
        result.warnings.emplace_back("no ELF header in memory: rebuilt one from the console maps "
                                     "(entry unknown, no section headers/symbols)");
    if (info) *info = meta;
    return result;
}

module_dump_result_t dump_raw_span(const std::vector<mapped_segment_t>& segments,
                                   const module_read_fn_t& read, std::vector<uint8_t>& output,
                                   const module_dump_options_t& options) {
    module_dump_result_t result;
    output.clear();
    if (!validate_segments(segments, result.error)) return result;
    const uint64_t base = segments.front().start;
    const uint64_t span = segments.back().end - base;
    if (span > kMaxOutputBytes) {
        result.error = "module span larger than the dump cap (512 MiB)";
        return result;
    }
    result.module_base = base;
    result.complete = true;
    output.assign(static_cast<size_t>(span), 0);   // gaps stay zero
    for (const auto& s : segments) {
        if (!read_segment(read, s.start, s.end, output.data() + (s.start - base), options, result)) {
            output.clear();
            result.complete = false;
            return result;
        }
    }
    result.ok = true;
    result.bytes_written = output.size();
    result.section_count = segments.size();
    return result;
}

bool write_dump_file(const std::string& output_path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& data,
                     std::string& error) {
    return write_atomic(output_path, data, error);
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

```hpp
#pragma once

#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::runtime { class session_t; }

namespace slop::core::process {

using module_read_fn_t =
    std::function<runtime::io_result_t(uintptr_t, void*, size_t)>;

struct module_dump_options_t {
    size_t chunk_size = 64u * 1024u;
    bool strict_reads = true;
};

struct module_dump_result_t {
    bool ok = false;
    bool complete = false;
    std::string error;
    std::string output_path;
    uint64_t module_base = 0;
    size_t bytes_written = 0;
    size_t section_count = 0;
    std::vector<std::string> warnings;
};

// rebuild a file layout pe from a mapped image, separated so it tests
// without a live process
module_dump_result_t reconstruct_mapped_pe(
    uintptr_t module_base,
    uint32_t module_size,
    const module_read_fn_t& read,
    std::vector<uint8_t>& output,
    const module_dump_options_t& options = {});

// dump one module through the active session, works with rpm and the
// driver alike
module_dump_result_t dump_module_pe(
    runtime::session_t& session,
    const runtime::module_info_t& module,
    const std::string& output_path,
    const module_dump_options_t& options = {});

// one mapped segment of a (console) module; prot uses FreeBSD VM_PROT bits
// (1 read, 2 write, 4 execute)
struct mapped_segment_t {
    uint64_t start = 0;
    uint64_t end   = 0;
    uint32_t prot  = 0;
};

struct elf_rebuild_info_t {
    bool     had_header = false;  // the first segment carried an in-memory ELF header
    uint16_t source_type = 0;     // that header's e_type (ET_SCE_* etc.), 0 if none
    uint64_t entry = 0;           // absolute entry point, 0 = unknown
    size_t   segments = 0;        // PT_LOAD headers written
};

// Build a loadable ELF64 (x86-64, ET_EXEC) from a module's mapped segments:
// one PT_LOAD per segment at its absolute VA (p_vaddr == runtime address, so
// loading with base_override = first segment start is a no-op rebase), data at
// page-aligned file offsets, no section headers. Memory images of PS4 modules
// usually lack the ELF header (the SELF loader does not map it); when the
// first segment does start with one, its e_entry/e_type are carried over.
// Unreadable chunks fail a strict dump, otherwise they are zero-filled with a
// warning and complete=false. Pure function over the read callback.
module_dump_result_t reconstruct_elf_from_segments(
    const std::vector<mapped_segment_t>& segments,
    const module_read_fn_t& read,
    std::vector<uint8_t>& output,
    const module_dump_options_t& options = {},
    elf_rebuild_info_t* info = nullptr);

// The raw mapped span [first.start, last.end): segment bytes at their
// offsets from the module base, gaps between segments zero-filled.
module_dump_result_t dump_raw_span(
    const std::vector<mapped_segment_t>& segments,
    const module_read_fn_t& read,
    std::vector<uint8_t>& output,
    const module_dump_options_t& options = {});

// write a buffer atomically (temp file + replace)
bool write_dump_file(const std::string& output_path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& data,
                     std::string& error);

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

`src/core/process/module_table.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/process/module_table.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/published.hpp"
#include "core/process/target_service.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

// kept sorted by base so va_to_module can binary search
infra::published_t<module_table_t> g_modules;

} // namespace

uint64_t refresh_modules() {
    auto s = active_session();
    if (!s || !s->valid()) return 0;
    // the job owns a reference to the session: its handle (and the backend
    // it was opened on) stay valid until the job finishes even if the user
    // detaches meanwhile; a result for a session that is no longer current
    // is dropped instead of published
    return infra::jobs::submit({
        "Enumerate modules", "module_table", false,
        [s](infra::job_context_t& ctx) {
            auto r = s->backend()->enum_modules(s->handle());
            auto snap = std::make_shared<module_table_t>();
            snap->sampled_ms = infra::wall_ms();
            if (r.ok) {
                snap->items = std::move(r.items);
                std::sort(snap->items.begin(), snap->items.end(),
                          [](const runtime::module_info_t& a,
                             const runtime::module_info_t& b) {
                              return a.base < b.base;
                          });
            }
            if (ctx.cancelled() || active_session() != s) return;
            g_modules.publish(std::move(snap));
        }});
}

std::shared_ptr<const module_table_t> cached_modules() {
    return g_modules.get();
}

const runtime::module_info_t* va_to_module(uintptr_t va) {
    const auto snap = g_modules.get();
    if (!snap || snap->items.empty()) return nullptr;
    // last module with base <= va, then check the span covers va
    auto it = std::upper_bound(snap->items.begin(), snap->items.end(), va,
        [](uintptr_t v, const runtime::module_info_t& m) { return v < m.base; });
    if (it == snap->items.begin()) return nullptr;
    --it;
    const uint64_t end = static_cast<uint64_t>(it->base) + it->size;
    if (va < end) return &*it;
    return nullptr;
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

`src/core/process/process_icon.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/process/process_icon.cpp

#include "core/process/process_icon.hpp"

#include <windows.h>
#include <objbase.h>
#include <shellapi.h>

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

// RAII for the handles this walk creates; several early-out paths otherwise leak
// a DC or a bitmap on failure
struct icon_guard_t {
    HICON h = nullptr;
    ~icon_guard_t() { if (h) ::DestroyIcon(h); }
};

std::wstring widen(const std::string& s) {
    if (s.empty()) return {};
    const int n = ::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.c_str(),
                                       static_cast<int>(s.size()), nullptr, 0);
    if (n <= 0) return {};
    std::wstring out(static_cast<size_t>(n), L'\0');
    ::MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.c_str(), static_cast<int>(s.size()),
                          out.data(), n);
    return out;
}

icon_bits_t bits_from_icon(HICON icon) {
    icon_bits_t out;

    // GetIconInfo hands back bitmap copies the caller owns; both must be
    // released on every exit path
    ICONINFO info{};
    if (::GetIconInfo(icon, &info) == 0) return out;
    struct bmp_guard_t {
        HBITMAP color;
        HBITMAP mask;
        ~bmp_guard_t() {
            if (color) ::DeleteObject(color);
            if (mask) ::DeleteObject(mask);
        }
    } bmps{info.hbmColor, info.hbmMask};

    if (bmps.color == nullptr) return out;

    BITMAP bm{};
    if (::GetObjectW(bmps.color, sizeof(bm), &bm) == 0) return out;
    if (bm.bmWidth <= 0 || bm.bmHeight <= 0 || bm.bmWidth > 512 || bm.bmHeight > 512)
        return out;

    HDC screen = ::GetDC(nullptr);
    if (screen == nullptr) return out;

    BITMAPINFO bi{};
    bi.bmiHeader.biSize = sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER);
    bi.bmiHeader.biWidth = bm.bmWidth;
    // Negative height requests a top-down DIB, matching what canvas ImageData
    // expects; a bottom-up buffer would render the icon upside down
    bi.bmiHeader.biHeight = -bm.bmHeight;
    bi.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
    bi.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
    bi.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;

    std::vector<uint8_t> pixels(static_cast<size_t>(bm.bmWidth) *
                                static_cast<size_t>(bm.bmHeight) * 4);
    const int copied = ::GetDIBits(screen, bmps.color, 0,
                                   static_cast<UINT>(bm.bmHeight), pixels.data(),
                                   &bi, DIB_RGB_COLORS);
    ::ReleaseDC(nullptr, screen);
    if (copied == 0) return out;

    // 32bpp icons carry their own alpha, but a 24bpp source leaves it zeroed,
    // which would render fully transparent. Fall back to opaque in that case
    bool any_alpha = false;
    for (size_t i = 3; i < pixels.size(); i += 4) {
        if (pixels[i] != 0) {
            any_alpha = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!any_alpha)
        for (size_t i = 3; i < pixels.size(); i += 4) pixels[i] = 0xFF;

    out.width  = static_cast<uint32_t>(bm.bmWidth);
    out.height = static_cast<uint32_t>(bm.bmHeight);
    out.bgra   = std::move(pixels);
    return out;
}

} // namespace

icon_bits_t icon_for_path(const std::string& image_path, bool large) {
    if (image_path.empty()) return {};
    const std::wstring wide = widen(image_path);
    if (wide.empty()) return {};

    SHFILEINFOW sfi{};
    const UINT flags = SHGFI_ICON | (large ? SHGFI_LARGEICON : SHGFI_SMALLICON);
    // SHGetFileInfo touches the shell, which needs an apartment on this thread
    // Tolerate an already-initialised one rather than failing
    const HRESULT co = ::CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);
    const bool uninit = SUCCEEDED(co) && co != S_FALSE;

    icon_bits_t out;
    if (::SHGetFileInfoW(wide.c_str(), FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, &sfi, sizeof(sfi),
                         flags) != 0 &&
        sfi.hIcon != nullptr) {
        icon_guard_t guard{sfi.hIcon};
        out = bits_from_icon(guard.h);
    }

    if (uninit) ::CoUninitialize();
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

```cpp
#include "core/process/process_list.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/published.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

// latest enumeration, published by the refresh job, read lock-free by the ui
infra::published_t<process_list_t> g_processes;

} // namespace

uint64_t refresh_processes(bool resolve_details) {
    // the backend is looked up inside the job: a ps4 connect/disconnect can
    // swap it between submit and run, and the job must not hold a stale ref
    return infra::jobs::submit({
        "Enumerate processes", "process_list", false,
        [resolve_details](infra::job_context_t& ctx) {
            runtime::backend_t& b = runtime::active();
            auto r = b.enum_processes();
            auto snap = std::make_shared<process_list_t>();
            snap->sampled_ms = infra::wall_ms();
            if (r.ok) {
                snap->items = std::move(r.items);
                // entries the backend could not open come back without a path
                for (const auto& p : snap->items)
                    if (p.path.empty() && !p.name.empty()) ++snap->inaccessible_count;
                if (resolve_details) {
                    const auto el = b.query_elevation();
                    snap->debug_privilege =
                        el == runtime::elevation_t::elevated ||
                        el == runtime::elevation_t::system;
                }
            }
            if (ctx.cancelled()) return;
            g_processes.publish(std::move(snap));
        }});
}

std::shared_ptr<const process_list_t> cached_processes() {
    return g_processes.get();
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

`src/core/process/target_service.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/process/target_service.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_ps4.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <mutex>

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

// the session is mutated from mcp workers and read from the ui, every
// access takes the lock and hands out a copy. Holders of a copy keep the
// session (and its backend handle) alive; it closes when the last one drops
std::mutex g_session_mu;
std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> g_session;

// heartbeat bookkeeping; the misses counter is reset from attach paths too
std::atomic<int64_t>  g_hb_interval_ms{1000};
std::atomic<int64_t>  g_last_hb_ms{0};
std::atomic<uint32_t> g_misses{0};
const runtime::session_t* g_hb_session = nullptr;   // target_tick thread only

// sessions never survive a backend/console swap: the registry calls this
// before it replaces the connection
const bool g_swap_hook_installed = [] {
    runtime::registry_set_before_swap([] { target_detach(); });
    return true;
}();

} // namespace

void target_init() {
    // make sure the swap hook is in place even if static init dropped it
    (void)g_swap_hook_installed;
    runtime::registry_set_before_swap([] { target_detach(); });
}

void target_shutdown() {
    target_detach();
}

bool target_attach(uint32_t pid) {
    std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> old;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
        old = std::move(g_session);
    }
    old.reset();   // closes now unless an in-flight call still holds it

    auto s = std::make_shared<runtime::session_t>();
    if (!s->open(pid)) return false;
    std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
    g_session = std::move(s);
    g_misses = 0;
    return true;
}

void target_detach() {
    std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> old;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
        old = std::move(g_session);
    }
    // dropping our reference closes the session once in-flight users
    // (a running scan, an async enumeration job) release theirs
}

std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> active_session() {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
    return g_session;
}

bool target_connect_ps4(const std::string& host, uint16_t port, uint32_t pid,
                        std::string& err) {
    // the registry detaches the current session before swapping (hook)
    if (!runtime::registry_connect_ps4(host, port, err)) return false;
    if (pid == 0) return true;
    if (!target_attach(pid)) {
        err = "connected to " + host + ":" + std::to_string(port) +
              " but attach to pid " + std::to_string(pid) + " failed";
        target_detach();
        runtime::registry_disconnect_ps4();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void target_disconnect_ps4() {
    target_detach();
    runtime::registry_disconnect_ps4();
}

bool target_reconnect_ps4(std::string& err, runtime::backend_ps4_t::reconnect_report_t* report) {
    // the session (and its handle) stays: the backend keeps handles valid
    // across a reconnect to the same console
    if (!runtime::registry_ps4_reconnect(err, report)) return false;
    g_misses = 0;
    return true;
}

bool target_connect_ps5(const std::string& host, uint16_t port, uint32_t pid,
                        std::string& err) {
    // the registry detaches the current session before swapping (hook)
    if (!runtime::registry_connect_ps5(host, port, err)) return false;
    if (pid == 0) return true;
    if (!target_attach(pid)) {
        err = "connected to " + host + ":" + std::to_string(port) +
              " but attach to pid " + std::to_string(pid) + " failed";
        target_detach();
        runtime::registry_disconnect_ps5();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

void target_disconnect_ps5() {
    target_detach();
    runtime::registry_disconnect_ps5();
}

bool target_reconnect_ps5(std::string& err, runtime::backend_ps5_t::reconnect_report_t* report) {
    if (!runtime::registry_ps5_reconnect(err, report)) return false;
    g_misses = 0;
    return true;
}

void target_tick() {
    // Heartbeat: drop the session if the target died. Work on a local copy,
    // the session may be replaced concurrently by an MCP attach
    std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> s;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
        s = g_session;
    }
    if (!s || !s->backend()) { g_misses = 0; g_hb_session = nullptr; return; }
    if (s.get() != g_hb_session) { g_hb_session = s.get(); g_misses = 0; }

    // a process enumeration per frame is too chatty (a console roundtrip, a
    // toolhelp snapshot locally); once a second is plenty
    const int64_t now = infra::steady_ms();
    if (now - g_last_hb_ms.load() < g_hb_interval_ms.load()) return;
    g_last_hb_ms = now;

    runtime::backend_t& b = *s->backend();
    if (b.kind() == runtime::backend_kind_t::ps4) {
        auto* p = static_cast<runtime::backend_ps4_t*>(&b);
        // a dropped connection is not a dead process: keep the session for
        // target.ps4_reconnect. While a debug session is attached the event
        // channel already reports the process going away (SIGKILL / channel
        // close) and a stopped debuggee must not be second-guessed
        if (!p->connected() || p->ps4_debug_attached()) { g_misses = 0; return; }
    }
    if (b.kind() == runtime::backend_kind_t::ps5) {
        auto* p = static_cast<runtime::backend_ps5_t*>(&b);
        // same contract as the PS4 branch: keep the session across a dropped
        // connection (target.ps5_reconnect) and never second-guess a debuggee
        // the payload is holding
        if (!p->connected() || p->ps5_debug_attached()) { g_misses = 0; return; }
    }

    auto procs = b.enum_processes();
    if (!procs.ok) return;   // a failed enumeration says nothing about the pid
    const uint32_t pid = s->pid();
    const bool alive = std::any_of(procs.items.begin(), procs.items.end(),
                                   [pid](const runtime::process_info_t& p) { return p.pid == pid; });
    if (alive) { g_misses = 0; return; }
    // one missing entry can be a transient payload hiccup or a game in a
    // loading transition; require several consecutive misses
    if (++g_misses < kHeartbeatMissesToDetach) return;
    g_misses = 0;
    std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> dead;
    {
        std::lock_guard lk(g_session_mu);
        if (g_session == s) dead = std::move(g_session);
    }
}

void target_set_heartbeat_interval_ms(int64_t ms) {
    g_hb_interval_ms = ms < 0 ? 0 : ms;
    g_last_hb_ms = 0;
}

} // namespace slop::core::process

```

`src/core/process/target_service.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/process/target_service.hpp
// Central target lifecycle, attach, detach, session management

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_ps4.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_ps5.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/session.hpp"

namespace slop::core::process {

// consecutive heartbeat misses (pid absent from a successful enumeration)
// before the session is dropped
constexpr uint32_t kHeartbeatMissesToDetach = 3;

// Initialise the target service (call once at startup)
void target_init();

// Shut down, detaches active session if any
void target_shutdown();

// Attach to a process by PID. Returns true on success
bool target_attach(uint32_t pid);

// Detach from the current target. The session closes once every in-flight
// holder of active_session() has released it
void target_detach();

// Connect to a PS4 running the ps4debug-NG payload and optionally attach to
// pid (pid == 0 connects without attaching). Any current session is detached
// first. On failure err says why and the local backend is active
bool target_connect_ps4(const std::string& host, uint16_t port, uint32_t pid,
                        std::string& err);

// Drop the remote console connection (and any session on it), back to local
void target_disconnect_ps4();

// Re-open the selected console after a dropped connection; the current
// session survives (see backend_ps4_t::reconnect)
bool target_reconnect_ps4(std::string& err,
                          runtime::backend_ps4_t::reconnect_report_t* report = nullptr);

// Connect to a PS5 running the ps5debug-NG payload and optionally attach to
// pid (pid == 0 connects without attaching). Any current session is detached
// first. On failure err says why and the local backend is active
bool target_connect_ps5(const std::string& host, uint16_t port, uint32_t pid,
                        std::string& err);

// Drop the remote PS5 connection (and any session on it), back to local
void target_disconnect_ps5();

// Re-open the selected PS5 after a dropped connection; the current session
// survives (see backend_ps5_t::reconnect)
bool target_reconnect_ps5(std::string& err,
                          runtime::backend_ps5_t::reconnect_report_t* report = nullptr);

// Returns the active session, or nullptr if none
std::shared_ptr<runtime::session_t> active_session();

// Per-frame tick, drives deferred operations, heartbeat checks
void target_tick();

// heartbeat period (default 1000 ms); tests shorten it
void target_set_heartbeat_interval_ms(int64_t ms);

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

```cpp
#include "core/process/thread_table.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/jobs.hpp"
#include "core/infra/published.hpp"
#include "core/process/target_service.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

namespace slop::core::process {

namespace {

infra::published_t<thread_table_t> g_threads;

} // namespace

uint64_t refresh_threads() {
    // the job holds the session so the pid is queried on the backend the
    // session was opened on (never a swapped-in one); stale results are
    // dropped instead of published
    auto s = active_session();
    if (!s || !s->valid()) return 0;
    return infra::jobs::submit({
        "Enumerate threads", "thread_table", false,
        [s](infra::job_context_t& ctx) {
            auto r = s->backend()->enum_threads(s->pid());
            auto snap = std::make_shared<thread_table_t>();
            snap->sampled_ms = infra::wall_ms();
            if (r.ok) snap->items = std::move(r.items);
            if (ctx.cancelled() || active_session() != s) return;
            g_threads.publish(std::move(snap));
        }});
}

std::shared_ptr<const thread_table_t> cached_threads() {
    return g_threads.get();
}

} // namespace slop::core::process
```

`src/core/re/rtti.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/re/rtti.cpp
// msvc x64 rtti layouts kept here as a reference while parsing; the Itanium
// pass is shared with the hyperion analyzer (core/analysis/itanium_rtti.h)

#include "core/re/rtti.hpp"

#include "core/analysis/itanium_rtti.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstring>

namespace slop::core::re {

namespace {

struct section_span_t {
    uint64_t va = 0;
    size_t   file_off = 0;
    size_t   raw_size = 0;
    bool     writable = false;
    bool     exec = false;
};

// File-backed bytes of each section; MSVC RTTI lives in .rdata/.data, so
// code sections are skipped unless the caller wants them (Itanium images
// may merge .rodata into the executable segment)
std::vector<section_span_t> data_spans(const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
                                       const std::vector<uint8_t>& file,
                                       bool include_exec) {
    std::vector<section_span_t> out;
    for (const auto& s : pe.sections) {
        if (s.raw_size == 0 || s.virtual_size == 0) continue;
        if (static_cast<size_t>(s.raw_offset) + s.raw_size > file.size())
            continue;
        if (s.is_executable() && !include_exec) continue;
        out.push_back({pe.image_base + s.rva,
                       s.raw_offset, std::min<uint32_t>(s.raw_size, s.virtual_size),
                       (s.characteristics & 0x80000000) != 0, s.is_executable()});
    }
    return out;
}

std::string demangle_msvc_name(const std::string& raw) {
    // ".?AVMyClass@@" -> "MyClass"; ".?AVns@Inner@@" -> "ns::Inner"
    const std::string prefix = ".?AV";
    if (raw.rfind(prefix, 0) != 0) return raw;
    std::string body = raw.substr(prefix.size());
    while (!body.empty() && (body.back() == '@')) body.pop_back();
    for (char& ch : body)
        if (ch == '@') ch = ':';
    return body;
}

} // namespace

rtti_result_t rtti_scan(const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
                        const std::vector<uint8_t>& file) {
    rtti_result_t res;
    if (!pe.ok || pe.image_base == 0) return res;

    const auto spans = data_spans(pe, file, false);
    for (const auto& sp : spans)
        res.scanned_bytes += sp.raw_size;

    // pass 1: type descriptors
    struct td_hit_t { uint64_t va; uint32_t rva; std::string name; };
    std::map<uint32_t, td_hit_t> tds_by_rva;   // image-relative offset

    for (const auto& sp : spans) {
        if (sp.raw_size < 20) continue;
        const uint8_t* base = file.data() + sp.file_off;
        for (size_t i = 16; i + 4 <= sp.raw_size; ++i) {
            if (!(base[i] == '.' && base[i+1] == '?' &&
                  (base[i+2] == 'A' || base[i+2] == 'W')))
                continue;
            // Name must be NUL-terminated within the span
            size_t end = i;
            while (end < sp.raw_size && base[end] != 0) ++end;
            if (end >= sp.raw_size || end == i) continue;
            const std::string name(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(base + i),
                                   end - i);

            td_hit_t hit;
            hit.va   = sp.va + (i - 16);       // name starts after vfptr+spare
            hit.rva  = static_cast<uint32_t>(hit.va - pe.image_base);
            hit.name = demangle_msvc_name(name);
            tds_by_rva[hit.rva] = hit;
            i = end;                            // skip past this name
        }
    }

    // pass 2: complete object locators
    struct col_hit_t {
        uint64_t va;
        uint32_t td_rva;
    };
    std::map<uint32_t, col_hit_t> cols_by_rva;

    for (const auto& sp : spans) {
        if (sp.raw_size < 24) continue;
        const uint8_t* base = file.data() + sp.file_off;
        for (size_t i = 0; i + 24 <= sp.raw_size; i += 4) {
            const auto rd32 = [base](size_t o) {
                uint32_t v;
                std::memcpy(&v, base + o, 4);
                return v;
            };
            if (rd32(i) != 0) continue;                       // signature x64
            const uint32_t td_rva = rd32(i + 12);
            const uint32_t self_rva = rd32(i + 20);
            const uint32_t self_calc =
                static_cast<uint32_t>(sp.va + i - pe.image_base);
            if (self_rva != self_calc) continue;              // self must match
            if (!tds_by_rva.count(td_rva)) continue;          // must hit a TD

            col_hit_t hit;
            hit.va     = sp.va + i;
            hit.td_rva = td_rva;
            cols_by_rva[self_calc] = hit;
        }
    }

    // pass 3: vftables whose [-1] slot points at a COL
    for (const auto& sp : spans) {
        if (sp.raw_size < 8) continue;
        const uint8_t* base = file.data() + sp.file_off;
        for (size_t i = 0; i + 8 <= sp.raw_size; i += 8) {
            uint64_t ptr;
            std::memcpy(&ptr, base + i, 8);
            if (ptr < pe.image_base || ptr < pe.image_base + 0x1000) continue;
            const uint64_t target_rva = ptr - pe.image_base;
            const auto it = cols_by_rva.find(
                static_cast<uint32_t>(target_rva));
            if (it == cols_by_rva.end()) continue;

            const uint64_t vftable_va = sp.va + i + 8;   // [-1] slot
            const auto& td = tds_by_rva[it->second.td_rva];
            auto& cls = [&]() -> rtti_class_t& {
                for (auto& c : res.classes)
                    if (c.td_va == td.va) return c;
                rtti_class_t nc;
                nc.name = td.name;
                nc.td_va = td.va;
                res.classes.push_back(nc);
                return res.classes.back();
            }();
            cls.col_vas.push_back(it->second.va);
            cls.vftables.push_back(vftable_va);
        }
    }

    std::sort(res.classes.begin(), res.classes.end(),
              [](const rtti_class_t& a, const rtti_class_t& b) {
                  return a.name < b.name;
              });
    return res;
}

rtti_result_t rtti_scan_itanium(const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
                                const std::vector<uint8_t>& file,
                                unsigned ptr_size) {
    rtti_result_t res;
    if (!pe.ok) return res;
    std::vector<hype::RttiSpan> spans;
    for (const auto& sp : data_spans(pe, file, true)) {
        res.scanned_bytes += sp.raw_size;
        spans.push_back({sp.va, std::span<const uint8_t>(file.data() + sp.file_off, sp.raw_size),
                         sp.exec});
    }
    for (auto& c : hype::scan_itanium_rtti(spans, ptr_size)) {
        rtti_class_t r;
        r.name     = std::move(c.name);
        r.mangled  = std::move(c.mangled);
        r.td_va    = c.type_info;
        r.vftables = std::move(c.vtables);
        r.methods  = std::move(c.methods);
        r.bases    = std::move(c.bases);
        res.classes.push_back(std::move(r));
    }
    return res;
}

std::optional<std::vector<uint64_t>> read_vftable(
    const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
    const std::vector<uint8_t>& file,
    uint64_t vftable_va, size_t max_slots) {
    auto off = pe.va_to_offset(vftable_va);
    if (!off || *off + max_slots * 8 > file.size()) return std::nullopt;
    std::vector<uint64_t> out;
    out.reserve(max_slots);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < max_slots; ++i) {
        uint64_t ptr;
        std::memcpy(&ptr, file.data() + *off + i * 8, 8);
        if (ptr == 0) break;
        // Stop at the first entry that leaves the image, end of table
        if (ptr < pe.image_base ||
            ptr >= pe.image_base + pe.size_of_image)
            break;
        out.push_back(ptr);
    }
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::re

```

`src/core/re/rtti.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// quick RTTI reconstruction without a hyperion session. MSVC x64 (PE): type
// descriptors by name, locators by self offsets, vftables by their minus one
// slot. Itanium ABI (ELF, PS4 clang): type_info objects by their name
// pointer, vtables by offset_to_top + type_info pointer

#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/disasm/pe_parser.hpp"

namespace slop::core::re {

struct rtti_class_t {
    std::string             name;        // demangled: "MyClass" from ".?AVMyClass@@" / "7MyClass"
    std::string             mangled;     // Itanium type_info name ("N2ns5InnerE"); empty for MSVC
    uint64_t                td_va = 0;   // TypeDescriptor VA / Itanium type_info VA
    std::vector<uint64_t>   col_vas;     // MSVC Complete Object Locator VAs
    std::vector<uint64_t>   vftables;    // vftable VAs (first virtual function slot)
    std::vector<uint64_t>   methods;     // Itanium: primary vtable's virtual functions
    std::vector<std::string> bases;      // Itanium: direct bases
};

struct rtti_result_t {
    std::vector<rtti_class_t> classes;
    size_t scanned_bytes = 0;
};

// MSVC RTTI in the non-executable sections of a PE image
rtti_result_t rtti_scan(const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
                        const std::vector<uint8_t>& file);

// Itanium RTTI over every section of an ELF image (`file` must hold
// relocated pointers). ptr_size 8 for x64/AArch64, 4 for 32-bit images
rtti_result_t rtti_scan_itanium(const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
                                const std::vector<uint8_t>& file,
                                unsigned ptr_size = 8);

// Read up to `max_slots` function pointers starting at `vftable_va`
std::optional<std::vector<uint64_t>> read_vftable(
    const disasm::pe_image_t& pe,
    const std::vector<uint8_t>& file,
    uint64_t vftable_va, size_t max_slots = 32);

} // namespace slop::core::re
```
