`src/core/re/type_catalog.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/re/type_catalog.cpp

#include "core/re/type_catalog.hpp"

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include "core/infra/paths.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>
#include <map>

namespace slop::core::re::type_catalog {

namespace {

using json = nlohmann::json;

struct catalog_t {
    // recursive: add_member holds the lock and layout_struct() calls
    // get_struct()/get_enum(), which take it again
    std::recursive_mutex mu;
    std::map<std::string, struct_def_t> structs;
    std::map<std::string, enum_def_t>   enums;
    uint64_t bound_hash = 0;             // binary hash this catalog mirrors
};

catalog_t g_cat;

// bumped by every mutation and by bind_binary; the decompile cache stamps
// entries with it so an edit re-renders on the next decomp.function
std::atomic<uint64_t> g_generation{1};

void bump_generation() { g_generation.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release); }

std::string store_dir() {
    const std::string& base = infra::paths::app_data();
    if (base.empty()) return {};
    const std::string dir = base + "/types";
    std::error_code ec;
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir, ec);
    return dir;
}

std::string store_path(uint64_t hash) {
    const std::string dir = store_dir();
    if (dir.empty()) return {};
    char name[32];
    std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "%016llX.json",
                  static_cast<unsigned long long>(hash));
    return dir + "\\" + name;
}

json to_json(const catalog_t& c) {
    json js = json::object();
    for (const auto& [name, s] : c.structs) {
        json fields = json::array();
        for (const auto& f : s.fields)
            fields.push_back({{"name", f.name}, {"type", f.type},
                              {"offset", f.offset}, {"size", f.size},
                              {"array_count", f.array_count}});
        js[name] = {{"size", s.size}, {"packed", s.packed}, {"fields", fields}};
    }
    json je = json::object();
    for (const auto& [name, e] : c.enums) {
        json vals = json::array();
        for (const auto& [vn, vv] : e.values)
            vals.push_back({{"name", vn}, {"value", vv}});
        je[name] = {{"underlying", e.underlying}, {"values", vals}};
    }
    json root = json::object();
    root["structs"] = js;
    root["enums"]   = je;
    return root;
}

void from_json(const json& root, catalog_t& c) {
    c.structs.clear();
    c.enums.clear();
    if (root.contains("structs")) {
        for (auto it = root["structs"].begin(); it != root["structs"].end(); ++it) {
            struct_def_t s;
            s.name   = it.key();
            s.size   = it.value().value("size", 0ull);
            s.packed = it.value().value("packed", false);
            if (it.value().contains("fields"))
                for (const auto& f : it.value()["fields"]) {
                    field_t fld;
                    fld.name = f.value("name", "");
                    fld.type = f.value("type", "");
                    fld.offset = f.value("offset", 0ull);
                    fld.size = f.value("size", 0ull);
                    fld.array_count = f.value("array_count", 0u);
                    s.fields.push_back(std::move(fld));
                }
            c.structs[s.name] = std::move(s);
        }
    }
    if (root.contains("enums")) {
        for (auto it = root["enums"].begin(); it != root["enums"].end(); ++it) {
            enum_def_t e;
            e.name = it.key();
            e.underlying = it.value().value("underlying", "u32");
            if (it.value().contains("values"))
                for (const auto& v : it.value()["values"])
                    e.values.emplace_back(v.value("name", ""),
                                          v.value("value", static_cast<int64_t>(0)));
            c.enums[e.name] = std::move(e);
        }
    }
}

bool save_locked(const catalog_t& c) {
    if (!c.bound_hash) return false;
    const std::string path = store_path(c.bound_hash);
    if (path.empty()) return false;
    std::ofstream f(path, std::ios::trunc);
    if (!f) return false;
    f << to_json(c).dump(2);
    return true;
}

// Bind to a binary's hash and load its persisted catalog (called from
// bind_binary on session open)
void load_locked(catalog_t& c) {
    if (!c.bound_hash) return;
    const std::string path = store_path(c.bound_hash);
    if (path.empty()) return;
    std::ifstream f(path);
    if (!f) return;
    try {
        json j;
        f >> j;
        from_json(j, c);
    } catch (...) {
        c.structs.clear();
        c.enums.clear();
    }
}

} // namespace

// the binding lives here since binary_state depends on this host layer

void bind_binary(const uint8_t* bytes, size_t len);

void bind_binary(const uint8_t* bytes, size_t len) {
    uint64_t h = 1469598103934665603ull;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; ++i) {
        h ^= bytes[i];
        h *= 1099511628211ull;
    }
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    g_cat.structs.clear();
    g_cat.enums.clear();
    g_cat.bound_hash = h;
    load_locked(g_cat);
    bump_generation();
}

// mini parser

namespace {

bool ident_start(char c) {
    return isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) || c == '_';
}
bool ident_char(char c) {
    return isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) || c == '_';
}

struct tokenizer_t {
    explicit tokenizer_t(const std::string& src) : s(src) {}

    void skip_ws() {
        while (pos < s.size() && isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[pos]))) ++pos;
    }

    std::string next() {
        skip_ws();
        if (pos >= s.size()) return {};
        const char c = s[pos];
        if (ident_start(c)) {
            const size_t start = pos;
            while (pos < s.size() && ident_char(s[pos])) ++pos;
            return s.substr(start, pos - start);
        }
        if (isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) ||
            ((c == '-' || c == '+') && pos + 1 < s.size() &&
             isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[pos + 1])))) {
            const size_t start = pos;
            ++pos;
            while (pos < s.size() &&
                   (isxdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(s[pos])) ||
                    s[pos] == 'x' || s[pos] == 'X'))
                ++pos;
            return s.substr(start, pos - start);
        }
        ++pos;
        return std::string(1, c);
    }

    std::string peek() {
        const size_t save = pos;
        const std::string t = next();
        pos = save;
        return t;
    }

    const std::string& s;
    size_t pos = 0;
};

} // namespace

uint64_t base_type_size(const std::string& type) {
    if (!type.empty() && type.back() == '*') return 8;
    if (type == "u8" || type == "i8" || type == "int8" || type == "uint8" ||
        type == "char" || type == "bool") return 1;
    if (type == "u16" || type == "i16" || type == "int16" || type == "uint16" ||
        type == "wchar_t") return 2;
    if (type == "u32" || type == "i32" || type == "int32" || type == "uint32" ||
        type == "float") return 4;
    if (type == "u64" || type == "i64" || type == "int64" || type == "uint64" ||
        type == "double" || type == "__int64") return 8;
    return 0;   // unknown -> named struct reference
}

void layout_struct(struct_def_t& def) {
    uint64_t off = 0, max_align = 1;
    for (auto& f : def.fields) {
        uint64_t sz = base_type_size(f.type);
        if (sz == 0) {
            // Named struct member (or pointer to one)
            std::string nm = f.type;
            bool ptr = !nm.empty() && nm.back() == '*';
            if (ptr) nm.pop_back();
            sz = 0;
            if (auto inner = get_struct(nm)) sz = inner->size;
            else if (auto en = get_enum(nm))
                sz = base_type_size(en->underlying);
            else sz = ptr ? 8 : 0;
            if (ptr) sz = 8;
        }
        if (f.array_count) sz *= f.array_count;
        if (sz == 0) { f.offset = off; continue; }

        const uint64_t align = def.packed ? 1 : std::min<uint64_t>(sz, 8);
        max_align = std::max(max_align, align);
        off = (off + align - 1) / align * align;
        f.offset = off;
        off += sz;
        f.size = sz;
    }
    def.size = def.packed ? off
                          : ((off + max_align - 1) / max_align) * max_align;
}

decl_parse_result_t parse_decls(const std::string& text) {
    decl_parse_result_t out;
    tokenizer_t tk(text);

    // Batch-local name resolution: members may reference types declared
    // earlier in the same declaration string (before the catalog knows them)
    std::map<std::string, uint64_t> batch_sizes;
    auto batch_lookup = [&batch_sizes](const std::string& n) -> uint64_t {
        const auto it = batch_sizes.find(n);
        return it != batch_sizes.end() ? it->second : 0;
    };
    auto layout_batch = [&](struct_def_t& def) {
        uint64_t off = 0, max_align = 1;
        for (auto& f : def.fields) {
            uint64_t sz = base_type_size(f.type);
            if (sz == 0) {
                std::string nm = f.type;
                const bool ptr = !nm.empty() && nm.back() == '*';
                if (ptr) nm.pop_back();
                sz = batch_lookup(nm);
                if (!sz && ptr) sz = 8;
            }
            if (f.array_count) sz *= f.array_count;
            if (sz == 0) { f.offset = off; continue; }
            const uint64_t align = def.packed ? 1 : std::min<uint64_t>(sz, 8);
            max_align = std::max(max_align, align);
            off = (off + align - 1) / align * align;
            f.offset = off;
            off += sz;
            f.size = sz;
        }
        def.size = def.packed ? off
                              : ((off + max_align - 1) / max_align) * max_align;
        batch_sizes[def.name] = def.size;
    };

    for (;;) {
        std::string kw = tk.next();
        if (kw.empty()) break;
        if (kw == ";") continue;   // stray terminators between definitions
        if (kw != "struct" && kw != "enum") {
            out.error = "expected 'struct' or 'enum', got '" + kw + "'";
            return out;
        }

        const std::string name = tk.next();
        if (name.empty() || name == "{") {
            out.error = "missing type name";
            return out;
        }

        if (kw == "enum") {
            enum_def_t e;
            e.name = name;
            if (tk.peek() == ":") { tk.next(); e.underlying = tk.next(); }
            if (tk.next() != "{") { out.error = "enum: expected '{'"; return out; }
            int64_t next_val = 0;
            for (;;) {
                std::string vn = tk.next();
                if (vn.empty()) { out.error = "enum: unexpected end"; return out; }
                if (vn == "}") break;
                if (vn == ",") continue;
                const std::string eq = tk.next();
                if (eq == "=") {
                    try {
                        next_val = static_cast<int64_t>(
                            std::stoull(tk.next(), nullptr, 0));
                    } catch (...) { out.error = "enum: bad value"; return out; }
                } else if (eq != "," && eq != "}") {
                    out.error = "enum: expected '=' after '" + vn + "'";
                    return out;
                }
                e.values.emplace_back(vn, next_val++);
                if (eq == "}") break;
            }
            out.enums.push_back(std::move(e));
        } else {
            struct_def_t s;
            s.name = name;
            if (tk.peek() == "packed") { tk.next(); s.packed = true; }
            if (tk.next() != "{") { out.error = "struct: expected '{'"; return out; }
            for (;;) {
                std::string ftype = tk.next();
                if (ftype == "}" || ftype.empty()) break;
                if (ftype == ";") continue;

                std::string tok = tk.peek();
                while (tok == "*") { tk.next(); ftype += "*"; tok = tk.peek(); }

                field_t f;
                f.type = ftype;
                f.name = tk.next();
                if (f.name.empty()) { out.error = "struct: missing member name"; return out; }

                std::string post = tk.next();
                if (post == "[") {
                    try {
                        f.array_count = static_cast<uint32_t>(
                            std::stoul(tk.next(), nullptr, 0));
                    } catch (...) { out.error = "struct: bad array count"; return out; }
                    if (tk.next() != "]") { out.error = "struct: expected ']'"; return out; }
                    post = tk.next();
                }
                if (post != ";" && post != "}") {
                    out.error = "struct: expected ';' after member";
                    return out;
                }
                s.fields.push_back(std::move(f));
                if (post == "}") break;
            }
            // trailing packed after the brace, the form the tool description documents
            if (tk.peek() == "packed") {
                tk.next();
                s.packed = true;
                if (tk.peek() == ";") tk.next();
            }
            layout_batch(s);
            out.structs.push_back(std::move(s));
        }
    }
    return out;
}

// queries

std::optional<struct_def_t> get_struct(const std::string& name) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    const auto it = g_cat.structs.find(name);
    if (it == g_cat.structs.end()) return std::nullopt;
    return it->second;
}

std::optional<enum_def_t> get_enum(const std::string& name) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    const auto it = g_cat.enums.find(name);
    if (it == g_cat.enums.end()) return std::nullopt;
    return it->second;
}

std::vector<struct_def_t> list_structs(const std::string& filter) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    std::vector<struct_def_t> out;
    for (const auto& [name, s] : g_cat.structs)
        if (filter.empty() || name.find(filter) != std::string::npos)
            out.push_back(s);
    return out;
}

std::vector<enum_def_t> list_enums(const std::string& filter) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    std::vector<enum_def_t> out;
    for (const auto& [name, e] : g_cat.enums)
        if (filter.empty() || name.find(filter) != std::string::npos)
            out.push_back(e);
    return out;
}

// mutations

bool create_struct(struct_def_t def, std::string* error) {
    if (def.name.empty()) { if (error) *error = "missing name"; return false; }
    layout_struct(def);
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    g_cat.structs[def.name] = std::move(def);
    if (!save_locked(g_cat)) { if (error) *error = "persist failed"; return false; }
    bump_generation();
    return true;
}

bool add_member(const std::string& struct_name, const field_t& field,
                std::string* error) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    const auto it = g_cat.structs.find(struct_name);
    if (it == g_cat.structs.end()) { if (error) *error = "unknown struct"; return false; }
    it->second.fields.push_back(field);
    layout_struct(it->second);
    if (!save_locked(g_cat)) { if (error) *error = "persist failed"; return false; }
    bump_generation();
    return true;
}

bool remove_struct(const std::string& name) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    const size_t n = g_cat.structs.erase(name);
    if (n) { save_locked(g_cat); bump_generation(); }
    return n != 0;
}

bool create_enum(enum_def_t def, std::string* error) {
    if (def.name.empty() || def.values.empty()) {
        if (error) *error = "missing name/values";
        return false;
    }
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    g_cat.enums[def.name] = std::move(def);
    if (!save_locked(g_cat)) { if (error) *error = "persist failed"; return false; }
    bump_generation();
    return true;
}

bool remove_enum(const std::string& name) {
    std::lock_guard lk(g_cat.mu);
    const size_t n = g_cat.enums.erase(name);
    if (n) { save_locked(g_cat); bump_generation(); }
    return n != 0;
}

uint64_t generation() { return g_generation.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }

// field reads

field_value_t read_field(const struct_def_t& strct, const std::string& field_name,
                         uint64_t base_va,
                         const uint8_t* file_bytes, size_t file_len,
                         read_cb_t reader, void* reader_user) {
    field_value_t out;
    const field_t* fld = nullptr;
    for (const auto& f : strct.fields)
        if (f.name == field_name) { fld = &f; break; }
    if (!fld) { out.error = "unknown field '" + field_name + "'"; return out; }

    // raw buffer view at base_va when provided, else the reader callback
    // fetches live memory
    const uint64_t rel_off = base_va + fld->offset;
    const size_t len = static_cast<size_t>(
        std::min<uint64_t>(fld->size ? fld->size : base_type_size(fld->type),
                           64));
    uint8_t buf[64]{};

    bool got = false;
    if (file_bytes && file_len && rel_off < file_len) {
        std::memcpy(buf, file_bytes + rel_off,
                    std::min<size_t>(len, file_len - rel_off));
        got = true;
    }
    if (!got && reader) got = reader(rel_off, buf, len, reader_user);
    if (!got) { out.error = "read failed at requested range"; return out; }

    out.ok = true;
    out.hex.resize(len * 2);
    static const char* d = "0123456789abcdef";
    for (size_t i = 0; i < len; ++i) {
        out.hex[i * 2]     = d[buf[i] >> 4];
        out.hex[i * 2 + 1] = d[buf[i] & 0xF];
    }

    if (len >= 8) {
        uint64_t v; std::memcpy(&v, buf, 8);
        out.uint_val = v; out.int_val = static_cast<int64_t>(v);
        if (fld->type == "double") std::memcpy(&out.dbl_val, buf, 8);
    } else if (len >= 4) {
        uint32_t v; std::memcpy(&v, buf, 4);
        out.uint_val = v; out.int_val = static_cast<int32_t>(v);
        if (fld->type == "float") { float f2; std::memcpy(&f2, buf, 4); out.dbl_val = f2; }
    } else if (len >= 2) {
        uint16_t v; std::memcpy(&v, buf, 2);
        out.uint_val = v; out.int_val = static_cast<int16_t>(v);
    } else if (len >= 1) {
        out.uint_val = buf[0]; out.int_val = static_cast<int8_t>(buf[0]);
    }
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::re::type_catalog
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// the struct and enum catalog over the loaded binary, computed layouts,
// a mini c parser, field reads from the file image or live memory,
// persisted per binary hash

#include <cstdint>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::re::type_catalog {

struct field_t {
    std::string name;
    std::string type;            // "u8..u64,i8..i64,f32,f64,ptr,<StructName>,char[N]"
    uint64_t    offset = 0;
    uint64_t    size   = 0;
    uint32_t    array_count = 0; // 0 = scalar
};

struct struct_def_t {
    std::string          name;
    uint64_t             size = 0;
    bool                 packed = false;
    std::vector<field_t> fields;
};

struct enum_def_t {
    std::string name;
    std::string underlying = "u32";
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, int64_t>> values;
};

// binary binding

// rebind to a binary hash and load its persisted types, safe to repeat
void bind_binary(const uint8_t* bytes, size_t len);

// queries

std::optional<struct_def_t> get_struct(const std::string& name);
std::optional<enum_def_t>   get_enum(const std::string& name);
std::vector<struct_def_t>   list_structs(const std::string& filter = "");
std::vector<enum_def_t>     list_enums(const std::string& filter = "");

// mutations (persist immediately)

// Monotonic counter bumped by every mutation and by bind_binary. Consumers
// that cache derived output (the decompiler) compare it to re-render.
uint64_t generation();

bool create_struct(struct_def_t def, std::string* error = nullptr);
bool add_member(const std::string& struct_name, const field_t& field,
                std::string* error = nullptr);
bool remove_struct(const std::string& name);
bool create_enum(enum_def_t def, std::string* error = nullptr);
bool remove_enum(const std::string& name);

// Layout helper: compute offsets/sizes for a struct definition in place
void layout_struct(struct_def_t& def);

// the mini c declaration parser, accepts one or more definitions
//   struct Name { u32 a; char b[16]; Other* c; i64 d; };
//   enum Tag : u8 { A = 1, B, C = 0x10 };
// base types are the iN uN float double family, pointers via trailing *

struct decl_parse_result_t {
    std::vector<struct_def_t> structs;
    std::vector<enum_def_t>   enums;
    std::string               error;
};

decl_parse_result_t parse_decls(const std::string& text);

// Type size lookup used by the parser and field readers (bytes)
uint64_t base_type_size(const std::string& type);

// field reads

struct field_value_t {
    bool        ok = false;
    std::string error;
    std::string hex;
    uint64_t    uint_val = 0;
    int64_t     int_val  = 0;
    double      dbl_val  = 0;
};

// read one field at base va from the file image or the live reader
using read_cb_t = bool (*)(uint64_t addr, void* dst, size_t len, void* user);
field_value_t read_field(const struct_def_t& strct, const std::string& field_name,
                         uint64_t base_va,
                         const uint8_t* file_bytes, size_t file_len,
                         read_cb_t reader, void* reader_user);

} // namespace slop::core::re::type_catalog
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/runtime/backend.hpp
// one interface: local user mode (test lab) and the remote PS4 console

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::runtime {

// enums

enum class backend_kind_t : uint8_t {
    user_mode,   // local process (internal test lab only)
    ps4,         // remote console over ps4debug-NG
    ps5          // remote console over ps5debug-NG
};

enum class arch_t : uint8_t {
    unknown,
    x86,
    x64,
    arm64
};

enum class elevation_t : uint8_t {
    unknown,
    standard,
    elevated,
    system
};

// pod types

struct process_info_t {
    uint32_t    pid          = 0;
    uint32_t    parent_pid   = 0;
    arch_t      arch         = arch_t::unknown;
    elevation_t elevation    = elevation_t::unknown;
    std::string name;
    std::string path;
};

struct module_info_t {
    uintptr_t   base         = 0;
    uint32_t    size         = 0;
    std::string name;
    std::string path;
};

struct thread_info_t {
    uint32_t tid             = 0;
    uint32_t owner_pid       = 0;
    uintptr_t start_address  = 0;
    int32_t  priority        = 0;
    std::string name;               // thread name when the backend knows it
};

struct region_info_t {
    uintptr_t base           = 0;
    size_t    size           = 0;
    uint32_t  protect        = 0;
    uint32_t  state          = 0;
    uint32_t  type           = 0;
};

struct handle_info_t {
    uintptr_t handle_value   = 0;
    uint32_t  type_index     = 0;
    uint32_t  granted_access = 0;
    std::string type_name;
    std::string object_name;
};

struct thread_context_t {
    uint64_t rip = 0;
    uint64_t rsp = 0;
    uint64_t rbp = 0;
    uint64_t rax = 0;
    uint64_t rbx = 0;
    uint64_t rcx = 0;
    uint64_t rdx = 0;
    uint64_t rsi = 0;
    uint64_t rdi = 0;
    uint64_t r8  = 0;
    uint64_t r9  = 0;
    uint64_t r10 = 0;
    uint64_t r11 = 0;
    uint64_t r12 = 0;
    uint64_t r13 = 0;
    uint64_t r14 = 0;
    uint64_t r15 = 0;
    uint64_t flags = 0;
};

struct target_handle_t {
    void*    native  = nullptr;
    uint32_t pid     = 0;
    bool     valid() const noexcept { return native != nullptr && pid != 0; }
};

struct io_result_t {
    bool     ok      = false;
    size_t   bytes   = 0;
    uint32_t error   = 0;
};

template <typename T>
struct enum_result_t {
    bool           ok    = false;
    uint32_t       error = 0;
    std::vector<T> items;
};

// the backend interface

class backend_t {
public:
    virtual ~backend_t() = default;

    // identity
    virtual backend_kind_t kind() const noexcept = 0;
    virtual const char*    badge() const noexcept = 0;

    // attach and detach
    virtual target_handle_t attach(uint32_t pid) = 0;
    virtual void            detach(target_handle_t& h) = 0;

    // memory
    virtual io_result_t read_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr, void* buf, size_t len) = 0;
    virtual io_result_t write_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr, const void* buf, size_t len) = 0;
    virtual io_result_t protect_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr, size_t len, uint32_t new_prot, uint32_t* old_prot) = 0;
    virtual io_result_t allocate_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr, size_t len, uint32_t prot, uintptr_t* out_addr) = 0;
    virtual io_result_t free_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr) = 0;

    // enumeration
    virtual enum_result_t<process_info_t> enum_processes() = 0;
    virtual enum_result_t<module_info_t>  enum_modules(const target_handle_t& h) = 0;
    virtual enum_result_t<thread_info_t>  enum_threads(uint32_t pid) = 0;
    virtual enum_result_t<region_info_t>  enum_regions(const target_handle_t& h) = 0;
    virtual enum_result_t<handle_info_t>  enum_handles(uint32_t pid) = 0;

    // thread context
    virtual io_result_t get_thread_context(uint32_t tid, thread_context_t& ctx) = 0;
    virtual io_result_t set_thread_context(uint32_t tid, const thread_context_t& ctx) = 0;

    // query
    virtual arch_t      query_arch(const target_handle_t& h) = 0;
    virtual elevation_t query_elevation() = 0;

    // identity of an attached handle (name/path/arch/elevation) without a
    // full process enumeration; false = backend cannot tell cheaply
    virtual bool handle_info(const target_handle_t& h, process_info_t& out) {
        (void)h; (void)out;
        return false;
    }
};

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```

`src/core/runtime/backend_posix.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/runtime/backend_posix.cpp
// POSIX (Linux) user-mode backend: /proc for enumeration, process_vm_readv /
// process_vm_writev for memory (with a /proc/<pid>/mem fallback).
//
// Capabilities are reported, not invented: protect/alloc/free only work on
// this process (mprotect/mmap need the target's address space), thread
// contexts and handles are not implemented, and cross-process memory access
// needs CAP_SYS_PTRACE or a parent/child relationship (Yama ptrace_scope).

#include "core/runtime/backend_posix.hpp"

#include "core/infra/limits.hpp"

#include <dirent.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/uio.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>
#include <map>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::runtime {

namespace infra = slop::core::infra;

namespace {

// Windows protection vocabulary the rest of the engine speaks
constexpr uint32_t kPageNoAccess       = 0x01;
constexpr uint32_t kPageReadOnly       = 0x02;
constexpr uint32_t kPageReadWrite      = 0x04;
constexpr uint32_t kPageExecute        = 0x10;
constexpr uint32_t kPageExecuteRead    = 0x20;
constexpr uint32_t kPageExecuteReadWrite = 0x40;
constexpr uint32_t kMemCommit          = 0x1000;
constexpr uint32_t kMemPrivate         = 0x20000;
constexpr uint32_t kMemMapped          = 0x40000;
constexpr uint32_t kMemImage           = 0x1000000;

constexpr uint32_t kErrInvalidHandle = 6;    // ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE
constexpr uint32_t kErrNotSupported  = 50;   // ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED

struct attach_state_t {
    int      mem_fd = -1;
    uint32_t pid    = 0;
};

std::string read_link(const std::string& path) {
    char buf[4096];
    const ssize_t n = ::readlink(path.c_str(), buf, sizeof(buf) - 1);
    if (n <= 0) return {};
    buf[n] = '\0';
    return buf;
}

std::string read_file(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) return {};
    std::ostringstream ss;
    ss << f.rdbuf();
    return ss.str();
}

// /proc/<pid>/stat: "pid (comm) state ppid ..." - comm may contain spaces and
// parentheses, so parse from the last ')'
bool stat_fields(uint32_t pid, std::string& comm, uint32_t& ppid) {
    const std::string s = read_file("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/stat");
    const size_t open = s.find('(');
    const size_t close = s.rfind(')');
    if (open == std::string::npos || close == std::string::npos || close < open) return false;
    comm = s.substr(open + 1, close - open - 1);
    std::istringstream rest(s.substr(close + 1));
    std::string state;
    rest >> state >> ppid;
    return !rest.fail();
}

arch_t arch_of_pid(uint32_t pid) {
    // ELF class of the executable: 1 = 32-bit, 2 = 64-bit
    const std::string exe = read_link("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/exe");
    if (exe.empty()) return arch_t::unknown;
    std::ifstream f(exe, std::ios::binary);
    unsigned char hdr[5]{};
    if (!f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(hdr), sizeof(hdr))) return arch_t::unknown;
    if (hdr[0] != 0x7F || hdr[1] != 'E' || hdr[2] != 'L' || hdr[3] != 'F') return arch_t::unknown;
    if (hdr[4] == 1) return arch_t::x86;
    if (hdr[4] == 2) return arch_t::x64;
    return arch_t::unknown;
}

uint32_t protect_from_perms(const std::string& perms) {
    const bool r = perms.size() > 0 && perms[0] == 'r';
    const bool w = perms.size() > 1 && perms[1] == 'w';
    const bool x = perms.size() > 2 && perms[2] == 'x';
    if (x && w) return kPageExecuteReadWrite;
    if (x && r) return kPageExecuteRead;
    if (x) return kPageExecute;
    if (w && r) return kPageReadWrite;
    if (r) return kPageReadOnly;
    return kPageNoAccess;
}

struct map_line_t {
    uintptr_t start = 0;
    uintptr_t end   = 0;
    std::string perms;
    std::string path;
};

std::vector<map_line_t> read_maps(uint32_t pid) {
    std::vector<map_line_t> out;
    std::ifstream f("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/maps");
    std::string line;
    while (std::getline(f, line)) {
        std::istringstream ss(line);
        std::string range, perms, offset, dev, inode;
        if (!(ss >> range >> perms >> offset >> dev >> inode)) continue;
        const size_t dash = range.find('-');
        if (dash == std::string::npos) continue;
        map_line_t m;
        m.start = std::strtoull(range.substr(0, dash).c_str(), nullptr, 16);
        m.end   = std::strtoull(range.substr(dash + 1).c_str(), nullptr, 16);
        m.perms = perms;
        std::string rest;
        std::getline(ss, rest);
        const size_t first = rest.find_first_not_of(' ');
        if (first != std::string::npos) m.path = rest.substr(first);
        out.push_back(std::move(m));
        if (out.size() >= infra::limits::max_regions_enumerated) break;
    }
    return out;
}

bool is_self(uint32_t pid) { return pid == static_cast<uint32_t>(::getpid()); }

} // namespace

// identity

backend_kind_t backend_posix_t::kind() const noexcept { return backend_kind_t::user_mode; }

const char* backend_posix_t::badge() const noexcept { return "posix"; }

// attach / detach

target_handle_t backend_posix_t::attach(uint32_t pid) {
    target_handle_t t;
    if (pid == 0) return t;
    auto* st = new attach_state_t;
    st->pid = pid;
    st->mem_fd = ::open(("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/mem").c_str(), O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
    if (st->mem_fd < 0)
        st->mem_fd = ::open(("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/mem").c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
    // a live pid with no readable mem is still a usable handle for enumeration
    if (::kill(static_cast<pid_t>(pid), 0) != 0 && st->mem_fd < 0) {
        delete st;
        return t;
    }
    t.pid = pid;
    t.native = st;
    return t;
}

void backend_posix_t::detach(target_handle_t& h) {
    if (auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native)) {
        if (st->mem_fd >= 0) ::close(st->mem_fd);
        delete st;
    }
    h.native = nullptr;
    h.pid = 0;
}

// memory

io_result_t backend_posix_t::read_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr,
                                         void* buf, size_t len) {
    io_result_t r;
    if (len == 0) { r.ok = true; return r; }
    auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native);
    if (!st) { r.error = kErrInvalidHandle; return r; }

    iovec local{buf, len};
    iovec remote{reinterpret_cast<void*>(addr), len};
    const ssize_t n = ::process_vm_readv(static_cast<pid_t>(st->pid), &local, 1, &remote, 1, 0);
    if (n > 0) {
        r.bytes = static_cast<size_t>(n);
        r.ok = r.bytes == len;
        if (!r.ok) r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
        return r;
    }
    if (st->mem_fd >= 0) {
        const ssize_t m = ::pread(st->mem_fd, buf, len, static_cast<off_t>(addr));
        if (m > 0) {
            r.bytes = static_cast<size_t>(m);
            r.ok = r.bytes == len;
            if (!r.ok) r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
            return r;
        }
    }
    r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
    return r;
}

io_result_t backend_posix_t::write_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr,
                                          const void* buf, size_t len) {
    io_result_t r;
    if (len == 0) { r.ok = true; return r; }
    auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native);
    if (!st) { r.error = kErrInvalidHandle; return r; }

    iovec local{const_cast<void*>(buf), len};
    iovec remote{reinterpret_cast<void*>(addr), len};
    const ssize_t n = ::process_vm_writev(static_cast<pid_t>(st->pid), &local, 1, &remote, 1, 0);
    if (n > 0) {
        r.bytes = static_cast<size_t>(n);
        r.ok = r.bytes == len;
        if (!r.ok) r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
        return r;
    }
    if (st->mem_fd >= 0) {
        const ssize_t m = ::pwrite(st->mem_fd, buf, len, static_cast<off_t>(addr));
        if (m > 0) {
            r.bytes = static_cast<size_t>(m);
            r.ok = r.bytes == len;
            if (!r.ok) r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
            return r;
        }
    }
    r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
    return r;
}

io_result_t backend_posix_t::protect_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr,
                                            size_t len, uint32_t new_prot, uint32_t* old_prot) {
    auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native);
    if (!st) return { false, 0, kErrInvalidHandle };
    if (!is_self(st->pid)) {
        // mprotect only ever changes this address space
        return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
    }
    int prot = 0;
    switch (new_prot & 0xFF) {
    case kPageNoAccess: prot = PROT_NONE; break;
    case kPageReadOnly: prot = PROT_READ; break;
    case kPageReadWrite: prot = PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE; break;
    case kPageExecute: prot = PROT_EXEC; break;
    case kPageExecuteRead: prot = PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC; break;
    case kPageExecuteReadWrite: prot = PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC; break;
    default: return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
    }
    const long page = ::sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
    const uintptr_t base = addr & ~static_cast<uintptr_t>(page - 1);
    const size_t span = static_cast<size_t>(addr + len - base);
    if (::mprotect(reinterpret_cast<void*>(base), span, prot) != 0)
        return { false, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(errno) };
    if (old_prot) *old_prot = 0;   // /proc/<pid>/maps has it, mprotect does not
    return { true, len, 0 };
}

io_result_t backend_posix_t::allocate_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr,
                                             size_t len, uint32_t prot, uintptr_t* out_addr) {
    auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native);
    if (!st) return { false, 0, kErrInvalidHandle };
    if (!is_self(st->pid)) return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
    int p = PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE;
    if ((prot & 0xFF) == kPageExecute || (prot & 0xFF) == kPageExecuteRead ||
        (prot & 0xFF) == kPageExecuteReadWrite)
        p |= PROT_EXEC;
    void* got = ::mmap(reinterpret_cast<void*>(addr), len, p,
                       MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
    if (got == MAP_FAILED) return { false, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(errno) };
    if (out_addr) *out_addr = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(got);
    return { true, len, 0 };
}

io_result_t backend_posix_t::free_memory(const target_handle_t& h, uintptr_t addr) {
    auto* st = static_cast<attach_state_t*>(h.native);
    if (!st) return { false, 0, kErrInvalidHandle };
    if (!is_self(st->pid)) return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
    // munmap needs the length: take the mapping that starts at addr
    for (const auto& m : read_maps(st->pid)) {
        if (m.start != addr) continue;
        if (::munmap(reinterpret_cast<void*>(m.start), m.end - m.start) != 0)
            return { false, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(errno) };
        return { true, 0, 0 };
    }
    return { false, 0, static_cast<uint32_t>(ENOENT) };
}

// enumeration

enum_result_t<process_info_t> backend_posix_t::enum_processes() {
    enum_result_t<process_info_t> r;
    r.ok = true;
    DIR* d = ::opendir("/proc");
    if (!d) {
        r.ok = false;
        r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
        return r;
    }
    while (dirent* e = ::readdir(d)) {
        const char* name = e->d_name;
        if (name[0] < '0' || name[0] > '9') continue;
        const uint32_t pid = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::strtoul(name, nullptr, 10));
        process_info_t pi;
        pi.pid = pid;
        std::string comm;
        if (!stat_fields(pid, comm, pi.parent_pid)) continue;
        pi.name = comm;
        pi.path = read_link("/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/exe");
        pi.arch = arch_of_pid(pid);
        pi.elevation = elevation_t::unknown;
        r.items.push_back(std::move(pi));
        if (r.items.size() >= infra::limits::max_handles_enumerated) break;
    }
    ::closedir(d);
    return r;
}

enum_result_t<module_info_t> backend_posix_t::enum_modules(const target_handle_t& h) {
    enum_result_t<module_info_t> r;
    if (!h.valid()) { r.error = kErrInvalidHandle; return r; }
    // one module per mapped file: base = lowest mapping, size = span, and the
    // executable bit of any mapping marks it as code
    std::map<std::string, module_info_t> by_path;
    std::map<std::string, bool> executable;
    for (const auto& m : read_maps(h.pid)) {
        if (m.path.empty() || m.path[0] == '[') continue;
        auto it = by_path.find(m.path);
        if (it == by_path.end()) {
            module_info_t mi;
            mi.base = m.start;
            mi.path = m.path;
            const size_t slash = m.path.find_last_of('/');
            mi.name = slash == std::string::npos ? m.path : m.path.substr(slash + 1);
            by_path.emplace(m.path, std::move(mi));
        } else {
            it->second.base = std::min<uintptr_t>(it->second.base, m.start);
        }
        auto& span = by_path[m.path];
        span.size = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::max<uintptr_t>(span.base + span.size, m.end) -
                                          span.base);
        executable[m.path] = executable[m.path] || (m.perms.size() > 2 && m.perms[2] == 'x');
    }
    r.ok = true;
    for (auto& [path, mi] : by_path) {
        if (!executable[path]) continue;   // data files are not modules
        r.items.push_back(std::move(mi));
    }
    return r;
}

enum_result_t<thread_info_t> backend_posix_t::enum_threads(uint32_t pid) {
    enum_result_t<thread_info_t> r;
    r.ok = true;
    const std::string dir = "/proc/" + std::to_string(pid) + "/task";
    DIR* d = ::opendir(dir.c_str());
    if (!d) {
        r.ok = false;
        r.error = static_cast<uint32_t>(errno);
        return r;
    }
    while (dirent* e = ::readdir(d)) {
        const char* name = e->d_name;
        if (name[0] < '0' || name[0] > '9') continue;
        thread_info_t ti;
        ti.tid = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::strtoul(name, nullptr, 10));
        ti.owner_pid = pid;
        std::string comm;
        uint32_t ppid = 0;
        if (stat_fields(ti.tid, comm, ppid)) ti.name = comm;
        r.items.push_back(std::move(ti));
    }
    ::closedir(d);
    return r;
}

enum_result_t<region_info_t> backend_posix_t::enum_regions(const target_handle_t& h) {
    enum_result_t<region_info_t> r;
    if (!h.valid()) { r.error = kErrInvalidHandle; return r; }
    r.ok = true;
    for (const auto& m : read_maps(h.pid)) {
        region_info_t ri;
        ri.base = m.start;
        ri.size = static_cast<size_t>(m.end - m.start);
        ri.protect = protect_from_perms(m.perms);
        ri.state = kMemCommit;
        if (m.path.empty())
            ri.type = kMemPrivate;
        else if (m.path[0] == '[')
            ri.type = kMemMapped;   // [heap], [stack], [vvar]
        else
            ri.type = kMemImage;
        r.items.push_back(ri);
    }
    return r;
}

enum_result_t<handle_info_t> backend_posix_t::enum_handles(uint32_t) {
    // no handle table to walk; an empty success is the honest answer
    enum_result_t<handle_info_t> r;
    r.ok = true;
    return r;
}

// thread context

io_result_t backend_posix_t::get_thread_context(uint32_t, thread_context_t&) {
    return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
}

io_result_t backend_posix_t::set_thread_context(uint32_t, const thread_context_t&) {
    return { false, 0, kErrNotSupported };
}

// query

arch_t backend_posix_t::query_arch(const target_handle_t& h) {
    if (!h.valid()) return arch_t::unknown;
    return arch_of_pid(h.pid);
}

elevation_t backend_posix_t::query_elevation() {
    return ::geteuid() == 0 ? elevation_t::elevated : elevation_t::standard;
}

bool backend_posix_t::handle_info(const target_handle_t& h, process_info_t& out) {
    if (!h.valid()) return false;
    out = process_info_t{};
    out.pid = h.pid;
    out.path = read_link("/proc/" + std::to_string(h.pid) + "/exe");
    const size_t slash = out.path.find_last_of('/');
    out.name = slash == std::string::npos ? out.path : out.path.substr(slash + 1);
    out.arch = arch_of_pid(h.pid);
    out.elevation = query_elevation();
    return !out.path.empty();
}

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```

`src/core/runtime/backend_ps4.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/runtime/backend_ps4.cpp
// Remote PS4 backend over the ps4debug-NG wire protocol (TCP 744).
// Wire formats verified against the payload sources: every request is a
// 12-byte header {magic, cmd, datalen} followed by datalen body bytes, all
// little-endian; replies start with a u32 status unless noted.
//
// Failure model: every exchange runs under the connection mutex with a
// whole-command deadline on top of the per-chunk idle timeout. Any send/recv
// failure, timeout or malformed reply closes the socket (the stream can no
// longer be trusted), so connected() goes false and every later call fails
// fast instead of paying another timeout. reconnect() restores the session.

#include "core/runtime/backend_ps4.hpp"
#include "core/compat/portable.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <winsock2.h>
#include <ws2tcpip.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <iphlpapi.h>
#else
#include "core/compat/posix_socket.hpp"
#endif

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"
#include "core/infra/diag.hpp"
#include "core/infra/event_bus.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <set>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#ifdef _WIN32
#pragma comment(lib, "iphlpapi.lib")
#endif

namespace slop::core::runtime {

namespace infra = slop::core::infra;

namespace {

constexpr int     kDefaultIoTimeoutMs   = 10000;   // idle time per chunk
constexpr int64_t kDefaultCmdBudgetMs   = 60000;   // whole normal command
constexpr int64_t kDefaultLongBudgetMs  = 600000;  // scans / analysis / elf upload
constexpr int     kShortTimeoutMs       = 500;     // optional trailing status words
constexpr int     kConnectTimeoutMs     = 5000;
constexpr uint32_t kMaxListEntries      = 1u << 20; // protocol sanity ceiling
constexpr int64_t kMapsCacheTtlMs       = 1500;
constexpr uint32_t kThreadInfoBatch     = 64;      // pipelined THREAD_INFO requests

struct wsa_init_t {
    wsa_init_t() { WSADATA d; WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2, 2), &d); }
    ~wsa_init_t() { WSACleanup(); }
};
wsa_init_t& wsa() { static wsa_init_t w; return w; }

std::string hex32(uint32_t v) {
    char b[16];
    std::snprintf(b, sizeof(b), "0x%08X", v);
    return b;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// conn_t: one TCP connection to the ps4debug-NG command server

class conn_t {
public:
    std::atomic<SOCKET> fd{INVALID_SOCKET};
    std::mutex mu;   // serializes whole command exchanges

    // guarded by mu: the exchange in progress
    int64_t  deadline_ms   = 0;     // steady clock; 0 = none
    int      io_timeout_ms = kDefaultIoTimeoutMs;
    uint32_t last_err      = 0;     // ps4::io_err_t of the last failure
    std::atomic<uint32_t> last_status{0};  // last error status word seen (structured errors)

    // invoked under mu when an I/O failure invalidates the socket
    std::function<void(uint32_t code, const std::string& why)> on_lost;

    // transparent reopen after the payload dropped us (the payload closes a
    // client whenever a handler fails). on_reopen re-runs per-connection
    // setup (handshake/auth) and resets state the payload tore down; it runs
    // with mu held
    std::function<bool(conn_t&)> on_reopen;
    std::atomic<uint64_t> generation{0};   // bumped on every transparent reopen
    // set when an error status arrived: the payload usually closes the
    // socket right after sending it, so the next liveness check waits a
    // moment for that FIN instead of racing it
    bool suspect = false;

    // current endpoint for revive(); "" when never opened
    std::string host;
    uint16_t    port = 0;

    // bumped by every fresh connect(); handles remember the epoch they
    // were created in so a handle never reaches a different console
    std::atomic<uint64_t> epoch{0};

    bool connected() const noexcept {
        return fd.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != INVALID_SOCKET;
    }

    // true when the server hung up, the socket errored, or stray bytes are
    // queued (a previous exchange desynced, e.g. a snapshot that stopped
    // streaming mid-region); any of those means the stream is unusable
    bool peer_gone() {
        if (fd == INVALID_SOCKET) return false;
        fd_set rset;
        FD_ZERO(&rset);
        FD_SET(fd, &rset);
        timeval tv{};
        if (suspect) tv.tv_usec = 100 * 1000;
        suspect = false;
        if (select(0, &rset, nullptr, nullptr, &tv) <= 0) return false;
        char b;
        const int n = ::recv(fd, &b, 1, MSG_PEEK);
        (void)n;
        return true;   // closed (0), error (<0) or unexpected bytes (>0)
    }

    bool revive() {
        std::string err;
        const std::string h = host;
        const uint16_t p = port;
        if (!open(h, p, err)) return false;
        if (on_reopen && !on_reopen(*this)) { close(); return false; }
        generation.fetch_add(1);
        return true;
    }

    bool open(const std::string& h, uint16_t p, std::string& err) {
        wsa();
        close();

        addrinfo hints{};
        hints.ai_family   = AF_INET;
        hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
        hints.ai_protocol = IPPROTO_TCP;
        addrinfo* list = nullptr;
        char port_str[8];
        std::snprintf(port_str, sizeof(port_str), "%u", static_cast<unsigned>(p));
        if (getaddrinfo(h.c_str(), port_str, &hints, &list) != 0 || !list) {
            err = "cannot resolve " + h;
            return false;
        }

        SOCKET s = socket(list->ai_family, list->ai_socktype, list->ai_protocol);
        if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) {
            freeaddrinfo(list);
            err = "socket() failed";
            return false;
        }

        // connect with a timeout: non-blocking connect + select
        u_long nonblock = 1;
        ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &nonblock);
        int r = ::connect(s, list->ai_addr, static_cast<int>(list->ai_addrlen));
        freeaddrinfo(list);
        // POSIX reports a non-blocking connect as EINPROGRESS, Winsock as
        // WSAEWOULDBLOCK; both mean "wait for writability"
        if (r == SOCKET_ERROR && WSAGetLastError() != WSAEWOULDBLOCK &&
            WSAGetLastError() != WSAEINPROGRESS) {
            const int wsa_err = WSAGetLastError();
            closesocket(s);
            err = "connect to " + h + ":" + port_str + " failed (WSA " +
                  std::to_string(wsa_err) + ")";
            return false;
        }
        if (r == SOCKET_ERROR) {
            fd_set wset;
            FD_ZERO(&wset);
            FD_SET(s, &wset);
            fd_set eset;
            FD_ZERO(&eset);
            FD_SET(s, &eset);
            timeval tv{};
            tv.tv_sec  = kConnectTimeoutMs / 1000;
            tv.tv_usec = (kConnectTimeoutMs % 1000) * 1000;
            if (select(0, nullptr, &wset, &eset, &tv) <= 0) {
                closesocket(s);
                err = "connect to " + h + ":" + port_str + " timed out";
                return false;
            }
            int soerr = 0;
#ifdef _WIN32
            int slen  = sizeof(soerr);
            getsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, reinterpret_cast<char*>(&soerr), &slen);
#else
            socklen_t slen = sizeof(soerr);
            getsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, &soerr, &slen);
#endif
            if (soerr != 0 || FD_ISSET(s, &eset)) {
                closesocket(s);
                err = "connect to " + h + ":" + port_str + " failed (SO_ERROR " +
                      std::to_string(soerr) + ")";
                return false;
            }
        }
        u_long block = 0;
        ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &block);

        int flag = 1;
        setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&flag), sizeof(flag));
        fd.store(s, std::memory_order_release);
        host = h;
        port = p;
        return true;
    }

    // explicit close (no on_lost notification)
    void close() noexcept {
        SOCKET s = fd.exchange(INVALID_SOCKET, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
        if (s != INVALID_SOCKET) {
            shutdown(s, SD_BOTH);
            closesocket(s);
        }
    }

    // the stream can no longer be trusted: drop the socket and tell the owner
    bool fail(uint32_t code, const std::string& why) {
        last_err = code;
        if (!connected()) return false;
        close();
        if (on_lost) on_lost(code, why);
        return false;
    }

    // milliseconds the next select may wait; -1 when the command deadline
    // already passed
    int wait_budget_ms() const {
        if (deadline_ms == 0) return io_timeout_ms;
        const int64_t left = deadline_ms - infra::steady_ms();
        if (left <= 0) return -1;
        return static_cast<int>(std::min<int64_t>(left, io_timeout_ms));
    }

    // wait for readability/writability; 1 ready, 0 timed out, -1 error
    static int wait_sock(SOCKET s, bool for_write, int ms) {
        fd_set set;
        FD_ZERO(&set);
        FD_SET(s, &set);
        timeval tv{};
        tv.tv_sec  = ms / 1000;
        tv.tv_usec = (ms % 1000) * 1000;
        const int sel = for_write ? select(0, nullptr, &set, nullptr, &tv)
                                  : select(0, &set, nullptr, nullptr, &tv);
        return sel < 0 ? -1 : (sel == 0 ? 0 : 1);
    }

    bool send_all(const void* buf, size_t len) {
        const SOCKET s = fd.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) { last_err = ps4::kErrNotConnected; return false; }
        const char* p = static_cast<const char*>(buf);
        size_t left = len;
        while (left > 0) {
            const int budget = wait_budget_ms();
            if (budget < 0) return fail(ps4::kErrTimeout, "command deadline exceeded while sending");
            const int w = wait_sock(s, true, budget);
            if (w == 0) return fail(ps4::kErrTimeout, "console stopped accepting data (send timeout)");
            if (w < 0) return fail(ps4::kErrSendFailed, "select failed while sending (WSA " +
                                                         std::to_string(WSAGetLastError()) + ")");
            const int n = ::send(s, p, static_cast<int>(left > 0x10000 ? 0x10000 : left), SLOP_SEND_FLAGS);
            if (n <= 0) return fail(ps4::kErrSendFailed, "send failed (WSA " +
                                                         std::to_string(WSAGetLastError()) + ")");
            p    += n;
            left -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
        }
        return true;
    }

    bool recv_all(void* buf, size_t len) {
        const SOCKET s = fd.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) { last_err = ps4::kErrNotConnected; return false; }
        char* p = static_cast<char*>(buf);
        size_t left = len;
        while (left > 0) {
            const int budget = wait_budget_ms();
            if (budget < 0) return fail(ps4::kErrTimeout, "command deadline exceeded while receiving");
            const int w = wait_sock(s, false, budget);
            if (w == 0) return fail(ps4::kErrTimeout, "console did not answer within " +
                                                      std::to_string(budget) + " ms");
            if (w < 0) return fail(ps4::kErrRecvFailed, "select failed while receiving (WSA " +
                                                        std::to_string(WSAGetLastError()) + ")");
            const int n = ::recv(s, p, static_cast<int>(left > 0x10000 ? 0x10000 : left), 0);
            if (n == 0) return fail(ps4::kErrRecvFailed, "console closed the connection");
            if (n < 0) return fail(ps4::kErrRecvFailed, "recv failed (WSA " +
                                                        std::to_string(WSAGetLastError()) + ")");
            p    += n;
            left -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
        }
        return true;
    }

    // timed variant for long-running streaming commands; the whole-command
    // budget still applies on top
    bool recv_all(void* buf, size_t len, int timeout_ms) {
        const int saved = io_timeout_ms;
        io_timeout_ms = timeout_ms > 0 ? timeout_ms : io_timeout_ms;
        const bool ok = recv_all(buf, len);
        io_timeout_ms = saved;
        return ok;
    }

    bool recv_u32(uint32_t& v) {
        if (!recv_all(&v, sizeof(v))) return false;
        // remember error status words so callers can explain a failure; the
        // set is narrow enough that counts/lengths never collide in practice
        if (ps4::status_name(v)[0] != '\0') {
            last_status = v;
            suspect = true;
        }
        return true;
    }

    // timed variant for long-running streaming commands (Turbo Scan passes);
    // the whole-command budget still applies on top
    bool recv_u32(uint32_t& v, int timeout_ms) {
        const int saved = io_timeout_ms;
        io_timeout_ms = timeout_ms > 0 ? timeout_ms : io_timeout_ms;
        const bool ok = recv_u32(v);
        io_timeout_ms = saved;
        return ok;
    }

    // an optional trailing word: none when nothing arrives within timeout_ms
    // (stream still in sync), failed when a partial word or error broke it
    enum class opt_t { got, none, failed };
    opt_t recv_u32_optional(uint32_t& v, int timeout_ms) {
        const SOCKET s = fd.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) { last_err = ps4::kErrNotConnected; return opt_t::failed; }
        const int w = wait_sock(s, false, timeout_ms);
        if (w == 0) return opt_t::none;
        if (w < 0) { fail(ps4::kErrRecvFailed, "select failed"); return opt_t::failed; }
        return recv_u32(v) ? opt_t::got : opt_t::failed;
    }

    // send one request header + body; the caller then drives the reply
    bool send_cmd(uint32_t cmd, const void* body, uint32_t bodylen) {
        if (bodylen > ps4::kMaxDatalen) return false;   // payload would desync us
        if (peer_gone() && !revive()) return false;
        ps4::packet_header_t hdr{};
        hdr.magic   = ps4::kPacketMagic;
        hdr.cmd     = cmd;
        hdr.datalen = bodylen;
        if (!send_all(&hdr, sizeof(hdr))) return false;
        if (bodylen > 0 && body) return send_all(body, bodylen);
        return true;
    }

    // our IPv4 as the sin_addr.s_addr numeric value, for CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH
    uint32_t local_ip_value() const {
        sockaddr_in sa{};
        slop_socklen_t len = sizeof(sa);
        if (getsockname(fd.load(), reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&sa), &len) != 0)
            return 0;
        uint32_t v;
        std::memcpy(&v, &sa.sin_addr, sizeof(v));
        return v;
    }
};

// holds the connection for one exchange and arms its overall deadline
class cmd_lock_t {
public:
    cmd_lock_t(conn_t& c, int64_t budget_ms) : c_(c), lk_(c.mu) {
        c_.deadline_ms = infra::steady_ms() + budget_ms;
        c_.last_err = 0;
    }
    ~cmd_lock_t() { c_.deadline_ms = 0; }
    cmd_lock_t(const cmd_lock_t&) = delete;
    cmd_lock_t& operator=(const cmd_lock_t&) = delete;

private:
    conn_t& c_;
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk_;
};

// failed wire step -> io_result_t
io_result_t wire_fail(const conn_t& c) {
    io_result_t r;
    r.error = c.last_err ? c.last_err : ps4::kErrNotConnected;
    return r;
}

io_result_t err_result(uint32_t code) {
    io_result_t r;
    r.error = code;
    return r;
}

// read a status word. A non-success *status* is a clean error; a word that
// is not a status at all means the stream is misaligned, so drop the socket
bool expect_success(conn_t& c, io_result_t& r) {
    uint32_t st = 0;
    if (!c.recv_u32(st)) { r.error = c.last_err; return false; }
    if (st == ps4::CMD_SUCCESS) return true;
    r.error = ps4::status_to_err(st);
    if (r.error == ps4::kErrProtocol)
        c.fail(ps4::kErrProtocol, "expected a status word, got " + hex32(st) + " (stream desync)");
    return false;
}

// owner of a TCP listener on port, "pid N (name)" or ""
std::string tcp_port_owner(uint16_t port) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    ULONG size = 0;
    GetExtendedTcpTable(nullptr, &size, FALSE, AF_INET, TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER, 0);
    if (size == 0) return {};
    std::vector<uint8_t> buf(size);
    if (GetExtendedTcpTable(buf.data(), &size, FALSE, AF_INET,
                            TCP_TABLE_OWNER_PID_LISTENER, 0) != NO_ERROR)
        return {};
    const auto* t = reinterpret_cast<const MIB_TCPTABLE_OWNER_PID*>(buf.data());
    for (DWORD i = 0; i < t->dwNumEntries; ++i) {
        const auto& row = t->table[i];
        if (ntohs(static_cast<u_short>(row.dwLocalPort)) != port) continue;
        std::string who = "pid " + std::to_string(row.dwOwningPid);
        if (row.dwOwningPid == GetCurrentProcessId()) return who + " (this process)";
        if (HANDLE h = OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, row.dwOwningPid)) {
            wchar_t path[MAX_PATH]{};
            DWORD n = MAX_PATH;
            if (QueryFullProcessImageNameW(h, 0, path, &n)) {
                char narrow[MAX_PATH * 3]{};
                WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, path, -1, narrow, sizeof(narrow), nullptr, nullptr);
                std::string s = narrow;
                const size_t slash = s.find_last_of("\\/");
                who += " (" + (slash == std::string::npos ? s : s.substr(slash + 1)) + ")";
            }
            CloseHandle(h);
        }
        return who;
    }
    return {};
#else
    return compat::tcp_listener_owner(port);
#endif
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// event_listener_t: accepts the server->client debug-event connection on 755.
// CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH fails server-side unless it can connect back to us, so we
// listen and drain interrupt packets (0x4A0 bytes each) for the session life.

class event_listener_t {
public:
    ~event_listener_t() { stop(); }

    // set once before start() and never mutated afterwards. Both run on the
    // listener thread. on_closed gets the attach id that was in flight when
    // the connection was accepted
    std::function<void(const uint8_t* pkt)> on_packet;
    std::function<void(uint64_t attach_id)> on_closed;
    // attach id currently in flight (set by ensure_debug before ATTACH)
    std::atomic<uint64_t> current_attach{0};

    // Only the console we attached to may deliver stop events. Port 755 is
    // bound on every interface because the payload connects back to us, so
    // without this any LAN host could forge a stop (fake RIP/DR6) or send
    // SIGKILL. 0 = no filter yet (before the first attach).
    void set_peer(const std::string& host) {
        uint32_t addr = 0;
        addrinfo hints{};
        hints.ai_family   = AF_INET;
        hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
        addrinfo* res = nullptr;
        if (::getaddrinfo(host.c_str(), nullptr, &hints, &res) == 0 && res) {
            addr = reinterpret_cast<sockaddr_in*>(res->ai_addr)->sin_addr.s_addr;
            ::freeaddrinfo(res);
        }
        allow_peer_.store(addr);
    }

    // false + err on failure (port in use names the owner)
    bool start(uint16_t port, std::string& err) {
        // A stop() in flight closes the socket and joins the accept thread
        // without holding mu_ the whole time; starting in that window used to
        // return true for a listener that no longer accepts (the payload's
        // connect-back then sat in a dead backlog and the attach timed out).
        for (int i = 0; i < 200 && stopping_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); ++i)
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        if (running_ && !stop_ && listen_fd_.load() != INVALID_SOCKET) {
            if (port == port_) return true;
            err = "debug-event listener already bound to port " + std::to_string(port_);
            return false;
        }
        wsa();
        // SO_REUSEADDR lets two sockets share a port on Windows, so refuse
        // up front when someone else is already listening there
        const std::string owner = tcp_port_owner(port);
        if (!owner.empty()) {
            err = "TCP port " + std::to_string(port) + " is already in use by " + owner +
                  "; the ps4debug-NG payload always connects back to port 755, so close "
                  "that program (or the other reverse-slop instance) and retry";
            return false;
        }
        SOCKET s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP);
        if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) { err = "socket() failed for the debug-event listener"; return false; }
        int flag = 1;
        setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&flag), sizeof(flag));
        sockaddr_in addr{};
        addr.sin_family      = AF_INET;
        addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
        addr.sin_port        = htons(port);
        if (bind(s, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof(addr)) != 0 ||
            listen(s, 4) != 0) {
            const int e = WSAGetLastError();
            closesocket(s);
            err = "cannot listen on TCP port " + std::to_string(port) + " (WSA " +
                  std::to_string(e) + ")";
            const std::string who = tcp_port_owner(port);
            if (!who.empty()) err += "; held by " + who;
            return false;
        }
        listen_fd_.store(s);
        port_    = port;
        running_ = true;
        stop_    = false;
        th_ = std::thread([this] { run(); });
        return true;
    }

    void stop() {
        stopping_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
            if (!running_) {
                stopping_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
                return;
            }
            stop_ = true;
        }
        SOCKET s = listen_fd_.exchange(INVALID_SOCKET);
        if (s != INVALID_SOCKET) {
            shutdown(s, SD_BOTH);
            closesocket(s);
        }
        if (th_.joinable()) th_.join();
        std::vector<std::thread> conns;
        {
            std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
            conns.swap(conns_);
        }
        for (auto& t : conns)
            if (t.joinable()) t.join();
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        running_ = false;
        stopping_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    }

    bool running() const {
        std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
        return running_;
    }

private:
    // Drain one event connection. Runs on its own thread so a silent peer can
    // no longer block accept() and starve the console's connect-back.
    void drain(SOCKET c, uint64_t attach_id) {
        ps4_event_reassembler_t ra(ps4::kDebugEventSize);
        // short recv timeout so stop_ is noticed even with no traffic
        DWORD rt = 500;
        setsockopt(c, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&rt), sizeof(rt));
        uint8_t buf[0x8000];
        bool peer_closed = false;
        while (!stop_) {
            const int n = ::recv(c, reinterpret_cast<char*>(buf), sizeof(buf), 0);
            if (n == 0) { peer_closed = true; break; }   // server closed the channel
            if (n < 0) {
                // the recv timeout exists only to notice stop_; keep the
                // connection open so later events from the payload arrive
                if (WSAGetLastError() == WSAETIMEDOUT) continue;
                peer_closed = true;
                break;
            }
            ra.feed(buf, static_cast<size_t>(n), [this](const uint8_t* pkt) {
                if (on_packet) on_packet(pkt);
            });
        }
        closesocket(c);
        if (peer_closed && on_closed) on_closed(attach_id);
    }

    void run() {
        while (!stop_) {
            const SOCKET ls = listen_fd_.load();
            if (ls == INVALID_SOCKET) break;
            fd_set rset;
            FD_ZERO(&rset);
            FD_SET(ls, &rset);
            timeval tv{};
            tv.tv_sec  = 0;
            tv.tv_usec = 200 * 1000;
            if (select(0, &rset, nullptr, nullptr, &tv) <= 0) continue;
            sockaddr_in peer{};
            slop_socklen_t peer_len = static_cast<slop_socklen_t>(sizeof(peer));
            SOCKET c = accept(ls, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&peer), &peer_len);
            if (c == INVALID_SOCKET) continue;
            const uint32_t want = allow_peer_.load();
            if (want != 0 && peer.sin_addr.s_addr != want) {
                closesocket(c);   // not the console this session is attached to
                continue;
            }
            const uint64_t attach_id = current_attach.load();
            std::lock_guard lk(mu_);
            if (conns_.size() >= 4) { closesocket(c); continue; }
            conns_.emplace_back([this, c, attach_id] { drain(c, attach_id); });
        }
    }

    mutable std::mutex mu_;
    std::atomic<SOCKET> listen_fd_{INVALID_SOCKET};
    std::atomic<uint32_t> allow_peer_{0};
    std::atomic<bool>     stopping_{false};   // stop() in flight
    std::vector<std::thread> conns_;   // guarded by mu_
    uint16_t port_ = 0;
    std::thread th_;
    std::atomic<bool> stop_{false};
    std::atomic<bool> running_{false};
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// prot translation: callers pass Windows PAGE_* constants, ps4debug wants
// FreeBSD VM_PROT_* bits

uint32_t win_to_vm_prot(uint32_t page) {
    page &= ~(0x100u | 0x200u | 0x400u);   // drop PAGE_GUARD/NOCACHE/WRITECOMBINE
    switch (page) {
    case 0x01: return ps4::kVmProtNone;                     // PAGE_NOACCESS
    case 0x02: return ps4::kVmProtRead;                     // PAGE_READONLY
    case 0x04: return ps4::kVmProtRead | ps4::kVmProtWrite; // PAGE_READWRITE
    case 0x08: return ps4::kVmProtRead | ps4::kVmProtWrite; // PAGE_WRITECOPY
    case 0x10: return ps4::kVmProtExec;                     // PAGE_EXECUTE
    case 0x20: return ps4::kVmProtRead | ps4::kVmProtExec;  // PAGE_EXECUTE_READ
    case 0x40: return ps4::kVmProtAll;                      // PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE
    case 0x80: return ps4::kVmProtAll;                      // PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY
    default:   return ps4::kVmProtAll;
    }
}

uint32_t vm_to_win_prot(uint16_t vm) {
    static const uint32_t kTable[8] = {
        0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x04, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x40
    };
    return kTable[vm & 0x7];
}

std::string fixed_str(const char* s, size_t cap) {
    size_t n = 0;
    while (n < cap && s[n] != '\0') ++n;
    return std::string(s, n);
}

std::string base_name(const std::string& path) {
    const size_t slash = path.find_last_of("/\\");
    return slash == std::string::npos ? path : path.substr(slash + 1);
}

uint32_t handle_pid(const target_handle_t& h) {
    return h.pid;
}

void reg64_from_ctx(ps4::reg64_t& r, const thread_context_t& c) {
    r = {};
    r.r15 = c.r15; r.r14 = c.r14; r.r13 = c.r13; r.r12 = c.r12;
    r.r11 = c.r11; r.r10 = c.r10; r.r9  = c.r9;  r.r8  = c.r8;
    r.rdi = c.rdi; r.rsi = c.rsi; r.rbp = c.rbp; r.rbx = c.rbx;
    r.rdx = c.rdx; r.rcx = c.rcx; r.rax = c.rax;
    r.rip = c.rip; r.rsp = c.rsp; r.rflags = c.flags;
}

void ctx_from_reg64(thread_context_t& c, const ps4::reg64_t& r) {
    c = {};
    c.r15 = r.r15; c.r14 = r.r14; c.r13 = r.r13; c.r12 = r.r12;
    c.r11 = r.r11; c.r10 = r.r10; c.r9  = r.r9;  c.r8  = r.r8;
    c.rdi = r.rdi; c.rsi = r.rsi; c.rbp = r.rbp; c.rbx = r.rbx;
    c.rdx = r.rdx; c.rcx = r.rcx; c.rax = r.rax;
    c.rip = r.rip; c.rsp = r.rsp; c.flags = r.rflags;
}

ps4_segment_t segment_from_entry(const ps4::vm_map_entry_t& m) {
    ps4_segment_t s;
    s.start  = m.start;
    s.end    = m.end;
    s.offset = m.offset;
    s.prot   = m.prot;
    s.name   = fixed_str(m.name, sizeof(m.name));
    return s;
}

struct attach_state_t {
    uint32_t pid = 0;
    uint64_t epoch = 0;
    std::shared_ptr<conn_t> conn;
    std::string name;
    std::string path;
};

} // namespace

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// public helpers

bool ps4_decode_event(const uint8_t* pkt, size_t n, ps4_event_t& e) {
    if (!pkt || n < ps4::kDebugEventSize) return false;
    ps4::debug_event_packet_t ep{};
    std::memcpy(&ep, pkt, sizeof(ep));
    e = ps4_event_t{};
    e.lwpid  = ep.lwpid;
    e.status = ep.status;
    e.signal = static_cast<int>((ep.status >> 8) & 0xFF);
    std::memcpy(e.thread_name, ep.tdname, sizeof(ep.tdname));
    e.thread_name[sizeof(ep.tdname)] = '\0';
    ctx_from_reg64(e.ctx, ep.regs);
    std::memcpy(e.dr, ep.dbregs, sizeof(e.dr));
    return true;
}

ps4_event_reassembler_t::ps4_event_reassembler_t(size_t packet_size)
    : packet_size_(packet_size ? packet_size : 1) {
    buf_.reserve(packet_size_ * 2);
}

size_t ps4_event_reassembler_t::feed(const uint8_t* data, size_t n,
                                     const std::function<void(const uint8_t*)>& on_packet) {
    size_t delivered = 0;
    size_t off = 0;
    // fast path: whole packets straight from the input when nothing is pending
    if (buf_.empty()) {
        while (n - off >= packet_size_) {
            if (on_packet) on_packet(data + off);
            off += packet_size_;
            ++delivered;
        }
        if (off < n) buf_.assign(data + off, data + n);
        return delivered;
    }
    buf_.insert(buf_.end(), data, data + n);
    size_t pos = 0;
    while (buf_.size() - pos >= packet_size_) {
        if (on_packet) on_packet(buf_.data() + pos);
        pos += packet_size_;
        ++delivered;
    }
    if (pos > 0) buf_.erase(buf_.begin(), buf_.begin() + static_cast<ptrdiff_t>(pos));
    return delivered;
}

std::vector<ps4_module_t> ps4_coalesce_modules(std::vector<ps4_segment_t> maps) {
    std::sort(maps.begin(), maps.end(),
              [](const ps4_segment_t& a, const ps4_segment_t& b) { return a.start < b.start; });
    std::vector<ps4_module_t> out;
    bool open = false;
    for (auto& m : maps) {
        if (m.name.empty()) continue;   // anonymous mapping: neither joins nor breaks
        if (open && out.back().path == m.name && m.start >= out.back().end) {
            out.back().end = std::max(out.back().end, m.end);
            out.back().segments.push_back(m);
            continue;
        }
        ps4_module_t mod;
        mod.path = m.name;
        mod.name = base_name(m.name);
        mod.base = m.start;
        mod.end  = m.end;
        mod.segments.push_back(m);
        out.push_back(std::move(mod));
        open = true;
    }
    return out;
}

std::vector<process_info_t> ps4_parse_proc_list(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) {
    std::vector<process_info_t> out;
    if (!data) return out;
    const size_t count = len / sizeof(ps4::proc_list_entry_t);
    out.reserve(count);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        ps4::proc_list_entry_t e{};
        std::memcpy(&e, data + i * sizeof(e), sizeof(e));
        process_info_t p;
        p.pid       = static_cast<uint32_t>(e.pid);
        p.name      = fixed_str(e.p_comm, sizeof(e.p_comm));
        p.arch      = arch_t::x64;   // Orbis userland is x86-64
        p.elevation = elevation_t::system;
        out.push_back(std::move(p));
    }
    return out;
}

namespace ps4 {

std::string io_error_str(uint32_t code) {
    switch (code) {
    case kErrNone:          return "ok";
    case kErrNotConnected:  return "not connected to a PS4 console (target.ps4_connect, or "
                                   "target.ps4_reconnect after a dropped connection)";
    case kErrSendFailed:    return "send to the console failed; the connection was dropped "
                                   "(target.ps4_reconnect restores it)";
    case kErrRecvFailed:    return "the console closed the connection or a receive failed; "
                                   "the connection was dropped (target.ps4_reconnect restores it)";
    case kErrTimeout:       return "the console did not answer in time (idle or whole-command "
                                   "deadline); the connection was dropped to keep the stream in "
                                   "sync (target.ps4_reconnect restores it)";
    case kErrStatus:        return "the payload rejected the command (CMD_ERROR): bad pid/address, "
                                   "process gone, or the operation is not allowed";
    case kErrProtocol:      return "malformed reply from the payload (stream desync); the "
                                   "connection was dropped";
    case kErrBadArg:        return "invalid argument (rejected before anything was sent)";
    case kErrUnmapped:      return "address range is not mapped (or lacks the needed protection) "
                                   "in the target process";
    case kErrNotAttached:   return "no ps4 debug session (debugger.ps4_attach first)";
    case kErrAlreadyDebug:  return "the payload is already debugging a process on this "
                                   "connection (CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG)";
    case kErrDataNull:      return "the payload reported CMD_DATA_NULL (missing data, or the "
                                   "scan family is locked: run debugger.ps4_auth)";
    case kErrTooMuchData:   return "the payload reported CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA (request too large)";
    case kErrNoSlot:        return "no free slot (30 software breakpoints / 4 hardware "
                                   "watchpoints); clear one first";
    case kErrNotArmed:      return "that slot/address is not armed by this client";
    case kErrStaleHandle:   return "the target handle belongs to an earlier console connection; "
                                   "attach again";
    case kErrAsm:           return "the on-device assembler reported an error";
    case kErrListen:        return "cannot listen on the debug-event port 755 (the payload "
                                   "connects back there); is another program using it?";
    case kErrDetachFailed:  return "the payload refused to detach the previous debuggee; it is "
                                   "still being debugged";
    case kErrTooMany:       return "result larger than the client cap";
    case kErrSlotBusy:      return "that slot is being armed/cleared by another request";
    default: break;
    }
    if (code < 0xE0000000u) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        char* msg = nullptr;
        const DWORD n = FormatMessageA(FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER | FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM |
                                       FORMAT_MESSAGE_IGNORE_INSERTS,
                                       nullptr, code, 0, reinterpret_cast<LPSTR>(&msg), 0, nullptr);
        std::string text = "Win32 error " + std::to_string(code);
        if (n && msg) {
            std::string m(msg, n);
            while (!m.empty() && (m.back() == '\n' || m.back() == '\r' || m.back() == ' '))
                m.pop_back();
            text += ": " + m;
        }
        if (msg) LocalFree(msg);
        return text;
#else
        // the code is a Win32 error value carried by the protocol; keep the
        // shared wording and append the host's text
        return "Win32 error " + std::to_string(code) + ": " +
               std::strerror(static_cast<int>(code));
#endif
    }
    return "error " + hex32(code);
}

} // namespace ps4

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// backend impl

struct backend_ps4_t::impl_t {
    impl_t() {
        conn->on_lost = [this](uint32_t code, const std::string& why) { on_conn_lost(code, why); };
        listener.on_packet = [this](const uint8_t* pkt) { push_event(pkt); };
        listener.on_closed = [this](uint64_t id) { on_event_channel_closed(id); };
        // transparent reopen after the payload dropped us (see conn_t). The
        // payload's free_client tore down this client's debug session and
        // Turbo Scan session, so forget them; auth is global on the payload
        // but is re-run when it had succeeded before (an old payload without
        // AUTH would drop us again)
        conn->on_reopen = [this](conn_t& c) {
            if (authed) {
                std::string e;
                bool ok = authed.load();
                const bool resumed = auth_locked(c, ok, 0x3, e);
                authed = ok;
                if (!resumed) return false;
            }
            dbg_pid = 0;
            invalidate_maps_cache();
            std::lock_guard lk(ev_mu);
            evq.clear();
            return true;
        };
    }

    // tuning
    int     io_timeout_ms = kDefaultIoTimeoutMs;
    int64_t cmd_budget_ms = kDefaultCmdBudgetMs;
    int64_t long_budget_ms = kDefaultLongBudgetMs;
    uint16_t event_port = ps4::kDebugPort;

    std::shared_ptr<conn_t> conn = std::make_shared<conn_t>();

    // handshake facts + endpoint bookkeeping
    mutable std::mutex info_mu;
    std::string host;            // current endpoint ("" when not connected)
    uint16_t    port = 0;
    std::string last_host;       // remembered for reconnect
    uint16_t    last_port = 0;
    std::string branding, version;
    uint16_t    fw = 0, platform = 0;
    bool        lost = false;
    std::string lost_reason;
    uint32_t    lost_dbg_pid = 0;    // debuggee the dropped connection had
    std::atomic<uint64_t> drops{0};
    std::atomic<bool> authed{false};

    // debug session. dbg_mu orders dbg_pid transitions against the
    // listener's channel-closed notification
    std::mutex dbg_mu;
    std::atomic<uint32_t> dbg_pid{0};
    std::atomic<bool>     dbg_held{false};   // a stop event is holding the debuggee
    uint64_t attach_counter = 0;     // ids handed to ATTACH attempts (dbg_mu)
    uint64_t live_attach = 0;        // id of the attach that is live (dbg_mu)
    event_listener_t listener;

    // debug event queue, fed by the port-755 listener thread
    std::mutex ev_mu;
    std::condition_variable ev_cv;
```
