`src/core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/runtime/ps4_protocol.hpp
// ps4debug-NG wire protocol constants and packed structs.
// Source of truth: the NetVar1337/ps4debug-NG fork (debugger/include/protocol.h,
// debugger/source/*.c, PROTOCOL.md), a superset of Pharaoh2k/ps4debug-NG. The
// fork adds CMD_PROC_MODULES / CMD_PROC_SNAPSHOT, structured CMD_ERR_* codes
// and a minimum-datalen guard on every command (cmd_guards.c). Every
// multi-byte field on the wire is little-endian; the payload sends packed
// structs raw.
//
// Connection contract (both payloads): when a handler fails it usually
// returns 1 and the server CLOSES the client socket, tearing down that
// client's debug session and Turbo Scan session. The backend reconnects
// transparently on the next command.

#include <bit>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

namespace slop::core::runtime::ps4 {

// every packed struct below is sent/received raw; the wire is little-endian
static_assert(std::endian::native == std::endian::little,
              "ps4debug-NG wire structs are sent raw and assume a little-endian host");

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// io_result_t.error codes produced by backend_ps4_t. They live above the
// Win32 error range used by the local backend so one table can name both.
// io_error_str() turns any code into text for MCP/UI messages.
enum io_err_t : uint32_t {
    kErrNone           = 0,
    kErrNotConnected   = 0xE0000001,  // no live console connection
    kErrSendFailed     = 0xE0000002,  // send failed; connection dropped
    kErrRecvFailed     = 0xE0000003,  // receive failed / peer closed; connection dropped
    kErrTimeout        = 0xE0000004,  // per-chunk or whole-command deadline exceeded
    kErrStatus         = 0xE0000005,  // payload answered CMD_ERROR
    kErrProtocol       = 0xE0000006,  // malformed reply (stream desync)
    kErrBadArg         = 0xE0000007,  // rejected client-side before sending
    kErrUnmapped       = 0xE0000008,  // range not mapped / lacks the needed protection
    kErrNotAttached    = 0xE0000009,  // needs a ps4 debug session
    kErrAlreadyDebug   = 0xE000000A,  // payload answered CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG
    kErrDataNull       = 0xE000000B,  // payload answered CMD_DATA_NULL
    kErrTooMuchData    = 0xE000000C,  // payload answered CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA
    kErrNoSlot         = 0xE000000D,  // no free breakpoint/watchpoint slot
    kErrNotArmed       = 0xE000000E,  // slot/address not armed by this client
    kErrStaleHandle    = 0xE000000F,  // handle from an earlier console connection
    kErrAsm            = 0xE0000010,  // on-device assembler reported an error
    kErrListen         = 0xE0000011,  // cannot listen on the debug-event port
    kErrDetachFailed   = 0xE0000012,  // previous debuggee could not be detached
    kErrTooMany        = 0xE0000013,  // result larger than the client cap
    kErrSlotBusy       = 0xE0000014,  // slot is being (re)armed by another call
};

// human readable text for any io_result_t.error (ps4 codes above, Win32
// codes from the local backend otherwise)
std::string io_error_str(uint32_t code);

constexpr uint32_t kPacketMagic   = 0xFFAABBCC;
constexpr uint16_t kDefaultPort   = 744;    // main command server (TCP)
constexpr uint16_t kDebugPort     = 755;    // server->client debug events (TCP)
// UDP discovery probe (ps4debug-mcp convention): a payload listening on
// kBroadcastPort answers the magic with the same magic
constexpr uint32_t kBroadcastMagic = 0xFFFFAAAA;
constexpr uint16_t kBroadcastPort  = 1010;
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderSize    = 12;     // magic + cmd + datalen
constexpr uint32_t kChunkSize     = 0x10000; // server streams payloads in 64 KiB chunks
constexpr size_t   kMaxIoLen      = 16u * 1024u * 1024u; // sanity cap for one transfer

// info / ping commands (handled inline by the server)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_VERSION       = 0xBD000001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_FW_VERSION    = 0xBD000500;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_BRANDING      = 0xBD000501;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PLATFORM_ID   = 0xBD000502;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_NOP      = 0xBDAACC06;

// process commands
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_LIST         = 0xBDAA0001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_READ         = 0xBDAA0002;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_WRITE        = 0xBDAA0003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_MAPS         = 0xBDAA0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_PROTECT      = 0xBDAA0008;

constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_FREE         = 0xBDAA000C;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_ALLOC_HINTED = 0xBDAA000E;

// debug commands (require CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH first)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH          = 0xBDBB0001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_DETACH          = 0xBDBB0002;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SET_BREAKPOINT  = 0xBDBB0003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SET_WATCHPOINT  = 0xBDBB0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_GET_THREAD_LIST = 0xBDBB0005;

// process RPC: install the payload's rpc stub and call arbitrary code in the
// target (debugger/source/proc.c). INTALL is the payload's own spelling.
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_INTALL = 0xBDAA0005;

constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_ELF     = 0xBDAA0007;

constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_MODULES  = 0xBDAA0025;  // body: proc_maps_packet_t

constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_WRITE_MULTI          = 0xBDAACC04;

constexpr uint32_t CMD_TURBO_CAPS    = 0xBDAACC10;

constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_NOTIFY        = 0xBDDD0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_INFO          = 0xBDDD0005;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_FOREGROUND_APP = 0xBDDD0006;
constexpr uint32_t kNotifyTypeGeneric        = 222;   // main.c's generic icon

// scan value types (cmd_proc_scan_valuetype)
constexpr uint8_t kValU8 = 0, kValI8 = 1, kValU16 = 2, kValI16 = 3;
constexpr uint8_t kValU32 = 4, kValI32 = 5, kValU64 = 6, kValI64 = 7;
constexpr uint8_t kValF32 = 8, kValF64 = 9, kValArrBytes = 10, kValString = 11;

// scan compare types (cmd_proc_scan_comparetype)
constexpr uint8_t kCmpExact = 0, kCmpFuzzy = 1, kCmpBigger = 2, kCmpSmaller = 3;
constexpr uint8_t kCmpBetween = 4, kCmpIncreased = 5, kCmpIncreasedBy = 6;
constexpr uint8_t kCmpDecreased = 7, kCmpDecreasedBy = 8, kCmpChanged = 9;
constexpr uint8_t kCmpUnchanged = 10, kCmpUnknown = 11, kCmpUnknownLow = 12;

// byte width of a scan value type (0 = variable: arrbytes/string use lenData)
constexpr uint32_t scan_value_size(uint8_t vt) {
    switch (vt) {
        case kValU8: case kValI8:   return 1;
        case kValU16: case kValI16: return 2;
        case kValU32: case kValI32: case kValF32: return 4;
        case kValU64: case kValI64: case kValF64: return 8;
        default: return 0;
    }
}
// does this compare type take a seed value in lenData?
constexpr bool scan_cmp_needs_value(uint8_t ct) {
    return ct == kCmpExact || ct == kCmpFuzzy || ct == kCmpBigger ||
           ct == kCmpSmaller || ct == kCmpBetween || ct == kCmpIncreasedBy ||
           ct == kCmpDecreasedBy || ct == kCmpUnknownLow;
}
// does this compare type read the previous value from the entry stream?
constexpr bool scan_cmp_needs_previous(uint8_t ct) {
    return ct >= kCmpIncreased && ct <= kCmpUnchanged;
}

constexpr uint32_t kReadStackMaxDepth  = 64;
constexpr uint32_t kReadStackLocalsCap = 0x1000;
constexpr uint32_t kReadStackCodeOff   = 10;
constexpr uint32_t kReadStackCodeLen   = 200;
constexpr uint32_t kDisasmEntrySize    = 32;
constexpr uint32_t kFpregsSize         = 832;  // savefpu_ymm payload sent by GETFPREGS
constexpr uint32_t kDbregsSize         = 128;  // __dbreg64 sent by GETDBREGS

// limits enforced payload-side
constexpr uint32_t kMaxSwBreakpoints = 30;   // software INT3 breakpoints
constexpr uint32_t kMaxWatchpoints   = 4;    // hardware DR0-DR3

// CMD_DEBUG_CONTINUE stop argument / CMD_DEBUG_PROCESS_STOP state
constexpr uint32_t kStopResume = 0;   // PT_CONTINUE signal 0 (or SIGCONT)
constexpr uint32_t kStopStop   = 1;   // SIGSTOP (17)
constexpr uint32_t kStopKill   = 2;   // SIGKILL (9)

// watchpoint breaktype values (server DR7-encodes breaktype | (4*length))
constexpr uint32_t kWpExec  = 0;      // execute
constexpr uint32_t kWpWrite = 1;      // write
constexpr uint32_t kWpRdWr  = 3;      // read/write

// size of the packed server->client debug event packet sent on port 755
// whenever a debuggee thread stops (debug.c: DEBUG_INTERRUPT_PACKET_SIZE)
constexpr size_t kDebugEventSize = 0x4A0;

// status codes
constexpr uint32_t CMD_SUCCESS       = 0x80000000;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERROR         = 0xF0000001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA = 0xF0000002;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DATA_NULL     = 0xF0000003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG = 0xF0000004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_INVALID_INDEX = 0xF0000005;
// structured errors (fork extension), returned instead of CMD_ERROR where the
// failure mode is known
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERR_PID       = 0xF0000010;  // pid not found / not permitted
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERR_UNMAPPED  = 0xF0000011;  // range not mapped/readable
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERR_NOATTACH  = 0xF0000012;  // debug cmd with no session
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERR_RANGE     = 0xF0000013;  // addr+len overflow / out of range

// payload-side hardening limits (fork cmd_guards.h / PROTOCOL.md section 10)
constexpr uint32_t kMaxDatalen       = 16u * 1024u * 1024u;  // CMD_MAX_DATALEN
constexpr uint32_t kMaxConsoleMsg    = 64u * 1024u;          // print/notify
constexpr uint32_t kMaxScanValueLen  = 4096;                 // scan values/patterns

constexpr bool is_fatal_status(uint32_t s) { return (s >> 28) == 0xF; }

// readable name for a status word, "" for CMD_SUCCESS / unknown values
constexpr const char* status_name(uint32_t s) {
    switch (s) {
        case CMD_ERROR:         return "CMD_ERROR";
        case CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA: return "CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA";
        case CMD_DATA_NULL:     return "CMD_DATA_NULL";
        case CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG: return "CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG";
        case CMD_INVALID_INDEX: return "CMD_INVALID_INDEX";
        case CMD_ERR_PID:       return "CMD_ERR_PID (pid not found or not permitted)";
        case CMD_ERR_UNMAPPED:  return "CMD_ERR_UNMAPPED (address range not mapped/readable)";
        case CMD_ERR_NOATTACH:  return "CMD_ERR_NOATTACH (no debug session attached)";
        case CMD_ERR_RANGE:     return "CMD_ERR_RANGE (address+length out of range)";
        default:                return "";
    }
}

// map a non-success payload status word to an io_err_t
constexpr uint32_t status_to_err(uint32_t st) {
    switch (st) {
    case CMD_DATA_NULL:     return kErrDataNull;
    case CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA: return kErrTooMuchData;
    case CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG: return kErrAlreadyDebug;
    case CMD_ERROR:         return kErrStatus;
    default:                return kErrProtocol;   // not a status word at all
    }
}

// FreeBSD VM_PROT_* flags used by CMD_PROC_PROTECT (not Windows PAGE_*)
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtNone  = 0;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtRead  = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtWrite = 2;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtExec  = 4;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtAll   = 7;
```

`src/core/runtime/ps5_protocol.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/runtime/ps5_protocol.hpp
// ps5debug-NG wire protocol constants and packed structs.
//
// Source of truth: ps5debug-NG v1.3.2 (github.com/Pharaoh2k/ps5debug-NG,
// common/include/protocol.h + PROTOCOL.md, commit a1a6cb2 of 2026-10-22).
// The payload is a PS5 port of ps4debug, so the framing is the ps4debug one:
// a 12-byte {magic, cmd, datalen} header followed by datalen raw body bytes,
// every multi-byte field little-endian, every struct packed.
//
// Where this differs from the ps4debug-NG backend in this tree:
//  - status words are bit-swapped on the wire (net_send_int32 swaps adjacent
//    bit pairs); the constants below are the *wire* values a client compares,
//    which is why CMD_SUCCESS is 0x80000000 and the error words sit one bit
//    apart from the payload's own macros;
//  - CMD_PROC_READ streams its payload in 64 KiB chunks and CMD_PROC_WRITE
//    reads its data phase in 64 KiB chunks (NET_MAX_LENGTH is 8192 in the
//    payload, so the client never needs larger sends);
//  - CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH carries only the pid (the payload takes the client IP
//    from the connection slot);
//  - there is no server-side module list: modules are grouped client-side
//    from CMD_PROC_MAPS;
//  - unknown opcodes answer CMD_ERROR and the payload closes the client, so
//    the backend never probes for commands it does not need.

#include <bit>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

namespace slop::core::runtime::ps5 {

// every packed struct below is sent/received raw; the wire is little-endian
static_assert(std::endian::native == std::endian::little,
              "ps5debug-NG wire structs are sent raw and assume a little-endian host");

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// io_result_t.error codes produced by backend_ps5_t. Same numeric space as
// the ps4 backend's table (0xE000...., above the Win32 range) so one formatter
// (ps4::io_error_str) names errors from either console.
enum io_err_t : uint32_t {
    kErrNone           = 0,
    kErrNotConnected   = 0xE0000001,  // no live console connection
    kErrSendFailed     = 0xE0000002,  // send failed; connection dropped
    kErrRecvFailed     = 0xE0000003,  // receive failed / peer closed; connection dropped
    kErrTimeout        = 0xE0000004,  // per-chunk or whole-command deadline exceeded
    kErrStatus         = 0xE0000005,  // payload answered CMD_ERROR
    kErrProtocol       = 0xE0000006,  // malformed reply (stream desync)
    kErrBadArg         = 0xE0000007,  // rejected client-side before sending
    kErrUnmapped       = 0xE0000008,  // range not mapped / lacks the needed protection
    kErrNotAttached    = 0xE0000009,  // needs a ps5debug debug session
    kErrAlreadyDebug   = 0xE000000A,  // payload answered CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG
    kErrDataNull       = 0xE000000B,  // payload answered CMD_DATA_NULL
    kErrTooMuchData    = 0xE000000C,  // payload answered its over-size status
    kErrNoSlot         = 0xE000000D,  // no free breakpoint/watchpoint slot
    kErrNotArmed       = 0xE000000E,  // slot/address not armed by this client
    kErrStaleHandle    = 0xE000000F,  // handle from an earlier console connection
    kErrInvalidIndex   = 0xE0000010,  // payload answered CMD_INVALID_INDEX
    kErrListen         = 0xE0000011,  // cannot listen on the debug-event port
    kErrDetachFailed   = 0xE0000012,  // previous debuggee could not be detached
};

constexpr uint32_t kPacketMagic   = 0xFFAABBCC;
constexpr uint16_t kDefaultPort   = 744;    // main command server (TCP)
constexpr uint16_t kDebugPort     = 755;    // payload->client debug events (TCP)
constexpr uint16_t kBroadcastPort = 1010;   // UDP discovery listener
constexpr uint32_t kBroadcastMagic = 0xFFFFAAAA;
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderSize    = 12;     // magic + cmd + datalen
constexpr uint32_t kChunkSize     = 0x10000;   // read/write stream chunk
constexpr size_t   kMaxIoLen      = 16u * 1024u * 1024u;  // sanity cap per transfer
// the dispatcher refuses a request body above 1 MiB (PROTOCOL.md 1.4)
constexpr uint32_t kMaxDatalen    = 1u * 1024u * 1024u;
constexpr uint32_t kMaxConsoleMsg = 64u * 1024u;   // client-side cap on print/notify text

// info / ping commands (handled inline by the dispatcher)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_VERSION     = 0xBD000001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_FW_VERSION  = 0xBD000500;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_BRANDING    = 0xBD000501;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PLATFORM_ID = 0xBD000502;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_NOP    = 0xBDAACC06;
constexpr uint16_t kPlatformPs5    = 5;    // CMD_PLATFORM_ID answer

// process commands
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_LIST    = 0xBDAA0001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_READ    = 0xBDAA0002;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_WRITE   = 0xBDAA0003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_MAPS    = 0xBDAA0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_PROTECT = 0xBDAA0008;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_INFO    = 0xBDAA000A;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_ALLOC   = 0xBDAA000B;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_FREE    = 0xBDAA000C;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_ALLOC_HINTED = 0xBDAA000E;
// raw literal upstream: start of the target's first VM map (main image base)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_PROC_BASE    = 0xBDAA000D;

// debug commands (require CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH first)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_ATTACH          = 0xBDBB0001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_DETACH          = 0xBDBB0002;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SET_BREAKPOINT  = 0xBDBB0003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SET_WATCHPOINT  = 0xBDBB0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_GET_THREAD_LIST = 0xBDBB0005;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SUSPEND         = 0xBDBB0006;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_RESUME          = 0xBDBB0007;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_GETREGS         = 0xBDBB0008;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_SETREGS         = 0xBDBB0009;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_CONTINUE        = 0xBDBB0010;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_THREAD_INFO     = 0xBDBB0011;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_STEP            = 0xBDBB0012;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DEBUG_STEP_THREAD     = 0xBDBB0013;

// console commands (0xBDDD....); REBOOT/END are deliberately not exposed
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_PRINT          = 0xBDDD0003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_NOTIFY         = 0xBDDD0004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_INFO           = 0xBDDD0005;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_CONSOLE_FOREGROUND_APP = 0xBDDD0006;
constexpr uint32_t kNotifyTypeGeneric         = 222;   // main.c's generic icon

// status words as they arrive on the wire (see the header comment)
constexpr uint32_t CMD_SUCCESS       = 0x80000000;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ERROR         = 0xF0000001;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA = 0xF0000002;   // over-size guard literal
constexpr uint32_t CMD_DATA_NULL     = 0xF0000003;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG = 0xF0000004;
constexpr uint32_t CMD_INVALID_INDEX = 0xF0000005;

constexpr bool is_fatal_status(uint32_t s) { return (s >> 28) == 0xF; }

// readable name for a status word, "" for CMD_SUCCESS / unknown values
constexpr const char* status_name(uint32_t s) {
    switch (s) {
        case CMD_ERROR:         return "CMD_ERROR";
        case CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA: return "CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA";
        case CMD_DATA_NULL:     return "CMD_DATA_NULL";
        case CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG: return "CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG";
        case CMD_INVALID_INDEX: return "CMD_INVALID_INDEX";
        default:                return "";
    }
}

// map a non-success payload status word to an io_err_t
constexpr uint32_t status_to_err(uint32_t st) {
    switch (st) {
    case CMD_DATA_NULL:     return kErrDataNull;
    case CMD_TOO_MUCH_DATA: return kErrTooMuchData;
    case CMD_ALREADY_DEBUG: return kErrAlreadyDebug;
    case CMD_INVALID_INDEX: return kErrInvalidIndex;
    case CMD_ERROR:         return kErrStatus;
    default:                return kErrProtocol;   // not a status word at all
    }
}

// FreeBSD VM_PROT_* flags used by CMD_PROC_PROTECT (not Windows PAGE_*)
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtNone  = 0;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtRead  = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtWrite = 2;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtExec  = 4;
constexpr uint32_t kVmProtAll   = 7;

// limits enforced payload-side
constexpr uint32_t kMaxSwBreakpoints = 30;   // software INT3 breakpoints
constexpr uint32_t kMaxWatchpoints   = 4;    // hardware DR0-DR3

// human readable text for any io_result_t.error (ps5 codes above, Win32 codes
// from the local backend otherwise)
std::string io_error_str(uint32_t code);

// CMD_DEBUG_CONTINUE stop argument
constexpr uint32_t kStopResume = 0;   // PT_CONTINUE signal 0
constexpr uint32_t kStopStop   = 1;   // SIGSTOP
constexpr uint32_t kStopKill   = 2;   // SIGKILL

// watchpoint breaktype values (the payload shifts them straight into DR7)
constexpr uint32_t kWpExec  = 0;      // execute
constexpr uint32_t kWpWrite = 1;      // write
constexpr uint32_t kWpRdWr  = 3;      // read/write

// the payload's DR7 length field (not a byte count): 0=1, 1=2, 2=8, 3=4
constexpr uint32_t wp_dr7_length(uint32_t bytes) {
    return bytes == 1 ? 0 : bytes == 2 ? 1 : bytes == 8 ? 2 : bytes == 4 ? 3 : 4;
}

// size of the packed payload->client stop packet on port 755
constexpr size_t kDebugEventSize = 0x4A0;

#pragma pack(push, 1)

struct packet_header_t {
    uint32_t magic;
    uint32_t cmd;
    uint32_t datalen;
};

struct proc_read_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint64_t address;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct proc_write_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint64_t address;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct proc_maps_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
};

struct proc_protect_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint64_t address;
    uint32_t length;
    uint32_t newprot;
};

struct proc_info_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
};

struct proc_info_response_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    char     name[40];
    char     path[64];
    char     titleid[16];
    char     contentid[64];
};

struct proc_alloc_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct proc_alloc_hinted_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint64_t hint;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct proc_alloc_response_t {
    uint64_t address;
};

struct proc_free_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    uint64_t address;
    uint32_t length;
};

// CMD_PROC_LIST entry, 36 bytes each
struct proc_list_entry_t {
    char    name[32];
    int32_t pid;
};

// CMD_PROC_MAPS entry, 58 bytes each
struct vm_map_entry_t {
    char     name[32];
    uint64_t start;
    uint64_t end;
    uint64_t offset;
    uint16_t prot;
};

struct debug_attach_packet_t {
    uint32_t pid;
};

struct debug_lwpid_packet_t {
    uint32_t lwpid;
};

// CMD_DEBUG_THREAD_INFO reply body after the status word (40 bytes)
struct debug_thread_info_response_t {
    uint32_t lwpid;
    uint32_t priority;
    char     name[32];
};

struct debug_setregs_packet_t {
    uint32_t lwpid;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct debug_set_breakpoint_packet_t {
    uint32_t index;
    uint32_t enabled;
    uint64_t address;
};

struct debug_set_watchpoint_packet_t {
    uint32_t index;
    uint32_t enabled;
    uint32_t length;     // DR7 length field, see wp_dr7_length()
    uint32_t breaktype;  // kWpExec / kWpWrite / kWpRdWr
    uint64_t address;
};

struct debug_continue_packet_t {
    uint32_t stop;   // kStopResume / kStopStop / kStopKill
};

// struct reg from debug.h; the payload sends exactly 176 bytes for GETREGS
struct reg64_t {
    uint64_t r15, r14, r13, r12, r11, r10, r9, r8;
    uint64_t rdi, rsi, rbp, rbx, rdx, rcx, rax;
    uint32_t trapno;
    uint16_t fs;
    uint16_t gs;
    uint32_t err;
    uint16_t es;
    uint16_t ds;
    uint64_t rip;
    uint64_t cs;
    uint64_t rflags;
    uint64_t rsp;
    uint64_t ss;
};

// payload->client stop event, sent packed on the port-755 connection whenever
// a debuggee thread stops (debug.c: dispatch_debug_events builds it by hand at
// these fixed offsets; byte-identical to ps4debug's packet)
struct debug_event_packet_t {
    uint32_t lwpid;
    uint32_t status;
    char     tdname[40];
    reg64_t  regs;
    uint8_t  savefpu[832];
    uint8_t  dbregs[128];
};

struct console_print_packet_t {
    uint32_t length;
};

struct console_notify_packet_t {
    uint32_t messageType;
    uint32_t length;
};

struct console_foreground_app_response_t {
    uint32_t pid;
    char     titleid[16];
    char     contentid[64];
    char     name[40];
    char     app_ver[16];
};

#pragma pack(pop)
```

`src/core/runtime/scan_bridge.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/runtime/scan_bridge.cpp

#include "core/runtime/scan_bridge.hpp"

#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
// the Windows protection vocabulary the backends report
inline constexpr uint32_t MEM_COMMIT = 0x1000;
inline constexpr uint32_t PAGE_GUARD = 0x100;
#endif

namespace slop::core::runtime {

std::vector<memory::scan_region_t> target_scan_regions(const target_handle_t& h) {
    std::vector<memory::scan_region_t> out;
    auto res = active().enum_regions(h);
    if (!res.ok) return out;
    out.reserve(res.items.size());
    for (const auto& r : res.items) {
        const bool commit = (r.state & MEM_COMMIT) != 0;
        if (!commit || r.size == 0) continue;
        if (r.protect & PAGE_GUARD) continue;
        out.push_back({r.base, r.size, r.protect, r.type});
    }
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```

`src/core/runtime/scan_bridge.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/runtime/scan_bridge.hpp
// region sets and readers sourced from the active backend so scans ride the driver when its live

#include <vector>

#include "core/memory/memscan.hpp"
#include "core/memory/reader.hpp"
#include "core/memory/session_reader.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"

namespace slop::core::runtime {

// reader over the active backend, kernel badge means dtb copies, user badge means rpm
class backend_reader_t final : public memory::reader_t {
public:
    backend_reader_t(backend_t& b, const target_handle_t& h)
        : backend_(b), handle_(h) {}

    bool read(uintptr_t addr, void* dst, size_t len) override {
        auto io = backend_.read_memory(handle_, addr, dst, len);
        return io.ok && io.bytes == len;
    }

    // remote backends get one worker and large read-ahead chunks
    memory::reader_hints_t hints() const noexcept override {
        return memory::hints_for_backend(backend_.kind());
    }

private:
    backend_t&            backend_;
    const target_handle_t handle_;
};

// committed region set for the target, preference filtering happens in the engine
std::vector<memory::scan_region_t> target_scan_regions(const target_handle_t& h);

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```

`src/core/runtime/session.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/runtime/session.hpp"
#include "core/runtime/backend_registry.hpp"

#include "core/infra/clock.hpp"

namespace slop::core::runtime {

session_t::~session_t() {
    close();
}

session_t::session_t(session_t&& other) noexcept
    : m_backend(other.m_backend)
    , m_handle(other.m_handle)
    , m_info(std::move(other.m_info))
    , m_epoch_ms(other.m_epoch_ms)
{
    other.m_backend = nullptr;
    other.m_handle = {};
    other.m_epoch_ms = 0;
}

session_t& session_t::operator=(session_t&& other) noexcept {
    if (this != &other) {
        close();
        m_backend  = other.m_backend;
        m_handle   = other.m_handle;
        m_info     = std::move(other.m_info);
        m_epoch_ms = other.m_epoch_ms;
        other.m_backend  = nullptr;
        other.m_handle   = {};
        other.m_epoch_ms = 0;
    }
    return *this;
}

bool session_t::open(uint32_t pid) {
    close();
    // bind to the backend that is active now: a later backend swap must not
    // route this handle's reads/writes/detach through a different backend
    backend_t& b = active();
    m_handle = b.attach(pid);
    if (!m_handle.valid()) {
        m_handle = {};
        return false;
    }
    m_backend = &b;
    // the attach already learned name/path; enumerate only when it cannot say
    if (!b.handle_info(m_handle, m_info)) {
        m_info = {};
        if (auto procs = b.enum_processes(); procs.ok) {
            for (const auto& p : procs.items) {
                if (p.pid == pid) { m_info = p; break; }
            }
        }
        if (m_info.arch == arch_t::unknown) m_info.arch = b.query_arch(m_handle);
    }
    m_info.pid = pid;
    m_epoch_ms = infra::steady_ms();
    return true;
}

void session_t::close() {
    if (m_backend && m_handle.native) {
        m_backend->detach(m_handle);
    }
    m_backend = nullptr;
    m_handle = {};
    m_info   = {};
    m_epoch_ms = 0;
}

bool session_t::valid() const noexcept {
    return m_backend != nullptr && m_handle.valid();
}

uint32_t session_t::pid() const noexcept {
    return m_info.pid;
}

const std::string& session_t::name() const noexcept {
    return m_info.name;
}

arch_t session_t::arch() const noexcept {
    return m_info.arch;
}

int64_t session_t::epoch_ms() const noexcept {
    return m_epoch_ms;
}

io_result_t session_t::read(uintptr_t addr, void* buf, size_t len) {
    if (!m_backend) return io_result_t{false, 0, 6 /*ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE*/};
    return m_backend->read_memory(m_handle, addr, buf, len);
}

io_result_t session_t::write(uintptr_t addr, const void* buf, size_t len) {
    if (!m_backend) return io_result_t{false, 0, 6 /*ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE*/};
    return m_backend->write_memory(m_handle, addr, buf, len);
}

const target_handle_t& session_t::handle() const noexcept {
    return m_handle;
}

backend_t* session_t::backend() const noexcept {
    return m_backend;
}

const process_info_t& session_t::info() const noexcept {
    return m_info;
}

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/runtime/session.hpp
// Session object, wraps an attached target with cached info and hot-path forwarders

#include "core/runtime/backend.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

namespace slop::core::runtime {

class session_t {
public:
    session_t() = default;
    ~session_t();

    session_t(const session_t&) = delete;
    session_t& operator=(const session_t&) = delete;
    session_t(session_t&& other) noexcept;
    session_t& operator=(session_t&& other) noexcept;

    // Lifecycle
    bool open(uint32_t pid);
    void close();
    bool valid() const noexcept;

    // Info
    uint32_t           pid() const noexcept;
    const std::string& name() const noexcept;
    arch_t             arch() const noexcept;
    int64_t            epoch_ms() const noexcept;

    // Hot-path forwarders
    io_result_t read(uintptr_t addr, void* buf, size_t len);
    io_result_t write(uintptr_t addr, const void* buf, size_t len);

    // Access to underlying handle and the backend it was opened on (the
    // session keeps using that backend even if the active one changes)
    const target_handle_t& handle() const noexcept;
    backend_t*             backend() const noexcept;
    const process_info_t&  info() const noexcept;

private:
    backend_t*      m_backend = nullptr;
    target_handle_t m_handle{};
    process_info_t  m_info{};
    int64_t         m_epoch_ms = 0;
};

using session_ref = std::shared_ptr<const session_t>;

} // namespace slop::core::runtime
```
