```cpp
const api_doc_t* find_doc(const std::string& key) {
    for (const auto& d : kApiDocs)
        if (key == d.key) return &d;
    return nullptr;
}

// slop.log is callable (legacy slop.log(msg)) and carries the level helpers
void push_log_table(lua_State* L) {
    lua_createtable(L, 0, 4);
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_log_debug); lua_setfield(L, -2, "debug");
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_log_info);  lua_setfield(L, -2, "info");
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_log_warn);  lua_setfield(L, -2, "warn");
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_log_error); lua_setfield(L, -2, "error");
    lua_createtable(L, 0, 1);
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_slop_log);
    lua_setfield(L, -2, "__call");
    lua_setmetatable(L, -2);
}

int l_api(lua_State* L) {
    const auto& entries = api_entries();
    lua_createtable(L, static_cast<int>(entries.size()), 0);
    int i = 1;
    for (const auto& e : entries) {
        lua_createtable(L, 0, 4);
        if (e.group.empty())
            lua_pushfstring(L, "slop.%s", e.name.c_str());
        else
            lua_pushfstring(L, "slop.%s.%s", e.group.c_str(), e.name.c_str());
        lua_setfield(L, -2, "name");
        lua_pushlstring(L, e.signature.data(), e.signature.size());
        lua_setfield(L, -2, "signature");
        lua_pushlstring(L, e.doc.data(), e.doc.size());
        lua_setfield(L, -2, "doc");
        lua_pushboolean(L, e.callable);
        lua_setfield(L, -2, "callable");
        lua_rawseti(L, -2, i++);
    }
    return 1;
}

// opens the libraries and builds the slop table; runs under lua_pcall so a
// memory-limit failure during setup is an error, not a panic
int open_env(lua_State* L) {
    if (ctx_of(L)->unsafe) luaL_openlibs(L);
    else open_sandboxed(L);

    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_log);
    lua_setglobal(L, "print");

    lua_createtable(L, 0, 16);
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_version); lua_setfield(L, -2, "version");
    lua_pushcfunction(L, l_api);     lua_setfield(L, -2, "api");
    push_log_table(L);
    lua_setfield(L, -2, "log");

    for (const auto& g : kApiGroups) {
        lua_createtable(L, 0, 8);
        set_funcs(L, g.regs);
        lua_setfield(L, -2, g.group);
    }

    lua_setglobal(L, "slop");
    return 0;
}

// the script's return value goes into the output; protected because
// __len/__index metamethods can run lua code (and hit the hook)
int serialize_return(lua_State* L) {
    out_append(L, "return: ");
    append_value(L, 1, 0);
    out_append(L, "\n");
    return 0;
}

std::string lua_error_text(lua_State* L, int status, const script_ctx_t& ctx,
                           const char* fallback) {
    if (status == LUA_ERRMEM) {
        if (ctx.alloc_timed_out) return "script execution timed out";
        return "script exceeded the memory limit (" +
               std::to_string(ctx.mem_limit >> 20) + " MiB)";
    }
    const char* msg = lua_tostring(L, -1);
    return msg ? msg : fallback;
}

} // namespace

// the api list is built from the registration tables above plus kApiDocs;
// a binding without a doc row still shows up with an empty doc
const std::vector<api_entry_t>& api_entries() {
    static const std::vector<api_entry_t> entries = [] {
        std::vector<api_entry_t> out;
        for (const auto& d : kTopDocs) {
            api_entry_t e;
            e.name      = d.key;
            e.signature = d.signature;
            e.doc       = d.doc;
            e.callable  = d.callable;
            out.push_back(std::move(e));
        }
        for (const auto& g : kApiGroups) {
            for (const luaL_Reg* r = g.regs; r->name; ++r) {
                api_entry_t e;
                e.group = g.group;
                e.name  = r->name;
                if (const api_doc_t* d = find_doc(e.group + "." + e.name)) {
                    e.signature = d->signature;
                    e.doc       = d->doc;
                }
                out.push_back(std::move(e));
            }
        }
        return out;
    }();
    return entries;
}

// ---- snippets --------------------------------------------------------------

namespace {

std::filesystem::path snippets_dir() {
    return std::filesystem::path(infra::paths::app_data()) / "scripts";
}

std::filesystem::path snippet_path(const std::string& name) {
    return snippets_dir() / (name + ".lua");
}

int64_t file_ms(const std::filesystem::path& p) {
    std::error_code ec;
    const auto ft = std::filesystem::last_write_time(p, ec);
    if (ec) return 0;
    // file_clock has no fixed epoch in the standard: anchor it to now
    const auto sys = std::chrono::system_clock::now() +
        std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::system_clock::duration>(
            ft - std::filesystem::file_time_type::clock::now());
    return std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
               sys.time_since_epoch()).count();
}

} // namespace

bool snippet_name_valid(const std::string& name) {
    if (name.empty() || name.size() > 64) return false;
    if (name == "." || name == "..") return false;
    return std::all_of(name.begin(), name.end(), [](char c) {
        return std::isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) != 0 ||
               c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '.';
    });
}

bool snippet_save(const std::string& name, const std::string& code, std::string& err) {
    if (!snippet_name_valid(name)) {
        err = "snippet name must be 1..64 chars of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -";
        return false;
    }
    const auto path = snippet_path(name);
    if (!infra::paths::write_file_atomic(path.string(), code)) {
        err = "cannot write " + path.string();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

std::vector<snippet_t> snippet_list(std::string& err) {
    std::vector<snippet_t> out;
    std::error_code ec;
    const auto dir = snippets_dir();
    std::filesystem::create_directories(dir, ec);
    if (ec) {
        err = "cannot create " + dir.string() + ": " + ec.message();
        return out;
    }
    for (const auto& entry : std::filesystem::directory_iterator(dir, ec)) {
        if (ec) break;
        if (!entry.is_regular_file(ec) || entry.path().extension() != ".lua") continue;
        snippet_t s;
        s.name = entry.path().stem().string();
        if (!snippet_name_valid(s.name)) continue;
        s.updated_ms = file_ms(entry.path());
        out.push_back(std::move(s));
    }
    std::sort(out.begin(), out.end(),
              [](const snippet_t& a, const snippet_t& b) { return a.name < b.name; });
    return out;
}

bool snippet_load(const std::string& name, snippet_t& out, std::string& err) {
    if (!snippet_name_valid(name)) {
        err = "snippet name must be 1..64 chars of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -";
        return false;
    }
    const auto path = snippet_path(name);
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f.is_open()) {
        err = "no snippet named " + name;
        return false;
    }
    out.name = name;
    out.code.assign(std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(f), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
    out.updated_ms = file_ms(path);
    return true;
}

bool snippet_delete(const std::string& name, std::string& err) {
    if (!snippet_name_valid(name)) {
        err = "snippet name must be 1..64 chars of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -";
        return false;
    }
    std::error_code ec;
    const auto path = snippet_path(name);
    if (!std::filesystem::remove(path, ec) || ec) {
        err = ec ? "cannot delete " + path.string() + ": " + ec.message()
                 : "no snippet named " + name;
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

int clamp_timeout_ms(int64_t ms) noexcept {
    return static_cast<int>(std::clamp<int64_t>(ms, kMinTimeoutMs, kMaxTimeoutMs));
}

lua_run_result_t lua_run(const std::string& code, int timeout_ms) {
    lua_run_options_t opt;
    opt.timeout_ms = timeout_ms;
    return lua_run(code, opt);
}

lua_run_result_t lua_run(const std::string& code, const lua_run_options_t& opt) {
    lua_run_result_t res;

    // ctx outlives the state: lua_close still frees through capped_alloc
    script_ctx_t ctx;
    ctx.cancel    = opt.cancel;
    ctx.tool_mu   = opt.tool_mutex;
    ctx.mem_limit = opt.mem_limit ? opt.mem_limit : kDefaultMemLimit;
    ctx.unsafe    = opt.unsafe ? *opt.unsafe
                               : infra::settings::get<bool>("script_unsafe", false);
    res.timeout_ms = clamp_timeout_ms(opt.timeout_ms);
    res.unsafe     = ctx.unsafe;
    ctx.deadline_ms = now_ms() + res.timeout_ms;

    lua_State* L = lua_newstate(capped_alloc, &ctx);
    if (!L) {
        res.error = "lua_newstate failed (memory limit too small?)";
        return res;
    }

    lua_pushcfunction(L, open_env);
    int st = lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0);
    if (st != LUA_OK) {
        res.error = "script environment setup failed: " +
                    lua_error_text(L, st, ctx, "unknown error");
    } else {
        lua_sethook(L, timeout_hook, LUA_MASKCOUNT, kHookInstructions);
        // sandboxed runs refuse precompiled chunks for the same reason as load()
        st = luaL_loadbufferx(L, code.c_str(), code.size(), "=slop_script",
                              ctx.unsafe ? nullptr : "t");
        if (st != LUA_OK) {
            res.error = lua_error_text(L, st, ctx, "load failed");
        } else if ((st = lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0)) != LUA_OK) {
            // one result slot: the return value is serialized into the
            // output so return x is not lost
            res.error = lua_error_text(L, st, ctx, "runtime error");
        } else {
            // the body is done: the deadline no longer applies, so result
            // serialization cannot trip the hook or the allocator
            ctx.deadline_ms = std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max();
            res.ok = true;
            lua_pushcfunction(L, serialize_return);
            lua_insert(L, -2);
            if ((st = lua_pcall(L, 1, 0, 0)) != LUA_OK)
                out_append(L, "\n[return value not serialized: " +
                                  lua_error_text(L, st, ctx, "error") + "]\n");
        }
    }

    lua_close(L);
    res.output = std::move(ctx.output);
    res.output_truncated = ctx.output_truncated;
    res.peak_mem = ctx.mem_peak;
    return res;
}

} // namespace slop::core::script
```

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/script/lua_engine.hpp
// embedded lua 5.4 over the core services on the raw c api
// the static analysis surface is the lua to reverse slop as python to ida
// layer, it all operates on the shared session so renames and comments
// made from lua or mcp appear everywhere:
//
//   slop.image.load(path[, base])     load a binary into the shared session
//   slop.image.load_from_target()     load the attached target's main module
//   slop.image.unload()               tear the session down
//   slop.image.status()               {ready,name,base,entry,hype={...}}
//   slop.image.wait_ready([ms])       block until hyperion analysis lands
//
//   slop.disasm.decode(addr[, n])     {addr,len,text,bytes,target,...} rows
//   slop.disasm.functions([limit])    {va,size,name[,blocks,loops,...]} rows
//   slop.disasm.function_at(va)       owning function row (nil outside)
//   slop.disasm.xrefs_to(va)          {from,kind} rows (hyperion-enriched)
//   slop.disasm.strings([min[,lim]])  {va,text,utf16} rows
//   slop.disasm.pe()                  headers, sections, imports, exports
//   slop.disasm.bytes(addr[, len])    raw file-image bytes (binary string)
//   slop.disasm.name(va) / set_name(va, name)       persisted rename
//   slop.disasm.comment(va) / set_comment(va, text) persisted annotation
//   slop.disasm.bookmark_toggle(va) / bookmarks()
//   unnamed functions are sub_<VA uppercase hex> (disasm::default_function_name)
//
//   slop.decomp.decompile(va)        pseudo-C lines + signature (hyperion)
//   slop.decomp.blocks(va)            CFG blocks + loops for a function
//   slop.decomp.vtables() / globals() / rtti()   rich analysis DB views
//
// live target surface:
//   slop.version() / slop.api() / slop.log(msg)
//   slop.log(level, msg) / slop.log.debug|info|warn|error(msg)
//   slop.target.list() / attach(pid) / status()
//   slop.mem.read_hex(addr,len)       lowercase hex string of the bytes read
//   slop.mem.read_bytes(addr,len)     raw bytes (binary lua string)
//   slop.mem.write_hex(addr,hexstr) / scan(cfg)
//   slop.disasm.disassemble(addr,count)     live-process disassembly
//   slop.analyze.packer([path])
//
// ps4 console + debugger surface, each call runs the matching mcp action
// (target ps4_* / debugger ps4_*) so slot bookkeeping and errors are shared:
//   slop.ps4.connect(host[,port]) / disconnect() / auto(host[,port]) / status()
//   slop.debugger.status() / attach(pid) / detach()
//   slop.debugger.bp_set(addr[,index]) / bp_clear(addr) / bp_list()
//   slop.debugger.watch_set(addr[,len[,type]]) / watch_clear(addr) / watch_list()
//   slop.debugger.continue([stop]) / step([lwpid]) / suspend(lwpid) / resume(lwpid)
//   slop.debugger.wait([ms]) / events([max]) / regs(lwpid) / set_reg(lwpid,name,value)
//   slop.debugger.callstack(lwpid[,depth]) / call(addr[,args[,pid]])
//   slop.debugger.run_until(addr[,ms]) / find_write(addr[,len[,ms]])
//   slop.debugger.trace_calls(addr[,count[,ms]])
//   slop.debugger.action(name, params)     any other debugger ps4_* action
// blocking waits are clamped to the script's remaining time budget
//
// sandbox: by default only base (without dofile/loadfile, load is text-only),
// string, table, math, utf8 and os.clock/os.time/os.difftime are opened.
// the settings key "script_unsafe" (bool) restores the full standard library
// (io, os, package, debug, coroutine) and host-file debugger actions
//
// every script runs under an instruction count hook (deadline + cancel
// checks every kHookInstructions vm instructions), an allocation cap and an
// output cap; print output is captured and the return value lands in the
// output as return: ...
//
// wall-clock backstop: the hook only counts vm instructions, so a loop of
// cheap C calls (slop.mem.read_bytes) or one long native call would outrun
// it. every slop.* binding re-checks the deadline on entry, the allocator
// refuses growth past the deadline, and blocking bindings clamp their wait
// to the remaining budget. the run therefore ends within one binding call
// of timeout_ms even when the vm never executes another instruction.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/infra/cancel.hpp"

namespace slop::core::script {

// one clamp shared by the engine and the mcp layer
inline constexpr int    kMinTimeoutMs     = 10;
inline constexpr int    kMaxTimeoutMs     = 60000;
inline constexpr int    kDefaultTimeoutMs = 5000;
inline constexpr int    kHookInstructions = 1000;
inline constexpr size_t kDefaultMemLimit  = 256u << 20;   // bytes of lua heap
inline constexpr size_t kMaxOutputBytes   = 4u << 20;     // captured print stream

int clamp_timeout_ms(int64_t ms) noexcept;

struct lua_run_options_t {
    int timeout_ms = kDefaultTimeoutMs;   // clamped with clamp_timeout_ms
    // nullopt reads the "script_unsafe" setting (default false = sandboxed)
    std::optional<bool> unsafe;
    size_t mem_limit = kDefaultMemLimit;  // lua allocations past this fail
    infra::cancel_token_t cancel;         // polled by the hook and blocking bindings
    // taken around each slop.* binding that touches shared state, never
    // across the whole script; null runs the bindings unserialized
    std::mutex* tool_mutex = nullptr;
};

struct lua_run_result_t {
    bool        ok  = false;
    std::string output;   // captured print/slop.log stream
    std::string error;    // non-empty on failure
    int         timeout_ms = 0;          // effective budget after clamping
    bool        unsafe = false;          // full stdlib was opened
    size_t      peak_mem = 0;            // high-water mark of the lua heap
    bool        output_truncated = false;
};

lua_run_result_t lua_run(const std::string& code, const lua_run_options_t& opt);
lua_run_result_t lua_run(const std::string& code, int timeout_ms = kDefaultTimeoutMs);

// ---- script.api: the slop.* surface, generated from the registration tables
//
// one row per registered binding plus the top-level functions; the Scripts
// panel builds its completion list from this and the MCP script.api action
// returns it, so the docs cannot drift from what open_env() actually binds
struct api_entry_t {
    std::string group;     // "" for slop.version / slop.log / slop.api
    std::string name;      // "read_hex"
    std::string signature; // "(addr, len) -> hex string"
    std::string doc;       // one line
    bool        callable = true;   // false: a table with __call (slop.log)
};
const std::vector<api_entry_t>& api_entries();

// ---- snippets: named scripts persisted under <app_data>\scripts
//
// names are 1..64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._-], never "." or "..", so a snippet
// name can never escape the folder

struct snippet_t {
    std::string name;
    std::string code;
    int64_t     updated_ms = 0;
};

bool snippet_name_valid(const std::string& name);
bool snippet_save(const std::string& name, const std::string& code, std::string& err);
std::vector<snippet_t> snippet_list(std::string& err);
bool snippet_load(const std::string& name, snippet_t& out, std::string& err);
```

`src/core/util/fs_tools.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/util/fs_tools.cpp

#include "core/util/fs_tools.hpp"

#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <fstream>
#include <functional>
#include <iterator>

namespace slop::core::util {

namespace {

constexpr int kSearchDepth = 8;
constexpr int kGrepDepth   = 6;

std::wstring to_w(const std::string& s) {
    if (s.empty()) return {};
    const int n = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.data(), static_cast<int>(s.size()),
                                      nullptr, 0);
    if (n <= 0) return std::wstring(s.begin(), s.end());   // not utf-8, keep bytes
    std::wstring out(static_cast<size_t>(n), L'\0');
    MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s.data(), static_cast<int>(s.size()), out.data(), n);
    return out;
}

std::string to_utf8(const wchar_t* w) {
    const int n = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w, -1, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr);
    if (n <= 1) return {};
    std::string out(static_cast<size_t>(n - 1), '\0');
    WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w, -1, out.data(), n, nullptr, nullptr);
    return out;
}

std::string lower_copy(std::string s) {
    for (char& c : s)
        c = static_cast<char>(tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
    return s;
}

std::string win32_error(const char* what) {
    return std::string(what) + " (win32 error " + std::to_string(GetLastError()) + ")";
}

// \\?\C:\x -> C:\x, \\?\UNC\srv\share -> \\srv\share, and a ":stream" suffix
// (NTFS alternate data stream) is dropped: the jail must judge the file the
// bytes land in, not the stream name
std::wstring normalise_input(const std::wstring& in) {
    std::wstring p = in;
    if (p.size() >= 4 && p[0] == L'\\' && p[1] == L'\\' &&
        (p[2] == L'?' || p[2] == L'.') && p[3] == L'\\') {
        p.erase(0, 4);
        if (p.size() >= 4 && (p[0] == L'U' || p[0] == L'u') &&
            (p[1] == L'N' || p[1] == L'n') && (p[2] == L'C' || p[2] == L'c') &&
            p[3] == L'\\')
            p.replace(0, 4, L"\\\\");
    }
    const size_t drive = (p.size() >= 2 && p[1] == L':') ? 2 : 0;
    if (const size_t colon = p.find(L':', drive); colon != std::wstring::npos)
        p.resize(colon);
    return p;
}

} // namespace

bool canonical_path(const std::string& path, std::string* out, std::string* error) {
    auto fail = [&](const std::string& why) {
        if (error) *error = why;
        return false;
    };
    if (path.empty()) return fail("empty path");
    const std::wstring w = normalise_input(to_w(path));
    if (w.empty()) return fail("empty path");

    // lexical pass first: GetFullPathName makes the path absolute and folds
    // `.` and `..` without touching the disk
    std::wstring full(MAX_PATH * 2, L'\0');
    for (;;) {
        const DWORD n = GetFullPathNameW(w.c_str(), static_cast<DWORD>(full.size()),
                                         full.data(), nullptr);
        if (n == 0) return fail(win32_error("cannot resolve path"));
        if (n < full.size()) { full.resize(n); break; }
        full.resize(static_cast<size_t>(n) + 1);   // n excludes the terminator
    }

    // then walk up to the nearest existing ancestor and let the kernel report
    // its real name: that is what expands 8.3 names and follows junctions
    std::wstring head = full, tail;
    for (;;) {
        HANDLE h = CreateFileW(head.c_str(), FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES,
                               FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE,
                               nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS,
                               nullptr);
        if (h != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
            std::wstring real(32768, L'\0');
            const DWORD n = GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(
                h, real.data(), static_cast<DWORD>(real.size()),
                FILE_NAME_NORMALIZED | VOLUME_NAME_DOS);
            CloseHandle(h);
            if (n == 0) return fail(win32_error("cannot resolve path"));
            real.resize(n);
            if (real.rfind(L"\\\\?\\UNC\\", 0) == 0)
                real.replace(0, 7, L"\\\\");
            else if (real.rfind(L"\\\\?\\", 0) == 0)
                real.erase(0, 4);
            *out = to_utf8(real.c_str()) + to_utf8(tail.c_str());
            return true;
        }
        const DWORD err = GetLastError();
        if (err != ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND && err != ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND &&
            err != ERROR_BAD_NETPATH)
            return fail(win32_error("cannot resolve path"));
        // a dangling link: creating through it would land outside every jail
        if (const DWORD attr = GetFileAttributesW(head.c_str());
            attr != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES && (attr & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT))
            return fail("cannot resolve reparse point (its target does not exist)");
        const size_t slash = head.find_last_of(L"\\/");
        if (slash == std::wstring::npos) return fail("cannot resolve path");
        // "C:\" itself is unreachable: there is no parent left to try
        if (head.size() <= 3 && head.size() >= 2 && head[1] == L':')
            return fail(win32_error("cannot resolve path"));
        tail = head.substr(slash) + tail;
        head.resize(slash);
        if (head.size() == 2 && head[1] == L':') head += L'\\';
        if (head.empty()) return fail("cannot resolve path");
    }
}

bool path_within(const std::string& path, const std::string& root) {
    if (root.empty() || path.size() < root.size()) return false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < root.size(); ++i)
        if (tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(path[i])) !=
            tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(root[i])))
            return false;
    if (path.size() == root.size()) return true;
    return root.back() == '\\' || path[root.size()] == '\\';
}

bool read_file(const std::string& path, uint64_t offset, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, uint64_t* total_size, std::string* error) {
    out->clear();
    std::ifstream f(to_w(path), std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot open file";
        return false;
    }
    f.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const auto end = f.tellg();
    if (end < 0) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot stat file";
        return false;
    }
    const uint64_t size = static_cast<uint64_t>(end);
    if (total_size) *total_size = size;
    if (offset >= size) return true;
    const size_t len = static_cast<size_t>(std::min<uint64_t>(size - offset, max_bytes));
    f.seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(offset), std::ios::beg);
    out->resize(len);
    f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(out->data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(len));
    if (static_cast<size_t>(f.gcount()) != len) {
        out->resize(static_cast<size_t>(std::max<std::streamsize>(f.gcount(), 0)));
        if (error) *error = "short read: got " + std::to_string(out->size()) + " of " +
                            std::to_string(len) + " bytes";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

bool read_file(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, std::string* error) {
    return read_file(path, 0, out, max_bytes, nullptr, error);
}

bool write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& bytes,
                bool append, std::string* error) {
    std::ofstream f(to_w(path), std::ios::binary |
                                    (append ? std::ios::app : std::ios::trunc));
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot open file for writing";
        return false;
    }
    f.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()),
            static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
    f.flush();
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "write failed (disk full or file locked?)";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

std::vector<file_entry_t> list_directory(const std::string& dir,
                                         std::string* error) {
    std::vector<file_entry_t> out;
    WIN32_FIND_DATAW fd{};
    HANDLE h = FindFirstFileW((to_w(dir) + L"\\*").c_str(), &fd);
    if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        if (error) *error = win32_error("cannot list directory");
        return out;
    }
    for (;;) {
        if (wcscmp(fd.cFileName, L".") != 0 && wcscmp(fd.cFileName, L"..") != 0) {
            file_entry_t e;
            e.name = to_utf8(fd.cFileName);
            e.path = dir + "\\" + e.name;
            ULARGE_INTEGER sz;
            sz.HighPart = fd.nFileSizeHigh;
            sz.LowPart = fd.nFileSizeLow;
            e.size = sz.QuadPart;
            e.directory = (fd.dwFileAttributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY) != 0;
            e.reparse   = (fd.dwFileAttributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT) != 0;
            out.push_back(std::move(e));
        }
        if (FindNextFileW(h, &fd)) continue;
        if (GetLastError() != ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES && error)
            *error = win32_error("directory enumeration stopped early");
        break;
    }
    FindClose(h);
    return out;
}

bool create_directory(const std::string& path, std::string* error) {
    if (!CreateDirectoryW(to_w(path).c_str(), nullptr)) {
        if (GetLastError() != ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) {
            if (error) *error = win32_error("create failed");
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

bool delete_path(const std::string& path, std::string* error) {
    if (DeleteFileW(to_w(path).c_str())) return true;
    if (RemoveDirectoryW(to_w(path).c_str())) return true;
    if (error) *error = win32_error("delete failed");
    return false;
}

std::vector<file_entry_t> search_files(const std::string& root,
                                       const std::string& needle,
                                       size_t max_results,
                                       const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel) {
    std::vector<file_entry_t> out;
    const std::string needle_l = lower_copy(needle);

    std::function<void(const std::string&, int)> walk =
        [&](const std::string& dir, int depth) {
            if (depth > kSearchDepth || out.size() >= max_results || cancel.cancelled()) return;
            for (const auto& e : list_directory(dir)) {
                if (out.size() >= max_results || cancel.cancelled()) return;
                if (lower_copy(e.name).find(needle_l) != std::string::npos)
                    out.push_back(e);
                // never descend through junctions/symlinks: loops and huge detours
                if (e.directory && !e.reparse) walk(e.path, depth + 1);
            }
        };
    walk(root, 0);
    return out;
}


std::vector<grep_hit_t> grep_in_files(const std::string& root,
                                      const std::string& needle,
                                      const std::string& glob_suffix,
                                      size_t max_hits,
                                      const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel) {
    std::vector<grep_hit_t> out;
    const std::string needle_l = lower_copy(needle);
    const std::string suffix_l = lower_copy(glob_suffix);

    std::function<void(const std::string&, int)> walk =
        [&](const std::string& dir, int depth) {
            if (out.size() >= max_hits || depth > kGrepDepth || cancel.cancelled()) return;
            for (const auto& e : list_directory(dir)) {
                if (out.size() >= max_hits || cancel.cancelled()) return;
                if (e.directory) {
                    if (!e.reparse) walk(e.path, depth + 1);
                    continue;
                }
                if (!suffix_l.empty() && !lower_copy(e.name).ends_with(suffix_l)) continue;
                std::ifstream f(to_w(e.path), std::ios::binary);
                if (!f) continue;
                std::string line;
                uint32_t lineno = 0;
                while (std::getline(f, line)) {
                    ++lineno;
                    if ((lineno & 0x3FF) == 0 && cancel.cancelled()) return;
                    if (lower_copy(line).find(needle_l) != std::string::npos) {
                        grep_hit_t hit;
                        hit.path = e.path;
                        hit.line = lineno;
                        hit.text = line.substr(0, std::min<size_t>(line.size(), 240));
                        out.push_back(std::move(hit));
                        if (out.size() >= max_hits) return;
                    }
                }
            }
        };
    walk(root, 0);
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::util
```

`src/core/util/fs_tools.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// host filesystem helpers behind the mcp fs tool
// paths are UTF-8; recursive walks never follow reparse points (junctions,
// symlinks, mount points) and stop as soon as the cancel token fires

#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "core/infra/cancel.hpp"

namespace slop::core::util {

struct file_entry_t {
    std::string name;
    std::string path;
    uint64_t    size = 0;
    bool        directory = false;
    bool        reparse = false;    // junction / symlink / mount point
};

// reads up to max_bytes starting at offset; *total_size (optional) gets the
// file size. a short read is an error, reading at/after EOF yields 0 bytes
bool read_file(const std::string& path, uint64_t offset, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, uint64_t* total_size = nullptr,
               std::string* error = nullptr);
bool read_file(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, std::string* error = nullptr);
bool write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& bytes,
                bool append, std::string* error = nullptr);
// error is set (and the partial listing returned) when enumeration fails midway
std::vector<file_entry_t> list_directory(const std::string& dir,
                                         std::string* error = nullptr);
bool create_directory(const std::string& path, std::string* error = nullptr);
bool delete_path(const std::string& path, std::string* error = nullptr);

// The path the filesystem will really use: `..` segments, symlinks and
// junctions (GetFinalPathNameByHandle), 8.3 short names, \\?\ / \\.\ prefixes
// and NTFS alternate data streams (`file.txt:stream`) are all resolved away.
// A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing parent,
// so a write/create target can be judged before it is created.
bool canonical_path(const std::string& path, std::string* out,
                    std::string* error = nullptr);

// true when `path` (already canonical) is `root` or below it, case-insensitive
bool path_within(const std::string& path, const std::string& root);

// Recursive case-insensitive filename substring search under `root`
std::vector<file_entry_t> search_files(const std::string& root,
                                       const std::string& needle,
                                       size_t max_results,
                                       const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel = {});

// Content grep: case-insensitive literal substring match across files under
// root whose name ends with glob_suffix (empty = every file)
struct grep_hit_t {
    std::string path;
    uint32_t    line = 0;
    std::string text;
};
std::vector<grep_hit_t> grep_in_files(const std::string& root,
                                      const std::string& needle,
                                      const std::string& glob_suffix,
                                      size_t max_hits,
                                      const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel = {});

} // namespace slop::core::util
```

`src/core/util/fs_tools_posix.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/util/fs_tools_posix.cpp
// POSIX twin of fs_tools.cpp: same contract, std::filesystem instead of the
// Win32 file API. Paths are byte strings; symlinks are resolved and never
// followed during walks, matching the Windows reparse-point rule.

#include "core/util/fs_tools.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <functional>
#include <system_error>

namespace slop::core::util {

namespace {

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

constexpr int kSearchDepth = 8;
constexpr int kGrepDepth   = 6;

std::string lower_copy(std::string s) {
    for (char& c : s)
        c = static_cast<char>(tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
    return s;
}

std::string err_text(const std::error_code& ec) {
    return ec.message();
}

} // namespace

bool canonical_path(const std::string& path, std::string* out, std::string* error) {
    if (path.empty()) {
        if (error) *error = "empty path";
        return false;
    }
    std::error_code ec;
    // weakly_canonical resolves the existing prefix and appends the rest, so a
    // write target can be judged before it exists
    fs::path p = fs::weakly_canonical(fs::path(path), ec);
    if (ec) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot resolve path: " + err_text(ec);
        return false;
    }
    *out = p.string();
    return true;
}

bool path_within(const std::string& path, const std::string& root) {
    if (root.empty() || path.size() < root.size()) return false;
    if (path.compare(0, root.size(), root) != 0) return false;
    if (path.size() == root.size()) return true;
    return root.back() == '/' || path[root.size()] == '/';
}

bool read_file(const std::string& path, uint64_t offset, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, uint64_t* total_size, std::string* error) {
    out->clear();
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot open file";
        return false;
    }
    f.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const auto end = f.tellg();
    if (end < 0) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot stat file";
        return false;
    }
    const uint64_t size = static_cast<uint64_t>(end);
    if (total_size) *total_size = size;
    if (offset >= size) return true;
    const size_t len = static_cast<size_t>(std::min<uint64_t>(size - offset, max_bytes));
    f.seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(offset), std::ios::beg);
    out->resize(len);
    f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(out->data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(len));
    if (static_cast<size_t>(f.gcount()) != len) {
        out->resize(static_cast<size_t>(std::max<std::streamsize>(f.gcount(), 0)));
        if (error) *error = "short read: got " + std::to_string(out->size()) + " of " +
                            std::to_string(len) + " bytes";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

bool read_file(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>* out,
               size_t max_bytes, std::string* error) {
    return read_file(path, 0, out, max_bytes, nullptr, error);
}

bool write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& bytes,
                bool append, std::string* error) {
    std::ofstream f(path, std::ios::binary | (append ? std::ios::app : std::ios::trunc));
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot open file for writing";
        return false;
    }
    f.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()),
            static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
    f.flush();
    if (!f) {
        if (error) *error = "write failed (disk full?)";
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

std::vector<file_entry_t> list_directory(const std::string& dir, std::string* error) {
    std::vector<file_entry_t> out;
    std::error_code ec;
    fs::directory_iterator it(fs::path(dir), ec);
    if (ec) {
        if (error) *error = "cannot list directory: " + err_text(ec);
        return out;
    }
    for (const auto& de : it) {
        std::error_code entry_ec;
        const bool is_link = de.is_symlink(entry_ec);
        file_entry_t e;
        e.name = de.path().filename().string();
        e.path = de.path().string();
        e.directory = de.is_directory(entry_ec);
        e.reparse = is_link;
        if (!e.directory) e.size = de.file_size(entry_ec);
        out.push_back(std::move(e));
    }
    return out;
}

bool create_directory(const std::string& path, std::string* error) {
    std::error_code ec;
    fs::create_directories(fs::path(path), ec);
    if (ec) {
        if (error) *error = "create failed: " + err_text(ec);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

bool delete_path(const std::string& path, std::string* error) {
    std::error_code ec;
    const bool removed = fs::remove(fs::path(path), ec);
    if (ec || !removed) {
        if (error) *error = "delete failed: " + (ec ? err_text(ec) : "not found");
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

std::vector<file_entry_t> search_files(const std::string& root,
                                       const std::string& needle,
                                       size_t max_results,
                                       const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel) {
    std::vector<file_entry_t> out;
    const std::string needle_l = lower_copy(needle);

    std::function<void(const std::string&, int)> walk = [&](const std::string& dir, int depth) {
        if (depth > kSearchDepth || out.size() >= max_results || cancel.cancelled()) return;
        for (const auto& e : list_directory(dir)) {
            if (out.size() >= max_results || cancel.cancelled()) return;
            if (lower_copy(e.name).find(needle_l) != std::string::npos) out.push_back(e);
            if (e.directory && !e.reparse) walk(e.path, depth + 1);
        }
    };
    walk(root, 0);
    return out;
}

std::vector<grep_hit_t> grep_in_files(const std::string& root,
                                      const std::string& needle,
                                      const std::string& glob_suffix,
                                      size_t max_hits,
                                      const infra::cancel_token_t& cancel) {
    std::vector<grep_hit_t> out;
    const std::string needle_l = lower_copy(needle);
    const std::string suffix_l = lower_copy(glob_suffix);

    std::function<void(const std::string&, int)> walk = [&](const std::string& dir, int depth) {
        if (out.size() >= max_hits || depth > kGrepDepth || cancel.cancelled()) return;
        for (const auto& e : list_directory(dir)) {
            if (out.size() >= max_hits || cancel.cancelled()) return;
            if (e.directory) {
                if (!e.reparse) walk(e.path, depth + 1);
                continue;
            }
            if (!suffix_l.empty() && !lower_copy(e.name).ends_with(suffix_l)) continue;
            std::ifstream f(e.path, std::ios::binary);
            if (!f) continue;
            std::string line;
            uint32_t lineno = 0;
            while (std::getline(f, line)) {
                ++lineno;
                if ((lineno & 0x3FF) == 0 && cancel.cancelled()) return;
                if (lower_copy(line).find(needle_l) != std::string::npos) {
                    grep_hit_t hit;
                    hit.path = e.path;
                    hit.line = lineno;
                    hit.text = line.substr(0, std::min<size_t>(line.size(), 240));
                    out.push_back(std::move(hit));
                    if (out.size() >= max_hits) return;
                }
            }
        }
    };
    walk(root, 0);
    return out;
}

} // namespace slop::core::util
```

`src/core/util/sha256.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/util/sha256.cpp
#include "core/util/sha256.hpp"

#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif

#include <vector>

#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <bcrypt.h>

#pragma comment(lib, "bcrypt.lib")
#else
#include <openssl/sha.h>
#endif

namespace slop::core::util {

std::string sha256_hex(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) {
#ifndef _WIN32
    unsigned char digest[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH];
    ::SHA256(data, len, digest);
    static constexpr char kHex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
    std::string out;
    out.reserve(sizeof(digest) * 2);
    for (unsigned char b : digest) {
        out.push_back(kHex[b >> 4]);
        out.push_back(kHex[b & 0xF]);
    }
    return out;
#else
    BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE alg = nullptr;
    BCRYPT_HASH_HANDLE hash = nullptr;
    std::string out;
    if (BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(&alg, BCRYPT_SHA256_ALGORITHM, nullptr, 0) != 0)
        return out;
    DWORD hl = 0, cb = 0;
    if (BCryptGetProperty(alg, BCRYPT_HASH_LENGTH, reinterpret_cast<PUCHAR>(&hl),
                          sizeof(hl), &cb, 0) == 0) {
        std::vector<uint8_t> digest(hl);
        if (BCryptCreateHash(alg, &hash, nullptr, 0, nullptr, 0, 0) == 0) {
            if (BCryptHashData(hash, const_cast<PUCHAR>(data),
                               static_cast<ULONG>(len), 0) == 0 &&
                BCryptFinishHash(hash, digest.data(), hl, 0) == 0) {
                static constexpr char kHex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
                out.reserve(digest.size() * 2);
                for (uint8_t b : digest) {
                    out.push_back(kHex[b >> 4]);
                    out.push_back(kHex[b & 0xF]);
                }
            }
            BCryptDestroyHash(hash);
        }
    }
    BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider(alg, 0);
    return out;
#endif
}

} // namespace slop::core::util
```

`src/core/util/zip_reader.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/util/zip_reader.cpp

#include "core/util/zip_reader.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <climits>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>

#include <zlib.h>

namespace slop::core::util::zip {

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kLocalSig     = 0x04034b50;
constexpr uint32_t kCentralSig   = 0x02014b50;
constexpr uint32_t kEocdSig      = 0x06054b50;
constexpr uint32_t kEocd64LocSig = 0x07064b50;
constexpr uint32_t kEocd64Sig    = 0x06064b50;

constexpr size_t kEocdSize       = 22;
constexpr size_t kEocd64LocSize  = 20;
constexpr size_t kEocd64Size     = 56;
constexpr size_t kCentralSize    = 46;
constexpr size_t kLocalSize      = 30;
constexpr size_t kMaxComment     = 0xFFFF;

uint16_t rd16(const uint8_t* p) noexcept {
    return static_cast<uint16_t>(p[0] | (p[1] << 8));
}
uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t* p) noexcept {
    return static_cast<uint32_t>(p[0]) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(p[1]) << 8) |
           (static_cast<uint32_t>(p[2]) << 16) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(p[3]) << 24);
}
uint64_t rd64(const uint8_t* p) noexcept {
    return static_cast<uint64_t>(rd32(p)) | (static_cast<uint64_t>(rd32(p + 4)) << 32);
}

// [off, off+size) inside a buffer of `len` bytes, overflow-safe
bool in_range(uint64_t off, uint64_t size, size_t len) noexcept {
    return off <= len && size <= static_cast<uint64_t>(len) - off;
}

bool fail(std::string* error, std::string msg) {
    if (error) *error = std::move(msg);
    return false;
}

} // namespace

bool has_zip_magic(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) noexcept {
    if (!data || len < 4) return false;
    const uint32_t sig = rd32(data);
    return sig == kLocalSig || sig == kEocdSig;
}

bool archive_t::open(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, std::string* error) {
    data_ = nullptr;
    len_  = 0;
    entries_.clear();
    index_.clear();

    if (!data || len < kEocdSize) return fail(error, "zip: file too small");

    // end of central directory: scan backwards through the comment window
    size_t eocd = SIZE_MAX;
    const size_t last  = len - kEocdSize;
    const size_t first = last > kMaxComment ? last - kMaxComment : 0;
    for (size_t pos = last + 1; pos-- > first;) {
        if (rd32(data + pos) != kEocdSig) continue;
        const size_t comment = rd16(data + pos + 20);
        if (comment <= len - pos - kEocdSize) { eocd = pos; break; }
    }
    if (eocd == SIZE_MAX) return fail(error, "zip: end of central directory not found");

    const uint8_t* e = data + eocd;
    uint64_t total   = rd16(e + 10);
    uint64_t cd_size = rd32(e + 12);
    uint64_t cd_off  = rd32(e + 16);

    // zip64: locator sits immediately before the classic record
    if (eocd >= kEocd64LocSize && rd32(data + eocd - kEocd64LocSize) == kEocd64LocSig) {
        const uint64_t rec = rd64(data + eocd - kEocd64LocSize + 8);
        if (!in_range(rec, kEocd64Size, len) || rd32(data + rec) != kEocd64Sig)
            return fail(error, "zip: bad zip64 end of central directory");
        const uint8_t* r = data + rec;
        total   = rd64(r + 32);
        cd_size = rd64(r + 40);
        cd_off  = rd64(r + 48);
    } else if (total == 0xFFFF || cd_size == 0xFFFFFFFFu || cd_off == 0xFFFFFFFFu) {
        return fail(error, "zip: zip64 locator missing");
    }

    if (!in_range(cd_off, cd_size, len))
        return fail(error, "zip: central directory outside the file");
    if (total > cd_size / kCentralSize)
        return fail(error, "zip: entry count exceeds central directory size");

    entries_.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(total));
    const uint8_t* cd  = data + cd_off;
    const size_t   end = static_cast<size_t>(cd_size);
    size_t         pos = 0;
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < total; ++i) {
        if (end - pos < kCentralSize || rd32(cd + pos) != kCentralSig)
            return fail(error, "zip: corrupt central directory entry " + std::to_string(i));
        const uint8_t* h = cd + pos;
        const size_t name_len    = rd16(h + 28);
        const size_t extra_len   = rd16(h + 30);
        const size_t comment_len = rd16(h + 32);
        const size_t var_len     = name_len + extra_len + comment_len;
        if (end - pos - kCentralSize < var_len)
            return fail(error, "zip: truncated central directory entry " + std::to_string(i));

        entry_t ent;
        ent.flags               = rd16(h + 8);
        ent.method              = rd16(h + 10);
        ent.crc32               = rd32(h + 16);
        ent.compressed_size     = rd32(h + 20);
        ent.uncompressed_size   = rd32(h + 24);
        ent.local_header_offset = rd32(h + 42);
        ent.name.assign(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(h + kCentralSize), name_len);

        // zip64 extended information: only the saturated fields, in order
        const bool need_u = ent.uncompressed_size   == 0xFFFFFFFFu;
        const bool need_c = ent.compressed_size     == 0xFFFFFFFFu;
        const bool need_o = ent.local_header_offset == 0xFFFFFFFFu;
        if (need_u || need_c || need_o) {
            const uint8_t* x    = h + kCentralSize + name_len;
            size_t         xpos = 0;
            bool           found = false;
            while (extra_len - xpos >= 4) {
                const uint16_t id = rd16(x + xpos);
                const size_t   sz = rd16(x + xpos + 2);
                if (extra_len - xpos - 4 < sz) break;
                if (id == 0x0001) {
                    const uint8_t* f    = x + xpos + 4;
                    size_t         fpos = 0;
                    auto take = [&](uint64_t& v) {
                        if (sz - fpos < 8) return false;
                        v = rd64(f + fpos);
                        fpos += 8;
                        return true;
                    };
                    if ((need_u && !take(ent.uncompressed_size)) ||
                        (need_c && !take(ent.compressed_size)) ||
                        (need_o && !take(ent.local_header_offset)))
                        return fail(error, "zip: short zip64 extra field in '" + ent.name + "'");
                    found = true;
                    break;
                }
                xpos += 4 + sz;
            }
            if (!found)
                return fail(error, "zip: missing zip64 extra field in '" + ent.name + "'");
        }

        index_.emplace(ent.name, entries_.size());
        entries_.push_back(std::move(ent));
        pos += kCentralSize + var_len;
    }

    data_ = data;
    len_  = len;
    return true;
}

const std::vector<entry_t>& archive_t::entries() const noexcept {
    return entries_;
}

const entry_t* archive_t::find(std::string_view name) const {
    const auto it = index_.find(std::string(name));
    return it == index_.end() ? nullptr : &entries_[it->second];
}

bool archive_t::extract(const entry_t& e, std::vector<uint8_t>& out,
                        std::string* error, uint64_t max_size) const {
    out.clear();
    if (!data_) return fail(error, "zip: archive not open");
    const std::string& n = e.name;
    if (e.is_encrypted()) return fail(error, "zip: '" + n + "' is encrypted");
    if (e.method != 0 && e.method != 8)
        return fail(error, "zip: '" + n + "' uses unsupported compression method " +
                               std::to_string(e.method));
    if (e.uncompressed_size > max_size)
        return fail(error, "zip: '" + n + "' is too large (" +
                               std::to_string(e.uncompressed_size) + " bytes)");
    if (e.uncompressed_size > std::numeric_limits<size_t>::max())
        return fail(error, "zip: '" + n + "' does not fit in memory");

    // the local header's own name/extra lengths may differ from the central copy
    if (!in_range(e.local_header_offset, kLocalSize, len_) ||
        rd32(data_ + e.local_header_offset) != kLocalSig)
        return fail(error, "zip: bad local header for '" + n + "'");
    const uint8_t* lh       = data_ + e.local_header_offset;
    const uint64_t data_off = e.local_header_offset + kLocalSize + rd16(lh + 26) + rd16(lh + 28);
    if (!in_range(data_off, e.compressed_size, len_))
        return fail(error, "zip: data for '" + n + "' is truncated");

    const uint8_t* src   = data_ + data_off;
    const size_t   csize = static_cast<size_t>(e.compressed_size);
    const size_t   usize = static_cast<size_t>(e.uncompressed_size);

    if (e.method == 0) {
        if (csize != usize)
            return fail(error, "zip: stored entry '" + n + "' has mismatched sizes");
        out.assign(src, src + csize);
    } else {
        out.resize(usize);
        z_stream zs{};
        if (inflateInit2(&zs, -MAX_WBITS) != Z_OK)
            return fail(error, "zip: inflateInit failed");

        uint8_t  dummy    = 0;
        uint8_t* out_base = usize ? out.data() : &dummy;
        size_t   in_left  = csize;
        // zlib needs a non-zero output window to make progress; with
        // avail_out == 0 it returns Z_BUF_ERROR even for a valid empty
        // deflate stream, so give an empty entry one scratch byte.
        size_t   out_left = usize ? usize : 1;
        zs.next_in  = const_cast<Bytef*>(reinterpret_cast<const Bytef*>(src));
        zs.next_out = out_base;
        std::string err;
        for (;;) {
            if (zs.avail_in == 0 && in_left) {
                const size_t chunk = std::min<size_t>(in_left, UINT_MAX);
                zs.avail_in = static_cast<uInt>(chunk);
                in_left -= chunk;
            }
            if (zs.avail_out == 0 && out_left) {
                const size_t chunk = std::min<size_t>(out_left, UINT_MAX);
                zs.avail_out = static_cast<uInt>(chunk);
                out_left -= chunk;
            }
            const int rc = inflate(&zs, Z_NO_FLUSH);
            if (rc == Z_STREAM_END) break;
            if (rc == Z_OK) continue;
            if (rc == Z_BUF_ERROR) {
                if (zs.avail_out == 0 && out_left == 0)
                    err = "zip: '" + n + "' inflates past its declared size";
                else
                    err = "zip: deflate stream of '" + n + "' is truncated";
            } else {
                err = "zip: corrupt deflate stream in '" + n + "'" +
                      (zs.msg ? std::string(" (") + zs.msg + ")" : std::string());
            }
            break;
        }
        const size_t produced = static_cast<size_t>(zs.next_out - out_base);
        inflateEnd(&zs);
        if (!err.empty()) {
            out.clear();
            return fail(error, std::move(err));
        }
        if (produced != usize) {
            out.clear();
            return fail(error, "zip: '" + n + "' inflated to " + std::to_string(produced) +
                                   " bytes, expected " + std::to_string(usize));
        }
    }

    uLong        crc  = ::crc32(0L, Z_NULL, 0);
    const Bytef* p    = out.data();
    size_t       left = out.size();
    while (left) {
        const size_t chunk = std::min<size_t>(left, UINT_MAX);
        crc = ::crc32(crc, p, static_cast<uInt>(chunk));
        p += chunk;
        left -= chunk;
    }
    if (static_cast<uint32_t>(crc) != e.crc32) {
        out.clear();
        return fail(error, "zip: crc-32 mismatch in '" + n + "'");
    }
    return true;
}

} // namespace slop::core::util::zip
```

`src/core/util/zip_reader.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once

// src/core/util/zip_reader.hpp
// read-only in-memory zip archive: central directory (zip64 aware),
// stored + deflate extraction with size and crc-32 checks

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace slop::core::util::zip {

struct entry_t {
    std::string name;                  // as stored, '/' separators
    uint16_t    method = 0;            // 0 stored, 8 deflate
    uint16_t    flags  = 0;
    uint32_t    crc32  = 0;
    uint64_t    compressed_size     = 0;
    uint64_t    uncompressed_size   = 0;
    uint64_t    local_header_offset = 0;
    bool is_directory() const noexcept { return !name.empty() && name.back() == '/'; }
    bool is_encrypted() const noexcept { return (flags & 1u) != 0; }
};

// "PK\x03\x04" (or an empty archive's "PK\x05\x06") at offset 0
bool has_zip_magic(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) noexcept;

class archive_t {
public:
    static constexpr uint64_t kDefaultMaxEntry = 2ull << 30;   // 2 GiB
    // Parse the central directory (ZIP64 aware). Borrows `data`, which must
    // outlive the archive
    bool open(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, std::string* error = nullptr);
    const std::vector<entry_t>& entries() const noexcept;
    const entry_t* find(std::string_view name) const;   // exact match
    // Stored or deflate; checks sizes and CRC-32. False + error on encrypted
    // entries, other methods, size > max_size, truncated or corrupt data
    bool extract(const entry_t& e, std::vector<uint8_t>& out,
                 std::string* error = nullptr,
                 uint64_t max_size = kDefaultMaxEntry) const;

private:
    const uint8_t*                          data_ = nullptr;
    size_t                                  len_  = 0;
    std::vector<entry_t>                    entries_;
    std::unordered_map<std::string, size_t> index_;   // name -> entries_ position (first wins)
};

} // namespace slop::core::util::zip
```

`src/core/util/zip_writer.cpp`:

```cpp
// src/core/util/zip_writer.cpp

#include "core/util/zip_writer.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <unordered_set>

#include <zlib.h>

namespace slop::core::util::zip {

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kLocalSig   = 0x04034b50;
constexpr uint32_t kCentralSig = 0x02014b50;
constexpr uint32_t kEocdSig    = 0x06054b50;
constexpr uint16_t kVersion    = 20;   // 2.0: stored + deflate, no zip64
// 2024-01-01 00:00:00 in MS-DOS form; a fixed stamp keeps bundles reproducible
constexpr uint16_t kDosTime = 0;
constexpr uint16_t kDosDate = ((2024 - 1980) << 9) | (1 << 5) | 1;

void put16(std::string& o, uint16_t v) {
    o.push_back(static_cast<char>(v & 0xFF));
    o.push_back(static_cast<char>((v >> 8) & 0xFF));
}

void put32(std::string& o, uint32_t v) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) o.push_back(static_cast<char>((v >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF));
}

bool fail(std::string* err, const std::string& msg) {
    if (err) *err = msg;
    return false;
}

} // namespace

bool write_stored(const std::vector<file_t>& files, std::string& out, std::string* err) {
    if (files.size() > 0xFFFF) return fail(err, "zip: too many entries");
    std::unordered_set<std::string> seen;
    std::string central;
    out.clear();

    for (const auto& f : files) {
        if (f.name.empty() || f.name.size() > 0xFFFF)
            return fail(err, "zip: bad entry name");
        if (!seen.insert(f.name).second)
            return fail(err, "zip: duplicate entry '" + f.name + "'");
        if (f.data.size() > 0xFFFFFFFFull)
            return fail(err, "zip: entry '" + f.name + "' is over 4 GiB");

        const auto size = static_cast<uint32_t>(f.data.size());
        uLong crc = ::crc32(0L, Z_NULL, 0);
        crc = ::crc32(crc, reinterpret_cast<const Bytef*>(f.data.data()), size);
        const auto offset = static_cast<uint32_t>(out.size());

        put32(out, kLocalSig);
        put16(out, kVersion);
        put16(out, 0);            // flags
        put16(out, 0);            // method: stored
        put16(out, kDosTime);
        put16(out, kDosDate);
        put32(out, static_cast<uint32_t>(crc));
        put32(out, size);         // compressed == uncompressed
        put32(out, size);
        put16(out, static_cast<uint16_t>(f.name.size()));
        put16(out, 0);            // extra length
        out += f.name;
        out += f.data;

        put32(central, kCentralSig);
        put16(central, kVersion); // version made by
        put16(central, kVersion); // version needed
        put16(central, 0);
        put16(central, 0);
        put16(central, kDosTime);
        put16(central, kDosDate);
        put32(central, static_cast<uint32_t>(crc));
        put32(central, size);
        put32(central, size);
        put16(central, static_cast<uint16_t>(f.name.size()));
        put16(central, 0);        // extra
        put16(central, 0);        // comment
        put16(central, 0);        // disk start
        put16(central, 0);        // internal attrs
        put32(central, 0);        // external attrs
        put32(central, offset);
        central += f.name;
    }

    if (out.size() + central.size() > 0xFFFFFFFFull)
        return fail(err, "zip: archive over 4 GiB");
    const auto cd_offset = static_cast<uint32_t>(out.size());
    out += central;

    put32(out, kEocdSig);
    put16(out, 0);   // this disk
    put16(out, 0);   // central directory disk
    put16(out, static_cast<uint16_t>(files.size()));
    put16(out, static_cast<uint16_t>(files.size()));
    put32(out, static_cast<uint32_t>(central.size()));
    put32(out, cd_offset);
    put16(out, 0);   // comment length
    return true;
}

} // namespace slop::core::util::zip
```

```in
          xmlns:asmv3="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3"
          manifestVersion="1.0">
  <assemblyIdentity type="win32"
                    name="reverse-slop-engine"
                    version="@PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR@.@PROJECT_VERSION_MINOR@.@PROJECT_VERSION_PATCH@.0"
                    processorArchitecture="*"/>
  <trustInfo xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v3">
    <security>
      <requestedPrivileges>
        <!-- asInvoker on purpose. The engine is a spawned sidecar: an elevated
             front end hands it an elevated token automatically, which is how it
             gets the rights the kernel bridge needs. Marking it
             requireAdministrator instead would make CreateProcess fail outright
             for any non-elevated parent (ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED) rather than
             degrade, and would block running it unelevated with the
             no-driver switch during development. -->
        <requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" uiAccess="false"/>
      </requestedPrivileges>
    </security>
  </trustInfo>
  <compatibility xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:compatibility.v1">
    <application>
      <!-- Windows 10 / 11 -->
      <supportedOS Id="{8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a}"/>
    </application>
  </compatibility>
</assembly>
```
